name: Bataan National Park
description: A 23000 ha protected forest area covering Mount Natib, a dormant volcano with a wide caldera encompassing most of northern and central Bataan.

name: Death March markers
description: The Bataan Death March passed through the center of Abucay, as marked by the life-size white obelisks lining the original route along Bataan National Road.

name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
description: Abucay's main Roman Catholic church, established in 1588 and is the oldest in Bataan. The church also doubled a fortress during the Dutch invasion and was subsequently repaired in the Baroque style.
address: Bataan National Road corner Laon Road, Laon
directions: in front of the town plaza

name: Pasukulan Falls
description: A 60 m cascade along the eastern slopes of Mount Natib.

name: Wawa Lati Lighthouse
description: A lighthouse at the mouth of the Abucay River overlooking Manila Bay.

name: Sibul Nature Spring Resort
description: A waterpark run by the municipal government that uses cold water from a natural spring supplied by the Mount Natib massif.

name: Country Pool Villas
description: An events venue with swimming pool, pickleball court and other recreational facilities

name: Abucay Public Market
directions: at the back of the new municipal hall

name: Puregold Abucay
directions: in front of Tomas Pinpin Elementary School

name: AJ Lugawan
description: Restaurant serving rice porridge.

name: Carpio Eatery
address: Roman Superhighway corner Decena Avenue, Gabon

name: Mang Ben's Kambingan
description: Restaurant serving goat dishes.

name: Abulug-Ballesteros Bayview Boulevard
description: An extensive seaside promenade along the Babuyan Channel running east towards the municipality of Ballesteros.

name: Lucban Bridge
description: The longest bridge in northwestern Cagayan, offering commanding views over the Abulug River.

name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Parish Church
description: Abulug's main Roman Catholic parish church. Nearby is the Dela Torre residence, home to a venerated image of the dead Christ (Santo Entierro).

name: Gandia Farm
description: An eco and agritourism venue and recreational space along the Abulug River.

name: Honey Bakes Cafe
address: Kabugao-Junction Luna Road, Purok Paraiso, Libertad

name: Travellers Inn by Java
description: Also has a restaurant.

name: SJD Sagana Resort
description: SJD Sagana Resort in San Pedro MacArthur Leyte offers comfortable rooms with air-conditioning, private bathrooms, and stunning pool views. Each room includes a dining table and inner courtyard views, ensuring a relaxing stay.

name: Aglipay Caves
description: The main tourist attraction in Aglipay, it is a 100 ha complex of forests and hills whose highlight is a 37-chamber cave system where Gregorio Aglipay was said to have gone into hiding during the Philippine wars of independence. The area also has camping facilities.

name: Pensal Falls
description: A 3-tier cascade over a gently-sloped rock formation.

name: Claredita Falls
description: A 5-tier cascade on a vertical rock face surrounded by blue-colored lagoons.

name: Napipiwongan Falls
description: A 7-tier cascade named after the local term for the swallows that reside in the area.

name: Panagsalukag Festival
description: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

name: Decentea
description: A milktea place with some snacks.

name: Basilica Minore of Our Lady of Charity
description: Agoo's main Roman Catholic church, destroyed multiple times by earthquakes and rebuilt in its present state in 1975. Its main draw is the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Charity. It also has an ecclesiastical museum.
address: Manila North Road corner Grotto Road, Consolacion

name: Eagle of the North Park
description: A park featuring a massive sculpture of an eagle, believed to symbolize the Marcos regime's influence in the Ilocos Region.

name: Museo de Iloko
description: A museum of local history and culture, set inside the old colonial-era municipal building. The first floor is partially leased out as commercial space.
address: Manila North Road corner Cases Boulevard, Santa Barbara

name: Agoo–Damortis Protected Landscape and Seascape
description: An extensive protected area along the coast of Agoo featuring a mix of beaches, forest and estuarine wetlands.

name: Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto
description: A Roman Catholic hillside shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary and the site of the alleged Marian apparitions to Judiel Nuerva, in what became known as the "Miracle of Agoo".

name: Splash Town Waterpark & Resort
description: A resort with swimming pools and other waterpark-related activities and overnight accommodation.

name: Camp Wagi
description: A mountainside nature park and campground.

name: Agoo Swimmersworld Resort & Hotel
address: Manila North Road, San Agustin Norte

name: Hundred Islands National Park
description: An archipelago of 123 small, pristine isles, four of which have been developed for tourists. They can be reached via chartered excursion or boat ride from the Lucap wharf outside of Alaminos.

name: Lucap Wharf/Lighthouse
description: The highlight of the area serving as the embarkation point to the Hundred Islands but also a seafront venue with stores, restaurants, a miniature model of the islands, and a very peculiar lighthouse with stairs wrapping around the outside of the structure.

name: Cathedral Parish of St. Joseph the Patriarch
description: The first church was built in 1770, but it was rebuilt a few times after being burned to where current church dates to about 1893. Also try People's Park adjacent if you need to stretch your legs.

name: Bolo Beach
description: Local beach at about where the Hundred Islands start, but may have to pay and also it is not as serene as some (e.g. seaweed, dirty toilets).

name: Nepo Mart-Alaminos
description: Outlet mall.

name: Alaminos Market Vendors Multi-Purpose Cooperative
description: Wet/dry market with San Roque Supermarket-Alaminos Branch.

name: Divimart-Alaminos
description: Home goods store.

name: Maxine By The Sea Seafood Restaurant
description: This one is nice because you can look out at Lingayen Gulf and all the launches to the Hundred Islands while you eat. But a little spendy. Also has 9 rooms for ₱3100.

name: Los Pedritos Alaminos
description: Tasty bread. There cinnamon roll is heavenly.There brazo however is a bit rough. Dine in food are good as well specially there bulalo and bangus sisig and crispy pata.
address: 2nd Floor Montemayor Commercial Complex, Marcos Avenue, Poblacion

name: Vinz Ihaw-ihaw Resto
description: Best seafood boodlefight in town.

name: Quadro Pizza
description: American food restaurant.

name: Celia's Cafe
description: American food restaurant.

name: Appetitoso Cafe & Bistro
address: Ground Floor RML building M.Montemayor St

name: Carribean Transient House
description: Friendly hosts, wifi, breakfast, restaurant/bar, patio, landscaping.

name: Monte Rio Gardens Bed & Breakfast
description: Another homey stay with wifi, a/c, breakfast.

name: Monte Rio Gardens Bed & Breakfast
description: Set amid cafes, eateries and shops, this unassuming hotel off a main road is a 3-minute walk from the closest bus stop. It's 5 km from Lucap Park, which offers boat access to Hundred Islands National Park.
address: Monte Rio Compound, M. Montemayor St., Poblacion

name: Nuestra Señora del Pilar Church
alt_name: Our Lady of the Pillar Parish Church
description: Alaminos' main Roman Catholic church, dating back to the Spanish colonial era near the municipal hall. Its patron is the Nuestra Señora del Pilar, after an image of it was retrieved from a town well.

name: Museo ni Cipra
description: An art museum featuring abstract and geometric art inside the Acropolis South subdivision. It was established by the Museo ni Cipra Foundation as a means of platform to showcase the works of its founder Cipra Kamatoy whose works has been featured in the Ayala Museum in Makati, and other local artists supported by the foundation. Some artworks are available for purchase.

name: Fule Mansion
description: An sea-green old mansion noted for its ornate façade. Its fence is adorned by statues of lions and eagles. A small but interesting number of heritage houses can be seen in the vicinity of the residence, particularly along J.P. Rizal and Del Pilar Avenues.

name: Alaminos Goat Farm
description: Buy fresh goat milk and other dairy products derived from goat milk like ice cream, and cheese locally known as kesong puti. The farm was established by local goat breeder Valeriano "Rene" L. Almeda in 2005 who pioneered dairy goat farming in the Philippines.

name: Kayumanggi Foods
description: Alaminos-based preserved-fruits manufacturer. They maintain a store where tourists can purchase preserved fruit products in jars. Also within the site is Francisco’s Halo Halo, ran by the same company where they sell halo-halo, a popular shaved-iced Filipino dessert mixed with various toppings including beans and fruits.

name: Robinsons Easymart Alaminos
address: KCD Commercial Complex, Maharlika Highway, Barangay II

name: Royal Palm Paradise Resort and Spa
Provincial Tourism, Culture and the Arts Office
address: Tourism Bldg, Albay Astrodome Complex, F. Aquende Dr, Legazpi

name: Holy Cross Parish Church
description: Alcala's main Roman Catholic church, first built in 1881. It was rebuilt in 1968 following an earthquake. It is as a popular pilgrimage site in Pangasinan for housing a relic of the Holy Cross.

name: Ben's Halo-Halo Ice Cream Alcala
address: Poblacion East, New Public Market Building

name: Mount Guiwan
description: A 1915 m high peak believed to be the highest in the Sierra Madre.

name: Galintuja Falls
description: A cascade along the boundary with Aurora province.

name: Canili Lake
description: A man-made reservoir formed by the Canili Dam used for agriculture, fishing and hydropower purposes. It covers the boundary with the municipality of Maria Aurora in Aurora province and is part of the hydropower system that includes Pantabangan Dam in Nueva Ecija.

name: eMpyrean Bliss Hotspring Farm Resort
description: A resort along the Digoliat River built around a natural hot spring.

name: Bundok Bakery
description: Restaurant and bakery. Its main specialty is coconut (buko) pie.

name: Tita Bebot's
directions: at the back of Petron gas station

name: Pata Negra Alona Beach Dive Center Resort
description: Padi dive center resort, providing dive courses and daily trips to Balicasag, Pamilacan, Cabilao and Bohol. Scuba guides with more than 3,000 dives. New Aqualung scuba equipment. Resort and accommodation included.

name: Piratas Alona Dive Center
description: Their PADI MSDT instructors teach students from beginners to professionals, plus specialty courses. They also do daily fun dives, dive trips to Balicasag, Pamilacan and Cabilao islands. They have brand new Cressi equipment.
directions: Turn left at the beach, walk 500 m.

name: Reef Seekers Alona Beach Dive Center
description: Padi Dive center, providing dive courses and daily trips to Balicasag and Pamilacan scuba diving. Aqualung partner center.

name: Dolphin watching
description: Boats leave from Alona Beach at dawn and will take you to see dolphins having their morning exercise. It is important to book your boat a day ahead of time because the dolphins appear quite early.

name: Jadski
description: A money changer, internet café and souvenir shop. Credit cards should not be used there, as credit card number thefts have been reported by tourists who used credit cards at the business.
directions: Near the police office just off of Alona Beach

name: Hera Greek Taverna
hours: Daily 9AM-10PM, with the exception of Tuesdays

name: Pyramid Bar and Restaurant
description: It is an al fresco restaurant along Alona Beach. Aside from fresh seafood catch, the restaurant serves other varieties like sandwiches, pasta, noodles, chili chicken, beef teriyaki and pork cordon bleu. The bar serves fresh fruit juices, carbonated drinks, beer, wine and cocktails. At night, torches complete the tropical dining atmosphere.

name: Trudi's
description: Trudi's on the beach is relatively cheap and quite good.

name: Casa-Nova Garden
description: Fan single/double with shared bathroom.

name: Chill-out Guesthouse Panglao
description: Chill-out Guesthouse Panglao offers fan and air-conditioned room with terrace, soft beds and private toilet and bath. Its facilities and services include chillout bar, wireless internet access, tour assistance and massage services.

name: Alonaland Resort
description: 100 m from Alona Beach. Rooms, casitas, and villas. A/C with a refrigerator, shower, luggage rack, balcony/deck, and internet. The casitas and villas come with more features and include a kitchenette, cable TV, and dining area.

name: Hayahay Resort
description: Alona Beach resort has an open restaurant on the beach, 11 comfortable rooms with private bath and Wi-Fi access, and exciting water activities like snorkelling, dolphin watching, and scuba diving.

name: Kalipayan Resort
description: Cottages with A/C in a huge garden at the far end of Alona Beach. 5 min walk to beach. Nice pool, excellent restaurant and dive centre. Free WiFi.

name: Lost Horizon Annex
description: Rooms with balcony, ceiling fans, private toilet and bath. Restaurant, bar, boat and land tours, and internet.

name: Panglao Regents Park Resort
description: 35 rooms with contemporary design and architecture, all with full amenities.

name: Villa Kasadya
description: Villa Kasadya is a boutique resort in Danao, Panglao, a short walk from Alona Beach. It offers 13 rooms across three categories — Deluxe Rooms, Garden Villas and two-bedroom Villas with private pool — making it suitable for couples and families. The property is close to Alona Beach's restaurants and dive operators, and within easy reach of Panglao's island-hopping departure points.

name: Alona Kew White Beach Resort
description: Bungalows and well-appointed rooms set in lush surroundings.

name: Amorita Resort
description: 6 ocean view villas with king-sized bed, individually-controlled split A/C, wide-screen LCD cable TV, and a mini bar refrigerator. Infinity pool, restaurant with free WiFi, wellness spa, boutique, leisure area, and garden.

name: Sun Apartelle
description: Apartment resort/hotel.

name: Jpark Island Resort Alona
description: Features 118 rooms and suites with ocean, pool, or garden views, and a direct access to Alona Beach. Has 3 swimming pools, a beachfront, 2 dining options, such as The Abalone Restaurant and Aqus Bar and Cafe, and event spaces.

name: Anda Falls
description: If you're tired of salt water stinging your eyes, there is a large and deep concrete cistern to swim in at the base of the falls.
directions: take the concrete road north that starts 1 block east of the church until it ends at the cemetery. Turn right on the track and then swing left to follow the eastern cemetery wall. Continue uphill following the track under the power line and follow the sounds of tumbling water

name: Anda water caves
description: There are many underground rivers with transparent water coming from the mountains to the sea.

name: Food center
description: Has 8 stalls offering cheap Filipino food, pizza & pasta in a long, open-air, covered area. Dawn to dusk.

name: On The Road Resto & Bar
description: On the Road is a place where local people and foreigners can learn about all cultures. BBQ, fresh beer, cocktail, many kind of music, Wi-Fi, Apple TV.

name: Old Castle
description: Looks like a European castle, except that it is on a beach with palm trees. Good food, mostly European menu.

name: Flower-Beach Resort
description: Solid houses with own terrace and sea view, shower and toilet. Standard with 2 single beds or 1 double beds, ceiling fan. Deluxe are bigger, one double bed and one single bed, space to add an additional bed, so comfortable for 4 persons, air-conditioning, warm water, minibar. Our restaurant serving international, Asian and Filipino dishes, beach bar. Own PADI dive center, all equipment and boats for snorkeling and diving. Our dive center offers a wide range of PADI courses. Transport service available, from and to all points on Bohol and also Cebu city/airport.

name: Little Miami Beach
description: Seven small but well maintained cabins, each with a tiny verandah, air-con, cable TV, en suite shower, WC & wash hand basin. Surprisingly it has better Wi-Fi than nearby resorts charging three times the price. Even more surprisingly, the German-made shower heater produces an adequate flow of water with a stable temperature. Volleyball & table tennis available.
directions: Go to the church. Walk to the sea's edge across the grassed plaza. Turn right and walk for 300 m; it's right on the water's edge. No direct access by road

name: 1PEACE beach resort
description: Chilled out and friendly atmosphere. Located right on a small beach, here you can enjoy the sea, by snorkeling on coral wall. They rent motorbikes for day trips to waterfalls, chocolate hills or just for exploring the island. Also bicycles and kayaks are available, you can paddle to see the sunset from the ocean or stay in the tower, listen the sounds of the nature in hammock. Every night you can sit around a big table with other guests and enjoy the family dinner what is freshly made everyday by their French and Finnish kitchen wizards. Cuisine changes by wishes of the guests. Breakfast & lunch is also available.

name: Kims Garden
description: Kims Garden is a quiet and beautiful place to stay. Best place for snorkeling.

name: Clark International Airport
description: Also called Diosdado Macapagal International Airport (DMIA)
directions: in Clark Freeport Zone, approximately 5 km from Angeles

name: Dau Bus Terminal
description: Angeles' central bus terminal (pronounced as “da-oo”), it serves buses headed for the city and also those headed toward Northern Luzon. There is one shelter, which has some shops and food stands. Nearby is a CityMall shopping mall, fast-food chains, and a Hotel Sogo location.

name: Five Star
description: Has trips from their terminals in Pasay and Cubao.

name: Philippine Rabbit
description: Plies the Santa Cruz, Manila-Dau route.

name: Genesis
description: Operates a direct service to Clark Airport from Trinoma Mall in Quezon City.

name: Fort Stotsenburg
description: The former headquarters of American cavalry divisions sent to the Philippines during the Philippine-American War. Destroyed in World War II, only its gateposts remains.

name: Pamintuan Mansion
alt_name: NHCP Museum of Philippine Social History
description: A century-old heritage house, which houses the Museum of Philippine Social History since 2015. The museum features exhibits and artifacts related to Filipino daily livelihood and leisure. It was used by the American soldiers during World War II, converted to the Angeles Hotel sometime after the war, and was the satellite office of the Philippine central bank from 1993 to 2009.

name: Founders' Residence
description: Located at the heart of Santo Rosario, it is the oldest building in the city. It was built in 1824 by the city founder, Don Ángel Pantaleón de Miranda, and his wife, Doña Rosalia de Jesus, and was inherited by their only daughter, Doña Juana de Miranda de Henson. This house, which is made of high stone and an ornate gate, nostalgically symbolizes the glorious past of Angeles amidst the overwhelming onslaughts of modernization.

name: Post Office Building
description: It is a building that was constructed in 1899 for the purpose of depositing religious statues and carriages of the Catholic Church, hence the name Deposito. It was also used as the headquarters of the 11th Film Exchange U.S. Army from 1946 to 1947 and was then used as a jailhouse for recalcitrant U.S. troops during the Philippine–American War. On February 6, 1967, the Angeles Post Office moved to this building. It is now the site of Angeles Physical Therapy Rehabilitation Center.

name: Pisamban Maragul
description: Colloquially called the "Big Church" in Kapampangan, it was constructed from 1877 to 1896 by the "Polo y Servicio" labor system, a kind of forced labor imposed on Filipino peasants by the Spanish colonial government. It was used as a military hospital by the U.S. Army from August 1899 to December 1900. Its backyard was the execution ground used by Spanish forces to shoot Filipino rebels and suspects. In 2026, its status was upgraded into a basilica.
address: Santo Rosario corner Santo Entiero Streets
directions: in front of Museo ning Angeles and beside Holy Angel University

name: Holy Family Academy Building
description: Holy Family Academy Building was once a convent and was served as a military hospital of the U.S. Army in 1900. It was later used as troop barracks, officers' quarters and arsenal by the Japanese Imperial Military Forces in 1942.

name: Museo ning Angeles
description: Housed in a vintage building located at the "Santo Rosario Historic District", this edifice was constructed in 1922 and served as the Town Hall until 1998. The museum has become the venue of the city's cultural activities be it from the or government sector. Since it opened in 1999, it has been a venue for various activities from exhibits, art classes, concerts, venue for performances and climax for traditional celebrations. In June 2012, the National Museum of the Philippines declared the Museo ning Angeles as an "Important Cultural Property of the Philippines," the first cultural property to be given such a distinction. The museum is administered by Kuliat Foundation, Inc.
address: Santo Rosario corner Santo Entiero Streets

name: Bale Herencia
description: Built in 1860, it is a picturesque house with the unsavory reputation of having been built for the mistress of a parish priest. The current owners have leased the place to various restaurants, food stalls, and other businesses like salons and computer shops. The antique architecture, however, is still preserved.
address: Lakandula St. corner Santo Rosario St

name: Center for Kapampangan Studies
description: A museum inside the Holy Angel University showcasing the history and culture of the Kapampangans, the main ethnic group in Pampanga.

name: Lily Hill / Goddess of Peace Shrine
description: Lily Hill is the highest point in the Clark area with an elevation of 32 meters (105 ft). The name of the hill, is the anglicized form of the word "lili" in the local language of the Aetas which means "lost". It was used as an outpost by American soldiers, and later by the Japanese during World War II. In 1998, the Goddess of Peace Shrine was set up, which has a large statue as its centerpiece accompanied by a plaque in English and Japanese.

name: Apung Mamacalulu Shrine
alt_name: Archdiocesan Shrine of the Lord of the Holy Sepulcher
description: A stone church which is known for hosting the image of Jesus Christ known as "Apung Mamacalulu" (Merciful Lord). The image commissioned in the mid-19th century during the Spanish colonial era, is believed to be miraculous by its devotees.

name: Expo Pilipino
description: An exposition center opened in 1998 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the declaration of Philippine independence. It features a 35,000-seater covered amphitheater.

name: Bayanihan Park
description: A park at the Clark Freeport Zone near SM City Clark shopping mall. It features the "Salakot", a large pavilion structure named after the native hat of the same name due to the shape of its roof.

name: Clark Freeport and Special Economic Zone
Chapel of the Holy Guardian Angel
description: The main chapel of the Holy Angel University. It is noted for its contemporary white facade which has an unconventional structure for modern churches. It is dedicated to the Guardian Angel, which is the patron of both the school and the city of Angeles. It also hosts an image which was commissioned in the Spanish colonial era in 1830 by Don Angel Pantaleon de Miranda.

name: SEA Games Clock Monument
description: A relic from the South East Asian Games in Clark in 2019.

name: Mount Arayat Trek
description: Available November through May. Prices range: day trips (minimum of 3 persons, ₱800 per person) and overnight trips (minimum of 3 persons, ₱2500 per person).

name: Trekking Mount Pinatubo
description: A once-in-a-lifetime experience, highly recommended for hiking enthusiasts. Board a Filipino 4x4 jeep and experience a thrilling drive across Crow Valley, a moon-like terrain, with vast ash fields and rocky rivers. You will hike up towards the summit passing through sandy cliffs and up a mountain path. The views of the Crater Lake are absolutely breathtaking. On the way back you have the opportunity to visit an Aeta Village and enjoy interacting with one of the oldest indigenous tribes in the Philippines. The trip is a full day tour departing early in the morning. You will hike between 3 and 6 hours depending on your fitness.

name: Clark International Speedway
description: Reserve a day for motorsports activity at the Clark International Speedway, a permanent race track. No walk-ins allowed. Closed Mondays.

name: MarQuee Mall
description: A major shopping mall under Ayala Malls.
directions: beside North Luzon Expressway near Angeles Exit

name: City Mall-Angeles City
description: A small retail center in Dau, Mabalacat.

name: Robinsons Angeles
description: A Robinsons shopping mall.

name: SM City Clark
description: A major shopping mall at the Clark Freeport Zone under the SM Supermalls chain.

name: Nepo Mall
address: Doña Teresa Avenue corner Saint Joseph Street

name: S&R Membership Shopping - Mabalacat
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.

name: Landers Superstore Angeles
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.

name: Angeles Fried Chicken
description: The oldest restaurant in Angeles City, offers a wide array of food. Locally famous for its juicy chicken (crispy or regular) with coleslaw and gravy. Also popular: gambas, sisig, calamares,Japanese fried chicken, pancit canton, bihon, clubhouse sandwich, iced tea.
directions: near Casino Filipino-Angeles- 2 km away from Clarkfield

name: Tequila Reef Cantina
description: Authentic Mexican cuisine, barbecue chicken & ribs, New Orleans “Cajun” specialties, steaks, burgers, sandwiches and Filipino food.
address: Corner of A. Santos and Real Streets

name: Camalig
description: A local restaurant open since 1973 known for "Armando's Pizza" which is billed as "the national pizza". It is purported to be made in-house using classic homegrown Pinoy pizza recipe. Camalig has a selection of 18 pizza flavors. It is housed inside a historic structure built in 1840 by Don Ciriaco de Miranda, the first gobernadorcillo of Angeles, and was used as a grain storehouse. It was restored in 1980 by Armando L. Nepomuceno.

name: Spanglish
description: Mexican food restaurant.
address: Pavilion Mall Building, Manuel A. Roxas Highway

name: Clark Lomi House
description: A large eatery inside Clark airbase serving a variety of Filipino local food. Prices are affordable and food tastes good. They have indoor and outdoor area dining. Parking is huge.They also serve coffee, fruit shakes, milktea and hot or iced coffee.

name: Makimura Ramen Bar
address: Tinio Building, Manila North Rd, Balibago

name: The Orange Bucket- Balibago Branch
description: Cajun Fusion restaurant.

name: 19 Copung Copung
description: Filipino & Exotic Filipino foods restaurant.
address: Manila North Road corner Looban Street

name: Z TAPA'S Tapsilog Atbp.
description: Filipino eatery.
address: Arayat Street Corner S. Rivera Lim Avenue

name: My Lola Nor's Meryendahan
description: Every dish is surprisingly delicious and authentic. They have short orders for merienda and lunch servings. All food is cooked very distinctively. Tidtad capampangan (dinuguan/pork blood stew), pork sinigang, fresh lumpia (the crepe is hand-made, smooth and soft) with peanut sauce (amazing), pancit luglug (the serving is generous), batirol (everyday Christmas!) and their batirol shake.

name: The Mansion
address: The Villages, Prince Balagtas Ave, Clark, 2009 Pampanga

name: Whythaus Grill & KTV
address: Severina Lim Avenue, Diamond Subdivision, Balibago

name: Spencer's Fusion Bar & Restaurant
directions: in Best Western Plus Metro Clark

name: R&B Music Venue
description: Offers amazing music performance.

name: Skytrax Superclub
description: Disco club.

name: The Palms Bar and Restaurant
description: Saturday live band night is great. Good food and beers.

name: Mi Amor
description: Highly recommend place for those who love singing but have a wallet friendly budget.

name: Moon Cafe
address: Moon Cafe Bldg. Madeira St. Riverside Subdivision, Angeles City, Pampanga

name: K Cafe
address: Nepo Quad, Plaridel St. Sto. Rosario and Diamond Subd. Balibago

name: LALA Garden Cafe
address: Lot 22, Poinsettia Ave, Pcs-35560, Golden Dragon Village, Brgy Pampang
price: A Korean-style bakery and cafe that also serves rice meals

name: Mind Control Cafe
address: LOT 1 BLK 2 Fields Ave, Cor Teodoro St, Balibago

name: Hotel Vanna
description: Well-maintained rooms, all equipped with air-conditioning, flat-screen cable TV and private toilet and bath. Facilities and services are room service, airport transfer and laundry service.

name: Affinity Condo Resort
description: Feel at home with your own kitchen, dining room, separate bedrooms, built-in-robes, linen cupboards and low-cost laundry facility. There are fully furnished studios, 1-bedroom and 2 -bedroom condominiums.

name: ABC Hotel
description: This four-star hotel is known as "The Party Hotel," with unique furnishings such as an in-room party Jacuzzi and a sauna cabin. Its main attractions are its tropical beach pool and bar, and the Sky Bar and Lounge on the ABC Hotel rooftop, which allegedly offers the best views of the sunset over the mountains west of Angeles City. The hotel has a free shuttle service for its guests to and from Clark International Airport, as well as a helicopter service to Manila, Subic, and Mt. Pinatubo. All its guestrooms have Wi-Fi internet access, and are furnished with imported king-size to XXL mattresses among other five-star caliber.
directions: in front of SM City Clark

name: Oasis Hotel
description: Once a favorite of visiting US Air Force officers, this quiet, respectable hotel is in a secure residential compound. The hotel has all the services you will need including a 24-hour room service, 24-hour foreign currency exchange, 24-hour high security and dual-key safe deposit boxes, laundry service, a beautiful swmimming pool, a business center with internet access and a gift shop. The hotel restaurant, Maranao Grill, is open 24 hours and there is an English pub. Standard and deluxe rooms. This is a place where you can bring your wife and kids if you are not able to leave them at home.
address: Clark Perimeter Road, Clarkview Compound, Malabanias

name: Fontana Hotel and Villas - Fontana Hot Spring Leisure Parks
description: It features a world-class wave pool that can electronically produce various types of waves and three giant aqua thrill slides. The park also has other attractions like the mad scientist water laboratory, the buccaneer ship and the lazy river. A prelude to the coming 18-hole championship course, the pitch and putt of the golf course is a perfect place for golfers to practice their game. It also has a casino which offers over a hundred slot and video machines and 40 gaming tables with games like Baccarat, Blackjack, Roulette and Pai-Gow.

name: Clarkton Hotel
description: This is a German-managed hotel that has 93 rooms. Large suites are available on the 3rd floor. It has an excellent restaurant, on-site go-go bar, a 24-hour room service and a large, clean pool. The pool area is a popular gathering place. Single deluxe room is ₱1650 while a suite is for ₱2500 or ₱2800.

name: Hotel Stotsenberg
description: This resort, with a casino, enjoys the best of worlds as it is a serene sanctuary, yet only a breeze away from an exciting nightlife. Just five minutes away from the Diosdado Macapagal International Airport, the hotel is accessible from all points in Greater Luzon via the North Luzon Expressway and other arterial highways - making it an excellent base for the discerning business as well as leisure travelers. Deluxe room is US$83, executive suit is $98, Clark suite is $263 and Stotsenberg suite is $299.

Here is a brief list of some of the amenities that await you: a 56 guest-room main building with elevator access to the roof top; a 50 guest-room Oahu Wing annex; and a large rooftop conference room for meetings, or other social functions.

The family superior deluxe rooms in the extension are huge. A large tropical garden of lawn and shrubs surrounds the 50 feet by 25 feet swimming pool. 24-hour room service is available from the hotel restaurant. Safe deposit box access is available 24 hours. Orchid rooms are priced from US$32-66.

name: Antipolo Cathedral
alt_name: International Shrine of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage
description: A circular Catholic church rebuilt in 1949 following the destruction of its original Spanish colonial building during World War II. Its main draw is a 17th-century wooden statue of the Virgin Mary that attracts pilgrims. The cathedral is popular with travelers who are about to embark on far away trips and other well-wishers and devotees. The actual image is said to have come from Mexico and survived the trip despite a fire erupting on the Galleon and later was evacuated to different locations during World War II, further establishing its popularity among devotees. A small museum behind the main cathedral shows the history of the church, the actual image (the one inside the cathedral is a replica), as well as the festivals held in the month of May (where lots of devotees flock to visit the cathedral). Below it is a souvenir shop. One can also offer a candle for loved ones or friends who are in faraway lands or about to take a trip out of town or the country.
address: P. Oliveros Street, Barangay San Jose

The cottages here are made of earth / concrete mix (as compared to Liberty which has a lot of bamboo/nipa). The company that owns this place also owns the Coco Grande hotel in Dumaguete; bookings and transport can be arranged through the hotel.

The mountain is part of a protected reserve known as Mount Arayat National Park. However, access to the area is partially restricted due to rudimentary facilities and landslides that have disrupted the usual hiking trails.

name: Our Lady of the Angels Parish
description: It was first built in 1643, but was repeatedly destroyed by a fire and an earthquake. The present church was built between 1687 and 1700. The church's ceiling and interior dome have paintings of archangels, the Virgin Mary, and symbols of heavenly authority.

name: Quezon Protected Landscape
description: It is a protected landscape on the southern end of the mighty Sierra Madre range, which straddles the boundary with Pagbilao. It was founded in 1934 as a national park until it was elevated into a protected area in 2003. It covers of tropical rainforests, home to endemic species of birds, reptiles, mammals, and trees. Inside the park is Mount Pinagbanderahan, where a Philippine revolutionary flag was raised, and is reachable through an hour of hiking. There are also caves and waterfalls within the park, and some campsites.
directions: Entrance along the Old Zigzag Road on the Pagbilao side.

name: Highest Point View
description: Located at 7400 ft above sea level, this attraction used to be the highest point in the Philippine Highway System until it was surpassed by another spot in Tinoc, Ifugao in 2019. The location also provides a view of the mountains of Atok and surrounding municipalities including Mt. Pulag.

name: Haight's Place
description: Located at 7937 ft above sea level, it provides a panoramic view of Atok's vegetable terraces which includes the Naguey Rice Terraces in the west. Frost occurs in the area from December to February. The place was named after an American soldier who fought during the Spanish-American war who brought the first vegetable seedlings for the area which has a temperate climate who also married a local and settled in Atok.

name: Benguet-Kochi Sisterhood Park
description: A park commemorating the 40th sisterhood ties between the province of Benguet and Kochi prefecture of Japan located within Haight's Place. At least 34 cherry blossom trees were planted in the area in mid-2016. A future tourist destination especially among the locals after the trees' first bloom expected to occur in 2019.

name: Tinawagan Hills Campsite and L-Farm

description: The seat of local government in Bacarra. Despite multiple renovations it has retained its original neo-classic façade.

name: Lazo Ancestral Home
description: A well-preserved Spanish-era residence built for one of Bacarra's elite families.
address: Rizal Boulevard corner Andres Lazo Avenue, Santa Rita

name: Peralta Ancestral Home
description: A Spanish-era residence used as a shooting location for domestic period films.

name: Natba Beach
description: Bacarra's main beach, named after its silver sand.

name: Municipal Tourism Activity Center
description: Information on accommodation, transport and tours to Pamilacan Island. The center also offers extremely clean, free-of-use toilets and showers, a welcome sight in Bohol.

name: Bohol–Panglao International Airport
description: Opened in November 2018. Air Juan has flights from Caticlan, Cebu, and Maasin. AirSWIFT has flights from El Nido. Cebu Pacific has flights from Clark, Manila, Cagayan de Oro, and Davao. Philippine Airlines has flights from Clark, Manila, and Davao. Philippines AirAsia has flights from Manila. Royhle Air Way Charter has flights from Dumaguete.

name: Baclayon Church and Museum
description: Baclayon is known for its historic Catholic Church, an important part of Boholano and national heritage, being declared in 1995 as a National Historic Treasure. This massive ancient edifice still retains its centuries old architectural design and is considered the best preserved of its kind in the region. The relics of antiquity found in the church, and museum, which date back to the early 16th century include crystal chandeliers, brightly colored window panes, life-size religious images, carved altars with gold embossing, and a silver tabanacle. Nearby are the centuries-old stone buildings like the belfry, the hermita and elementary school.

name: Historic Marketplace
description: Another Spanish-era building in the town ís the spacious public market with giant stone columns supporting the roof. The products of local industries like the sarok, winnowing baskets, fans, shopping bags, mats and the like are sold at the market day every Wednesday. Fruits, vegetables, pigs, chickens, dried fish, and other products from people in the hinterlands are also sold to serve the needs of the town’s residents.

name: Ancestral Houses
description: Spared through community advocacy from a provincial road-widening project’s plan for their demolition, the Spanish colonial ancestral houses that line the main road of Balcayon have instead been preserved and stand as compellingly as ever. There are over 67 ancestral houses in the municipality, which are within easy walking distance from Baclayon Church. The houses show Spanish-Filipino wooden craftsmanship and styling, some of which were constructed as early as 1853. In an effort to further fund the preservation of the heritage houses, they are often utilized for cultural shows and tours, festivals and fiestas, as well as some having been turned into home-stays; a great accommodation option for those wanting a true taste of Boholano culture and lifestyle.

name: Pamilacan Island
description: part of the Municipality of Baclayon, is a small island 14 km, or a 1-hour pump-boat ride, from the mainland. There are only around 235 families living on the island, whose main livelihoods now concentrate on dolphin and whale watching tours and subsistence fishing, but in the past have also included whale, dolphin and manta ray hunting. Officially Pamilacan means “resting place of the mantas’, but is also been interpreted to derive from the word ‘pamilac’ or harpoon, a weapon that was historically used to capture the mantas, dolphins and whales. Pamilacan Island is now seen as a success story in the transformation of the community from their destructive, unsustainable hunting practices, to the protection of their marine life with dolphin and whalewatching tours now providing a valuable alternative livelihood. Pamilacan Island has also been the recipient of numerous awards from tourism councils and environmental organizations in recognition of their remarkable makeover. The island has beautiful white sand beaches, and is endowed with some great dive sites, such as ‘Dakit-Dakit’. Additionally, the island is also home to a 200-year-old Spanish fort at the northeast of the island, which served as a watch station for the Spaniards against intruders, such as pirates and other enemies. Pump-boat rides from Baclayon to Pamilacan Island can cost upward from ₱1500 per boat and it is normally advisable to organize this a day in advance if possible through the Municipal Tourism Information Center (see Contacts). However, Wednesdays are Market Days in Baclayon, and as such, more pump-boats operate to cater for the islanders visiting the market. Boat rides on Wednesday therefore can be as little as one tenth of the normal price.

name: Dolphin and Whale Watching Tours
description: The waters of Baclayon are renowned throughout the Philippines as being the premier site for Dolphin and Whale Watching Tours. The Whale species to be found are the Short-finned Pilot Whale, Melon-headed Whale and Pygmy Killer Whale, while the Dolphin species include the Rissoís, Spinner, Bottlenose and Spotted Dolphins. As of February 2011, many Whale Sharks have also been spotted off the cost of Pamilacan Island, suggesting a regeneration of a once thriving species in the area. Tours start in Baclayon around 5AM; the best time for sightings and appreciating their antics. Tours typically run until around 2PM including a rest stop at a nearby beach for snorkeling. Tour prices depend upon boat size and start from around ₱1500.

name: Buggy Rides
description: Now run through Peacock Garden Resort, an exhilarating buggy ride through the rural barangays (villages) of Baclayon is available. If merely speed and tight turns aren’t your things then the tour can also be ideal for naturists, with flora and fauna, and bird watching information stops included along the way. The tour is designed to be beneficial for the remote barangays, with a portion of the revenue from every tour going back into the barangays that are accessed. Tour price for two people in one buggy for 1½-2 hr is ₱1500 with all safety equipment is provided.

name: Scuba diving
description: Baclayon offers an extremely rich and biodiverse marine system perfect for Scuba diving. An especially popular dive site off Pamilacan Island is ‘Dakit-Dakit’, where the once damaged coral reefs from dynamite-fishing are on the repair with many varieties of coral heads, soft corals and coral strings growing. The sloping reef dive also provides encounters with huge schools of large Jackfish, Napoleon Wrasse, as well as Barracudas, Batfish, Turtles and occasionally Manta Rays.Dive sites have also been created off the coast of the Baclayon Mainland with two areas being converted into Marine Protected Areas (MPAS) in 2008 in Barangays Taguihon and Guiwanon. Already there are vast improvements observed in coral cover and fish abundance within the two, and they provide some very nice macro diving for underwater photography enthusiasts

name: Mountain biking
description: Many of Baclayon’s off-road trails have been developed for mountain biking, and the municipality is fast becoming a hub for the sport in Bohol. The mountain biking trails include easy and moderate cross-country rides, using barangay roads and single track, carabao trails. Baclayon also has long off-road trails connect different municipalities, such as Loboc, Albur, Loay, Corella, Sikatuna and Tagbilaran city. As has been well publicized in the adventure magazine “Action Asia”, the most popular and longest of which is “Bong’s Trail”. This 20-km off-road ride begins at Mount Banat-i, passing through Baclayon’s upland barangays and neighboring municipalities, and ends 2 to 4 hours later at Loboc River. Additionally, the Baclayon to Corella route is a 2-hour off-road ride, ending at the Philippine Tarsier Foundation, a great place to view Tarsiers in their natural habitat. Bike rentals are scarce in Baclayon, as well as nearby Tagbilaran City, so it is preferable to bring your own bike. However, it is possible to organize bike rentals, mountain biking guides, and gain further information ahead of time by contacting +63-928-197-9165 or +63-906-531-0860.

name: Heritage Walk
description: Baclayon Ancestral Homes Association (BAHANDI) is a neighborhood organization set up to promote and preserve not only the Baclayon ancestral houses, but also the heritage of the community. BAHANDI offer a Heritage Walk, touring the historic church, elementary school, ancestral houses, and visit a demonstration of Broas making; a Baclayon delicacy. The tour also includes a beautiful table set-up outside Baclayon Church serving refreshments of the aforementioned Broas, and traditional hot chocolate. Meals and nighttime entertainment can be organized upon request. Contact +63-38-540-9030 or +63-38-540-9327 for tour bookings.

name: Market Day Wednesdays
description: Poblacion - Set in the historic, Spanish-era Baclayon marketplace, the Wednesday Market Days provide a great opportunity to see and taste Baclayon culture up close. Native handicrafts are available, along with delicious, locally produced delicacies and sweets such as Broas (ladyfingers), nut bars, pastels, tortas, rice cake and suman. An impressive variety of fruit, vegetable and dried fish are also tempting to the curious. It is important to stay away from buying dried Manta Ray in the dried fish section, as doing so encourages the hunting of these endangered, but only supposedly “protected” animals.

name: Aproniana Souvenir Shop
description: Self proclaimed “Bohol’s ultimate souvenir destination”, Aproniana sells a wide range of souvenirs covering all of Bohol’s major tourist attractions at more affordable prices than sold near at the destinations themselves. The air-conditioned store covers 100 m² over 2 levels, but can still get somewhat overcrowded if multiple tourist buses are passing through at the same time.

name: 6 to 7
description: A small restaurant along the main highway in Poblacion underneath an ancestral house.

name: Boo Boo's Pride
description: A large floating restaurant beside the wharf, which has been converted into a Karaoke Bar. This is a favorite amongst the locals of Baclayon who can be found singing 7 nights a week until the small hours of the morning. Meals are also available on board.

name: Bohol Narra Homestay
description: Nestled in a tranquil locality beside the sea and surrounded by luscious trees, Bohol Narra Homestay provides a great family option with one room comprising of four beds available. ₱1200 per night (for 2) including breakfast.

name: Homestay de Bai
description: Located very centrally beside the Baclayon Church, Homestay de Bai offers simple and clean air-con rooms with an ideal location.

name: Mary's Pamilacan Cottages
description: Located right on the shore front of Pamilacan Island, these very basic but clean cottages offer an ideal escape from the hustle and bustle of mainland towns. Prices are; Cottage ₱500pppn including breakfast and dinner; Cottage including 3 meals ₱750pppn; Large cottage including meals ₱1000pppn.

name: Malon House
description: Dating back to the 19th century, Malon House is the largest of the ancestral houses in Baclayon. As unassuming as it looks from the outside, inside its historic grandeur is realized with antique furniture, religious icons, paintings, and impressively large wooden floorboards. Rooms including breakfast are ₱900 per night.

name: Bohol Coconut Palms Resort
description: Resort with function room for 200 people; leisure facilities include a semi-Olympic-size swimming pool with slides and kiddie pool with fountain.
price: Best rates on official website start at ₱1300

name: The Peacock Garden Luxury Resort and Spa
description: Peacock Garden is an elegant German-owned and managed resort perched on a hill with an extremely impressive infinity pool overlooking the seascape and Pamilacan Island. This was the first resort in Bohol to be granted 5-star accreditation. The resort features a fine-dining restaurant, a Roman-inspired spa, a wine cellar, music and dance club, fitness room and a members only cigar lounge.

name: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish Church
description: Bacnotan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a combined Baroque and neoclassical style during the Spanish era in 1819.
address: Guerrero Avenue corner Gabaldon Street, Raois

name: Zim-sim-og Twin Falls
description: A twin cascade facing each other on opposite sides of the Maragayap River with a height of 20 ft and a basin pool with a depth of 8-9 ft. It is named after a Kankanaey term to describe the sound of rock crashing against each other.

name: Sapilang Falls
description: A cascade located within the sprawling forested compound of the Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University - North La Union Campus.
price: entry permission required from university officials

name: Bussaoit Lake
description: A man-made reservoir used for irrigation purposes.

name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
description: A post-modern Roman Catholic church design by national artist for architecture Leandro Locsin in 1956.

name: Galongen-Quirino Surfing Area
description: A popular surfing spot along a sandbar at the mouth of the Maragayap River.

name: LU Riverfarm Seafood Resturant
description: A seafood restaurant along the Baroro River.

name: Alpas La Union
description: A beachside cafe known for hosting live performances of some of the Philippines' leading musicians.

name: La Playa Ursula
description: A beachside resort.

name: Ceres Southbound Terminal
description: Buses departing for and arriving from Dumaguete (via Mabinay) and Cebu City (via Dumaguete) arrive and depart in this terminal.

name: Ceres Northbound Terminal
description: Buses departing for and arriving from Bayawan (via Cauayan and Sipalay) and Kanlaon City (via La Carlota, La Castellana, Moises Padilla).

name: Bacolod Public Plaza
description: The Bacolod version of Central park but smaller; fountains are scattered around the plaza and a gazebo stands in the middle. The Unknown Soldiers Monument (also known as Theodore Vinther Monument) is found here. The plaza is used for events like the MassKara Festival and for activities such as Arnis (Filipino martial arts). It is also a hub for joggers and people doing aerobics during the morning.

name: Negros Occidental Provincial Capitol
description: The official seat of the provincial government and perhaps the most impressive building in Bacolod City. It served as the headquarters of the Japanese Imperial Army during World War II. The Romanesque-style building stands in landscaped grounds with a park and lagoon, and features Ang Paghimud-os ("The Struggle" in Hiligaynon), a sculpture by Eduardo Castrillo, as well as The Man and the Carabao sculpture by Felix V. Garzon.

name: Iron Dinosaurs (vintage steam locomotives)
description: Locomotives were used in Bacolod to transport sugarcane from the fields to the azucareras (sugar factories), thus they were part of making Bacolod the sugar bowl of the Philippines.
directions: One within the Bacolod Murcia Milling Co. compound and another at the La Herencia Subdivision entrance

name: Bacolod City Hall
description: A modern civic building with a neoclassical-style facade, including prominent columns and a large fountain in front.
directions: Take Central Market - Homesite jeepney route

name: Panaad Park and Sports Complex
description: The park surrounding the stadium is filled with eucalyptus trees.

name: San Sebastian Cathedral
description: Bacolod’s main Catholic church, begun in the late 19th century and completed in 1894. Built of coral stone and later covered with cement, it is one of the city’s key landmarks. The cathedral is also known for its Centennial Bells and the nearby Palacio Episcopal.

name: St. Jude Thaddeus Shrine
description: This relatively new church is dedicated to St. Jude Thaddeus, patron saint of lost causes. It is notable for its richly decorated, gold-toned Baroque-style altar, ceiling mural, and Divine Mercy shrine.

name: Carmelite Monastery
description: This Carmelite church and monastery is known for its quiet, contemplative atmosphere. Visitors may leave prayer requests, and the monastery also has a shop selling religious items and souvenirs.
directions: Short walk from Robinson's Bacolod Shopping Mall

name: Sacred Heart Church and Seminary
description: This church is notable for its European-inspired architecture, high ceilings, and tall spire, which give it a Gothic Revival look. It also has side chapels dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Virgin Mary.
directions: Just near Neg. Occ. high school and Paglaum sports complex

name: Barangay Sang Birhen Parish Church
description: This chapel, designed by Archbishop Norman Campus, is notable for its extensive shellwork. It features Leticia Sia Ledesma’s Barangay Sang Birhen ("Village of the Virgin"), a mosaic made from 95,000 shells, as well as other shell-made images of saints, Stations of the Cross, and altar pieces created from a further 30,000 shells.

name: Pope John Paul II Monument
description: Marks the site where Pope John Paul II celebrated Mass for thousands of Bacolodnons.

name: Museum Negrense De La Salle
description: A university museum with exhibits ranging from indigenous woven textiles, plantation-era furniture, religious vestments, santos, and other devotional objects to rotating works by local and international artists on social, cultural, religious, and political themes.

name: Negros Museum
description: Housed in the former Provincial Government building, The Negros Museum traces the history of Negros Occidental from its beginnings through the colonial era, the rise of the sugar industry, the revolution, and the province’s cultural development. It also features material on past governors and murals by Negrense artists, and serves as a venue for exhibitions by Filipino artists.
directions: take Mandalagan-Libertad jeep from Downtown Bacolod

name: Bacolod Art District
description: A city block with art galleries, restaurants, and cafés. The galleries showcase the work of local artists.

name: Christmas Village
description: This private display is the result of many years of collecting figurines and related items. Its miniature Christmas village features intricate hand-painted details, including cliffs, lakes, and mountains, all made by the owner. Photography is not allowed, but souvenir photos and postcards are available.
address: San Juan St and San Sebastian St

name: Negros Forests and Ecological Foundation Inc.
description: A movement of concerned citizens to conserve the forests of Negros Island as well as animals that are under threat of extinction. Visit the foundation and see their rare warty pigs, leopard cats, spotted dear, bleeding heart pigeon and many more animals, most of which are endangered. Help the foundation by adopting an animal or tree, or by becoming an NFEFI volunteer.

name: Mt. Kanla-on Natural Park
description: A possible day trip, this is a nature park surrounding the Kanlaon Volcano. Many waterfalls and a spectacular area for birdwatching, featuring species such as the bleeding-heart pigeon and the endangered Negros fruit dove.

name: Bacolaodiat Festival
description: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) celebrated by the Filipino-Chinese community in Bacolod. This is held in the Provincial Lagoon. Bacolaodiat is derived from the words "Bacolod" and "Laodiat"; a Hokkien word meaning "Celebration".Rows of stalls serving Chinese cuisine form "chopsticks alley". Live bands play, there are displays of Chinese culture, and a cookfest is also held.

name: Holy Week
description: This religious event is held either in March or April is considered as one of the most important events in Christianity. Witness Cenaculo/Senakulo reenactments of the Passion of Christ, Du-aw — a Hiligaynon tradition of veneration of Christ's Crucifix and his Dead Body and Visita Iglesia — a Catholic tradition of visiting 7 churches and praying at each church.

name: Panaad sa Negros
description: Held annually in either March or April in Bacolod, is considered as the "mother of festivals" in the province of Negros Occidental. It represents the festive nature of the Negrense, commences with a mass, which is then followed by banners and displays of every town and city in Negros Occidental, and showcases of provincial products, from food to handicrafts. Firework displays at night also are held during the festival.

name: MassKara Festival
description: A big annual Mardi Gras-like parade event celebrated every 3rd week of October. Each of the city's barangays (districts) joins the fierce competition for the best-costumed groups, best in choreography, and many others. Lots of food and handicraft stalls, street dancing and an Oktoberfest-like event at the Bacolod Plaza area making the city for a span of a week, a city that never sleeps! "Masskara" means "Mask" in Hiligaynon and Tagalog. The use of colorful masks with large smiles represent the nickname for the city, "City of Smiles", the masks are usually the icons for the festival and sometimes of Bacolod itself.

name: Negros Occidental Golf and Country Club
description: This golf club has 18-holes, with a panoramic view of the Mount Mapara and Patag.
price: 18 holes: ₱2200 weekdays; ₱3000 holidays/weekends. 9 holes: ₱1650 weekdays; ₱2300 holidays/weekends. Caddie and umbrella girl extra

name: Yuang Thong Temple
description: A Mahayana Buddhist temple. If you haven't seen Tai chi before, this is your chance.
hours: Tai chi sessions on Sundays from 07:00 to 08:30

name: Caribbean Water Park
description: This water park features Negros Occidental’s first and largest water slide. It has a main pool, a kiddie pool, a jacuzzi, two large slides, and a pirate-ship replica for children to explore. Function rooms, locker rooms, huts, and air-conditioned rooms are also available for rent.

name: Buro-Buro and Bocal-Bocal springs
description: Located just outside of Bacolod, the Buro-Buro and Bocal-Bocal springs are popular for their cool spring water despite the name Bocal-Bocal, which suggests boiling. The site has both an artificial swimming pool and a natural pool, as well as small waterfalls near the main pool where visitors can sit under the falling water. Huts are available for rent, and the area is popular for family outings, barbecues, and reunions.

name: Casino Filipino
description: Operated by Pagcor.

name: Central Market
description: A good option for affordable souvenirs such as local handmade products, sweet delicacies and uga (dried fish). Be sure to bargain.

name: Libertad Market
description: Great place to buy fresh fruit and produce, particularly at its eastern corner.

name: Ayala Malls Capitol Central
description: Another popular mall, right behind the Provincial Capitol, it features multiple restaurants, a supermarket, and a small park right in front of the entrance.

name: 888 Chinatown Mall
description: Sells dirt-cheap goods, such as imitation name-brand clothing.

name: Mayfair Plaza
description: Cheap secondhand clothes, toys, home decor, etc.

name: Robinsons Place Bacolod
description: The second-largest mall in the city.

name: SM City Bacolod
description: The largest mall in the city. Just like any other SM Supermall in the Philippines, it has its large department store, grocery store, famous brand stores, restaurants, and a cinema. It is also one of the few SM malls of the country that has its own convention center.

name: ANP Hub
description: Sells high-quality local handicrafts, albeit at higher prices.
address: S Capitol Rd and Gatuslao St

name: Jojo Vito Designs Gallery
description: Locally made maskara, lighting, wall art, furniture, refrigerator magnets, etc. You can even paint your own maskara!

name: Bong Bong's Pasalubong
description: More popular than Merci Pasalubong, however they have fewer products. Their specialty is their piaya and barquillos. They have many locations in Bacolod.

name: Merci Pasalubong
description: Merci's specializes in piaya, biscocho, and napoleones. They have a number of locations around Bacolod.

name: 888 China Mall food court
description: Low-cost food court with some Vietnamese food.

name: Terraplaza food court
description: Air conditioned food court.
directions: across the street from the plaza

name: Marby Plaza
description: Low-cost food court.

name: Manokan Country
description: A row of stalls and restaurants serving cheap local fare, and the home of the original chicken inasal recipe.

name: Ting-Ting's Native Restaurant
description: Bacolodnon cuisine. The place is open air and fresh air fills the open air area which is suitable for brunches and lunches.

name: Malaspina Inaslan
directions: near Bacolod-Mindanao Lumberyard, at the back of Bacolod Public Cemetery

name: Pala-Pala Market
description: Buy fresh seafood in the wet market then go to a restaurant nearby and have it cooked. From oysters to crabs to blue marlins.

name: Sian Tian Health Food Center
description: Beloved vegan/vegetarian Chinese restaurant.

name: Sanders Coffee & Sausages
description: Multiple locations.

name: D'Baker's Cakes & Pastries
description: Chain that sells bread, cakes and pies. Multiple locations.

name: Apollo Restaurant
description: The oldest Chinese restaurant in town.

name: Bascon Cafe
description: Serves pastries and cakes.
directions: near Univ. of St. La Salle

name: Calea
description: Residents of Iloilo take the trip to Bacolod just to taste their irresistible cakes.

name: Cafe Bobs
description: Must-tries include their gelato, mini-cakes, and coffee-shakes.
directions: not to be confused with just Bob's

name: Inaka
description: Japanese buffet with a wide variety of choices.

name: L'Kaisei Express
description: L'Kaisei has a smaller branch in SM City Bacolod Mall which is much more accessible and affordable. Serves typical Japanese cuisine, sushi, and bento boxes.

name: Kuppa
description: Their Spanish chocolate and milk is delicious. The gelato is worth trying too.
directions: across from St. John's Institute High School

name: Mu Shu
description: Restaurant and bar that serves Asian fusion cuisine. Try their pritchon or pritong lechon. Has a good sampling of Southeast Asian dishes such as pad Thai, Hainanese chicken, and nasi goreng.

name: Quan
description: Quan's is a one stop shop for local delicacies, from napoleones to kutsinta. They also serve meals such as ciabatta pizzas and lasagna.

name: Bob's
description: One of the oldest restaurants in Bacolod, the restaurant serves authentic Filipino cuisine within a beautiful interior.
directions: not to be confused with Cafe Bobs

name: Veego
description: Tiny restaurant with phenomenal vegan food.

name: Nato's Cafe and Garden
description: Good food and coffee with a pleasant outdoor seating area.

name: Italia Restaurant
description: Serves pizza straight from the brick oven, as well as a range of pasta dishes and steaks. Also offers a good variety of fine wines. Italia is a regular venue of several art exhibits of both local and national artists.

name: 21 Restaurant
description: Serves authentic Filipino cuisine including great seafood which is harvested from a specially-built aquarium.

name: Cafe Uma
description: Pricey, but the portions are large and delicious. Serves international cuisine.

name: L'Kaisei
description: Japanese restaurant with reasonable prices and a relaxed atmosphere.

name: Bar 21
description: 21 Restaurant has a bar which turns into a club at night.

name: Gypsy Tea Room
description: Beer, cocktails, and appetizers are served here. Shisha is also available, along with henna, tattooing, and palm reading, giving the place a Middle Eastern feel.

name: Mu Shu
description: By day an Asian restaurant, by night a nightclub, as chairs and tables are moved aside to create a dance floor; dancing often continues until sunrise.

name: Zagu
description: One of the most popular juice bars in the city.

name: Sweet City Captel Hostel
description: Dormitories. Has to be the cheapest place to stay in Bacolod.
address: North Capital Rd and Gatusiao St

name: Ong Bun Pension House
description: Fan single shared Cr. a/c double with own bathroom and cable TV. Free wifi in some rooms. Free drinking water and can do laundry.
directions: down town next to Central Market

name: Bacolod Pension Plaza
description: a/c single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable tv, 66 rooms.

name: Rosita Hometel
description: Fan doubles with common bathroom.

name: Tindalo Pension house
description: Fan and A/C rooms.

name: Co-z Pension House Bacolod
description: Standard A/C double room with hot water bathroom. Cable TV. Free wifi.

name: Nirvana Pension House
description: Fan single/double room with own bathroom and cable TV. Wifi, A/C.

name: O Hotel
description: 55 Air conditioned rooms with cold and hot showers, a deposit safety box, telephone and refrigerator, laundry service, cable TV, coffee shop and bar, aside from their own facilities, a Banco De Oro ATM is available.
address: San Sebastian St and Locsin St

name: Kasa Boutique Hotel Bacolod
description: Excellent value, well-equipped air conditioned rooms. Conveniently located near the Ceres southbound bus terminal.

name: L'Fisher Hotel
description: Perhaps the most well-known hotel in Bacolod. Executive suites have king sized beds, walk in closets, dining areas, receiving area, etc., while cheaper rooms have ordinary facilities such as a cable TV, refrigerator, and dresser.

name: Planta Hotel & Residences
description: Swimming pool, gym; rooms have an electronic safe, cable TV, minibar, WiFi connection and hair dryer.

name: Park Inn by Radisson Bacolod
address: SM City Bacolod Complex Reclamation Area, Block 12 Palanca

name: San Guillermo Parish Church
description: Bacolor's main Roman Catholic church, which also doubles as a memorial to the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption. The original church building dates back to 1587 but was destroyed by an earthquake, and the present church is from 1897. During a lahar flow from Mount Pinatubo exacerbated by a typhoon in 1995, the church, along with its cemetery became half-buried in lahar, which has since hardened.The church remains a place of worship, following an effort to hollow out the structure's ceiling to provide space and the conversion of the choir loft into the main entrance. It also hosts an ecclesiastical and local history museum housing religious artefacts and paintings by local artists of the 1991 eruption, along with photographs showing what the church looked like before it was half-sunk. At the museum's exit is a stall selling church-related souvenirs.
address: Don Ceferino Joven Street, Barangay Cabambangan

name: Sunken Shrine of Our Lady of Lourdes of Cabetican
description: A Catholic shrine built in the Brutalist style. It was also buried to its roof by lahar flows from Mount Pinatubo in 1995, but was partially excavated in 2005. The structure lost 6 m of its height to the volcanic mud, and its interior, which was partially cleared out, exudes a cave-like atmosphere, with the jungle-like altarpiece also carved from lahar.

name: De Jesus Ancestral House
description: An 18th century residence that somehow managed to survive the Pinatubo eruption intact and unburied by lahar.

name: Bacolor Public Market
address: Don Ceferino Joven Street, Barangay Cabambangan

name: Puregold Bacolor
address: at the junction with Don Ceferino Joven Street

name: Kapampangan Asan Pakamalan
description: A restaurant serving Kapampangan dishes.

name: Nuan Café
address: Nuan Farm and Resort, San Vicente

name: Artisanos Cafe
address: A.M. Gratia Bldg, Don Bosco Hway, Brgy. Cabalantian

name: Blanc & Blue Cafe
address: Blanc & Blue in front of DHVSU

name: Coftea Cafe
address: 2nd Floor, Chu Building, Don Ceferino Joven St., Cabambangan

name: Happy Kopi
directions: Near DHVSU Bacolor Main Campus, beside Bacolor Water District

name: Zapote Bridge
description: A historic arch bridge at the boundary with Las Piñas, where two battles during the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American War, the 1897 Battle of Zapote Bridge and the 1899 Battle of Zapote River, occurred. The 1897 battle was a Filipino victory, while the 1899 battle was an American victory (as they used gun boats to devastate the Filipino positions). At the middle of the bridge, since bypassed by a modern six-lane one, is a National Historical Marker commemorating the two battles.

name: Bacoor Church
description: The Spanish-era church was first built in the 18th century, but had to be rebuilt several times due to wars and earthquakes. One of the Gomburza, Mariano Gomez, became one of its parish priests until he was arrested in 1872 for alleged involvement in the Cavite Mutiny and was executed at the garrote in Bagumbayan, Manila. There is a historic marker dedicated to Gomez in front of the convent, along with a plaza beside the church.

name: Cuenca Ancestral House
description: One of the few remaining bahay na bato residences from the Spanish era, the privately-owned house became the first headquarters of the Philippine revolutionary government following the declaration of independence in June 1898 until September that same year, when it was transferred to Malolos, Bulacan. It became the temporary seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Bacoor in the early 1900s when Bacoor Church was taken over by the Aglipayans.

name: Minor Basilica and Parish of Saint John the Baptist
description: Badoc's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period in the 17th century in the Baroque style and housing the venerated Marian image of the Virgen Milagrosa.

name: NHCP Museo nina Juan at Antonio Luna
description: A museum dedicated to the lives of Juan and Antonio Luna, brothers who originated in the town (Juan was born in Badoc while Antonio was born in Manila where his family moved to) and dedicated their lives to upholding Filipino nationalism against Spanish and American prejudices. Juan excelled in realist and romanticist painting, while Antonio made his name commanding Filipino forces during the Philippine-American War, only to be assassinated in factional fighting with forces loyal to President Emilio Aguinaldo in Cabanatuan.
address: Juan Luna corner Rizal Streets, Garreta

name: La Virgen Milagrosa Chapel
description: A chapel built by the cove where the Virgen Milagrosa was said to have washed up in 1620 from Japan, where it had been hidden away by Christians being persecuted by the Tokugawa Shogunate. The cove was subsequently named in the Virgin's honor. At the same time, a twin image of the crucified Christ, known as the Santo Cristo Milagroso, washed up in the neighboring village of Dadalaquiten, part of Sinait, and is also venerated in that town’s basilica.
address: Ian Pan Road, Sitio Paguetpet, La Milagrosa

name: Badoc Island
description: A 36 ha island with pristine white beaches and rock formations.
directions: take a boat at La Virgen Milagrosa Cove or at Pagsanahan. The journey will take roughly 25 minutes.

name: Ilocos Norte Welcome Arch
description: A massive archway marking the boundary between Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur provinces. Behind the Badoc side of the arch is a small visitor center with rest area.

name: Saint Jerome Parish Church
description: Bagabag's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era but largely destroyed by an earthquake in 1949 and replaced by a drab building. A surviving relic is the partially destroyed Spanish-era belltower, which has been blighted by the construction of a water tank on top.

name: Zero Kilometer Death March Marker

These markers are distinguished with their white color and pyramidal appearance.

directions: Between Jollibee and McDonald's and directly beside the Mariveles Public Library

description: A living museum housing a growing collection of Spanish-era buildings, which are either reconstructions, replicas or houses dismantled and reassembled from across various towns in the Philippines. Bluewater Falls and Cave
description: The main tourist attraction in Baggao, it is a sprawling natural complex composed of dense forests, pristine springs, a 13-tier waterfall and rapids along the foothills of the Sierra Madre. Its highlights are the Blue Lagoon, whose turquoise waters are accessible following a lengthy hike, and the Bluewater Cave, a water-filled chamber with an estimated length of 6 km.

name: Victory Liner
description: Victory Liner has hourly bus service to Baguio from its Monumento main terminal in Caloocan City, Cubao and Pasay terminals. Buses are generally modern and air-conditioned, but seats are sized generally for Filipinos and tall people would need to take advantage of the various stopovers to stretch their legs. Fare is ₱616 per person one way (most expensive among Aircon buses going to Baguio). A non-stop deluxe bus service is also available for ₱999 per person one way, water and snack are served during the trip. Some buses have free WiFi.

name: Dagupan Bus
description: Also serves the Manila to Baguio route via its Cubao Terminal. Buses leave on an hourly basis.
address: New York St., Cubao, Quezon City

name: Genesis
description: Buses depart every hour from Cubao, Pasay, and Avenida bus stations. Since July 15, 2019, they operate a premium bus service (via the expressways) from Parañaque with stops at all terminals of Ninoy Aquino International Airport, between 5AM and 9PM.

name: Burnham Park
description: Go for a walk or go rowing on Burnham Lake. Visit the Rose Garden or have fun with the kids in the Burnham Park Playground.

name: Camp John Hay
description: This former R&R facility for American military personnel during the American occupation was turned over to the Philippine Government in 1991. Now under the auspices of the Bases Conversion & Development Authority (BCDA), Camp John Hay is a sort of country club complete with an 18-hole golf course, horseback riding and camping, among other activities. A condotel is in operation. Renovations in the resort have added different activities such as a paintball arena and zip-lining. This place can get very crowded on weekends.

name: Mines View Park
description: Enjoy the view of the beautiful mountain scenery with other various attractions... And that's just it. This place is more of a tourist trap. The scenic view is honestly mediocre - with lots of houses dotting the hills; not too breathtaking. There are lots of vendors selling plants and souvenirs. Probably the best place to buy garden plants in Baguio, but there is no need to hastily buy souvenirs and trinkets here, they are just as available elsewhere in the city. The park itself kinda looks makeshift, with garden plant stalls hugging the winding stairs.The "various attractions" are more like animals really. There is a horse with tacky pink dyed hair, and a big St. Bernard dog with red eyes (why?). Keep in mind that these animals are probably already part of the local tourist landscape for being here so long. Take note that having the "guides" take a picture of you with the animals will cost you ₱50-100. There is also a wishing well. You can also have your picture taken while dressed up in Igorot costumes, but this is best avoided, for not only do the costumes look tacky, but it smacks of cultural appropriation.

name: Session Road
description: The main thoroughfare of Baguio, where most of the city activity is centered. SM Mall and Burnham Park are walking distance. Take a look at the cool robot sculptures and the mascots that sometimes pass by.

name: Lion's Head
description: Limestone sculpture of a lion by the Baguio chapter of the Lions Club. It is carved by Ifugao artist Anselmo Bayang Day-ag and is considered as the Baguio's "entrance marker" for tourists coming from south of the city.

name: Igorot Stone Kingdom
description: A contemporary stone attraction made through the traditional method of riprap and reinforced with concrete. Made from the concept of an Igorot child's fantasy of castles, the Igorot Stone Kingdom is meant to showcase Igorot culture and folklore.

name: Pine Trees of the World Park
Laperal White House

name: Mojon Church
description: Just inside the southern boundary of Bais with Tanjay, this church is often overlooked because drivers' attentions are concentrated on the blind curve in the road. The inside, with its gracefully curving screens and woodwork and finely carved mahogany altar pieces, is prettier than the outside. Next door are some fine, large colonial houses sheltering beneath a canopy of mature trees with epiphytes growing on them.

Users of Australian debit cards might want to try the "Savings" option if "Current" does not work. Maximum withdrawal in any one transaction is ₱20000.

name: Casa Don Julian

This is a well-kept secret since there is no sign outside and most locals will know it as "Aunty Teves' place".

En suite rooms have nice shower rooms (unusual for accommodation of this price range in the Philippines) and small cable TVs (usual for accommodation of this price range in the Philippines)
price: ₱450 fan room, ₱650 air-con room, ₱750 en suite air-con room

name: La Planta Hotel
description: Purpose built, two-story hotel in an attractive Spanish colonial style with a dark green and white colour scheme throughout. Seventeen medium size double rooms with individual air-con and hot showers, cable TV. Well kept, chlorinated outside swimming pool accessible by non residents for a daily charge of ₱50 per child. A surprisingly stylish and atmospheric restaurant in the former power plant generating house has a very high ceiling and gallery with a mediocre and badly cooked menu; powerful fans but no air-con. Secure parking with night watchman is separated from the rooms by a garden.
price: Twin air-con rooms cost ₱1450 (or ₱1650 with hot shower & a morning egg!)

name: Balanga Cathedral
alt_name: Diocesan Shrine and Cathedral of St. Joseph
description: The headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church in Bataan and seat of the Diocese of Balanga. Built in 1793, this church was used as an artillery embattlement by the Filipinos during the Battle of Bataan. The cathedral was declared a National Historical Site in 1940.

name: Balanga City Hall

name: Immuki Island
description: Not really an island but a series of three lagoons, mangroves, tidal pools and flats with clear waters and teeming with marine life. The entire site is walkable during low tide.
directions: at the back of Paraoir Barangay Hall

name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentino Parish Church
description: Balaoan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1864.
address: Manila North Road, Dr. Camilo Osias

name: Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto
