description: A Roman Catholic hillside shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

name: Balayan Baywalk
description: Once a littered waterfront, it has been cleaned in 2019, and provides views of Balayan Bay that are similar to those in Manila's Baywalk.

name: Immaculate Conception Church
description: Baroque church built with coral stones, and completed in 1752. Parts of the original structure have been demolished due to earthquake damage. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

name: Casa Cacao
description: A private Spanish era bahay na bato belong to one of Balayan’s old rich families, which includes actor and comedian Leo Martinez, who introduced many common Batangas tropes in popular culture. The house is named in honor of the family’s fortunes in the cacao industry. The house is .

name: Balayan Presidencia
description: One of the few remaining municipal government buildings in the Philippines remaining from the Spanish era.

name: Casa Grande
description: The oldest surviving house in Balayan, dating from the 1850s. The residence's namesake was a friend of national hero Jose Rizal and, along with his sister, vigorously lobbied for Philippine independence against the United States.

name: Parada ng Lechon
description: Mostly a celebration for a plentiful harvest, it also doubles as the feast day of St. John the Baptist. The day starts with water battles on the streets, like those also done at Watah-watah in San Juan in Metro Manila. In the morning, prepare to get wet with pails of water and water cannons from fire engines, and have a Super Soaker ready. After the water battles, lechon (roast pig) dressed in different ways are paraded through the streets. The festivities end with sumptuous feasts at every home.

name: WalterMart Balayan
address: Balibago Road corner Paz Street, Caloocan

name: Espineli's
description: Hotel with air-conditioned rooms. Has free WiFi, parking. Free breakfast served at rooms.

name: Baler Central Terminal
description: Baler's central bus station, also used by UV Express. Most bus companies base their operations here.

name: D'Liner
description: Ordinary buses run the Cabanatuan-Casiguran route, with a layover at Baler.

name: Genesis Transport
description: A/C and luxury services depart from Bocaue, stopping at Angeles, Tarlac City and Cabanatuan. Trip takes 6 hours (including stopovers).

name: Dr. Juan C. Angara Airport
description: Air Juan flies from Manila using amphibious planes.

name: Museo de Baler
description: Cultural hub showcasing artifacts, paintings, memorabilia & ethnic exhibits of the region.

name: Doña Aurora Aragon-Quezon House
description: Modest, historic house museum owned by the family of Aurora Quezon, First Lady from 1935–1944.

name: Ermita Hill
description: Tromba Marina was the name given to the destructive tidal wave that struck Baler on December 27, 1735. This monstrous wave caught everyone off-guard when it arrived around 2:00 AM. The town was devastated in seconds and many lives were immediately lost. Seven families managed to survive the great blow of the tidal wave and found their safe haven in Ermita Hill. The ones who made it through were the Angara, Bijasa, Bitong, Carrasco, Ferreras, Lumasac and Poblete clans.

name: Cemento Beach
description: Known for its chill atmosphere, this secluded, rocky beach is a popular destination for surfers.

name: Diguisit Beach
description: Popular for picture-taking, this picturesque coral beach features pebbly sand & unique boulders.

name: Baler Lighthouse
description: Stunning view of Baler and Baler Bay.

name: Hanging Bridge
description: beautiful view of river, mountains and Baler Bay.

name: Ditumabo Mother Falls
description: Popular waterfall with a cold-water pool at its base, reachable by a lush 45-minute nature trek.

name: Tromba Marina Sculpture
description: Tromba Marina was the name given to the destructive tidal wave that struck Baler on December 27, 1735. This monstrous wave caught everyone off-guard when it arrived around 2:00 AM. The town was devastated in seconds and many lives were immediately lost. Seven families managed to survive the great blow of the tidal wave and found their safe haven in Ermita Hill. The ones who made it through were the Angara, Bijasa, Bitong, Carrasco, Ferreras, Lumasac and Poblete clans.

name: Diteki Bridge
description: Beautiful river underneath the bridge.
address: Nueva Ecija - Aurora Rd, San Luis

name: Balete Tree (Millenium Tree)
description: A balete tree locally called "Millennium Tree" in Barangay Quirino, Maria Aurora is claimed to be the largest of its kind in Asia. It is estimated to be about more than 600 years old and 60 metres (200 ft) tall with its roots about 10 metres (33 ft) to 15 metres (49 ft) in diameter.

name: Buencamino View Point
description: This place is really beautiful and majestic scenery of Aurora Memorial National Park.
address: Nueva Ecija - Aurora Road, San Luis

name: Aurora Province Welcoming Arch
description: This place is the gateway to Aurora, If you are looking for a nice fun of sight seeing this place is highly recommended. The place is suited for exploring the mountains and road cycling, Now the most visited area in Bongabon .

name: Doña Aurora Old Rest House
description: Historical landmark, beautiful view.

name: National Museum of the Philippines - Baler
description: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, with exhibits on Aurora's natural history and culture.

name: Sabang Beach
description: Relaxed beach featuring strong waves suitable for surfing, with a peaceful vibe.

name: Cemento Beach
description: Known for its chill atmosphere, this secluded, rocky beach is a popular destination for surfers.

name: Lipit Beach
description: It's a nice sandy beach. Big waves are good for surfing. It's facing the Pacific Ocean.

name: Baler Moto Park
description: Motocross Park.

name: Barangay Zabali Peak
description: Hiking area.

name: Pacita's Pasalubong
description: Souvenir store.

name: NE Baler
description: Supermarket.

name: Eat All You Can Buffet
description: An all-you-can-eat with drinks.
directions: inside the Ne mall in Baler

name: Gerry Shan's Place
description: Chinese & seafood restaurant.

name: Miggo’s
description: Western restaurant.

name: Kainan ni ALEXA
description: Filipino restaurant.

name: Kusina Luntian
description: Filipino restaurant in Nipa Hut (traditional Filipino house).

name: Bay's Inn
description: It has a restaurant by the beach, good value Filipino-western style meals.

name: Bahia de Baler Garden Resort & Restaurant 1
description: More expensive than its neighbor, Day's Inn, but a bit more classy too.

name: Akyang’s Restaurant, Goto and Ihaw-Ihaw
description: Filipino restaurant.

name: Casitas Stay and Surf
description: Air conditioned.

name: Penny Lane Transient House
description: Fan double rooms with outside bathrooms and TV.

name: Pasillio Surf And Lodge
description: 600 metres from Sabang Beach. The hotel features an indoor pool and a 24-hour front desk.

name: La Flor Lodge
description: A/C double rooms. Has a swimming pool.

name: Costa Pacifica
description: The only 5-star hotel and resort in Baler.

name: RedDoorz @ Isla Virginia Beach Resort Aurora Baler
Baliwag Transit
description: This bus company, with buses on a green and white livery and is headquartered in this town, has frequent trips from their terminals in Manila and Cubao (Quezon City). The company has two terminals, one at Sampaloc junction (northeast of downtown), and another at the downtown. Both terminals are shared with a sister bus company, Golden Bee, which has gold colors and the aforementioned bee on its livery. Baliwag-bound buses pass through the Old Cagayan Valley Road from Pulilan and the populated areas of Baliwag, and make a penultimate stop at Plaza Naning, the main center of downtown Baliwag.

name: Baliwag Clock Tower
description: The first and only free-standing clock tower in Bulacan, also a local symbol and landmark. It is constructed in 1999 and inaugurated in 2000, during the 137th birthday anniversary of hero, Mariano Ponce.
address: Dr. Gonzales Street, and Senator Ninoy Aquino Avenue

name: Baliwag Museum and Library
description: It was the first town hall (munisipyo or municipio) which was built during the American occupation in 1899. It used to house the municipal government until 1971, when a new town hall was inaugurated. Today, it houses a museum dedicated to the town's history. As of 2026, the museum is closed for renovations.

name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint Augustine
description: Baliwag's main Roman Catholic church, built in the 19th century during the Spanish era.

name: NHCP Museo ni Mariano Ponce
description: A museum dedicated to national hero Mariano Ponce, one of a series of writers who advocated for autonomy and later independence from Spain in the late 19th century. The museum was built on the site of Ponce’s residence, which burned down in 1962.

name: Sub-Parish Church of Santo Cristo
description: A Spanish-era chapel built in 1881.

name: Holy Week processions
description: On Holy Week, particularly Holy Wednesday and Good Friday, Baliwag hosts the longest Lenten procession in the Philippines, featuring up to 120 statues showing the passion of the Christ and related images being transported on floats from the San Isidro Labrador parish church in neighboring Pulilan to San Agustin parish in Baliwag. Many of the images are family heirlooms that are only displayed in public for that occasion.

name: SM City Baliwag
description: Has numerous restaurants, a SM Store (department store), and a SM Hypermarket.

name: S&R Membership Shopping - Baliwag
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.

name: Robinsons Easymart Gil Carlos
address: Gil Carlos corner P. Angeles Streets, San Jose

name: Puregold Baliwag
address: Benigno S. Aquino Avenue, Santo Cristo

name: Bulacan's Prime
description: A store selling Bulacan longganisa.

name: Hotel Sogo
description: A love motel.

name: Bamban World War II Museum
description: Bamban saw heavy fighting during World War II for control of the approaches to Clark Field. This small museum run by a former tour guide and head of the Bamban Historical Society keeps artefacts from that period such as photographs, letters, weapons, costumes and other equipment.

name: Santo Niño Parish Church
description: Bamban's main Roman Catholic church, known in town for its distinctive spires.

name: Baofu Compound
description: This sprawling compound that was built as a self-sustaining business hub, complete with mid to high-rise buildings and condominiums commonly seen in Metro Manila and Angeles, has become the inadvertent poster image of Bamban after police raids in 2024 discovered the existence of criminal activities such as online extortion, fraud and unregulated gambling inside and ultimately led to the downfall of Alice Guo as mayor. While the complex has been abandoned and access is sealed off as the government ponders on what to do with it, it has become a destination for recent history buffs and urban explorers seeking to comprehend how such a vast enterprise managed to operate at all.

name: Bamban Bridge
description: Connecting Bamban with Mabalacat in Pampanga, this 174 m long bridge, built over a tributary of the Sacobia River, is commonly used as a photography and filming location for its distinctive concrete and steel arches.

name: Japanese Cave
description: A network of caves and tunnels on a hill that was used as a hideout by Japanese forces during World War II. Nearby is the town's official war memorial.

name: Grotto Of Our Lady Of Lourdes
description: A hilltop Catholic shrine inspired by the original in Lourdes, France. It is accessible after an ascent of 100 steps.

name: Goshen Hotel and Resort
description: A resort complex with replicas of Greco-Roman structures such as the Colosseum.
address: One Clark Boulevard North, Sitio Gumain, Lourdes

name: St. Catherine of Siena Parish Church
description: The main Roman Catholic church in Bambang, built during the 18th century in a Baroque style. With the exception of the ruinous post-colonial porte-cochere, its facade resembles that of Dupax Church.

name: Salinas Natural Monument
description: The remains of a natural salt spring that stopped producing salt and whose rocks turned from white to gray following the 1990 Luzon earthquake. Despite this, it has managed to maintain its natural settings and is also a wildlife refuge.

name: Banti Falls
description: A rapids-like cascade along a tributary of the Magat River.

name: Nueva Vizcaya Mural
description: An extensive mural along the highway leading to Bayombong outlining Nueva Vizcaya's history and culture.

name: Nueva Vizcaya Agricultural Terminal
description: A major wholesale retail market for vegetable producers in southern Nueva Vizcaya to sell their products to traders who usually resell the crops in Metro Manila and elsewhere.

name: Primark Center Bambang
description: Retail department store with a Savemore grocery and a McDonald's.

name: Big Eats Barbeque
description: A cafeteria-style barbecue and grill also selling frozen steaks for takeout.

name: Boo Le Vous Cafe
description: A cafe serving native-grown coffee infused with fruit flavors derived from locally-grown produce.

name: Ohayami Trans
description: Provides trips directly to Banaue. They have two daily trips leaving Manila at 9PM and 10PM with an additional trip during the holidays. Wear warm clothing, the air-con can be quite strong and the trip takes 9-10 hr.
address: corner of Lacson Ave & Fajardo St, Sampaloc, Manila
directions: near University of Sto. Tomas or take the train from the Legarda Station then just take a trickshaw to the terminal

name: Museum of Cordilleran Sculpture
description: The Museum of Cordilleran Sculpture was founded by George and Candida Ida Schenk over 30 years ago, and evolved from a small antique store in Manila, into dream to preserve a culture that is slowly dying. There are over 1,000 pieces in the collection of the museum, ranging from large-scale, carved wooden Bululs, masks to smaller scale figures, textiles, utilitarian objects, and composite objects. Temporarily closed as of September 2023.

name: Hot Spring
description: A geothermal hot spring next to a river can be reached via walking across rice terraces starting from Hungduan Elementary School. The road to the school however is not yet paved. Arrangements to visit will likely need to be made in town.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces
description: Sometimes called the "Eighth Wonder of the World", the 2000-year-old Banaue rice terraces are a designated National Cultural Treasure, and while many are still in use, the outer rims are showing signs of deterioration. They were created by the Ifugao (local native people), in a massive engineering project to cover the sides of the valleys (probably 200 m from floor to rim) for several miles, irrigated by means of mountain streams and springs that have been tapped and channelled into canals that run downhill through the rice terraces.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces Main Viewdeck
address: Nueva Vizcaya - Ifugao - Mountain Province Road

name: Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort
description: Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort is on a six hectare lot in a pine forest above downtown Banaue. It has large grassy areas, picnic shelters, swimming pools, and a large function hall. This would be an ideal place for a school or other organization to have training sessions or meetings.

name: Banaue Welcome Arch
description: Breath taking views and friendly shop keepers.
address: Nueva Vizcaya - Ifugao - Mountain Province Road, Hingyon

name: Banaue Museum
description: Natural history museum. Very small museum. Interesting things to see about Ifugao Culture, attire, handicraft, etc. Good to visit. High steps/stairs to reach the entrance to the museum, then another stairs to the lower level.

name: ATM
description: There are no ATMs in Banaue. The nearest Visa Card ATM is at the PNB Bank ATM in Lagawe, a one-hour Jeepney ride from Banaue. The nearest Master Card ATM is at Metro Bank in Solano, a 2½-hour jeepney ride from Banaue. There is also a PNB Bank Visa Card ATM in Bontoc.

name: ATM
description: Does not accept all western cards!

name: Almost ATM
alt_name: Uyami's Green View Lodge and Restaurant
description: At this restaurant, you can withdraw cash from your credit card, but 10% fee!

name: Sanafe Lodge & Restaurant
description: Indoor and al fresco dining on a wide veranda with great views. Filipino, Asian & Western dishes. Set meals start at ₱140.

name: Ilob Village Inn
description: Native Ifugao house with restaurant, surrounded with rice terraces. You can also request to see a traditional Ifugao show.

name: Kiben
description: Local eatery. Good local food provided by friendly family. Main dishes usually ₱50, sometimes ₱40. Tea and coffee ₱10.
directions: right at the top of the main road on the left side

name: Banaue Hotel & Youth Hostel
description: Set in a rural area with a mountain backdrop, this casual hotel is a kilometer from the Banaue Museum and 3 km from the Banaue Rice Terraces.
address: Banaue - Mayoyao - Aguinaldo - Lista - Ramon Road, Ilogue

name: Uyami's Green View Lodge and Restaurant
description: No power outlets in the rooms, charging for a fee at the reception. Free Wi-Fi and drinking water. Restaurant is open 6AM-9:30PM.

name: Banaue Homestay
description: Basic but comfortable rooms view views of Banaue rice terraces. Some rooms with shared bathrooms. Has small restaurant for all meals. Allows for luggage hold before bus leaves. 200 m up the road from Ohayami Bus dropoff/pickup.

name: Sanafe Lodge and Restaurant
description: Nice balcony at the back with pleasant views. Basic but comfortable rooms, plus a dormitory.

name: Halfway Lodge and Restaurant
description: Offers private rooms for 2 with shared bathroom or private bathroom.
address: Banaue - Mayoyao - Aguinaldo - Lista - Ramon Road
directions: From the tourism turn back on it and go down the street on the left. It's the third lodge of the street

name: Randy's Brookside Inn
description: 1 km from center/bus stop. Includes pickup, free breakfast.

name: 7th Heaven's
directions: 500m up the road from the main town

name: Bogah Homestay
description: Small, but well-managed homestay. Short walk (500m) from downtown via hanging bridge. Staff can organize tours to rice terraces and hot spring.

name: Spring Village Inn
address: Nueva Vizcaya - Ifugao - Mountain Province Road

name: Terraceville Inn
description: The Terraceville Inn is only about 200 meters from the bus stop.

name: Saint Christopher Parish Church
description: Bangar's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in the 19th century.
address: Manila North Road corner Boughton Street, Central East No. 1

name: Paratong Beach
description: Bangar's main seaside promenade, featuring grayish sands and extending from the Amburayan River delta down to the boundary with Luna.

address: Manila North Road, Central East No. 2
directions: facing Bangar Public Plaza and Bangar Church

name: Bangui Wind Farm
description: Constructed in 2003 and opened in 2005, this is the first wind farm in the Philippines. Even after the Burgos and Caparispisan wind farms were completed, the Bangui wind farms remain the main tourist attraction in its region.

name: Sentinela Hill
description: During the Spanish era, a redbrick watchtower was placed on top of the hill as a lighthouse and watchtower against marauding Moro pirates and foreign navies, hence the hill's name. The watchtower has been carefully preserved.
address: C. Torres Street, Barangay San Lorenzo

name: Saint Lawrence Parish Church
description: Bangui's main Roman Catholic church, built in 1877 and extensively renovated since then.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Stevrena Cottages
description: Fan double rooms or air-conditioned double rooms. Has free WiFi.
directions: on road from port going to santa fe town

name: Casa Isabel Hostel
description: a/c Six bed dorm. free wifi. free breakfast.

name: Montemar Pension House
description: fan double room own bathroom.

name: B M Island Inn
description: A/c double room with own bathroom. free wifi.

name: Beach People Hostel
description: 6/8 bed a/c dorm. free wifi. free breakfast, security Lockers. max age 60 year old.
address: F Roska street Purok Aries Brgy Talisay Santa fe

name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint Joseph
description: Home of the image of San Jose de Baras. The Church was completed by the Franciscan missionaries in 1686. It features a dark and austere interior thanks to its unplastered bricks, lined with a set of original carvings of the Stations of the Cross. Its ceiling remains uncovered, revealing a ribcage-like row of wooden beams supporting the roof.
address: San Jose Street, Barangay San Juan

name: Masungi Georeserve
description: A conservation area near the boundary with Tanay which consists of the geological formations of Masungi rock. It is characterized by rugged limestone karst peaks, steep slopes, and surrounding lush montane rainforests. It contains several caves, including the Yungíb ni Ruben (Ruben's Cave), which features stalactite and stalagmite formations.

name: Palo Alto Falls
description: This man-made falls in Palo Alto is an hour drive from the town center.
address: East Dr., Palo Alto Residential Estates

name: Kinamatayan Falls
description: Legend says two lovers who had family issues committed suicide at the falls so no one will be able to separate them, hence the falls' name, which literally means "place of death". A few minutes of hiking will take you to the cold-as-ice falls of Kinamatayan.

name: Kasarinlan Eco-park
description: A park situated where the Baras River empties into Laguna de Bay, with views of the lake itself and surrounding wetlands.

name: Mangantila Café
description: A Filipino restaurant at a secluded location beside Laguna de Bay.
hours: No reservations on weekends and holidays

name: Basco Airport
description:
There are seasonal international flights to Basco and year round domestic flights. It is also the only airport serving the neighboring island of Itbayat. Due to Batanes’ infamously volatile weather, delays and cancellations happen more than in other airports, particularly during the rainy season. A rule of thumb among aviation veterans is to check whether Mount Iraya is obscured by clouds before landing.

PAL Express flies from Manila-Basco. Sky Pasada flies from Tuguegarao-Basco.

name: Basco Lighthouse
description: Spiral stairs wind upwards to a 5th-floor deck, popular for its panoramic hill, sea & sunset views.

name: Basco Rolling Hills
description: Scenic hilly area offering views of the ocean and Mt. Iraya, with grazing cows, goats & other animals.

name: Chawa View Deck
description: A perfect place to watch the sunset. Romantic sunset viewing. Highly recommended for sunset lovers.

name: Rakuh A Payaman (Marlboro Country)
description: Scenic trails through rolling hills & lush meadows offering sweeping views of a rugged coast & sea.

name: Basco Cathedral
alt_name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, Santo Domingo de Guzman Parish Church
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Batanes, built during the Spanish era in 1812.

name: Mahatao Church
description: A 19th century Spanish colonial church that was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2001.

name: Mount Iraya
description: The highest peak in Batanes, with a height of 1009 m. It is a dormant volcano that is home to endemic species such as the Batanes pit viper. It also serves as a local weather instrument of sorts; clouds obscuring the peak mean that bad weather is expected all over Batan Island.

name: Casa Napoli Pizza
description: Best, real handmade pizza in Batanes! Handmade crust made from scratch, good mozzarella, and awesome flavor.

name: Beehan Meals & Snacks
description: This is probably the most affordable place to eat in Basco.

name: Harbour Cafe-Basco
description: They serve a mixture of Filipino and Italian food. Try out their pasta and pork Sinigang.

name: Cafe du Tukon
description: Great food and view, a must visit when you go to Batanes compete with outdoor and indoor dining.

name: HiroJoy Cafe
description: Don't be fooled by the carinderia/eatery set up of this place. This is the best restaurant in Basco!

name: Fundacion Pacita Batanes Nature Lodge
description: This Batanes resort was once the home studio of renowned artist Pacita Abad. Today, it has been transformed into a lovely building offering charming Batanes accommodation for visitors who want to get closer to nature. It offers 9 rooms, all with viewing decks where you can enjoy the breathtaking landscape of Batanes. Complimentary breakfast is served to all guest, and a half-day heritage tour of the mainland is also included.

name: Batanes Octagon Bed and Dine
description: Octagon Bed and Dine started out as a simple octagon shaped restaurant serving local Ivatan cuisine and Batanes' own take of the favorite Filipino dishes.

name: Basey Church
alt_name: St Michael The Archangel Parish Church
description: A 17th-century church

name: Sunkai Cafe & Resort
description: This beachside hangout features beautiful cottage designs, a glass-walled swimming pool, and spectacular sunset views. It has quickly become a popular spot for weekend getaways, family reunions, and vibrant events like pool parties.

name: Bataan National Park
description: A 23000 ha protected forest area covering Mount Natib, a dormant volcano with a wide caldera encompassing most of northern and central Bataan.

name: Florida Bus Terminal
directions: near the junction with Manila North Road

name: Marcos Museum and Mausoleum
description: A museum dedicated to President Marcos and his achievements, but avoids its excesses. It also used to house the president's preserved remains inside an airconditioned separate mausoleum building, although doubts persisted on whether the wax-looking cadaver on display was the real thing until he was reburied in Metro Manila in 2016, revealing the displayed corpse to be a fake. The dummy remains on display in Batac.

name: Immaculate Conception Parish
description: The city's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Romanesque style.

name: Aglipay Mausoleum
description: Gregorio Aglipay, the founder of the Iglesia Filipina Independiente, is interred here, at the back of the Aglipayan Cathedral of Saint Mary.

name: General Artemio Ricarte National Shrine & Museum
description: A small shrine with a park and museum dedicated to General Artemio Ricarte, a Filipino revolutionary who is acknowledged as the father of the Philippine Army.

name: Batac Public Market
description: The building burned down following a fire in July 2026. Vendors have been temporarily relocated to the nearby Bagsakan Center.

name: Batac Riverside Empanadaan
description: A covered food hall along the Quiaoit River hosting multiple stalls selling the signature Batac empanada.
directions: Beside Quiaoit Bridge and Immaculate Conception Parish Church

name: North Stellar Hotel And Events Place
Ifugao Rice Terraces
description: These amazing irrigated rice paddies were carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago. The village is nestled among perhaps the finest examples of them in the region. Anywhere in or above the village provides phenomenal views. Also, you may walk along them if you like.

name: Viewpoints
description: There are several viewpoints on the opposite side when coming from the Saddle. The first few are easy to reach, except for the strenuous hike up lots of concrete steps. For the brave, there is another viewpoint on the highest point; you should not be afraid of hights and sure-footed if you attempt to go there. The valley view is wonderful.

name: Tappiyah Waterfalls
description: A beautiful 70-meter falls about a 30-minute walk from the village. It's a great place to go for a swim. To go there without a guide, when arriving from the Saddle head on the opposite side of the rice terraces amphitheater (through the rice terraces or down to the village and up to the promontory). From here go down again with the only path with stairs to the other side.

name: Patpat Sitio (Sub-Village)
description: Patpat is a small sub-village of Batad. While this sitio itself does not have too many attractions, the two-hour hike going there passes through some amazing sights. You first cross a river with a hanging bridge, then hike up rice terraces which lead into a small forest with numerous little waterfalls and springs. Upon reaching the ridge of the mountain, relax in a waiting shed which gives you both a full-frontal view of the Batad Rice Terraces and the sweet potato plantations of Patpat. There is one store in the village, and the elderly owner speaks perfect American colonial-period English. She only sells snacks and canned sardines, but you can ask her to cook the sardines and some rice for you. She might even give you some boiled sweet potatoes for free! Beside her store is a male basketweaver who might have some native backpacks for sale. There is also a tiny elementary school with tiny tots who will chorus a cheerful English greeting to visitors.Do get a guide in Batad Village, because you can get lost in the uphill climb. The fee is ₱400-500.

name: Ifugao weaving
description: Beside the Foreigner's Inn at the main village there is a small hut with an elderly woman weaving traditional clothing with a backstrap loom. Her items cost ₱400-500 each.

name: Handmade Ifugao knives
description: Also in the main village of Babluy is Juan Buy-a, the village blacksmith. He usually makes items for actual use (not lousy souvenirs), and you may chance upon him finishing a lovely blade with carved handle and scabbard. With some good haggling and a bottle of gin (which you should always carry around in Batad), you may get it at a great price!

name: Sweet potato fries
description: Sweet potato is planted in the swidden farms around Batad. So, before going on any mountain hike, an energy-boosting snack of fried sweet potato fries is a must! You can also order a few pieces of boiled sweet potato to take with you. Available at any of the restaurants in Batad.

name: Cristina's
description: Offers simple but filling meals many of which are featuring locally grown rice. They also have bright but basic rooms upstairs for ₱250 per person.
directions: next to the church in the main village

name: Camping
description: You can pitch a tent at any of the covered viewpoints overlooking the rice terraces. Basically you can set up your tent anywhere for free, so if you do not want to be as isolated, you can also stay next to the church (main village) or on the grounds of the elementary school (upper village.)

name: Ramon's Home Stay/Restaurant
description: Ramon is an excellent source of help and information about the local history and culture. He will show you traditional artifacts, host bonfires at night, and prepare you freshly ground, freshly roasted organic coffee made from beans grown right in his garden.
directions: in the upper part of the village; on the right hand side when walking down towards the main village
price: ₱150 per person for a regular room; ₱250 to stay in a traditional Ifugao hut

name: Rita's
description: Clean rooms, spotless shared bathroom, ran by friendly family. It's also possible to sleep in a traditional hut.

name: Pandan Hill
description: Refreshing verdant hills, overlooking Sibuyan Sea.

name: Batangas Provincial Tourism Office
address: Capitol Site, Kumintang Ibaba, Batangas City

name: Batangas City Tourism Office
address: City Hall Complex, P. Burgos Street

name: Batangas City Grand Terminal
description: Central bus station, serving trips to and from Metro Manila and Lucena. Buses boarding RoRo ferries also stop here to drop off passengers. Jeepneys and UV Express are available from there.

name: Batangas Port Bus Terminal
description: Terminal for southbound buses from Manila, and stopover for buses taking ferries.
directions: Take the Batangas-Pier jeepney from downtown

name: Batangas Port
description: Locally known as the Pier (pronounced as pee-YUHR locally), this is the sea transport hub for the Southern Luzon region, and the alternative to Manila's congested seaport for both passenger and freight boats.
directions: Jeepney route: BP-01 Batangas-Pier. Southbound buses from Manila terminate here before deadheading to their depots or starting their return trips from the Grand Terminal.

name: Sitio Berberabe boat pier
description: Serves smaller wooden motorboats (bancas) from Sabang pier at Puerto Galera, since those boats are banned from Batangas Port since 2018 (see the Sabang article for further information).
directions: Take any of the jeepneys with destinations beyond San Isidro or Tabangao, then walk from the nearby jeepney stop

name: Acosta-Pastor House
description: Built in 1883, it is the ancestral home of Don Alejo Acosta, who served as a capitan de barrio. It remains the property of Acosta's descendants, and has been turned into a museum

name: Assemblyman Rafael Recto People's Park
description: Provincially-maintained park, with wide grassy spaces and mini-amphitheatre
directions: behind the Provincial Capitol complex and beside Lyceum Philippines University Batangas

name: Bahay Pamahalaan, Lungsod ng Batangas
description: The historic city hall which has been renovated in 2009 with a newer facade.

name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
alt_name: Basilica de la Immaculada Concepcion, Minor Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
description: The historical Roman Catholic church at the downtown, it has a Baroque façade and interior, and houses both the images of the Infant Jesus (Santo Niño) and the Immaculate Conception.

name: Batangas Provincial Capitol Building
description: A Neoclassical capitol building housing the office of the governor of Batangas. First built in 1926, it was destroyed by bombing twice, during World War II and in 1950. Around the façade is a tall flagpole, the provincial seal of Batangas, a marble terrace, and two fountains
address: Jose P. Laurel Highway, Kumintang Ibaba

name: Borbon-Rosales House
description: Dating back to 1870, it was the ancestral home of the Borbon family, as well as the Rosales family, where the former archbishop of Manila, Cardinal Godofredo Rosales, is part of

name: Laurel Park
description: A fenced circular park dedicated to the historical contributions of the Batangueños (people of Batangas). Inside the park is sculptures representing the five Batangueño virtues of nobility, bravery, industriousness, wisdom, and beauty, as well as
address: National Highway cor. Telecom Road, Kumintang Ibaba

name: Monte Maria Batangas
description: Constructed in 2013, this Catholic pilgrimage site includes the Santo Niño Chapel (a replica of the Church of Our Lady Victorious in Prague) and the statue of the Virgin Mary, the Mary, Mother of All Asia, which will become the largest in Asia. The location in the coast also provides views of Puerto Galera and Verde Island.

name: Museo Puntong Batangan
description: Opened in 2006, it presents the city's cultural heritage and history, as well as the history and culture of Batangueños.

name: Plaza Mabini
description: A 2 ha Spanish-era downtown plaza in Poblacion, named in honor to revolutionary Apolinario Mabini. The present plaza dates to 1915, and was redesigned in 2004 by the firm of renowned Filipino architect and urban planner Jun Palafox. It has a monument to Apolinario Mabini, pedestrian space with sunrays design, dancing fountains, playground, a covered amphitheater, flower stalls, souvenir shops, and tourism office.

name: Verde Island
description: An island which gives its name to the eponymous strait separating Batangas and Mindoro. In contrast to the mainland, this is a mostly unspoiled ecotourism destination and base to explore the marine biodiversity of the waterway.

name: Batangas City Sports Complex
description: Has a 20- by 50-meter 8-lane swimming pool, running track and basketball courts.
directions: Beside Batangas State University. Accessible by jeepney from Bago.

name: Batangas Coliseum
description: Multi-purpose arena, sometimes hosts professional league games held in Batangas, as well as local sports events and concerts.
directions: Beside Batangas State University. Accessible by jeepney from Bago.

name: Bay City Mall
description: Owned by a local retail company, it is a local favorite. It houses a Citimart department store and supermarket, a National Book Store, numerous ukay-ukay outlets, Jollibee and Chowking, and other local businesses.

name: Citimart
description: Owned also by the retailer owning Bay Mall, this is a large department store building with a supermarket below. The department store remains closed, but it hosts a Greenwich and a Chowking restaurant.

name: Nuciti Central
description: A more upscale shopping mall, owned by the same retailer running Bay Mall, with mid-range restaurants and several food kiosks, with a Citimart Supermarket (opened 2023) that replaced the Robinsons Supermarket. Has a PNB ATM.

name: Unitop
description: A local favorite, with its own supermarket, in the basement. It sells household items, clothes, and groceries.

name: SM City Batangas
description: Opened in 2005, it hosts a large department store, hundreds of shops, and movie theaters. It underwent expansion that added more restaurants, and a Kidzoona children's play area. Also has a SM Supermarket. The rear parking lots hosts terminals for jeepneys headed south to as far as Ilijan.

name: Xentro Mall Batangas
description: Opened May 2018. Single-story mall with some shops and restaurants. The Savemore supermarket that used to be here has been closed since 2024.

name: Batangas City Public Market
description: An important marketplace for the city for years since the 1900s, it hosts small services, clothing stalls, and local meat, fish and produce. It also has some small restaurants specializing in the regional cuisine and a McDonald's ice cream stall. Parking is also available at a fee of ₱10.
directions: reachable by jeepney from almost all routes on Poblacion

name: Julian Pastor Memorial Market
description: A newer public market built to the south, with separate buildings for the wet and dry sections.
directions: served by numerous jeepney routes through Poblacion, except for the Batangas-Capitolio-Hospital route

name: Bafoo's
description: Specializes in the Batangueño favorite, lomi, but also serves other regional dishes. It now has branches in Pallocan West (near Calumpang Bridge) and Kumintang Ibaba (near University of Batangas).
directions: near the traffic light with DJPMM Access Road 2

name: Batangas City Restaurant formerly known as Canton Restaurant
description: Best noted for their affordable pancit and chop chicken. Location is also not too far from downtown shopping areas.

name: Johanna's Grill
description: Retro-themed restaurant specializing in baby-back ribs.

name: Eat n' Be Well Vegetarian Haven
description: Cooperative-owned restaurant serving vegetarian dishes.
directions: near the corner with P. Canlapan

name: Ho Tsai
description: One of the first Filipino-Chinese restaurants in the city. Serves Filipino-Chinese fast food like pansit, lomi and mami, as well as common Filipino favourites, like Filipino-style spaghetti, fried rice and pulutan dishes.
directions: at the corner with P. Dandan

name: Hungry Hippo
description: Small hamburger restaurant with stall below and tables above. Another branch exists in SM Batangas.
directions: on commercial building outside University of Batangas

name: Mirellis Diner
description: Little sit-in restaurant serving Filipino and Western meals, including burgers, sandwiches, pancit, silog, and others.
directions: beside Golden Gate Colleges Integrated School

name: Nung Ru Thai
description: Owned by a Filipino who lived in Thailand, this is only one of a few restaurants that serve Thai and Indian cuisine in Batangas.

name: Mr. Kimchi
description: Korean dining, complete with hot pot, barbecue, and soju, within the downtown at a reasonable price.

name: Taza Mia!
description: Part of local coffeeshop chain, serving coffee and pastries.

name: Big Mike's Grill House
description: Serves sizzling favorites like sisig, bangus and gambas. You can also try their house style baby back ribs, fried rice, and burger.

name: F. Baylosis Crispy Pata
description: Houses the city's favorite crispy pata and chicken, for locals and tourists alike. There is also a wide variety of Filipino dishes and sides, starting at ₱190. The restaurant has an ambient atmosphere and friendly staff, and prices of meals are reasonable. You can eat with the sounds and voice of an acoustic guitar player. Private karaoke rooms are available for rent for those who want a feast with eating, drinking and singing. There is also a function hall, "Hall of Fame" for large events and meetings.

name: Wanam sa Bukid
description: Serves various Filipino favorites, such as chop suey, miki noodles, fried chicken, fried lumpia (spring rolls), and crispy pata.
address: Doña Romana Building, National Highway, Gulod Labac
directions: near Gulod Labac Barangay Hall, just past Santisima Trinidad Parish

name: Jocas Lomi Haus
description: Open-air eatery specializing in lomi, Batangas's major contribution to the Filipino cuisine.

name: Appleville Resto-bistro
description: Serves a variety of Filipino dishes, but its specialty is its beef caldereta and tadyang. Previously known as A&M restaurant before its refurnishing (August 2024).

name: Al Goto King
description: Small and often crowded restaurant, specializing in bulalo and goto. The restaurant has parking spaces beside.
directions: near the bus stop in front of Talipapa

name: Forkie's
description: Restaurant serving a fusion of Filipino breakfast and American fast food. Previously known as Brand X Burgers.
directions: in front of the Epic Center

name: Cafe de Alps
description: Bus-themed restaurant and cafe, serving Western and Filipino dishes. Ciudad Food Park and along with it, Cafe de Alps has long been closed as of December 2024.
address: Ciudad Food Avenue, Diversion Road, Alangilan

name: Hinomaru
description: Permanently Closed as of December 2024.
directions: away from Batangas Grand Terminal, near Honda Cars Batangas

name: Jhorjanes
description: Specializes in the lomi and bulalo recipes, but they also serve local seafood, chicken, and vegetable dishes.
directions: beside 7-Eleven near Balagtas Rotonda; annex beside car repair shop

name: Jovita Cafe
description: Casual restaurant not far from 3 nearby hotels, and another branch near SM City Batangas. They serve coffee, pasta, pastries, and other. This is the only place in town that serve bagel sandwiches.
directions: in front of RLR Travellers Inn

name: The Other Place
description: Filipino-themed restaurant serving common local fare. Relocated to P. Burgos due to a fire accident in 2023.

name: D' Brothers Sports Bar
description: Sports-themed restaurant and bar, perfect place to talk, drink, and watch sports. Popular among locals and foreigners alike
directions: between F. Baylosis Crispy Pata and St. Therese of the Child Jesus Multiple Intelligence School annex

name: City Star Travel Lodge
address: Jose P. Laurel Highway, Sorosoro Karsada

name: Yellowbell Country Inn
description: Clean, has parking, cold water shower, TV, free Wi-Fi, generator. They also have some 2-bedroom 2-storey apartments with kitchen at ₱2000 a night. Tricycles can usually be found parked right outside.

name: Mac-Ro Lodge
description: Air-conditioned rooms with cable TV and backup generator.
directions: at the corner with Lt. Col. D. Atienza Street

name: RGR Traveller's Inn
description: Air-conditioned rooms, but without cable TV or Wi-Fi. You can board a jeepney if you are going to Mabini once you check out.

name: Hotel Quinio
description: Cheaper option downtown, but lacks most frills. Has no Wi-Fi or elevator

name: La Tropicana Motorists' Lodge
address: Jose P. Laurel Highway, Sorosoro Karsada

name: RLR Travellers Inn
description: AC rooms with cable TV, hot water shower and free Wi-Fi. No free breakfast and swimming pool.

name: Meaco Royal Hotel Batangas City
description: Relatively new mid-range choice not far from cheap shopping spots at Poblacion. You can either stay in a single or twin room, or family rooms, all with air-conditioning, cable TV, and Wi-Fi. Refreshments are available just on the third floor. Free parking available.
directions: at top of Novo Department Store

name: D' Mariners' Hotel
description: Air-conditioned rooms, with an option of Deluxe (single or twin) and Family, with cable TV, telephone, and room service. Has WiFi, free breakfast and swimming pool.
directions: turn left from National Highway before Kainan sa Sawali

name: The Alpa Hotel and Restaurant
description: Under new management and ongoing refurbishment. Air-conditioned rooms with cable TV, but without much of the frills carried over by the old management. Has swimming pool.

name: Batangas Country Club
description: Classy hotel and resort within of Batangas Port, mostly serving travellers to Mabini or Puerto Galera. A/C rooms with cable TV, Wi-Fi, laundry, coffee or tea makers, and restaurant. Has amenities like swimming pool, billiard hall, and gym.

name: Days Hotel Batangas
description: Tours to churches and communities in Taal, Lipa, Malvar and Tanuan can be arranged.
directions: from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport, car rentals are readily available in the form of taxi cabs that are waiting outside the airport; the hotel is in the Pastor Village

name: Hotel Pontefino
description: A/C rooms equipped with internet access and cable TV. Some of its facilities and services are business center, fitness room/ gym and recreational room.

name: Luks Lofts Hotel
description: Though housed in a small 3-story building, it is the most luxurious in town, having air-conditioned rooms with cable TV, free Wi-Fi, living room and kitchen. Amenities include indoor pools, sauna, billiard room, café, and spa.
directions: beside the IntegrityNet call center and near Days Hotel Batangas and SM City Batangas

name: SM Travelodge
description: Luxury traveller's hotel, with air-conditioned bedrooms with cable TV, living room, and hot tub bathrooms. You can also arrange tricycle services to Poblacion or to the port once you check out.

name: St. John the Baptist Church
description: Built between 1830 and 1883 using coral blocks and mortar, this landmark is the oldest standing stone church in Catanduanes and a key historical site in the province.
directions: along the main provincial highway, beside the Bato River and Bato Bridge

name: Batalay Shrine
description: A historic pilgrimage site marking the spot where the first Christian cross was planted in Catanduanes. It honors Father Diego de Herrera, the first apostle of the province, who was shipwrecked and buried here in 1576.
directions: along the coastal road, accessible via tricycle or local transport from Bato town

name: Mary's Woods
description: A peaceful outdoor sanctuary and pilgrimage site featuring a tree-lined walking path, outdoor Stations of the Cross, and a Marian grotto set amidst lush forest surroundings.
directions: near the Virac–Bato boundary, off the main provincial highway

name: Bato Bridge
description: A prominent local landmark spanning the wide Bato River, connecting the town center to outer barangays and providing scenic views of the riverbank, surrounding hills, and historic Bato Church.
directions: crosses the Bato River along the main provincial highway near Bato Church

name: Bato River Park
description: A scenic riverside park and promenade offering relaxed views of the wide Bato River, local fishing boats, surrounding green hills, and nearby Bato Bridge.
directions: along the Bato River bank near Bato Bridge and Bato Church

name: Bato Boulevard
description: A scenic coastal and riverside boardwalk along the Bato River, popular among locals and visitors for relaxing strolls, sunset views, and local street food stalls.
directions: along the Bato River waterfront, near Bato Bridge and the town center

name: Bato Municipal Hall
description: The seat of local government for the municipality of Bato, situated right in the town near major historical and riverfront landmarks.
directions: in the town center along the Bato River waterfront, near Bato Bridge and Bato Church

name: Maribina Falls
description: The most popular and accessible multi-tiered waterfall in Catanduanes, featuring cool freshwater swimming pools, shaded picnic huts, and lush tropical surroundings.
directions: near the Virac–Bato border off the main provincial highway; accessible via a short tricycle ride or private vehicle

name: Balongbong Falls
description: A scenic and lesser-visited waterfall set amidst lush countryside, offering cool freshwater pools and natural river landscapes ideal for swimming and quiet nature breaks.
directions: accessible via local road from the main provincial highway

name: Carorian Wonders & Poseidon Rock
description: A coastal island-hopping destination featuring towering white rock formations (Poseidon Rock), twin natural turquoise saltwater swimming pools, hidden lagoons, and dramatic ocean cliffside landscapes.
directions: accessible via motorboat/banca from Barangay Carorian. Hire local guides at the barangay hall or tour registration point
hours: Open daily (best visited during morning calm seas)

name: Bote Lighthouse
description: Local tour guide is mandatory. Perched on a high hill overlooking the Pacific Ocean, this historical lighthouse requires a short, continuous hike to reach, rewarding visitors with panoramic 360-degree views of Sakahon Beach, surrounding green hills, and the ocean coastline.
directions: accessible via a 30– to 45-minute uphill trek starting from Sakahon Beach

name: Sakahon Beach
description: A peaceful, secluded cove featuring clear blue waters, fine white sand, and scenic coastal rock formations, popular for relaxing away from crowds and serving as the trail head for Bote Lighthouse.
directions: accessible via local road from the town center or as the starting point for the trek to Bote Lighthouse

name: Mt. Lantad
description: A prominent high peak in Bato offering scenic mountain views, rich local flora, and trekking routes suitable for outdoor enthusiasts and hikers looking to explore the municipality's interior highlands.
directions: accessible via local mountain trails; arrange for a local guide before starting your trek

name: Batalay Mangrove Eco-Park
description: A scenic coastal mangrove sanctuary featuring elevated wooden boardwalks through dense mangrove forests, ideal for nature walks, birdwatching, and learning about local marine ecosystem conservation.
directions: along the coastal area of Barangay Batalay, accessible via local road from Bato

name: Batalay Bayview Inn
description: A local seaside inn offering comfortable accommodations with views of Cabugao Bay, situated close to coastal attractions and historical landmarks in Bato.
directions: along the coastal road, near Batalay Shrine and the Batalay Mangrove Eco-Park

name: Island Country Homes
description: A traveler's transient villa and guesthouse. It offers a home-like stay for families, tourists, and adventurers exploring the island.

name: Embers Cafe and Restaurant
description: It features a cozy, casual, and trendy setting with an Instagrammable vibe. It is well-regarded as a quiet spot that accommodates solo diners, groups, and remote work.

name: TEA'cao King
description: Tea store

name: Bauan Church
description: Founded as a chapel in what is now the town center of Alitagtag municipality, it is a Neoclassical church dating back to 1894, although a botched restoration by parish officials in 2021 stripped the facade bare to the frustration of residents and heritage advocates. The church also houses a giant image of the Holy Cross made from anubing, a species of Artocarpus. It is also known for subli, a devotional dance.

name: Sampaguita Beach
description: A remote stretch of white-sand beach

name: Robinsons Easymart Bauan
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Bauan Plaza Hotel
description: Bauan's first major hotel, with its exterior resembling a Bahay na Bato. Just below the hotel is a commercial strip
address: J.P Rizal corner Kapitan Ponso Streets, Barangay II

name: Saints Peter and Paul Parish Church
description: Bauang's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1590 and consistently repaired to its original state following multiple earthquakes and wars.

name: Bauang Bakawan Eco-Tourism Park
description: An extensive ecotourism reserve featuring mangroves (bakawan) along the coasts of Barangays Parian Oeste, Pudoc, and Payocpoc Sur

name: Mount Kabugbugan
description: The highest point in Bauang with a height of 251 m. Its peak offers commanding views of Lingayen Gulf.

name: Arguilla House
description: A colonial-era house belonging to Manuel Arguilla, one of the leading English-language Ilocano writers during the American period who was beheaded by the Japanese in 1944 for joining the guerrilla resistance during World War II.

name: Bauang Watchtower Ruins
description: The remains of a Spanish-era watchtower meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

name: Gapuz Grape Farm
description: Established in 1980, it is one of 61 grape farms in the area after it was found that Bauang's semi-arid soil and climate was ideal for growing the fruit. Offers grape-picking to be paid by weight.

name: Nariz Grapes Farm
address: Manila North Road, Payocpoc Norte Oeste

name: Ciano Umok Gallery Cafe
description: A cafe and art gallery featuring folk and local artworks.

name: PNB Bank
description: Has a Visa Card ATM.

name: Mang Inasal
description: Fast food.

name: Bayawan Pension House
description: Fan double rooms. A/C double rooms.

name: Bliss Pension house
description: Fan single/double rooms with outside bathrooms.

name: Casa Rosario Pension House
description: A/C single/double with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: J. R. Pension House
description: Simple fan rooms have no TV and bathroom, while better fan rooms have TV and bathroom. AC rooms include TV, bathroom and free breakfast.
price: ₱200 for simple fan rooms, ₱250 for better fan rooms, ₱500 for AC rooms

name: GV Hotel
description: Fan and AC single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV. 45 rooms.

name: Bangan Hill National Park
description: A historical landmark, it is the location of an annual "Stations of the Cross" held during the Lenten season, with live actors portraying Jesus' suffering, death, and resurrection. Aside from that, it is also visited by hikers, and the hilltop provides a wide view of the surrounding area and the Caraballo and the Cordilleras.

name: Bayombong Cathedral
description: Bayombong’s main Roman Catholic Church and the seat of its eponymous diocese. Built during the Spanish era, it was razed by fire twice and lost its belltower in the 1990 Luzon earthquake. With subsequent rebuilding, it is now approximately twice its original size. The cathedral maintains its original Baroque façade, which is similar to other colonials churches in Nueva Vizcaya except that its plaster was removed as part of a botched DIY restoration attempt.
address: Dela Cruz Street, Don Tomas Maddela

name: Nueva Vizcaya Provincial Capitol Complex
description: The current headquarters of Nueva Vizcaya’s provincial government was built during the administration of Governor Patricio G. Dumlao. The capitol building is a study of architectural ingenuity. It has a park with exotic plant species, concrete benches and sidewalks lighted with giant lamps and man-made lagoon ideal for rowing the colorful mini-boats operated by people with disabilities. The complex’s design is such that it has also been called the Luneta of the north.

name: People's Museum and Library
description: A museum on the history, culture and ethnography of Nueva Vizcaya, housed in a two story building that used to be the headquarters of the provincial government during the Spanish era. The permanent exhibition is at the second floor, with temporary exhibits at the lobby.
address: Del Pilar Street, Don Tomas Maddela
directions: beside Children's Park and facing Saint Dominic Cathedral Park

name: Rizal Shrine
description: A hillside monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal, commissioned by a Jordanian turned Filipino citizen in gratitude for having been rescued by a Filipino migrant worker went he went missing in the Saudi desert. It contains the second-largest statue of Rizal, a bronze and composite fibreglass sculpture with a height of 16 m and weighing 12 tons. The monument can be seen from as far as Solano.

name: Mount Palali
description: A 1705 m high peak on the eastern boundary with the municipality of Quezon that looms over northern Nueva Vizcaya.

name: Batara Firing Range
description: Shooting range.

name: Rocel's Farm
description: An agritourism resort with swimming pool.

name: Courage Integrated Farm
description: An agritourism resort.

name: Ammungan Festival
description: An annual celebration of Nueva Vizcaya's history, culture and resources, featuring parades, fairs and pageants.

name: 7-Eleven-Bayombong 1
address: 2978 Saquing Street corner National Road, Don Domingo Maddela

name: Savemore Supermarket Bayombong
address: Dumlao Boulevard corner Jose Abad Santos Street, Don Tomas Maddela

name: Mrs. Baker's Restaurant & Pastry Shop
description: A relatively splurge casual dining restaurant serving Filipino and western dishes. It also has a bakeshop.

name: Per Os Resto
description: Steak house.

name: Fratelli's Grill & Restaurant
description: Filipino food wrapped in banana leaf.
address: National Road corner Ponce Street, District IV

name: Bacolod Grill
description: A grilled chicken inasal restaurant that has been in operation as early as the 1990s.

name: Kamayan sa Kainyugan
description: An alfresco Filipino restaurant with unlimited soup.

name: Apayao Brew
description: This coffee shop has great location, awesome staff, and of course some lovely coffee.

name: Zen Hotel
address: Maharlika Highway, Purok I, Bonfal Proper

name: Benguet Museum
description: Provincial museum containing ethnographic materials relating to the indigenous people of Benguet.

name: National Museum-Kabayan Branch Museum
description: Kabayan Museum is established to protect and care the Kabayan Mummy Caves in the province. Mummy Caves are one of the country's national cultural treasures. It is a burial caves that holds mummies sited in Kabayan especially in the Timbac Caves. The building is placed in a lot donated by citizens who value the culture of the Ibaloi and the Kankanaey. It is a one-story building and a basement builds in a 500-m² lot in 1989. Also kept here are ethnographical, ecological and geological collections including artifacts and other relics of the Kabayan Mummies.

name: Mountain biking
description: Coordinate with the Philippine Tourism Office.

name: Mountain climbing
description: Coordinate with the Philippine Tourism office.

name: Mt. Pulag hike
description: Coordinate with the Philippine Tourism Office

name: Attend a kanyaw
description: This is an Igorot practice, Visitors can easily be in one during Benguet Day, or the Adivayan Festival.

name: Metro Bank
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: PNB Bank
description: Has a Visa Card ATM.

name: D Jan Dells Cabin
description: Fan/a.c. single/double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: G V Hotel
description: A.C. single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Marvins Seaside Inn
description: A.C. single/double with own bathroom. Has a swimming pool.

name: Biliran Garden Resort
description: A.C. single/double with own bathroom cable TV.

name: Binangonan Port
address: Osmeña corner Santa Ursula Streets, Libid

name: Binangonan Church
description: Binangonan's main Roman Catholic church, built in 1792 in the Baroque style and declared a national cultural treasure in 2025. Its highlights are the original Spanish-era altarpieces and a statue of Saint Ursula in the main altar.

name: Mount Tagapo
description: The highest point in Talim Island, with an elevation of 438 m, and a popular hiking spot for daytrippers from Metro Manila.

name: Mount Kalbaryo
description: A hilltop Catholic shrine involving a flight of 288 steps to see a grotto of the Virgin Mary and a Cross.

name: Punta del Diablo
description: A rocky 100 m promontory stretching into Laguna de Bay, named as such because it was said by folk legends to have been made by the Devil in a failed bid to woo a local girl.

name: Marian Hill
description: A hilltop Catholic shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary.
directions: turn left from the junction from San Carlos Loop Road
hours: Reservations only Mon-Fri. General admission Sat-Sun

name: Nuestra Señora de los Angeles de Binangonan
description: A Roman Catholic church in the rural Morong Peninsula that houses a venerated 19th-century sculpture of the Virgin Mary which, along with the statue of Saint Ursula in Binangonan Parish, are the two most important religious icons of Binangonan.

name: Binangonan Recreation and Conference Center
description: A multipurpose sports and swimming venue.

name: Puregold Pag-asa
directions: facing the junction with Quezon Avenue

name: Our Lady of Purification Parish Church
description: Binmaley's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era.

name: Sigay Fiestahan - Buffet of the North
description: Very spacious place, great place to eat, good for wedding receptions, birthday parties and reunions.

name: Doña Nora HQFSC Grill and Restaurant
Enchanted River Hianatuan
description: A deep spring river of rather mesmerizing shades of blue and home to numerous species of fish, popularized in a poem called Rio Encantado. Daily feeding by conservationists in the afternoon but swimming disallowed as of 2017.

name: Tinuy-an Falls
description: 55 meters high. 18 km from town, a 30-minute tricycle ride.

name: Baywalk Bislig
description: Promenade/photo-op along bay.

name: Tonys Superstore
description: A small supermarket.
address: Abarca street, corner of P. Lindo street

name: Prince Supermarket.
description: Full-size supermarket.

name: Gmar Food Court
description: Breakfast from 7AM-11AM.

name: Hotel One Eleven
description: Fan single/double, A/C rooms.

name: St Francis Pension House
description: Fan single/double with shared bathroom.

name: Sleep Inn
description: Fan single or double rooms.

name: Bonsay river view inn
description: A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: White Palace Inn
description: a/c double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Pensionne La Salle
description: Fan single, A/C single.

name: Casa de Babano
description: Restaurant, bar, wifi, a/c.

name: Alberto Mansion
description: Historic location of Jose Rizal's first formal schooling previously owned by an uncle of the national hero. It collapsed in 2012, but was expropriated by the city government and restored into a museum and cultural center in 2019.
directions: in front of San Isidro Labrador Parish

name: School of Rizal Site and Museum
description: Preserved Spanish-era schoolhouse, where Jose Rizal did his formal education between 1869 and 1871. Declared a National Historical Site, it used to be a private residence, until it was expropriated by the city government and turned into a museum.

name: Plaza Rizal
description: It is near the church San Isidro Labrador Parish, The Historic Alberto Mansion (maternal house of Rizal), The Sentrong Pangkultura ng Biñan and more. Rizal monument believed to be a work of the National Artist Guillermo Tolentino.

name: Museo ng Biñan
alt_name: Sentrong Pangkultura ng Biñan, Cultural Center of Biñan
description: A Spanish-era warehouse that was converted into a school and later the municipal hall. After local government offices moved to a larger complex in barangay Zapote in 2010, the building has hosted the city museum and a cultural center.

name: Capilla De San Jose
description: A Spanish-era chapel.

name: Shrine and Parish of San Isidro Labrador
description: Biñan's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present modernist state in 1970 after being destroyed multiple times since the Spanish era by fires, natural disasters and wars. Its belfry is a copy of a Spanish-era original that was destroyed by lightning in 1870.

name: Splash Island
description: Prime water park with long, winding slides and an artificial wave pool. It is frequented by Manila locals, and was once a common filming location for some Filipino movies. Outside food and drinks are not allowed, and you are required to buy them in-park, albeit at extortionate prices.
directions: visible along SLEX, just south of a power line that separates it from the Southwoods complex; served by Southwoods Exit from SLEX

name: Biñan Day
description: A three-day festival to commemorate Biñan's cityhood, liberation from the Japanese, and its original founding.

name: Puto Latik Festival
description: Held every May 15-23, it showcases Biñan's local delicacy, Puto Biñan (or Putong Latik)

name: Pavillion Mall
description: Managed by the retail arm of real estate giant, Ayala Corporation, it has fast food and some upmarket chain restaurants, various shops, and a Puregold supermarket.

name: Central Mall Biñan
description: A three-storey mall with some fast-food chains, and a Savemore supermarket.
address: Jeepneys headed for Olivarez stop/terminate here

name: Saigon Cà Phê & Restaurant
address: Blk 4 lot 13 North Rd, Silmer Village

name: National Museum - Marinduque-Romblon Area Museum
description: Perfect place to learn the warm and thriving culture of Marinduque. It is a must visit.

name: Boac Public Market
description: with food court.

name: Mercury Drug Store - Marinduque
address: Governor Damian Street corner Gov D. Reyes Street

name: North Luzon Express Terminal
description: A partially complete bus station inside the Ciudad de Victoria complex, intended to be used as the new terminal for long-distance services to Ilocos, the Cordilleras and Cagayan Valley. It opened in 2020, intended as a diversion terminal for northbound buses amid the COVID-19 pandemic, but has been announced as another bus station to complement the Valenzuela Gateway Complex.

name: Philippine Arena
description: With a 55,000 seating capacity, the arena is the biggest domed indoor arena not only in the Philippines but in the world. Built by local Christian sect, Iglesia ni Cristo for their centennial, the Philippine Arena hosts several events including sporting events, church events and concerts.

name: Philippine Sports Stadium
description: Also part of Iglesia ni Cristo's Ciudad de Victoria complex. The stadium is mainly for football events. It also hosts a blue athletics track.

name: St. Martin of Tours Parish Church
description: One of the oldest churches in Bulacan, established in 1578. The church is the home of the Cross of Wawa, a Catholic relic, which is paraded in the Pagoda Festival. Its pointed-edge altarpieces resemble those in medieval European churches.

name: Francisca Reyes Aquino Shrine
description: Shrine built in honor of Philippine National Artist Francisca Reyes Aquino, who was credited for her contributions to Philippine art and culture in the field of native dance. The place is managed by the National Historical Institute.

name: The Garden
description: A leisure area within the Ciudad de Victoria which features a variety of plants. It also hosts the Animal Kingdom, a mini-zoo with various wild animals, and a merry-go-round.

name: Bunducan Welcoming Arch
description: Historical landmark.

name: Shrine of Saint Andrew Kim
description: A Catholic shrine dedicated to Andrew Kim Taegon, a 19th century Korean priest who served in the area before returning to his homeland, where he was martyred for his beliefs. The chapel resembles an East Asian pagoda, while the gardens have been manicured on the same lines.
directions: enter Mendoza Street at the back of McDonald’s Lolomboy and follow the signage at Villa Modesta leading to Garahe Street to the right. The street itself is narrow and difficult for vehicles larger than a tricycle to maneuver, although parking at the site is spacious
price: PHP20, parking fees of PHP20 for cars and PHP10 for motorcycles, tricycles and bikes

name: Bocaue Pagoda Festival
description: An annual fluvial parade, also part of the annual Feast of the Holy Cross, where the Krus ng Wawa, which is believed to have saved an old woman's life who drowned, is paraded on the Pagoda, a gaily structure mounted on large wooden boat (banca), which is then paraded through the Bocaue River.

name: Karilagan Stevia Farm & Pavilion
description: A farm-resort and events venue with its own restaurant and cafe.

name: Plaza Centralle
description: Food court.
address: Plaza Centralle, Ciudad de Victoria Bypass Road

name: Embrace Cafe & Restaurant
address: The Garden - Ciudad de Victoria, Ciudad de Victoria

name: Padrino Food Park
description: Food court.

name: The HangOut FoodZone by MangCook-an
description: Fast food restaurant.

name: BigBrew Lolomboy Branch
description: affordable Milk Tea and Coffee.

name: PNB Bank
description: Visa Card ATM.

name: Metro Bank
description: Master Card-Visa Card ATM.

name: Jollibee fast food
description: Breakfast 7AM-11AM.

name: Maning's Garden
address: A. Pedroza Street, La Purisima Concepcion 6010

name: Northhomes Pensione
description: Fan single/double rooms with outside bathrooms.
directions: just down the road from the Gaisano mall

name: R & F Pension House
description: Fan double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Bogo Park Lodge
description: Fan double room with own bathroom

name: Nagano Pension House
description: Fan and a.c. double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Danao Adventure Park
description: Extreme/eco/educational adventure park that offers various activities for all ages. It boasts a sky-ride, zip-line, river tubing, caving and trekking activities.
price: Rates vary depending on choice of package or activity

name: Cape Bolinao Light House
description: A 30.78 m lighthouse built in 1905 to guard the approaches to Lingayen Gulf from the South China Sea.

name: Saint James the Great Parish Church
description: Bolinao's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque and Renaissance style during the Spanish era in the 17th century.

name: Bolinao Falls
description: There are 3 falls in this area: Bolinao Falls 1, 2, and 3, all in a relative east-west line on the Bolinao River. Just follow the crowd or ask for directions if needed. Really nice curtain falls and emerald pools you can swim in. Also there are resorts here if you decide you'd like to stay a while.

name: Enchanted Cave
description: Very grotto-like, with cross and Mary figure.

name: Cindys Cave
description: Subterranean pools so wear your aqua booties and hopefully the water is fairly clean.

name: Balingasay River
description: Balingasay river is one of the rivers in the Philippines that is awarded as the cleanest river. The water is flowing from the sea so the water is salty specifically near the bridge where children are jumping into the river. A variety of fish are living here. Beside the river is a restaurant where you can buy food and pay for a river cruise. This river cruise takes you for a ride and explore the river for a total of 1 hour river ride. If you really want to explore and swim in the river, you can rent a boat and look for a place you want to swim. Or maybe you can join the children swimming and jumping off the bridge.

name: Batong Bugtong
description: A big rock formation.

name: Patar White Sand Beach
description: One of those knockout beaches that make a lot of lists for reason of its beauty and warm, calm, tropical surf.

name: Cape Bolinao Beach
description: Very inviting.

name: Tondol White Beach
description: Calm breakwater and white sand.

name: Giant Taklobo Seafood and Grill Ilog Malino Branch
CIAO Pizzeria By The Sea & Mezze Club
Ilog Malino Beach Resort
description: This is a private resort.

name: El Pescador
description: It's a beautiful hotel and resort. The staff are very friendly.

name: Puerto Del Sol Beach Resort and Hotel Club
Treasures of Bolinao Beach Resort and Hotel
Sundowners Vacation Villas
description: Be ready to dispense with considerable pesos if you want to stay here.

name: Punta Riviera Resort
description: On a lush tropical farm by the East China Sea, this laid-back resort with a river crossing through is a 6-minute walk from Buena Beach. It's 16 km from Bani National Forest Preserve Park and 208 km from Clark International Airport. Accommodations range from low-key rooms with sitting areas to relaxed suites with outdoor kitchens. All have Wi-Fi, flat-screens and minifridges. Some sleep up to 20 guests. Breakfast is available. Amenities include 4 restaurants and a bar, plus 2 outdoor pools, a spa and a private beach. There are also loaner kayaks and guided nature tours, plus parking.

name: Amarela Resort
description: An upscale resort with an art gallery, gardens, a swimming pool, outdoor dining and beach access. Great beachfront views.

name: Bohol Beach Club
description: The resort boasts of an exclusive 1.5km stretch of white sand, the largest shoreline in that area. Guests can also enjoy a relaxing swim in the kidney-shaped pool set in lush greenery or simply laze at the outdoor jacuzzi. The club has aqua sports that include snorkeling, fun island dives, sailing, kayaking, and whale and dolphin watching.

name: Chiisai Natsu Resort
description: Caters to single vacationers, families and corporate groups.

name: Mount Labi
description: Believed to be the highest mountain in town, it is a 1620 m peak whose summit requires a 2-day climb. Along its slopes are the Silangan and Deesap falls, the latter being the tallest waterfall in Nueva Ecija.

name: Aurora Quezon Ambush site
description: Perhaps the main claim to fame (or infamy) of Bongabon in Philippine history is that it was the place where former first lady Aurora Quezon was assassinated along with her daughter, son-in-law, and several others when their convoy was ambushed along the highway by Huk rebels in 1949. The killing provoked national and international outrage and saw support for the Huks, then riding on popular demands for land reform, precipitously decline. The site of the killing is marked with a roadside shrine lined with shady trees which is often overlooked by travelers heading to Baler, where Mrs. Quezon's party was also heading to at the time.

name: Ilog Jordan
description: A pristine waterway (ilog means "river" in Tagalog) originating from Mount Olivete that is used for irrigation and swimming purposes by surrounding resorts.

name: Dilalam Lake
description: A man-made reservoir used primarily for irrigation purposes.

name: Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church
description: Bongabon's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and retaining its red-brick facade.

name: Museo de Bongabon
description: A museum on local history and culture, housed inside the former municipal hall.
price: ₱25 adults, ₱20 elderly/disabled, ₱10 students, additional fees for filming and commercial photography

name: Bongabon Bike Park
description: A complex featuring dirt biking trails on hilly terrain catering to mountain bikes.

name: Sibuyas Festival
description: The town's annual festival dedicated to its main agricultural product (sibuyas means onion in Tagalog).

name: Sanga-Sanga Airport
description: Cebu Pacific, Cebgo and Platinum Skies from Zamboanga

name: Bolobok Rock Shelter Cave
description: Archaeological site.

name: Panam Pangan Island
description: Panampangan Island is an island in the municipality of Sapa-Sapa, Tawi-Tawi.

name: Mount Bongao
description: Hike

name: Inay Restaurant
description: A casual dining family restaurant at the heart of Tawi-Tawi

name: Maligcong Rice Terraces
description: A series of rice terraces in a remote village. Views from the terraces can be seen following a hike on Mount Kupapey.

name: All Saints Cathedral
description: The seat of the Anglican Church in Bontoc.

name: Santa Rita Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in Mountain Province, built in an octagonal layout with multiple towers.

name: Bontoc Museum
description: Bontoc museum is a must-see if you are only stopping briefly into town. It has many great pictures and artifacts from the local tribes.

name: Francis Pain
description: Francis is a great guide who knows 13 local dialects, he will take you up from Bontoc to the Kalinga tribes. Check out Buscalan where you can see Whang Od perform traditional tattoos, and other very remote villages.

name: PNB Bontoc
description: Has a 24-hour ATM which only takes Visa Card.

name: Etag
description: Dried salted meat.

name: Dog meat
description: They serve dog menus in some of the karinderias there.

name: Cable Café
description: This is your really only option for drinking in town. It has some great live music there and has a friendly atmosphere.

name: Kidlaa Hotel and Restaurant
description: A pretty decent bar with live bands.

name: Churya-a Hotel & Restaurant
description: For budget travellers, and also has a great food menu. Single/double with outside bathrooms.

name: Archog Hotel and Restaurant
description: Clean, very affordable, friendly staff, great food. Single/double with own bathroom.
directions: other side of the Chico River

name: Mountain Hotel
description: Cheap and basic single/double rooms. No power outlets but will charge anything for free. Close to D Rising Bus Lines terminal.

name: Ayadwa Cafe and Resto
description: Single room.

name: Caticlan or Godofredo P. Ramos Airport
description: Much smaller and closer airport, only a few kilometers away from Caticlan Jetty Port and Tabon Port. It now handles jet flights to Manila operated by Philippines Airlines and Cebu Pacific, as well as turboprop aircraft from Cebu operated by Cebgo, PAL Express and SkyJet. The airline will drop you off at the east side of the airport. After exiting the airport on at east side, find the tricycle stand across the street, past the various resort offerings. A tricycle from the airport to the Tabon jetty is ₱50 per person. Ground transportation. From the Caticlan airport, you can either take a tricycle (₱50) or walk (10 minutes) to Caticlan Jetty Port. Besides, Cebu Pacific offers hotel transfer for ₱350 per person.

name: Kalibo International Airport
description: This airport can handle larger aircraft such as Boeing 737 and Airbus A320, however it is much farther from Boracay than Caticlan airport. Its international destinations include Beijing, Busan, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei, Singapore, Shanghai and Seoul, operated by Cebu Pacific, China Airlines, Philippine Airlines and AirAsia. Domestic flights are from both Cebu and Manila. There is a ₱200 terminal fee for domestic flights and ₱700 for international (2016).Ground transportation. There are vans, minibus shuttles and buses that serve travellers between Kalibo International Airport and Caticlan Jetty Port.
