A van and ferry ride takes 1½-2 hours and costs ₱250, and ₱300 for an AC bus. Additionally you will be asked to pay environmental taxes and terminal fees of ₱175 on top of the fare. Besides, AirAsia offers hotel transfers for ₱520 per person.
address: 2 km away from Kalibo and 70 km away from Caticlan Jetty

name: White Beach
description: This is what most people are here for, but there are environmental rules and the beach is a challenge for people with disabilities. It is a lovely stretch of powdery white sand against azure water, it's also the commercial center of the island. The long beach is divided into three sections, Station 1, Station 2, and Station 3. Station 1 is the northernmost and has the widest beachfront, where prime hotels and resorts are located. Accommodations are pricier, but quality is generally the best as well. Station 2 is the commercial and geographical center of white beach. This is the center of it all for shopping, eating, and partying. That said, the beach here is also the most crowded, and the area the nosiest. Station 3 is the southernmost section; quieter than station 2, it is the least developed, and also the lowest priced. All of White Beach from the northernmost tip of Station 1 to the southernmost of Station 3 (~4 km) is open to the public, so one can relax and/or swim wherever they like, regardless of hotel location.In every station, there are two lifeguards patrolling on foot equipped with whistle, life buoy and hand-held radio. The boat station 2 is the lifeguard and rescue command center.

name: Puka Beach
description: A quiet stretch of white sand along the northern tip of the island, Puka Beach is an image of what most people expect on a tropical island: white sand, azure water, and relatively empty. This is where locals gather the small puka shells for some of the jewelry that is sold on the island so expect the sand to be more coarse than on White Beach. The water tends to be a little rougher on this side of the island but it is much quieter. Similarly, there are fewer services—there are only a couple of restaurants, but you likely won't have a problem getting a cold drink or an ice cream as there are a few vendors that patrol the beach. The main road in Boracay terminates at Puka Beach therefore you'll be able to hire a tricycle to get there in less than 10–15 minutes from central White Beach. Make sure you arrange a pickup if it is a quiet day and no tricycles are hanging around the beach. Most people experience Puka as one of their sailboat or banca stops during a day trip. This is a good spot for a picnic, but be sure to bring your trash home with you.

name: Baling Hai Beach
description: This is a quiet little cove just north of Diniwid Beach, where you can enjoy swimming, snorkeling and dining in a relaxed, peaceful environment. There are some fantastic views from the clifftop restaurant. Baling Hai is often included as a stop-off on an island boat tour.

name: Bulabog Beach
description: Come there on a windy days to see kiteboarders doing high jumps and crazy tricks.

name: The Bat Cave
description: You will see in several tour guides and maps of Boracay something called the Bat Cave, which houses many small insectivorous bats (the larger fruit bats roost in the trees on the hillside above Punta Bunga Beach), and locals will be more than happy to accompany you there for a fee, or "tip". The cave is on the western-end of the island and down several dirt roads. The guide will then take you on a short hike through the forest to the mouth of a cave, which drops down at a very steep angle. The mouth of the cave is littered with large boulders, and is extremely difficult to enter and walk down. There is no visible path, no handrail, and the stones are extremely slippery with slime and bat guano, as well as extremely dangerous, since the cave is at such an extreme angle. Also, the air inside the cave is very warm and humid, and in addition to the amount of guano, is very difficult to breathe. Additionally, several snakes live inside the cave. Caution should be taken by those visiting and entering the cave. There are bats in the cave, but down at the bottom of it in the dark, and unless you have a flashlight or are there at dusk, you won't see them. The ceiling of the cave is interesting, however, with multiple, small stalactites. Just nearby, you can find another cave, called "crystal" cave which has a lot of stalactites and a hole on the opposite site of the entrance, from which you can watch out to the sea if you dare to climb up to it. You will have to pay ₱50 entry-fee to visit both caves for the family that owns the land, in addition to paying your guide. Visiting both caves can cost up to ₱2500 for the guide, but this is the "rich tourist price", so try to bargain if you like.

name: Freestyle Academy Kitesurfing School
description: Offers lessons from beginner to advanced. All instructors are IKO-certified.

name: Hangin Kite Center
description: The island's first kite center. Offers lessons from beginner to advanced. All instructors are IKO-certified.

name: Isla Kiteboarding school
description: The biggest school on Boracay. Very passionate about kitesurfing and very professional.

name: Pinas Kite Boarding
description: Locally owned kite-boarding shop, offers courses from level 1 to 3. All instructors are IKO-certified.

name: Bella Isa Salon & Spa
description: A little spot on the beach in Station 3 with upscale decor and professional staff. They provide a full range of services including massage, facials, foot spa, and hair services.

name: Tirta SPA
description: — found in Sitio Malabunot, Manoc-Manoc, area. Indian treatments in a stunning environment. Friendly and helpful staff. It is a good idea to compare prices between Tirta Spa, Mandala Spa, and Shangri-La Boracay to find the best deal.

name: Ariel's Point
description: Ariel’s Point is an affordable eco-adventure destination for Boracay travellers who want to experience the natural splendor of the Philippines and meet fellow travellers. Located 30 minutes away from Station 1 by outrigger boat, Ariel’s Point allows travelers to enjoy a wide array of adventurous activities such as cliff diving (the destination has five different platforms ranging in height from 3 meters to 15 meters), snorkeling, and paddling in an unspoiled setting with volcanic caves, mangrove forests, turquoise coves, and remote beaches. Visitors can reach Ariel’s Point by purchasing tickets at Ariel's House (along the White Beach in front of the Boracay Beach Club) before 11AM on the day of departure.
price: ₱2000 for round-trip boat transfer, a BBQ buffet, unlimited drinks (bottled water, beer, soda, rum), and access to cliff diving, snorkeling, kayaking

name: Parasailing
description: Take a parasailing tour around the island, to explore quiet beaches and snorkel sites. Ask your crew to organize a romantic BBQ on the beach with fresh grilled seafood, if you like. Cruise back at sunset to experience breathtaking views.

name: Motorbiking
description: It is worth hiring motorbikes or scooters out to explore the island, as there are other beautiful beaches on the other side of the island that are even better for snorkeling that will be completely deserted. Hire them for a couple of days and you should get a discount. The roads are a bit dodgy, and some are still being constructed, but it's a good laugh and better than plunking yourself on a patch of white sand and seeing nothing.

name: Horseriding
description: Horse riding is a fun activity in Boracay. Get off the beaten path and experience villages and scenery most other visitors don't get to see. All levels of experience are catered to. Ask a tricycle to take you to the Boracay Horse Riding Stables.

name: Paulo Collection BodyWear
description: Variety of beach wear and other souvenir items.
address: D'Mall, Bamboo Beach Resort, PC Main

name: CityMall Boracay
description: A new shopping mall with a big Savemore supermarket and many fast food outlets.

name: Kolai Mangyan Fudhaus
description: Good local cafe serving Filipino cuisine. Excellent value and quality. Good reviews.

name: Andok's
description: Andok's, which has 5 locations, sells rotisserie and fried chicken as well as favorite Filipino dishes.

name: D'Talipapa Market
description: Fresh seafood market with relatively cheap prices. Around the place are a variety of food stores that offer to cook for you. You can buy fresh seafood, etc., right near the stores, then have the stores cook it for you however you like. For example, you can get crabs for ₱400 for 1 kg opposed to buying in restaurants that charge ₱200 per 100 grams. However, most of the seller are quite pushy and anyone buying needs to be prepared to bargain hard to get a good deal.
price: scallops ₱300/kg, lobster ₱1000, fish steak ₱150. Cooking prices ₱100-200

name: Smoke
description: A very good budget eatery. Local dishes, meat and seafood dishes, omeletes and excellent sandwiches are on offer. Most meals cost around ₱120 and are all cooked fresh. If you are around between 11AM and 2PM you get a free drink of iced lemon tea with every rice meal.
address: down one of the alleys opposite Lemon cafe in D'Mall

name: Jammers
description: Up and running for more than 8 years, amazing burgers, hotdogs, fruit shakes, etc. A lot of negative reviews, people say it's overrated.
address: on the front beach of D'Mall

name: True Food
description: Offers fiery Indian cuisine that will awaken the tastebuds. The place is cozy with straw mats and over-sized cushions. The staff is polite and very accommodating. For those who enjoy the spicier side of life, try the tandoori chicken.

name: The Sunny Side Cafe Restaurant
description: Good place to have a breakfast. Very high ratings on rating sites.

name: Lemoni Cafe
description: This place serves a variety of breakfasts, lunches and light meals. The service and presentation is excellent.

name: Dos Mestizos
description: This restaurant is the brainchild of respected Boracay chef & restaurateur Binggoy Remedios and his close childhood friend, Jose Ramon Valdes Nieto. Both owners have Spanish ancestors, hence the name "Dos Mestizos". This restaurant serves a selection of excellent tapas and is located between stations 2 and 3, behind the Tourist Center.

name: Aria
description: Delicious Italian food. If they don't give you the spicy olive oil bottle on the side for your custom made pizza, make sure you ask for it.

name: Hama
description: A Japanese restaurant located at the D'Mall and just across The Hobbit House.

name: Fridays Boracay
description: All day dining, themed dinner, Friday night buffet, seafood grill, plus 3 cultural dance shows every week with fire dance.

name: Heidiland Deli
description: Next to the main plaza at the D'Mall Phase IV is a fully air-conditioned European style deli selling all kinds of deli food as cheeses, cold cuts, salami, yoghurt, wines, etc. Locally famous for reasonably priced sandwiches, other stuff is usually expensive.

name: The Hobbit Tavern
description: With great food, drinks and live music, this place is the best of the Hobbit House chain. The main draw is the midget staff, however.

name: Valhalla Bar & Restaurant
description: In the mall is a refurbished steakhouse with a varied and interesting menu.

name: Kasbah
description: Authentic Moroccan cuisine serving exquisite tagines and couscous.

name: Bamboo Lounge
description: Serves a good selection of Chinese food in a relaxed beachfront setting. Quite average reviews.

name: Manana
description: Serves large portions of tasty Mexican food. Guacamole is only available when avocados are in-season despite what the menu says. Average reviews left by customers.

name: Obama Grill Bar-Restaurant
description: Steak restaurant, opened April 2009. Some say it's expensive and the portions are small.
directions: across from Andok's Station 1 and Shore Time Hotel

name: Ole
description: A great place to go for Spanish tapas and other specialties. Beware - the main courses are enormous!

name: Tilapia 'N Chips
description: Visit this place for good beer-battered fish and chips. They also serve Asian and Western style fish dishes, burgers, sandwiches and soup at this modern, airconditioned restaurant. Take out also available.

name: Titos (Resto & Grill)
description: Serve modern Filipino cuisine that combines the casual comfort of a home cooked meal with the relaxed sophistication of fine dining. Drop by for a quick snack or a delicious meal and enjoy the live music coming from Pat's Creek and Bom Bom Bar.

name: Deparis Beach Resort
description: One of the first European restaurants on the island, the first in fact to have chocolate mousse and Italian pizza when the island was without electricity in the early 1980s. Owned by the infamous and eccentric Frenchman Roger Deparis who has lived on the island since his backpacking days, it is a throwback to the old island style of mismatched decorations and heavy foliage.
directions: beside Le Soleil and The Mandarin

name: Cowboy Cocina
description: Serves tasty steaks, ribs and other grilled dishes, and arguably the best burgers in Boracay.

name: Cyma
description: Excellent food and service at this Greek restaurant. Try the mezedes combination, the spinach and artichoke fondue and the chicken souvlaki.
address: in the new part of the D'mall

name: Real Coffee
description: Serves a variety of pancakes, sandwiches, omelettes, baked goods and salads as well as freshly brewed coffee. The mother-and-daughter owners also get repeat customers who have been going there for years. They are also famous for their lemon muffin cupcakes, which are very much in demand.
hours: 7AM-7PM, take away shop downstairs works till 9PM

name: Starbucks
description: Of the coffee shops of this famous chain. On the other side, it's extremely small cafe without even places to seat.

name: Bom Bom Bar
description: A native-style beach bar that often has live music. It's a popular hang out for artists and musicians.

name: Charlie's Steakhouse & Diner Restaurant
description: This bar is a long-time favorite on Boracay with live bands that play covers. Customers are invited to sing with the bands.
directions: Right in the middle of the beach

name: Cocoloco Beach Resort
description: An attractive beach bar and restaurant that also serves tasty food. You can enjoy your drink by the beach, under the coconut trees, and there's a pool table in the bar too. Several years ago it started offering bungalows for rent as well.

name: Juice Bar
description: Offers top notch cocktails and a variety of "sneaky smoothies". with a wide open courtyard opening up to the beach it tends to fill up by around 11PM but still very comfortable. The crowd is a nice mix of locals and foreigners. Great staff and charming bartenders. There was a report in 2016 that it was closed.
address: right between Boracay Regency and Boat Station 2

name: Bei Kurt und Magz Restaurant
description: Run by friendly Bavarian Kurt and his wife Mags. It's a very popular spot to meet and chat, and one of the few places on the island serving draft beer. Serve German and Filipino food.

name: Nigi Nigi Nu Noos
description: A popular, centrally located spot to have a cool drink and enjoy a little people-watching. The manager is an expat. It is a hotel as well.
address: between boat stations 2 and 3, three minutes walk north of the tourist center

name: Red Pirates Pub
description: A native style beach bar (Angol, near boat station 3) with a relaxed and friendly atmosphere and good selection of fruity cocktails as well as affordable ice cold beer. It's a good place to meet other travelers and chat, and on weekends, selected weekdays and full moon nights there is live music and an all-you-can-eat beach BBQ and buffet (Fridays).

name: Shantal's Resto Bar
description: Revered, family-owned cantina on the beach with great value homemade food. The menu offers a bit of everything and the friendly staff will go out of their way to make you feel right at home. Has a popular Happy Hour from 2PM-8PM, offers one of the best beachside and sunset views on the island, and bumps a non-stop soundtrack of the best in electronic, hip-hop, R&B/soul, and reggae music.
address: Station 3 at the pathway to Dave's Straw Hat Inn, Morenos, and Escurel

name: W Hostel Boracay
description: Backpackers' hostel with 4- to 6-bed dorms. Free breakfast and free Wifi.
address: 2nd floor Gill & Park Bldg Zone 5 Bolabag Road
directions: D mall is 350 yards from the W hostel.

name: Escurel Inn
description: Amidst the vast complex of station 3 accommodations tucked behind the pathway next to Arwana's cafe, this is a friendly Filipino-owned establishment. Spacious, private rooms with fan, Hot and cold shower, cable TV, kitchenette, fridge, and unlimited free Wifi close to the beach access. All rooms have a nice balcony to lounge out and laze on; the fan-only huts also each have a nice hammock out front. Rooms are priced according to season; either peak or off-peak.

name: Little Corner of Italy
description: Better known as "Da Mario's" as it is owned and run by an Italian businessman. The hotel offers budget common rooms which can be shared by a maximum of 4 persons which have a fan and common shower and toilet, while rooms with bungalows are slightly expensive and can be shared by a minimum of 2 persons and a maximum of 4 persons. Rooms are priced according to stay and per person. If you don't plan to sleep there, consider trying their lasagna.

name: Moreno's Place
description: Run by a different owner of the same family as Escurel's, one will find similar accommodations and friendliness here. Prices are roughly similar to Escurel better publicized (read: Lonely Planet listed) accommodations. It's a 15-second walk to the beach.

name: Dive Gurus Boracay Beach Resort
price: Dormitory (sleeps 1-2 people in bunk beds) ₱200/₱250/₱300 for low season/mid season/high season

name: Treffpunkt
description: One of the best budget options on the island. Clean, simple, quiet rooms with television, A/C, private bathroom and shower, and patio. There is also a boarding house upstairs, a general store, a treehouse kitchen, and the cheapest breakfast and sandwiches in Boracay. Friendly, accommodating staff.
directions: along the same pathway to Dave's Straw Hat Inn, Morenos, and Escurel

name: Villa Romero Boracay
description: Villa Romero Boracay is a 26-room hotel located just a few steps from the front beach of Boracay Island. The hotel also has a restaurant, guest lounge, coffee shop and a convenience store. It is far from the hustle and bustle of central Boracay but at the same time, close to the beachfront bars, souvenir shops, the market, restaurants, and dive shops.

name: Dormitels Boracay
description: Fan single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV. Has 20 rooms.

name: Alta Vista De Boracay
description: Beautiful resort.

name: Baling Hai Beach Resort
description: Baling Hai Beach Resort has a secluded beach surrounded by cliffs located on the northern part of Boracay, two coves away from the main White Beach.

name: Blue Coral Resort Boracay
description: Small resort with six rooms equipped with AC, hot water, minibar, modern bathroom, safe, cable TV, wifi.
directions: right at the White Beach, behind Cocoloco Bar

name: Crown Regency Prince Resort
description: The resort draws its ambiance from the past and contemporary art echoed in the 36 rooms.
address: Main Road, Station 1, Bolabog Road, Barangay Balabag
directions: at the crossing of the main road and the road leading to Bolabog Beach

name: Crown Regency Beach Resort
description: This 41-unit resort has beautiful sunset views. It also has an infinity pool at the deck.

name: Crown Regency Resort & Convention Center
description: It includes an impressive 1,800-m² wave swimming pool with kiddie pool and a country's first wave rider (a pool you can surf on); 479 elegant units; a 1,600-guest conference center; restaurants; an adventure park; and Pricelite Outlet Store, where you can find many US brand items at ₱99, from personal care items to liquors.

name: Blue Mango
description: In Angol, at the southern end of White Beach. A friendly, family run establishment. The location is peaceful - less crowded than at station 2.

name: Sundown Resort Boracay
description: Nice resort right on the beach at the nicest part of Boracay with new rooms equipped with ac, hot water, fridge, modern bathroom, cable tv, wifi. Great restaurant on the beach. Austrian management.
directions: right at the White Beach, behind Cocoloco Bar

name: Argonauta Boracay- Boutique Hotel with Villas and Apartments
description: Boutique hotel situated on a 5,000-m² hillside property facing west (sunsets) over Punta Bunga Beach. Rooms are equipped with AC, hot water, mini-bar, cable TV, wifi. The Argonauta-Mobil brings guests to the White Beach and to Puka Beach.
directions: follow main road direction to Shangri La, Turn right after Grand Vista Hotel

name: Boracay Cottage Island Resort
description: The rooms are in Filipino-inspired design with walls made of Banig and bamboo furniture.

name: Boracay Terraces Resort
description: has its own swimming pool and offers deluxe accommodation and fully-furnished suites and apartelles. Activities like swimming, island hopping, snorkeling, diving and parasailing can be enjoyed.

name: Asya Premier Suites
description: It offers premier and executive suites, all of which have views of the sea, and is equipped with cable TV with DVD player, mini-bar, and NDD/IDD phone service. Some of its amenities include private shuttle speedboat and van, nanny & butler service, a fitness center, and Wi-fi internet services.

name: Bamboo Bungalows
description: 4000 m² of beachfront property. Offers various categories of rooms, ranging from aircon and hot water-equipped hotel rooms to basic fan-cooled cold-shower bungalows.

name: Beachcomber Resort Boracay
description: 11-room resort across the road from the beachfront. Sun loungers on the beach, pool, roof deck, spa, complimentary breakfast.

name: Boracay Beach Chalets
description: Air-conditioned cottages.

name: Boracay Beach Club
description: Modern 30-room resort featured in Travel + Leisure magazine. Amenities include a rooftop deck, swimming pool, and beachfront lounge. Special packages with discounts to Ariel's Point and complimentary breakfast included. Family-owned and managed.

name: Boracay Gold Crowne Resort
description: Beachfront rooms with private balconies.

name: Boracay Grand Vista Resort
description: Claims the largest swimming pool in Boracay.

name: Villa Sunset Resort
description: Villa Sunset is an 8-room apartment type hotel located at the heart of Boracay's White Beach at Station 2. The rooms are fully-furnished with their own balcony overlooking the swimming pool. The hotel offers day tour activities to those that would like to explore Boracay and its neighboring islands.

name: Boracay Sands Hotel
description: It offers suites that are equipped with a DVD player, cable TV, Internet connection, refrigerator, IDD phone, writing desk and chair, safe, and hair dryer. Some of its facilities include a spa, swimming pool, restaurant and bar, café, and function rooms.

name: Erus Hotel and Restaurant Boracay Island
description: A new hotel located right at the heart of station 2.

name: Fairways & Bluewater Newcoast Boracay
description: Fairways & Bluewater Newcoast Boracay offers rooms equipped with air conditioning, cable television, minibar, refrigerator, safe, hairdryer and baby cot (subject to availability). Some of its facilities and services are clubhouse, restaurant, golf course on site, swimming pool, spa, parking, full service health spa, complimentary area shuttle and room service.

name: Fridays Boracay
description: Comfortable cottages.

name: Jay Jays Club Boracay Resort
description: A hilltop private resort above Boat Station 1 with incredible ocean and beach views. Apartments have aircon, hot water, kitchens, cable TV and wifi.

name: Jony's Beach Resort Boracay
description: One of the oldest family-run establishments on the island.

name: La Isla Bonita Resort & Spa Boracay
description: Nice, basic, aircon room with cable TV and private bathroom.

name: Boracay La Reserve
description: Elegant rooms, private balcony with garden views.

name: Lingganany
description: Located on a hillside, 22 apartments available, with views, a pool, and free shuttle service to and from the hotel.

name: Microtel Inn and Suites Boracay
description: 51-room beachfront hotel.

name: Monaco Suites de Boracay
description: All-suite hotel, 40 apartments available, with an ocean view, infinity pool, and free shuttle service to and from the hotel.

name: Nami Resort
description: A/C rooms equipped with cable television, minibar, coffee and tea maker, jacuzzi and king-size bed. Some of its facilities and services are restaurant and bar, water sports, airport and city transfers.

name: Nigi Nigi Nu Noos
description: Good "traditional" cottages that look great. Food is good there too.

name: One Azul Boracay Resort
description: A/C suites equipped with cable tv, private toilet and bath, deluxe bathroom amenities and free continental breakfast. Some of its facilities and services are wireless internet, safety deposit box, massage service, laundry and dry cleaning service and airport, land, and boat transfers.

name: Orinda Boracay
description: resort right on the beach of Boracay with rooms equipped with AC, hot water, fridge, modern bathroom, cable tv, wifi. Hotel restaurant on the beach.

name: One Crescent Place Hotel
description: The resort is in Station 1 of Boracay Island, a two-minute walk to the powdery white sands and crystal-blue waters of White Beach. Each guestroom features a deck, dining area, kitchenette, microwave oven, refrigerator, private toilet and shower, mini-bar, and Internet access. It is also fitted with a DVD player, writing desk and chair, hair dryer, iron and ironing board, and safe.

name: Le Soleil de Boracay
description: Right in the center of White Beach, near Boat Station 2. The resort as a whole has a nice ambiance, rooms are also brightly decorated. Lounging area available right on the beach front as you step out of the hotel. Breakfast is served à la carte and portions aren't that impressive so if your package doesn't come with breakfast, you might as well have it outside of the hotel.

name: Panoly Resort Hotel
description: 45 bungalows and 55 veranda-equipped hotel rooms.

name: Paradise Garden Resort Hotel & Convention Center Boracay
Patio Pacific Boracay
description: Formerly known as Pink Patio Resort. Facilities include a gym, pool and climbing wall. The 65 aircon rooms are adequate if a bit bland in decor. Breakfast is served buffet style though choices may be limited at times. Three-minute walk to White Beach.

name: Pearl of the Pacific - Beach Resort Boracay
description: At Boat Station one with ocean view suites right on the beach.

name: Punta Rosa Boracay Resort
description: Northern end of White Beach. Breakfast included.

name: Sea Wind Boracay
description: 50-room luxury resort. Spacious, Filipino-style rooms with pseudo-antique furniture.

name: Serendipity Resort Boracay
description: Simple but tastefully-fitted aircon rooms with hot water and cable TV. Fan-cooled cottages, inspired by huts in the Philippine highlands, are also available. Additional features include a commercial arcade, a guest’s lounge and landscaped gardens.

name: Mito's Palace Boracay
description: A cozy hotel located at station 1, White Beach. All rooms air conditioned, with hot and cold shower, cable television, patios, minibar, 24-hour room service. Newer hotel.

name: Shore Time Boracay Resort
description: In station 1, across from the beach with their own private guests sun loungers on the beachfront.
directions: next door to Andok's- Station 1 & across from Obama Grill Restaurant)

name: The Strand Boracay Resort
description: Small 13-room resort in a fusion Asian-Scandinavian style, one minute away from the beach. Salt-water pools.

name: Sur Beach Resort
description: One of the smaller but charming hotels in the Station 1 area.

name: The Tides Hotel Boracay
description: Boracay's most notable boutique hotel located at the heart of D'Mall.

name: Villa Camilla
description: Nice and quiet beachfront hotel with a swimming pool in Boat Station 3. Can be quite a bargain in low season.

name: Villa Sunset Resort Boracay
description: Eight apartments with own terrace/balcony, cable TV, telephone, kitchenette, shower, air conditioning and a fully stocked fridge.

name: Willy's Beach Club Hotel Boracay
description: 40 Mediterranean-style villas with aircon.

name: Swiper's Inn
description: Swipers Inn has an amazing view of the white sandy beach. The suites have their own kitchen and dining area.

name: Islakite Center
description: Offers 9 nice fan rooms, private bathroom with hot shower, cable TV and free Wi-Fi. Perfectly located, right on the beach. Kitesurf as soon as you wake up. Good breakfast and free storage for the gear are included in the rate.

name: 7Stones Boracay Suites
description: is a boutique hotel situated on a 4,000-m² beachfront property located at the famous water sports paradise otherwise known as Bulabog Beach. This new and modern boutique hotel has of stunning roomy suites and breathtaking sights.

name: The Lazy Dog Bed and Breakfast
description: This B&B offers 15 fully air conditioned rooms, hot showers, cable TV and free Wi-Fi. Set inside a private garden enclave and conveniently located at the center of the island. On-site cafe offers breakfast and lunch. Dogs are welcome.

name: Reef Retreat Boracay
description: A nice cozy 12 room hotel owned by a couple from the UK. It's right near windsurf/kiting schools and breakfast is also served in one of these schools. Free Wi-Fi is available in all rooms. All rooms are equipped with cable TV, aircon, mini bar, hot/ cold shower and ceiling fan. Bulabog beach is only 1min walk away from the hotel. The walk to White beach takes about 10 min and the same goes for the walk to D*Mall. The hotel is clean and newly built with comfortable rooms.

name: Boracay Butterfly Garden Cottages
description: Cottages with kitchens, separate air conditioned bedrooms, hot showers, cable TVs, free Wi-Fi, and sea view patios. 10 min from beach, 7 min from D'Mall.

name: Palm Breeze Villa Boracay
description: A small luxury resort in a slightly elevated position at the north end of Bulabog Beach. The resort features a swimming pool with swim-up bar. Free wifi throughout. Stunning views over the swimming pool and ocean from all rooms. En-suite bathrooms feature modern fixtures and oversized shower-heads. They also include quiet split-system air-conditioning, cable TV, mini-bar and tea/coffee making facilities.

name: Cohiba Villas Boracay Resort
description: Tel. Furnished villas intended for families staying a week or more, located on a cliff overlooking Bulabog Beach. Quiet split-system air-conditioning, cable TV, mini-bar.

name: Ocean Breeze Inn
description: Offers budget cottages or air conditioned guesthouse rooms (various room sizes for single travellers or families) at affordable rates. Guest kitchen also available. Ocean Breeze Inn is located at Station 3, around 2-3 minutes walk to White Beach.

name: Trafalgar Cottages
description: Double fan rooms, shared bathroom. Nice garden.
directions: behind the New souvenir shops at D original talipapa.

name: Shangri-La's Boracay Resort and Spa
description: Boracay's first international branded resort. 219 rooms, suites and villas, with 350m of dedicated beach and 12 hectares of grounds. They also offer airport transfers through their private speedboat.

name: Boracay Holiday Resort
description: A Mediterranean inspired resort located at the heart of Manggayad (Station 2), a three-minute leisurely walk to white beach.

name: Grand Boracay Resort
description: Grand Boracay is in the center of Boracay island. Known for its wide space and quiet atmosphere with its affordable prices.

name: Mandala Spa and Villas Boracay
description: A sanctuary for the body and soul where a culture of respect for the individual and an atmosphere of beauty, wellness and personal growth pervades. Relax and revive in a romantic and secluded resort villa with spa therapies, yoga or natural foods, walking distance from Boracay’s famous White Beach in this award winning Boracay resort and spa.

name: Turtle Inn
description: This is one of the island's newer establishments. Located just a couple of minutes walk from the beach near boat station 3, this hotel has a high standard of accommodation at surprisingly reasonable rates.

name: Fat Jimmy's Resort
description: Fat Jimmy's Resort in Boracay, Philippines offers the best quality and friendly service with neat, clean and comfortable accommodations at a price everyone can afford and make the best Boracay experience in their life.

name: La Bella Casa
description: It offers air-conditioned rooms, all of which are equipped with a cable TV, mini-fridge, and private shower and bathtub. Superb room service is also offered to guests.

name: Beachcomber Resort Boracay
description: 11 accommodations, all equipped with Cable TV, Air-conditioning and Private veranda. Facilities and services are Spa, Outdoor swimming pool, Restaurant and bar.

name: Boracay Holiday Resort
description: Sprawling Mediterranean inspired resort located right at the heart of Manggayad (Station 2) and affords its guests with a 3-minute leisurely walk to the famous white beach. Just by walking alone through the resort's breezy corridors and airy verandas is enough to make you feel the holiday ambience. Boracay Holiday Resort is an affordable luxury. It surely will be a part of your memorable experience here in the island, not just a place to stay
address: Station 2, Corner Main Rd. & Tirol Rd., Manggayad, Balabag

name: Gran Prix Boracay Hideaway
description: A cool beach retreat nicely tucked a few meters away from the buzz of the Boracay coastline. Offers an oasis of calm and understated luxury with its wonderfully modern ambience.

name: Real Maris Resort
description: Their air-conditioned rooms are equipped with cable TV, DVD player, Internet access, room safe, mini-bar. Some of their facilities are restaurant, an outdoor swimming pool, a beach bar, and massage services

name: Roque’s Place Boracay
description: It offers 15 rooms, all of which have air-conditioning, cable TV, and a mini-bar. Some of its amenities include bar and restaurant, beauty parlor, and water sports facilities. While staying here, you can visit some interesting places like Diamond Sea Sports, Boracay Scuba, and Willy's Rock.

name: The Sitio Boracay
description: From the native cogon roofing to the endearing Filipino-Balinese theme, your air-conditioned Boracay villa is a place rife with comfort and charm.

name: Boracay Hills Resort
description: One of the most exclusive places to stay on Boracay Island. Located in the lush and hilly hammock of Bantud 10 minutes walk from the beach; free shuttle service available.

name: Lorenzo's Villa
description: At the southern tip of Boracay, 10-15 min to White Beach by free hotel shuttle. All rooms feature ocean view balconies. There is a pool and spa services on site, but beach access to a small stretch of sand is limited due to the resort being perched on a cliff.

name: Paradise Bay Resort Boracay
description: Tulubhan is popular with German travellers. It offers a middle range accommodation rate with a small pool, a free van-ride to anywhere on the island and a billiard table.

name: Boracay Amor Apartments
description: Serviced apartment built on top of a limestone cliff giving good view over Boracay Island.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: This is the south end of White Beach which is quieter, cleaner and less busy than station 1 or 2. The Inn has 4 standard rooms, 4 deluxe garden rooms, 3 ocean view suites and two large family rooms. The inn also has a highly regarded restaurant and dive center, and there is a designated area with lounge chairs. If you get the opportunity, spend some time with the owner, Vaughn, an exceedingly friendly and accommodating American expat. All the rooms also have air-conditioning, hot water, cable TV, wireless Internet connection and come with free bottled water, beach towels, and breakfast.

name: Balaihara
description: A cluster of villas sprawled over the resort community of Fairways and Bluewater in the Newcoast area. Each villa has roomy and cozy rooms furnished with modern amenities. Recreational facilities include an 18-hole Graham Marsh-designed golf course and a swimming pool.

name: Boracay Mandarin Island Hotel
description: Set in the heart of Boracay’s vibrant culture and warm atmosphere is Boracay Mandarin Island Hotel, a AAA beachfront resort with 52 luxurious rooms and suites, an in-house restaurant by the sea, hotel spa, swimming pool, kiddie pool and convention center.

name: Argonauta Boracay - Boutique Hotel with Villas and Apartments
description: At a hillside near Punta Bunga Beach overlooking the ocean to the west, near Shangri La Resort. Available are Boutique Hotel Rooms, Apartments good for 4 guests and Villas good for 6 guests. 2 small swimming pools on site.
address: Hagdan, Yapak, Overlooking quiet Punta Bunga
directions: tunr left on the main road going to Balinghai

name: Borongan Airport
description: Has a runway, but no commercial flights. Cebu Pacific once served this airport using turboprop jets, but ceased service due to security concerns.

name: Cabong Beach
description: Suitable for swimming.

name: Borongan Cathedral
description: Place of worship.

name: Kaputian Falls
description: Refreshing running water wherein some tourists choose to visit here to calm themselves.

name: Hilangagan Beach
description: Enjoy the white sand and natural pool in the secluded nook beach facing the Pacific Ocean.
directions: It is a 20– to 30-minute tricycle ride from Borongan City Transport Terminal to Punta Maria

name: Hebacong Sea of Clouds and Nature Park
description: The best time to visit is from 5AM to 7AM.
price: Tourists are required to pay an environmental fee amounting to ₱20 for students, senior citizens, and PWD; P40 for local residents and ₱70 for non-residents; and ₱100 for foreigners.

name: Ganap Cave
description: With beautiful spring. Stalactites and Stalagmites of various colors and sizes.
directions: 13 km northwest of Borongan town proper

name: Baybay Boulevard
description: Big waves, ideal for surfing.

name: Ando Island or Andis Island
description: Aside from enjoying the picturesque view from the top of Bantayan Cliff, you can also do rappelling with your friends and families at Bantayan Cliff which is a 10-minute trek from the jump-off point of the island.
directions: from the city you can ride a tricycle to Brgy. Sabang South Fish Port and a half an hour boat ride from Fish Port to Ando Island

name: Margielyn Didal Skate Park
description: Located beside I Love Borongan Landmark. Scrimmages available from 3PM till evening.

name: Basketball park
description: Located beside Rottea borongan at Baybay4. Scrimmages available at 3PM till sundown everyday.

name: Soccer
description: Located at Surf City tower. Soccer enthusiast are welcome to experience sports that also available in the area.

name: Ultimate Frisbee
description: Located at the back of the Borongan Ticketing office, Everyone is welcome to try such extreme and unique sport played in Borongan. Scrimmages are from 3PM to sundown.

name: Metro Bank
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: Wilsam Uptown Mall
description: Has a supermarket.

name: 578 Emporium Department Store and Supermarket
description: Budget friendly store.

name: Puregold Borongan Branch
description: It is a supermarket where you can buy food products and home essentials.
directions: across Wilsam Uptown Mall and at the groundfloor of J & F Mall

name: Salukara
description: Salukara is a crepe-like delicacy which is a mixture of ground rice, coconut milk, water, sugar and coconut wine as a riser instead of baking powder.

name: Jollibee
description: Philippines-based chain known for its burgers, fried chicken, spaghetti & Filipino dishes. Dine-in, takeout, delivery.

name: Brew & Bistro
description: Open for dine-in and take-out.

name: Tuba
description: It is a fermented alcoholic beverage obtained from the sap of coconut palm.

name: Tacos & Beer
description: Open Tuesday and Thursday from 4PM to 11PM; Friday and Saturday from 4PM to midnight, closed on Wednesdays.

name: McDonald's Borongan
description: First drive-thru Golden Arches in Eastern Samar.

name: Hotel Dona Vicenta
description: A/C single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: GV Hotel
description: Fan/air-con single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Domsowir Hotel
description: Fan/air-con single/double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Primea Hotel Borongan
description: Experience a safe, comfortable and clean rooms designed to enhance your stay. They also offer additional amenities such as complimentary breakfast, key card lock system, key card lock system, wireless internet access, cable television, access to dipping pool and hot and cold showers.
directions: near Capito Cultural Stage and Hamorawon Park

name: Rawis Resort and Restaurant
description: With view of the ocean. Live bands play at the venue.
directions: ride a tricycle going to Barangay Alang Alang Detour

name: Melindas Resort and Restaurant
description: With scrumptious foods, KTV rooms, acoustic bands, beautiful and affordable hotel rooms, as well as safe playground and swimming pools for children.

name: Golden Creek Farm & Resort
description: Various activities are offered in the resort: swimming, play golf, mountain climbing and sight seeing where you can see the town of Borongan and the seashore. and the resort also offers other event such as birthdays,debut, and seminars.
directions: ride a tricycle from Borongan City Market

name: Mount Pinatubo
description: Inevitably associated with the town, the volcano is the biggest draw in the area, particularly its crater lake and the lunar landscapes created along its gullies following the 1991 eruptions. In comparison to the trails in Pampanga and Tarlac, the trails from the Botolan side involve longer distances through the lunar landscapes of the Bucao River, and lesser amenities.

name: Saint Monica Parish Church
description: Botolan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1736 with a triangular facade.

name: Tukal-Tukal Falls
description: A waterfall on the slopes of Mount Mangkirat.

name: Bancal Ecopark
description: An ecotourism park along the Bancal River featuring kayaking trips and tours of the mangroves at the nearby estuary.

name: Capayawan Beach
description: A stretch of beach used more often by local residents and tourists seeking budget-friendly options.

name: Ina Poonbato Shrine
description: A shrine dedicated to the venerated Marian image of Ina Poonbato (Mother Lord of the Rocks), a sculpture of the Virgin May discovered on a rock by Aeta villagers in the 1600s and relocated following the Pinatubo eruption in 1991. Its religious importance increased when the statue was found undamaged by lahar flows amid the ruins of its original location in the barangay of Poonbato.

name: Camp Kainomayan
description: The base camp for expeditions leading to Pinatubo. It also features recreational amenities such as a swimming pool, a zip line and wall climbing spots, in addition to a tourist information center from where packages to Pinatubo and related attractions can be negotiated.

name: Sundowners Beach Villas
description: A resort overlooking a gray sand beach with an infinity pool and individual swimming pools for some rooms.

name: Village Cafe
description: Juices, coffee, snacks, Filipino and Western-style dishes. Free WiFi. Charming little cafe serving good food.

name: Elizabeth Pension
price: air condition double with own bathroom 800.

name: Sunset Lodge
description: Fan single/double rooms with common bathroom. Overlooks the sea.

name: Benitta & Flora's Bistro Cafe
description: Known for its cozy, charming ambiance and budget friendly menu, it serves as a popular hangout for college students, families and travelers alike.

name: Baliwag Transit
description: Serves Hagonoy, Paombong, Malolos, and the municipalities along the Cagayan Valley Road, especially Baliwag, the bus company's namesake and headquarters.

name: German Espiritu Liner Bus Terminal
description: The only bus company servicing Bulakan. Trips from Divisoria (Manila) begin at 5:10AM and end at 9:30PM, while the return journey from Bulakan begins at 3:40AM until 7:30PM. Trips from Cubao (Quezon City) begin at 5:20AM and end at 10:30PM, while the return journey from Bulakan begins at 3:30AM until 8PM.

name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion
description: Bulakan's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present style in 1812. Unlike most colonial churches in the Philippines, which are Baroque, Romanesque or even Gothic, Bulakan Church is built in the neo-Byzantine style. At a side chapel to the right of the main doorway is an ecclesiastical museum.

name: Marcelo H. del Pilar Shrine
alt_name: NHCP Museo ni Marcelo H. del Pilar
description: A museum dedicated to Marcelo H. del Pilar, an anti-clerical activist who criticized the theocratic influence of Spanish Roman Catholic friars in the 19th century Philippines and advocated for equal rights for Filipinos under the Spanish Crown before shifting to outright independence in his last years. Built on the site of the del Pilar residence, it features a replica of a Spanish-era house that serves as exhibition space. In the spacious grounds of the complex are a monument to del Pilar and a mausoleum carrying his remains and that of other relatives. To avoid confusion with the small shrine to his nephew, Gregorio del Pilar, tricycle drivers refer to the museum as Marcelo.

name: Soc Rodrigo Residence
description: A colonial-era heritage house built in 1929 that was the ancestral home of Francisco "Soc" Rodrigo, a figure who took on multiple roles in Philippine social and political life such as playwright, journalist, author, politician and senator. While closed to the public, its iron-grilled fences allow for viewing of its surrounding gardens and the striped façade of its upper floors.

name: Ycasiano-Enriquez Ancestral House
description: A Spanish era bahay na bato built for the family of one of Bulakan's gobernadorcillo (mayor) in the 18th century.

name: General Gregorio del Pilar Birthplace
description: A small park and shrine built on the site of the house where General Gregorio del Pilar, a revolutionary commander who died aged 24 in a battle in Ilocos Sur against US forces during the Philippine-American War in 1899, was born. It has a statue of the boy-general and a flagpole. Wreathes are laid at the statue on November 14, his birthday and on December 2, the anniversary of his death.
directions: in front of Iglesia ni Cristo

name: Dakip
description: A Holy Week ritual memorializing the Way of the Cross. It features men in Biblical-era costumes reenacting the Passion of the Christ while walking for 15 km around the barangay for between 4 to 5 hours. Expect to see participants flagellating themselves or being beaten with palm leaves by spectators in commemoration of Jesus Christ's sufferings as part of their devotion and Lenten penance, although the Roman Catholic Church officially disapproves such acts of self-harm.

name: Puregold Bulakan
directions: in front of Bulakan Public Market

name: Majoh Chowmaster
description: Restaurant serving chao fan (Chinese fried rice) based meals.

name: Mahagnao Volcano National Park
description: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) classifies Mahagnao as Inactive volcano. Although the volcano has been inactive, it is classified as potentially active due to the active thermal features of the mountain.

name: Burgos Wind Farm
description: The largest wind farm in the Philippines. It is operated by the EDC Burgos Wind Power Corporation.

name: Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
description: A cultural heritage structure in Burgos established during Spanish colonial times. The lighthouse was first lit on March 30, 1892.

name: Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
description: Rock formations created by forces of the ocean on the rocky coast of Burgos, located just a few minutes from the lighthouse

name: Kaangrian Falls
description: A multi-tiered stair like formation with the water cascading on every step until it drops to a pool below.

name: Military Park Cape Bojeador
description: A small park in front of a military garrison that showcases some heavy weaponry and vehicles of the Philippine military
directions: in front of Camp Cape Bojeador

name: Bolikewkew Rice Terraces
description: A rice terrace complex on the slopes of the Cordilleras overlooking the rapids of the Bolikewkew River. Its name derives from the Ibaloi word for "spiral".

name: Libtong Lake
description: A lake with no known water source. While not fit for swimming due to its mud-colored waters, visitors can instead rent bamboo rafts for picnics.

name: Budahaw Falls
description: A 2-tier cascade with a 2-3 m deep basin along the boundary with Sablan in Benguet that is accessible following a 2-hour hike from downtown Burgos. Its name derives from the Ibaloi word for "shooting star", after a legend in which many of these meteors are said to land upon the falls.

name: Kananaskis Mountain Resort
description: A mountainside resort with swimming pools, flower gardens and accommodations.

name: Burgos Eco Park & Resort
description: Another mountainside resort with swimming pool and events venue.

name: Adawan Resort & Restaurant
description: A mountainside resort with swimming pool and restaurant overlooking a tributary of the Balili River.

name: Saint Isidore the Farmer Parish Church
description: Burgos' main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1876.

name: Cabongaoan Beach
description: Perhaps the most well-known beach in Burgos, Cabongaoan Beach is pleasantly sandy, with little to no rocks prickling visitors’ feet as they pad about. The beach is also known to have tidal pools both shallow and deep, and a viewpoint where visitors can enjoy the scenery of the coast. The so-called "Depth Pool" is a tidal pool on the rocky side of the beach gets filled with water when the waves crash against it. The sunsets in Burgos are especially and notably beautiful.

name: Nambalan Beach
description: Unlike most beaches where there are stretches and stretches of sand, Nambalan Beach also has grassy areas shaded by coconut trees where anyone could lay down blankets and enjoy the breeze and scenery before heading out to get a suntan. Visitors are also allowed to set up camp for free so that they could enjoy the stars come nighttime.

name: Sangbay Falls
description: It can be challenging for some to get there because of the 30-minute walk from the main road but the rewards at the other end are well worth the effort.

name: Coffee Hub
address: Stall no. 3, Luisa Commercial Building M. Ruiz St., Poblacion

name: White Beach Front and Cottages
description: Secluded beachfront accommodation. Free WiFi and breakfast.

name: Francisco B. Reyes Airport
description: serves the general area of Busuanga, you can fly into Busuanga with Cebu Pacific, or Philippines Airlines. The flight from Manila takes one hour. The trip from the airport to the town of Coron will take about 40 to 50 minutes.

name: Calauit Game Preserve and Wildlife Sanctuary
description: This reserve created by Presidential decree in 1976 houses various African species (giraffes included...) wandering in the wild.
directions: on the north side of Busuanga

name: Fishing
description: Fishing is very good. You can find lots of fish at there, for example tuna. Local men always go fishing there. You can buy simple equipment to fish there, where it is very cheap.

name: Ocam Ocam Beach
description: A beautiful beach with a little village and beach cottages to rent.
directions: follow the south coast highway to New-Busuanga and then turn left

name: Discovery Resort
description: Perhaps the only place near Coron where you will be free from the calls of roosters and karaoke. On Decanituan Island (Discovery Island) about a 10-minute boat ride from Coron. A little isolated and very beautiful.

name: Busuanga Island Paradise
description: A quiet resort located in a forest 10 minutes from Coron town. Private property of 21 hectares with a small river cutting through it - relaxing.

name: Puerto Del Sol Resort @ Discovery Dive Center
description: Located in Puerto Del Sol Bay, Coron, on the West Coast of Busuanga Island, Northern Palawan, Philippines. 2 minutes from the huge wreck of the Japanese tanker the "Okikawa Maru" at the entrance to our Bay, 5 minutes from the Japanese warship the "Akitsushima", and 8 minutes from the many other Historic Shipwrecks of the large Japanese Supply Fleet sunk in 1944. You may talk to Angelica at Discovery Bar (where the main office is) at Coron Town or give her a call through +63 9209012414 and she will help you to get into the resort.

name: Bancasi Airport
description: Flights from Manila (one hour) or Cebu (45 minutes), either by Cebu Pacific or PAL Express. Ground transportation: Taxis are available outside the landside security gate. Alternatively, you can walk into the highway to catch a bus or a multicab to downtown.

name: 2GO Travel
description: Ferries depart from Manila, with a stop at Cebu.

name: Cokaliong Shipping Lines
description: Services from Cebu City

name: Lite Ferries
description: Operates the Jagna-Nasipit route

name: Trans-Asia Shipping Lines
description: One ferry departs from Cebu City.

name: Butuan City Integrated Transport Terminal
description: There are three terminals: one for buses and another for jeepneys. Each of them is within walking distance from each other.

name: Robinsons Butuan Bus Terminal
description: Bachelor Express, Philtranco and Davao Metro Shuttle buses headed for or coming from CDO and Davao City, use this better but simple bus station over the older and crowded central bus station. UV Express minibuses and vans also use this terminal as of 2022.
directions: Behind Robinsons Place Butuan. To downtown, catch a jeepney from the mall.

name: Balangay Shrine Museum
description: Graveyard of the Balangay 1 dated 320 AD. This wooden plank-build and edge-pegged boats measured an average of 15 meters in length and 3 meters wide across the beam. Nine balangays have already been discovered in Ambangan, Libertad sites. Three have been excavated and others are still in situ.

name: Butuan Regional Museum
description: This museum is the repository of historical and cultural materials and artifacts that proves Butuan's prehistoric existence and rich cultural heritage. There are two exhibit galleries. The Archaeological Hall and Ethnological Hall specimens of stone crafts, metal crafts, woodcrafts, potteries, goldsmith, burial coffins, and other archaeological diggings are exhibited. At the Ethnological Hall are exhibits of contemporary cultural materials the Butuanon or every Filipino for matter used for a living.

name: Bood Promontory 1st Easter Mass Eco Park
description: This historic site is where Magellan and his men erected a cross and celebrated the 1st Mass on Philippine Soil on March 31, 1521. It is the highest elevation and promontory overlooking the whole of Butuan bay then. Today, the indigenous “Hadlayati Tree” still abound lording over a Clonal nursery and tree park, and the serpentine Masao River (El Rio de Butuan) amidst fishponds and archaeological treasures.

name: Banza Church Ruins
description: This site was one of the old poblacion of the city. The church built here in 1625 by the Recollect Friars was reduced to ashes in 1753 by Moro pirates. What remains of this church is its bell tower banyan (balete) trees. Now enveloped by as the most beautiful church in the region before its destruction. Today, it is the oldest ruin of a stone church in the entire island of Mindanao.

name: Magellan's Landing Site
description: Every year on March 31, the city celebrates Mazaua Discovery Day to commemorate a historic milestone, the 1st Easter Mass on Philippines' soil on 1521, celebrated by Ferdinand Magellan. No matter what, Butuanons proclaim with pride that such historic event took place in Butuan, not in Limasawa.

name: St. Joseph Cathedral
description: This is like an iconic landmark for Butuan, even though there are Catholic churches everywhere in the Philippines. Also there's the opportunity to see the Filipino flag flying from a tall mast in Guingona Park across the way.

name: Delta Discovery Park
description: Zip-line course through the tropical hills and swimming pool.

name: Flavored otap
description: Buy flavored otap (a Filipino delicacy) with flavors Durian and Ube.

name: Balangay souvenirs
description: Models of Balangay (an ancient boat used by first native Filipinos) are particularly popular as souvenirs.

name: Gaisano Mall
description: Has a McDonald's, a Jollibee and a Pizza Hut.

name: SM City Butuan
description: mall with a supermarket

name: BPI
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: RIBBS
description: Their specialty are ribs BBQ & seafoods

name: Almont Inland Hotel/Resort
description: Nice breakfast; nice pool.

name: Balanghai Hotel and Convention Center
description: Has a big circular pool with a waterslide.

name: Hotel Karaga
description: Good location downtown, clean. Air conditioned room with hot shower.

name: Hensonly Plaza Inn
description: Only fan rooms with outside bathrooms.

name: Imperial Hotel
description: Fan rooms with own bathroom. A/C rooms with own bathrooms. hot water and cable TV.

name: Albecks Inn
description: A/C room with outside bathroom.

name: Julians Inn Annex
description: Fan room with outside bathroom, cable TV and free Wi-Fi.

name: Mejestic Pension
description: A/C single double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Uccp Guest house.
description: Fan dorm beds.

name: Jets Inn
description: A/C single or double rooms with bathrooms.

name: Flor-al-Mansion
description: A/C double room with own bathroom. 40-inch cable TV. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Watergate Hotel Butuan
description: Has a chic designer-type pool you can dip your toes in but not much else. Limited free breakfast and wifi.

name: Almont City Hotel
description: Restaurant/bar, free breakfast, a/c, wifi, airport shuttle.
directions: In center of town, across from cathedral and Guingona Park

name: Grand Palace Hotel
description: Establishment and pool are pretty basic. Has restaurant.

name: Go Hotels Butuan
description: This branch is the first Go Hotels property to open in Mindanao. Go Hotels Butuan is located only 11 minutes away from Butuan's Bancasi Airport.
address: J C Aquino Ave, Butuan City, 8600 Agusan Del Norte

name: Cabagan Square Park
description: Houses the largest carousel in the Philippines

name: Tulap Falls
description: Newly discovered waterfall, but access is still hard.
directions: From Maharlika Highway, enter the junction at Barangay Balasig leading to Masipi East. From Masipi East, a trail leads to the falls

name: Biwag Shrine
description: A makeshift shrine featuring a tacky statue of Biwag, a folklorical giant. Offerings of gin and cigarettes are commonly left at the shrine, while a celebration is also held to commemorate Biwag on the feast day of Barangay Tallag, also known alternately as Biwag, every May 6.

name: Malasi Lake Sanctuary
description: A sanctuary for the endangered Philippine Duck, it is a 178 ha preserve centered around a pair of lakes.

name: Horno
description: The ruins of a towering structure that used to be an oven (horno) for making bricks during construction of the parish church during the Spanish era, which was not completed due to the Philippine Revolution. The present church is of a later 20th century construct.
directions: Enter the school compound and walk towards the back section. The structure is obscured by trees

name: Cabagan-Santa Maria Bridge
description: A multi-arched bridge that took nearly 10 years to build, only to collapse a month after its opening in 2025. After repairs, it reopened a year later to light vehicles. Despite this, the structure retains its imposing look and provides great views over the Cagayan River. Is it visible as far away as San Pablo, more than 10 km away.
address: Cabagan-Santa Maria Road, Barangay Casibarag Norte

name: San Pablo Church
alt_name: St. Paul the Apostle Parish Church, San Pablo Church Ruins
description: The oldest church in Isabela, built in a Baroque style during the 17th century. Its belfry looms above the town center and is visible as far away as Cabagan.

name: Cabagan Triangle Park
description: A small park in the middle of a road junction. It features a clock tower using LED screens and a statue of a horse-drawn carriage (calesa), a monument to Cabagan being one of the few places in the country to retain this mode of transport.
directions: in front of Iglesia ni Cristo

name: Tupa
description: A stretch of rapids at the point where the Pinacanauan River leaves the Sierra Madre that is a favorite swimming spot for locals.

name: Cabagan Museum
description: A one-room exhibition space on local history and culture, set inside the upper floor of the former municipal hall.
address: Aggabao Hall, Cabagan-Santa Maria Road, Barangay Centro

name: Cabagan Science Elementary School
description: The administrative building of the town's main primary school is an American-era bungalow (commonly known as the Gabaldon) dating from the early 1900s.

name: Balai Rosalinda Resort
description: A recreational venue with swimming pool, accommodations, and karaoke in the town center.

name: Round Rock Resort
description: A recreational venue with swimming pool and karaoke near Cansan junction. For those who are not squeamish, a cockfighting arena opened a few meters away in 2026.
directions: at the back of the CENRO building

name: Josefina T. Albano Sports and Cultural Complex
description: Said to be the largest municipal arena in Cagayan Valley at the time of inauguration, this hosted travelling matches of the Philippine Basketball Association in the 2000s. It now hosts barangay level leagues and pageants, while during vacant times, residents just play basketball in the court.

name: Kalesa, Kabayu, Kalaseru Festival
description: Cabagan celebrates its patronal fiesta in honor of Saint Paul the Apostle on January 25. Starting January 15, a variety of events are held to celebrate the town's culture, including its pancit and especially the kalesas, hence the names Kalesa (cart), Kabayu (horse) and Kalaseru (coachman).

name: Baka Festival
description: San Pablo's patronal fiesta is held on January 15 and celebrates the town's agrarian tradition, particularly the raising of cows. Highlights include rodeo and motorbike competitions.

name: Xentro Mall
description: Has a Savemore grocery and a BDO bank branch with ATM.

name: Cabagan Public Market
description: Has a gift shop (OTOP Hub) run by the municipal government selling local delicacies and handicrafts. Market day on Sundays, when there are more merchandise to be bought than usual.

name: GM's Food House
description: A restaurant serving Chinese-Filipino dishes. Also does bulk orders.

name: Aling Kikay's Panciteria
description: The oldest surviving panciteria in Cabagan, founded by a descendant of a Chinese immigrant who invented pancit Cabagan during the American period. Aling Kikay's children also run adjacent panciterias.
directions: in front of Milagros District Hospital

name: Mariloi's
description: Panciteria serving pancit Cabagan. Due to its popularity, an extension with more seating and menu items, along with a gift shop selling foodstuffs was opened a few meters down the highway.

name: Urban Cafe + Kitchen
description: A chicken wings and pork ribs restaurant offering meals paired with rice as well as pancit Cabagan. Group-sized platters are also available.

name: Alfresco Pizzeria and Bistro
description: A rooftop Italian restobar serving pizza and pasta. Has live music on weekends.

name: El Bistro
description: A restaurant serving Filipino and some Western cuisine.

name: The Hood
description: A restaurant set up in the yard of a private residence that also serves fried rice meals.

name: Hot Plate Steakhouse
description: A grill house with live music on weekends.
address: Alfonso Binag Street, Purok 2, Barangay Anao

name: Sy Bakery
description: A bakery and food store run by the same Filipino-Chinese family since the 1950s, as evidenced by the interior displays and the old wood-fired oven used to make their breads. Among the highlights are the tasty bread (slang for loaf bread), pan de coco (buns filled with coconut jam) and egg (custard) pie.

name: Pin-tag Restobar
description: A restaurant serving fried rice meals with meat, also fried.

name: Rollan's
alt_name: Don Francisco Albano corner Antonio Luna Streets, Centro
description: A snackbar known in town for its halo-halo and empanadas.

name: Apayao Brew
description: A coffeeshop that also serves a favorite hanging-out spot for residents.

name: Cafe Eggspresso
description: A cafe that also serves Korean egg drop sandwiches.
directions: in front of Milagros District Hospital

name: Four J's Hotel and Inn
description: Each room has a carport, but the place may be infested with flies due to a nearby chicken farm.
directions: near the junction leading to Barangay Angancasilian

name: Super 5R Hotel and Resort
description: Accommodation with swimming pool and 12 rooms.

name: Josefina Resort and Hotel
description: The largest hotel and resort complex in Cabagan, with 17 standard and 6 drive-in rooms, as well as two adult-size swimming pools and four others for children.

name: Big Brother Drive-in Hotel
description: A motel accommodation near the main highway, with six standard rooms and four motel-types.

name: Cabanatuan City Central Transport Terminal
description: There are food stalls, a restroom and convenience stores (7-Eleven and Alfamart). There are transfers to UV Express and jeepneys. Beware of scammers who will bring your baggage and lead you to overpriced shops.

name: Camp Pangatian
description: A former American military camp turned into a Japanese concentration camp for American and Filipino prisoners of war, it was known for the raid at Cabanatuan, one of the largest military operations of World War II in the Pacific. The camp has been turned into a memorial for the prisoners of war detained here, and is also part of itineraries for American war veterans.

name: Plaza Lucero
description: A little plaza built on where Antonio Luna, a Filipino general during the Philippine-American War, was assassinated. A statue of Luna in horseback is erected on the spot where he was killed.
address: Rizal Street and Del Pilar Streets, Nabao

name: Nueva Ecija Old Provincial Capitol
description: A neoclassical capitol building designed by the American architect and urban planner E. William Parsons. It used to house the government offices of the Nueva Ecija provincial government until it was relocated to the new capital at Palayan.

name: Cabanatuan Cathedral
alt_name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentine Parish Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in central and southern Nueva Ecija, built in its present form following a major fire in the 1970s. Its convent was where General Antonio Luna and his aide were assassinated in 1899.

name: WalterMart Cabanatuan
description: Shopping mall and supermarket.

name: N E Pacific Mall
description: Shopping mall.

name: Robinsons Townville Cabanatuan & Robinsons Supermarket
address: KM #111, Brgy. H. Concepcion, Pan-Philippine Hwy

name: SM City Cabanatuan
address: Maharlika Highway, Hermogenes C. Concepcion Sr

name: S&R Membership Shopping - Cabanatuan
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.

name: Cabanatuan City Public Market
description: Very big public market with stores selling meat, fruits, vegetables and dry goods. The famous Longanisa of Cabanatuan is available inside.

name: Robinsons Easymart Bangad
address: Nueva Ecija-Aurora Road, Purok Fortaleza, Bangad

name: Robinsons Easymart Kapitan Pepe
address: M. de Leon Avenue, Kapitan Pepe Subdivision

name: Kinnobuta Ramen House - IEKEI Ramen
description: If you want to eat an authentic Japanese cuisine, this is the best place to go!
address: 31 General Tinio Street Extension, corner St Joseph Avenue

name: KC's Grill & Restobar
description: The ambience is relaxing, and the service is good. The ihaw ihaw food is delicious.

name: Kuys' Avenue - Snack Bar and Sizzling House
Kumpares Cabanatuan-Mabini St.
description: Filipino eatery.

name: Vicenticos
description: Great Filipino food showcasing the best of Cabanatuan. Food is authentic. It tastes as if it has been prepared the way that your lola would prepare it.

name: Hola Cabanatuan
description: Cheezebread, pasta, salads, milk & fruit shakes.
address: Nambawan Building, M. De Leon Avenue, Kapt. Pepe Subdivision

name: Kamayan Food Park Main Branch
description: Authentic Filipino foods. The restaurant is completely outdoors and good for large groups and boodle fights. Also serving hot coffee, iced coffee, and milk shakes.
address: between 19th and General Tinio Street Extension

name: Yolky Toasty by Berean's-Cabanatuan
description: Korean sandwiches, salads, Japanese rice dishes.
address: St Joseph avenue, corner Santander, Kapitan Pepe

name: Annapoorna
description: An Indian restaurant serving dishes from both the north and south of the country. Has vegetarian-friendly options. All their fish dishes use cream dory.
address: Maharlika Highway, Hermogenes C. Concepcion Sr

name: N.Y.O.R.K. Café
description: Good food and coffee drinks.
address: M. De Leon Avenue corner General Tinio Avenue Extension

name: Tomo's Bar and Restaurant
description: Amazing place with wide variety of food and drink choices of excellent quality.
address: General Tinio Street Extension, Kapitan Pepe

name: Ben and Jessa
description: Bakes & coffee.

name: 33rd Bottle Shop
address: 33rd Street corner General Tino Street Extension

name: CCLAND Cafe (World of Sweets)
description: Pasta, iced coffee.

name: Hotel Sogo - Cabanatuan
description: A good deal is the ₱300 rooms from 8PM till 6AM.
directions: not far from the new SM mall and Robinsons

name: Microtel by Wyndham Cabanatuan
description: The only international brand of hotel in Cabanatuan. Well-maintained and comfortable rooms.

name: Harvest Hotel-Cabanatuan City
description: A 4-minute walk form the nearest bus station, this informal hotel is a 7-minute walk from Freedom Park and a 12 minutes on foot from the Antonio Luna Death Place Marker.

name: Top Star Hotel Cabanatuan
address: PCG Building, KM 114 Maharlika Highway, Brgy. H. Concepcion,

name: Acropolis North Water Camp & Country Club
Mount Mariglem
description: A 573 m peak involving a 2- to 3-hour climb through exposed terrain with the only vegetation being grass, not the best option during the summer heat from March to May. Most climbs involve a descent afterwards to the Maligha and Agbobotilya Rivers to cool off.
hours: Registration required at Cabangan Tourism Office, and a maximum of 150 climbers are allowed daily. Reservations only Sat Sun, walk-ins open Mon-Fri

name: Cabangan Beach
description: Cabangan's beachfront stretches through eight barangays along the South China Sea and consists of grayish sand. However, the strong waves make the beach more ideal for surfing than long-range swimming.

name: Dapya River
description: A stretch of clear waters included in hiking itineraries for Mount Mariglem.

name: Agbobotilya River
description: A stretch of clear waters included in hiking itineraries for Mount Mariglem, featuring water-sculpted cliffs and natural pools.

name: Cabangan Pier
description: A privately-built pier that was built to host barges extracting sand from Cabangan. It is also used by residents as a recreational and boating area at the estuary of the Bangan River.

name: Cabangan Public Market
description: Market days on Tuesdays and Fridays, when there are more merchandise to be bought than usual.

name: Bonita's Kitchen
description: A restaurant serving Filipino dishes. Their main draw is the bulalo (beef soup with bone marrow).

name: 1st Streat Snack Bar
description: Serves varied dishes such as sandwiches, burgers and seafood. Offers takeaway platters for those trying to buy picnic meals to the beach.

name: Arya's Chill and Grill
description: A restaurant serving Middle Eastern cuisine.

name: Mami Madz
description: A small place serving goto (rice porridge with tripe) and mami (chicken noodle soup) near Cabangan Beach.

name: Woods Pizza
description: Serves hand-kneaded dough and locally-sourced toppings.

name: You-Han's K-Bap Restaurant
description: Restaurant serving Korean cuisine.

name: Casa Baraka
description: Restaurant serving Filipino comfort food. Also hosts live bands on some occasions.

name: 21st Bean Cafe
description: Coffee with pastas and Mexican snacks.

name: Villa Mi Amor Resort And Hotel
Club Monet Beachfront Resort by Cocotel
Susong Dalaga
description: Translated as "Maiden's Breasts" because of their appearance, they are a pair of forested limestone hills with a height of 182 m separated by a creek. It also has a cave that is accessible following a hike along a 275-step trail.

name: Quirino Province Museum and Library
description: A museum on provincial history and culture.
directions: inside the provincial capitol compound and beside Quirino Capitol Peoples Mart

name: Quirino Watersports Complex
description: A multilevel recreational complex featuring facilities for watersports, overnight accommodation and large-scale events.

name: Ginnamuluan Festival
description: The town's patronal festival, also celebrating its heritage and culture.

name: Panfe
description: Japanese restaurant

name: Tea Empire
description: Taiwanese restaurant with milk tea.

name: Quirino Watersports Complex
description: Has hostel and villa options.

name: Salomague Port
description: A maritime transport hub on Salomague Harbor that has been redeveloped and expanded to enable cruise ships to dock as part of efforts to attract foreign tourists to the Ilocos Region.

name: Saint Mark the Evangelist Parish Church
description: Cabugao's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style.

name: Pug-os Beach
description: A white-sand cove that is also used as a production center for sea salt.

name: Poro Island
description: A secluded, uninhabited island with white sand beaches.
directions: rent a boat at Sabang Pier

name: Sabang Coral Baywalk
description: A seaside promenade facing Poro Island.

name: Rebba Falls
description: A set of rapids at the point where the Cabugao River exits the Cordillera Mountains into the coastal plain.

name: St. Polycarp Parish Church
description: The city's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 18th century and restored in the 2020s. A few 19th-century bells are displayed at the side, while in front, a memorial commemorates the 35 people killed at the churchyard during an agrarian revolt known as the Sakdalista Uprising in 1935.
address: P. Burgos Street, Barangay Poblacion Uno
directions: Beside Cabuyao Town Plaza. Side entrance: Manuel Quezon Street

name: Diocesan Shrine of San Vicente Ferrer
description: The city's second Roman Catholic church, containing a revered image of Saint Vincent Ferrer.

name: La Serena
description: Restaurant with Western fare.

name: Laguindingan Airport
directions: in Barangay Moog, in the municipality of Laguindingan, 46 km west of Cagayan de Oro and 61 km east of Iligan

name: Cokaliong Shipping lines
description: Ferry from Cebu City three times a week (Sa Tu Th) leaving at 7PM, arriving at 5:30AM.

name: Bachelor Express
description: Operates bus services from Balingoan port (for ferry services to Camiguin), Gingoog, Butuan, and Surigao.

name: Philtranco
description: Operates bus services from Manila via Butuan, Surigao, Tacloban, and Legazpi City.

name: Rural Transit
description: Operates bus services from Bukidnon, Davao, Koronadal, General Santos, Iligan (via the airport), Ozamiz, Oroquieta, Dipolog, Pagadian, and Zamboanga City.

name: Super 5 Transport
description: Operates bus services from Balingoan port (for ferry services to Camiguin), Bukidnon, and Iligan via the airport.

name: Eastbound Integrated Bus Terminal
description: The busier and more congested of the two, this is where buses bound for destinations north, south or east of CDO serve. These include buses to Butuan, Surigao, Manila, Bukidnon, Davao, Koronadal, and General Santos. There are also a few (mid/expensive) hotels nearby. You can take jeepneys labelled R2 to Divisoria for ₱8.

name: Westbound Integrated Bus Terminal
description: Buses bound for destinations west of CDO, like Iligan, Ozamiz and Zamboanga serve this.
directions: near the BIR office and the Bulua Fish Markets

name: Saint Augustine Metropolitan Cathedral
description: A Gothic-inspired cathedral and is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Cagayan de Oro, since it houses the cathedra (seat) of the Archbishop of Cagayan de Oro. The present-day cathedral was constructed in 1946, after being destroyed during World War II. Inside the cathedral are centuries-old stained glass windows, while outside its main entrance is a wooden cross from 1888, erected by Augustinian Recollect missionaries.

name: Archdiocesan Shrine of the Black Nazarene
description: A shrine dedicated to the Black Nazarene located in the heart of the city. The Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene in Quiapo Church decided to move the replica statue of the Black Nazarene to Nazareno Parish Church, so that Nazarene devotees from Mindanao do not have to travel to Manila for their annual pilgrimage.
directions: next to Gaisano City Mall and across from Centrio Mall

name: Santuario Eucaristico
description: Formerly the Archdiocesan Shrine of the Holy Eucharist, Santuario Eucaristico is a shrine dedicated to St. Peter Julian Eymard, Apostle of the Eucharist. Along the rear, semi-circular wall of the shrine are intricately-designed Mosaic Stations of the Cross, while above the secondary entrances/exits are stained glass windows depicting the Stations of the Eucharist. These stained glass windows are based on the Stations of the Holy Eucharist at the Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament in Hanceville, Alabama. They are the only one of their kind in the Philippines.

name: Carmelite Church
description: The area surrounding the monastery is also the residence of several religious orders, including the Discalced Carmelites, as well as the St. John Vianney Theological Seminary. Carmelite Church contains an image of the Santo Niño, or Holy Child which is said to be miraculous.

name: Divine Mercy Shrine
alt_name: Archdiocesan Shrine of the Divine Mercy
description: Its focal point is a statue of Jesus as the Divine Mercy overlooking Macajalar Bay. The site attracts many pilgrims every Divine Mercy Sunday, one week after Easter Sunday, as well as during solemnities and other feast days throughout the year.
address: Divine Mercy Hills, PSB-Ulaliman, El Salvador City

name: Gaston Park
