description: Fan rooms with cable TV.

name: GV Hotel
description: A/C single and double rooms all with own bathrooms and cable TV. The GV Hotel in Dipolog has 58 rooms.

name: Green Mellow Court
description: Fan rooms with own bathrooms. A/C rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Bamboo Garden Business Inn
description: A/C double room with outside bathroom. A/C double with own bathroom and cable TV.
address: 26 Burgos Street corner Bonifacio Street, Central

name: Eustacia's Pension House
description: Fan double room with outside bathroom. A/C single with own bathroom and cable TV. A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: CHIP'N By d' Sea Resort
description: Fan, A/C rooms with own bathroom and cable TV. Free breakfast.

name: FSA Traders Inn 2
description: A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV, free Wi-Fi.
address: 5th Floor Felicidad 1 Building, Quezon Avenue, Miputak

name: Antonio's Pension House
description: A/C double room with own bathroom, cable TV, free Wi-Fi.
address: General Luna Street corner Martinez Street, Barangay Central

name: Hapytelle Hotel
description: Free Wi-Fi, child-friendly, air conditioned rooms.
address: Magsaysay Street corner Malvar Street, Miputak

name: Meaco Royal Hotel - Dipolog
description: Free Wi-Fi, free parking, air-conditioned rooms, child-friendly.
address: Rizal Avenue corner Martinez Street, Central
directions: near Dipolog Boulevard, blocks away from the Santa Cruz marker

name: Mibang Hotel
description: Offers air-conditioned rooms, hot & cold showers, cable TV, room service, PABX telephone system, swimming pool and poolside bar, Wi-Fi zone, function halls, hotel van service, and complimentary bottled water.

name: Royal Farm Resort
directions: behind the NFA Zamboanga del Norte bodega

name: Top Plaza Hotel
description: Offers fully air-conditioned rooms, PABX telephone system, cable TV, hot & cold shower, Wi-Fi zone, function halls, and hotel transport service.
address: Quezon Avenue corner Echavez Street, Central

name: D'Hotel & Suites
address: Rizal Avenue corner Osmeña Street, Central

name: Gwandalan House Bed and Breakfast
description: Offers concierge service, complimentary Wi-Fi and bottled water, pick-up from Dipolog Airport, fine art collection, 24/7 CCTV security surveillance, and coffee.

name: Parish and National Shrine of Our Lady of Sorrows
description: The main Roman Catholic church in Dolores.

name: Bangkong Kahoy Valley
description: A secluded, forested valley between Mounts Banahaw and San Cristobal that is home to campsites, natural springs and other attractions deemed holy by Banahaw pilgrims.

name: Lake Gunao
description: A volcanic crater lake near the Tiaong-Dolores Road west of downtown Dolores. It was formed as part of the Laguna Volcanic Field and is an extension of the more famous Seven Lakes of neighboring San Pablo, but is less visited and has fewer tourist infrastructures.

name: Mount San Cristobal
description: A towering 1470 m inactive volcano along the boundary with Laguna. Situated alongside Mount Banahaw, a religious pilgrimage site, it is said to be the mountain's "evil twin", having been dubbed the "Devil's Mountain" for malevolent entities said to inhabit its slopes.

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people.

name: Whale Shark Interaction
description: Swimming with whale sharks. Register at the Visitor's Center located at Barangay Dancalan. Shark watchers are assigned a Butanding Interaction Officer and have to follow strict guidelines. All whale shark tour boats are provided by the center inclusive of an interaction guide called a Butanding Interaction Officer or BIO. Some resorts can do pre-booking for a minimal service fee. Price is ₱300 (₱100 for Filipinos and local residents with ACR card) for the registration (valid for 5 days), and ₱3500 per boat (up to 6 people). There is no guarantee of seeing a whale shark the chance of seeing them have now (March 2018) become almost zero. Boat operators will take you out even if no Butanding have been sighted for weeks and they will not tell you of this beforehand. No refunds or credits. Avoiding weekends and booking multiple days increases your chances of success.

name: Frontier Whale Shark Tours
description: Leads guided whale shark tours every year from February to May with experienced naturalists as guides. The guides enter the water with the group and are experts at maintaining a safe approach to the sharks. Tours start in Manila and include domestic flights, all transfers, resort accommodation and full meals.

name: Bicol Dive Center
description: Dive center is just across from the tourist center. Offers dive course & day trips to San Miguel Island and Manta Bowl, island hopping and snorkeling, the price is ₱4500 for 3 dives (minimum of 4 divers)and give special rates for big groups. Gear is in good condition, the boat is spacious and the people are really friendly. Accepts cash payments only. Dive shop is open year round.

name: Frontier Scuba
description: Leads guided whale shark tours every year from February to May with experienced naturalists as guides. Tours start in Manila and include domestic flights, resort accommodation and meals.

name: Giddy's Place PADI Dive Resort
description: Open year round. It is the only PADI accredited facility in Donsol and the only one with Philippine Commission on Sports Scuba Diving (PCSSD) accreditation. Has the only dive training pool in Donsol and the surrounding towns. Has Donsol's only resident dive instructor and has Grade A Air. Has the lowest rate for the solo diver. Accepts credit cards (Visa, MC, Amex, JCB) without surcharge.

name: D'Spa
description: The only full service spa in Donsol and the surrounding towns and is attached to Giddy's Place. You have a lot of options including scrubs, body, foot and stone massages.

name: ATMs
description: There are two ATMs in Donsol which take Master Card and Visa Card.

name: Butanding Bar & Restaurant
description: Popular for its icy cold beer, mixed drinks, good food and seafood, good music and well-stocked bar and separate video karaoke area. One of the few places to eat past early dinner time. Free WiFi. Try the local dish "Crispy Pata" or deep fried pork leg which is a Philippine specialty. Accepts credit cards.

name: Sadtong Panawn Restaurant
description: 500 m after the Visitor Center going east, houses few antique collections, including an old piano, pre-World War II bicycle and chair, 300-year-old vases, antique televisions and so on. The restaurant serves fresh seafoods like squid sisig and grilled squid in sweet sauce. and before leaving Donsol, try their signature flaming chicken inasal. The restaurant has free WiFi and has shows and events every Friday, Saturday and Sunday featuring Bettina Bexina and company.

name: BARacuda
description: The owner, Juliet, goes fishing in the day to offer you fresh fish at night. You can choose your own fish from the day's catch and they will cook it for you. They also serve cocktails. The bar is alongside the beach on a terrace, overlooking the sea. Really friendly place, Juliet will come and chat with you if you are alone. She also tends to bring rum at the end of dinner, for free. The prices are quite high, especially for Philippine standards.
directions: 500m after the Visitor center going west

name: AGM Beachfront Resort Restaurant
description: Serves freshly caught fish, crabs, shrimps and other seafood, and also meat and fresh vegetables sourced from nearby farms. Chinese, Filipino, and Continental foods are available for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

name: Amor Farm Beach Resort
description: The restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner with both Western and Filipino food. At dinner time ask what fish arrived that day as fishermen arrive daily in their boats to sell their catch directly to the restaurant. They will cook it any way you like. They also have a bar and a great atmosphere.

name: Amor Farm Beach Resort
description: Amor Farm Beach Resort has a nicely landscaped garden and is on the beach. There is a good restaurant serving both local and Western menus. Along the beach there are plenty of nice places to have a drink - on the beach, in one of the many gazebos, or at the beach bar. It is walking distance from the outstanding visitor's center.
price: Air-conditioned rooms (king-size bed, en suite toilet and bath) - ₱1500. Fan room (1 single bed and 1 double bed, en-suite toilet and bath) - ₱1000.

name: Hernandez Guest House
description: In the downtown, this is a budget option with basic rooms (shared bath and toilet) close to a busy street. You can get to the Visitors' Center in 5 minutes/₱15 per head tricycle ride.

name: Vitton & Woodland Resort
description: Room rates ₱2000-3200, all rooms are air-conditioned with individual bathrooms and hot shower. They have 2 restaurants inside: Mommy Nems Resto & Vitton Cafe, wide swimming pool, Dive Center (Bicol Dive Center). They offer kayak tours, firefly watching, and van transfer. Directly next to the Butanding center. Considered to be the nearest place to stay in the area near the jump-off point for whale shark interaction. As of March 2018 they seem to have a serious problem with bruised and sick street dogs roaming around the resort and especially in the restaurant area, begging for food. Bear this in mind if you have reservations about personal hygiene and safety.

name: Casabianca Resort
description: Beachside resort with restaurant inside that serves fresh seafood, and an array of local and international dishes. Has Wi-Fi. 5-10 min walking distance to the tourist center.

name: Elysia Beach Resort
description: They have a swimming pool with wooden deck and an international restaurant and cocktail bar, coffee shop (espresso and brewed coffee). Also you can use beach bed. All the rooms have a beach view.
directions: 5 minutes walk from the visitor center going west, at the beach front

name: Victoria's Guest House
description: The place is accessible by the local road on the left side of the TOP (Tourist-Oriented Police) Cop Police Station, 15 minutes' walk to the Butanding Interaction Office. They have private ecological beach cottages being shared with small group of travellers who prefer a quiet place in a rural setting. En suite bathrooms with hot shower. The small kitchen offers fresh sea foods and vegetables. Firefly watching nearby.

name: Santiago Homestay
description: Fan double room shared bathroom.
address: Corner of SanJose street & Tres Marias Dr

name: Giddys Place Homestay
description: Backpackers' fan double rooms with shared bathroom.

name: Angat Watershed Forest Reserve
description: A popular birdwatching site and a biodiversity hotspot containing most of the remaining closed-canopy forests in Central Luzon. The site also covers parts of the city of San Jose del Monte, and the towns of Norzagaray, Angat, San Rafael, and San Miguel, as well as parts of Rizal, Quezon, Aurora and Nueva Ecija provinces.

name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
description: A sprawling 2117 ha national park that also covers parts of the neighboring towns of San Miguel and San Ildefonso. Famous as the site of the Biak-na-Bato Republic, a proto-state founded by Filipino separatists during the Philippine Revolution against Spain in 1897, it also contains caves, rivers and forested highlands of the Sierra Madre that belie the misconception of Bulacan as a largely flat province.

name: 13 Falls
description: A segment of rapids with 13 cascades deep in the forests of DRT. Within the complex is the Candle Monument, a memorial to the guerrillas who set up a base in the area while fighting Japanese forces during World War II.

name: Mount Brigino
description: A mountain with campsite offering views reaching up to the neighboring provinces of Pampanga, Nueva Ecija and even Metro Manila.

name: Mount Manalmon
description: A 196 m peak that is popular among hikers in Biak-na-Bato National Park. It also contains Madlum Cave and forms one side of a gorge along the Madlum River that is also shared with Mount Gola, another popular hiking destination. The area is also claimed by the municipality of San Miguel.

name: Kabayunan Viewdeck
description: A highland observation point with campgrounds.

name: Tila Pilon Hills
description: A series of grass-covered hills that are nicknamed the "Chocolate Hills of Bulacan" after its resemblance to the original in Bohol.

name: Balistada Hills
description: A 328 m sequence of highlands that offers views of surrounding peaks such as Mounts Pinagbanderahan (named because Japanese soldiers and guerrillas kept contesting who could plant their respective flags at its summit during World War II), Susong Dalaga (literally "Maiden's Breast" in Tagalog), and Mabio. Treks to Balistada are often combined with climbs to any of the three mountains.

name: Talon ni Eva
description: Translated as "Eva's Waterfall" in Tagalog, although some locals will say Eva is actually the nickname of a man named Evaristo. It is a 30 m cascade at the foot of Mount Sumacbao accessible by hiking through a 4 km trail.

name: Verdivia Falls
description: A secluded cascade that is accessible through a 3 km hike.

name: Digo's Hills
description: A series of hills with a panoramic viewdeck.

name: Talon Pari Falls
description: A cascade that translates to "Priest's Waterfall".

name: Puning Cave
description: A cave with chambers of varying sizes. Its interior is also a pathway for the Puning River.

name: Talon ni Lukab at Pedro
description: A pair of waterfalls.

name: Secret Falls Resort
description: An ecotourism venue built around a natural waterfall.

name: Antonio's Nature Park
description: A resort complex built around the Mandala Waterfalls.

name: Sibulan Airport
description: The airport is in Sibulan, the next town to the north, but is not far from Dumaguete city center (3 km). It has a runway that in many countries would be considered too short for medium sized civilian jet aircraft, but both Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines fly in and out with Airbus and Boeing jets daily. Most jets take off toward the sea, where the runway ends abruptly at the salt water of the Tañon Strait/Bohol Sea, so both takeoffs and landings are thrilling affairs.For ground transportation there is a sign on the terminal building stating fixed rates. As of mid-2020 cost to city center was ₱100 by tricycle, ₱300 by van. To return to the airport, tricycles will quote ₱100-150. Jeepneys go between the highway next to the airport and Dumaguete Public Market downtown for ₱8 either way, but you have to walk a few hundred meters from the terminal to the highway.

name: Dumaguete Port
description: All the direct-to-Dumaguete ferries arrive and depart here, though other ferries run from southern parts of Cebu Island to Sibulan. Most of the traffic is ferries, though there are some small-to-midsize freighters and container ships. There are no cruise ships and the local fishing boats anchor elsewhere. There may be a few private small cruising vessels, but Tambobo Bay to the south is the main port for those on Negros.

name: Ocean Jet
description: Fast hydrofoil ferries to and from Cebu via Tagbilaran on Bohol. From Dumaguete, departs 7:30AM (arrives 11:10AM) and 2:20PM (arrives 7:20PM).

name: 2Go
description: larger than most other ferries. They have one Manila-Dumaguete departure a week leaving Manila Sunday evening, arriving Tuesday morning, and leaving Wednesday for the return voyage. They also have a ferry from Dumaguete to Zamboanga via Dipolog.

name: Cokaliong Shipping Lines
description: Daily from Cebu City (7 hours, ₱355 and up). They also sail from Dapitan on Mindanao Tu-Th & Sa at 4 PM and return the same days at 7AM. for Dapitan departs at 7AM.

name: George and Peter Shipping
description: out of service

name: Montenegro shipping lines
description: to and from Dapitan and Siquijor.

name: Aleson Shipping Lines
description: Daily to and from Dapitan and Siquijor.

name: Super Shuttle Ferry
description: Daily to and from Dapitan.

name: FastCat
description: Dumaguete to Dapitan.

name: Ceres
description: A major bus line serving Cebu and Negros islands. Their buses are a conspicuously bright yellow. Like the other bus lines, their drivers are recklessly fast and drive on the klaxon.

name: Jeepneys to Dauin
directions: around the corner from the bell tower

name: Jeepneys to San Jose
directions: next to the park, just off Perdices

name: Jeepneys Valencia-to-Dumaguete
description: This is where jeepneys from Dumaguete arrive and the ones going back depart.

name: Jeepneys to Zamboanguita
description: Some park a bit north of the corner, pointing south on the highway, others just west of the corner, ready to turn south. Zamboanguita is a seaside town south of the city.

name: Jeepneys to several places
description: This terminus has jeepneys to Bacong, Dauin, Zamboanguita and Valencia.

name: Bell Tower
description: This is the oldest surviving structure in the city, a relic of the long Spanish occupation of Negros Island. It used to be a watchtower to warn the locals against marauding pirates from Mindanao. The first two storeys date from the mid-1700s with the structure above that added later. Its largest bell is engraved with a date of 1818.

name: Cathedral of Santa Catalina
description: A fine old Roman Catholic church, built under Spanish rule in the 1700s and consequently the oldest stone church in the whole of the province of Negros Oriental. It's dedicated to Saint Catherine of Alexandria who is the patron saint of the city. Her festival is vigorously celebrated around the end of November each year since a Mass celebrating liberation from the Spanish took place in its grounds on the 24 November 1898. The entrance gates are supported by sculptures of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John on tall pedestals.

name: Silliman University Hall
description: Built in 1902-1903, this is the oldest U.S. structure in the Philippines still standing. Its architecture is reminiscent of the Stick Style or Victorian type of architecture that characterized U.S. buildings in the late 19th century. On the east or ocean side of the hall is a bronze bust of Horace Silliman.

name: Luce Auditorium
description: Considered the cultural center of the South. Named for the American Luce family, media magnates who owned Time, Life and other magazines. The tin ceiling was salvaged from an old theater in New York.

name: Marine Laboratory Museum
description: Houses the second-largest whale bone collection in the world.

name: Silliman University Church
description: A Protestant church with some fine stained glass windows. Like the university, it was set up by American Presbyterian missionaries, but its outlook today is very ecumenical; it describes itself as "a church ministering to all Sillimanians, regardless of their denomination and religious affiliations".

name: Silliman University Anthropology Museum
description: The Anthropology Museum houses some Philippine artifacts that were excavated from many parts of the country dating back hundreds or thousands of years.
price: Base rate ₱40 for locals, ₱60 for others, with discounts for children and seniors. Rates double on weekends or holidays

name: Silliman Zoo
description: It conserves endangered Philippine native animals which are rarely seen; eg, spotted deer, warty pigs and crocodiles. Well worth the ₱10 entry fee. They also need financial support. It's a 15-min walk from the city center or a ₱8 pedicab ride.

name: Mt. Talinis
description: The second-highest mountain in Negros Oriental at 1903 m, a dormant volcano, one of a group called the Cuernos de Negros (Horns of Negros). It has lakes, waterfalls and a mossy forest as well as a stream with sulfur vents. Local mountaineering groups frequent the mountain.
directions: Southwest of the city in Valencia Municipality

name: Palinpinon Geothermal Plant
description: This geothermal plant provides electric power for all of Negros Island, Panay, and Guimaras, plus parts of Cebu Province. The power station plaza is closed to visitors at the guard house.
directions: Palinpinon is a barangay of Valencia

name: Volcanic Road
description: Get up close and personal with some sulphur vents along the roadside
directions: On the way to the power station

name: Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park
description: A large protected forest area centered on two volcanic crater lakes. The flora and fauna have been considerably degraded, but it's still an interesting daytrip.
directions: northwest of the city in Sibulan Municipality

name: Harold's Dive Center
description: Has its own dive boats

name: SCUBA Ventures
description: PADI instruction and other services.

name: Cheeki Diver
description: private Dive Guide for diving Dumaguete, Dauin, Siquijor and Apo-Island​.

name: Bravo Golf Course
description: Beautifully kept 18-hole course with plenty of shade trees and Zebu cattle has a view of the sea and an air-conditioned club room. Quarterly green fees are ₱15000 while 'walk-ins' pay ₱750 for 9 holes, ₱1250 for 18 holes M-Th rising to ₱1000 & ₱1500 at weekends. Caddy fees are ₱175 or ₱275, golf cart rental ₱400 or ₱650, an umbrella girl ₱120 or ₱180 and golf set rental ₱650 or ₱650 for 9 or 18 holes respectively. There is a hotel on-site with rooms from ₱2250. The restaurant has a large, brick pizza oven and some other Italian dishes on the menu.
address: San Antonio Barangay Rd, Pancil, Looc, Sibulan

name: Ang Tay Golf Course
description: A 9-hole course close to downtown, before the airport.

name: Cang's Department Store
description: Moderate prices with UnionPay, Visa, JCB and MasterCards accepted, this is a good option for a weekly grocery shop on the ground floor since the basement car park is both free and underutilised. There is a food court on the top floor and the Filomena Cafe 2 (of Bethel Guest House fame) accepts cards too. Purified and cooled water is available free of charge from a self-service drinking fountain with glasses. On the first floor above the ground, small Philippines flags at ₱6 each make good value and lightweight souvenirs if you are flying from nearby Dumaguete airport.

name: Cang's downtown
description: Newer and smaller second location, with no cafe.
address: San Jose, corner of Maria Christina

name: Lee Plaza & Supermarket
description: Main department store in the city centre with a large supermarket in the basement; accepts Visa, JCB and MasterCard. Two bakeries, ground floor and basement; the basement one may be the only place in town with bagels. Food court on top floor.
directions: near the middle of the town's main commercial street

name: Robinson's
description: Supermarket, bakery (with seating & coffee) and drugstore on ground floor. Appliances and hardware store in basement.
directions: in the same block of Perdices Street as Lee Plaza but on the opposite side of the road

name: AAC Tech
description: Computers, Apple products from laptops to i-Pods, other gadgets.

name: Unitop Department Store
description: Generally cheaper than Lee or Robinson, popular with locals.

name: YanYan Baking and Culinary
description: Primarily supplies bakers with all imaginable and unimaginable ingredients, but also carries an interesting selection of other hard-to-find groceries.
address: corner of Mabini St and Santa Rosa St
directions: a few blocks south of Dumaguete Market

name: Lee Plaza Hypermart
description: One large store, plus a food court.

name: Robinson's Place Mall
description: This is a large, air-conditioned suburban mall.
price: Expensive, but there is no surcharge for Visa or MasterCards in its supermarket, although none of the chain eateries take plastic

name: Silliman Farm
description: A 24-hectare (60-acre) farm run by the university's College of Agriculture. High-quality milk and eggs, sometimes other products including turkeys.
directions: north of the campus, toward the airport

name: Citi Mall
description: Has a Savemore supermarket. Watsons pharmacy, Ace hardware, and many fast food outlets. Coffee shop.
directions: On the highway, just before the airport

name: Dumaguete market
description: Around this market is the best place in town to look for small services: key cutting, shoe or bicycle repair, tailors, manicure.

name: Valencia market
description: Has several restaurants.

name: Albertos Pizza
description: Free home delivery.

name: Bakery
description: A range of espresso variants and baked goods, done well enough that the regulars include a group of European French speakers. One of very few places in town that sell bagels. Cheapest brewed coffee downtown at ₱36, though some people prefer Scooby's at ₱50 for larger cups and better chairs.

name: Chow King
description: A chain offering moderately-priced Chinese (mainly Cantonese) food. Pork or beef fried rice, with four shui mai (small noodle-wrapped pork items) and a soft drink, ₱99.
directions: on Perdices, diagonally opposite Lee Plaza

name: Filomena Cafe
description: A very hygienic, air-conditioned cafeteria-style place with a good selection of reasonably priced dishes. Their vegetable fried rice is particularly tasty. All-you-can-eat buffet on Friday evenings for ₱200. Visa and MasterCard are accepted. They give a 20% discount on most things for seniors with Philippine ID, such as the government ACR card which many longer-term visitors have.
directions: two locations: see Bethel Guest House listing under #Sleep, and Cang's under #Buy

name: Food Net
description: Food Net are a chain with several locations around town. They have cafeteria-style service, Filipino food, moderate prices and a largely student crowd. A basic meal — meat dish, veggie dish, rice, soft drink — is about ₱90.
directions: a block inland from the boulevard

name: Food Net
directions: across the street from the Coco Grande hotel

name: Gyro Monsters
description: Cheap and tasty shawarma; the best seller is beef or chicken shawarma wrapped in pita at ₱30, or 35 with cheese. The most expensive thing on the menu is shawarma rice for ₱50; two of the sandwiches are a better buy.If you expect shawarma as you would find it in the Middle East, you will be disappointed here. For that, at slightly higher prices, walk a block north to Mediterranean Food (Turkish, listed at #Other downtown places) or go to Tarbush (Lebanese, #North of the center).
directions: a block east of Lee Plaza

name: Scooby's
description: Scooby's is a chain with various locations around town. Their brewed coffee at ₱50 is both a larger serving and (at least for some tastes) better quality than most coffee offered on Rizal Boulevard at ₱70-120. They also have all the usual variations on espresso, several types of herbal tea, a range of mostly western-style baked goods, and moderately-priced mostly Filipino hot foods. There is a seniors' discount if you have a Philippine senior ID. ACR card not accepted.For Western tastes, most Filipino spaghetti sauces are appallingly sweet, and many will find the spaghetti here downright ghastly. Order the lasagna here (₱55) or go to Filomena for a much better cheap (₱45) spaghetti. For excellent pasta at considerably higher prices, try Mafioso or Pasta King.
directions: a bit east of Lee Plaza

name: Scooby's
description: Another location.
directions: In the university's Portal West building

name: Wah Crepe
description: A small stand selling coffee, crepes, waffles & fruit shakes. All are freshly made and good quality; plum crepes and avocado shakes are remarkable. Best buy is a combo, shake plus waffle. It is only one of a group of food stands, so ordering a shake here and getting food elsewhere is possible.The place is popular with the town's resident foreigners; it gets more younger ones and fewer drunks than their other hangouts.
directions: ground floor, back right hand corner

name: Kimstaurant
description: New in 2019, large, clean and modern. Korean food.

name: Tom 'n Tom's Coffee
description: Part of a chain, large with nice decor. Has good air conditioning, free Wifi, and a good selection of both baked goods and variations on the theme of espresso. Prices might be considered good by tourists but are high by local standards.

name: Just Do Eat
description: Large, with much seafood on the menu. Popular with Asian tourists. The city's resident foreigners more often go to Lantaw, listed at #North of the center.
directions: on the second floor, above Tom 'n Tom's

name: Bo's Coffee
description: A national chain with several locations in Dumaguete, serving mainly coffee & baked goods. Prices are high by local standards.
directions: inside an office building, on the ground floor

name: La Residencia Almar
description: (listed under #Sleep) has three upmarket restaurants. All are somewhat expensive, and all have some customers who consider them worth it. There is also a moderately priced burger bar.

name: Don Atilano
description: Spanish decor & menu, steaks a specialty. All-you-can eat lunch buffet Friday & Saturday, ₱339.

name: Wakagi
description: Japanese food.

name: The Filipino
description: Filipino food.

name: Das Bürgery
description: Small, clean & modern. Menu is limited — only burgers, fries and soft drinks — but quality is good & prices are quite reasonable for what you get. No beer and not much seating, so do not plan an evening here; just grab a burger then go elsewhere for the beer.

name: Hamburg joints
description: Two small cheap places with mostly Filipino customers, one with BBQ chicken as well as burgers. The burgers are not nearly as good as in the tourist restaurants on the Boulevard, and they are smaller as well, but then they are about a quarter the price. The waitress who brings you the expensive burger elsewhere quite likely eats here on her breaks.

name: GameOn Sportsbar
description: Small and plain compared to other places, with no a/c but many fans, big-screen TVs for sports, sometimes live music.

name: Japanese place
description: Nice decor, sake and other Japanese drinks.

name: Sans Rival
description: One of the oldest cake shops in the city. They occupy a pair of buildings on a corner with the cake shop in the smaller one on the side street and "Sans Rival Bistro" on Rizal.

name: Sans Rival cake shop
description: Offers baked goods (surprise!), drinks, and some pasta and salad dishes.

name: Sans Rival Bistro
description: The bistro offers a broader range including a half dozen breakfast options at ₱200-odd. All-you-can-eat breakfast buffet on Sunday 7:30-10AM for ₱285.

name: Chin Loong
description: Good Chinese (Cantonese) food, with reasonable service and prices. Large covered patio.

name: Casablanca
description: European food, elegant décor, and a good wine list. Their patio is above street level and has a wall, so customers here are not bothered by beggars or street vendors as often as at other establishments.There are several breakfast options starting at ₱230, all including unlimited coffee and a glass of juice. The American breakfast at ₱295 is bacon, two eggs, bread, and some fried tomatoes and onions.The Austrian owner/chef sold the place to Filipinos in 2021 and some say it has gone downhill since then.

name: 7-Eleven
description: Chain convenience store with a few tables; the best-selling item is a large soft ice cream cone for ₱15. It also sells soft drinks, snacks and cigarettes; for those it is more expensive than supermarkets but cheaper than the bars. The chain is expanding; there are several other locations around town and more coming.

name: Paseo Perdices
description: A building with two floors, built on the location of the Perdices family home; one family member was the provincial governor and has one of the town's main streets named for him. There are two levels, and the lower level has a large shaded central courtyard.

name: Yellow Cab Pizza
description: Part of a chain. Delivery available; they use yellow scooters.

name: Max's Restaurant
description: Part of a chain. Their specialty is fried chicken. Breakfast from 7:30AM.

name: Infini Tea
description: Their specialty is milk tea.

name: Gabby's Bistro
description: Second location; the first one is an in-house restaurant at Hotel Florentina.

name: Why Not?
description: One-stop shopping? Restaurant, deli, disco, karaoke, cyber cafe, billiard room, and travel agent under one roof. Beer here is sometimes among the cheapest in town, at ₱42 in the restaurants in the afternoon, but higher at other times and ₱90 at the disco.

name: Le Chalet
description: Salads, pasta, other types of European and American food, with decent quality and prices. Inside with a/c or patio. The current chef is from Milan but the menu emphasizes German and Swiss specialities. There are also a few Thai dishes, competently done, for those who prefer something spicier. All-you-can eat breakfast buffet on Sundays, ₱331.

name: Chiccos Deli
description: Selling meats, wines, cheese & chocolate, with many imported European items. Has a bakery with good croissants and pretzels. There are few tables inside and a small patio in front. Both offer the same menu as Le Chalet, but many customers just come for coffee or beer.

name: Why Not? disco
description: A lively and very loud disco, popular with both travellers and locals, and well known as a pick-up bar. A mix of people come for the dancing, for flirting, or to find a partner for the night or longer. Prostitution is present but not the primary character of the place. The occasional drunken brawl is not unheard of. Attitudes among resident foreigners range from enthusiastic regulars to those who avoid it entirely.

name: Honeycomb Tourist Inn
description: (listed under #Sleep) has a restaurant with a large patio area out front, with live music most evenings. Around the side is a small Japanese restaurant, and inside the building a disco and a sports bar.

name: Allegre
description: A large restaurant offering mainly Italian and Filipino dishes. Highest prices in town for pasta.Pool table downstairs, table is in better shape than at the one at Why Not? and there are usually fewer players competing for it.

name: Starbucks
description: Another place for coffee and baked goods at prices that are high by local standards.

name: Gerry's Bar and Grill
description: A fine old house renovated in 2018 to become a large restaurant. Part of a large chain with reasonable quality but some unreasonable prices.

name: Mooon Cafe
alt_name: The 3rd 'o' in the name is deliberate
description: Part of a chain that advertises "Mexican-inspired" food. They offer that, various pizza and pasta dishes, and other western dishes; most of it is done competently. Good soups ₱59, burrito ₱139 (quite good, provided you tell them not to put lettuce in it!), pizza from ₱165, small but good steak ₱300. The best-buy drink is bottomless iced tea at ₱58. Other dishes, such as the "nachos" (overpriced chips & salsa) or the "enchiladas" (a salad served in a tortilla), are distinctly unimpressive. Senior's discount 20% but you may need the Philippines senior's ID to claim it; sometimes they will take an ACR card, but not always.

name: El Amigo
description: Live jazz on weekends

name: Captain Ribber's
description: The specialty is ribs, but they have a range of other dishes.

name: Jo's Chicken Inato
description: Part of a chain specializing in barbeque chicken. Favorite among locals and tourists.

name: Poppy Coffee and Cupcakes
description: In a Silliman University building called Portal West which also has a bank, Scooby's, and several other shops. They also have sandwiches and a breakfast menu.
directions: corner of Silliman and Hibbard, facing Hibbard

name: Harbour City Dim Sum
description: Many types of dim sum, plus various soups and rice or noodle dishes.
directions: Silliman Avenue, across from Portal West

name: Cafe Antonio
description: Fantastic wide-ranging menu, very reasonable prices, lovely chilled out studenty vibe and a great building to host it. Quite honestly a breath of fresh air in the Philippines. Wonderful coffee too!
directions: 2nd floor, Spanish Heritage Building, entrance on Santa C

name: Mediterranean Food
description: Good Turkish kebabs and donair. They have distinctly unexciting hamburgs for ₱30.

name: Mifune
description: Japanese restaurant. All-you-can eat buffet ₱333, Tu & Sa evenings.

name: MELs Cafe
description: This place serves and advocates healthy food, has a certified nutritionist supervising the food. It is small and a bit difficult to find, but worth the trouble. Serves great four season themed salads, a variety of scrumptious sandwiches and unique rice meals like CoFFeeCHoP (pork chop marinated in coffee) or their cheesy delightful fish dish called 'cheesy dory' a favorite among the locals. You can also try their Butter beer in variety of flavors, including vanilla and banana. It is the only place in town that serves beer (non-alcoholic) to minors.
address: 2nd Floor UTH Bldg, Sta Catalina St., near Cnr Locsin St

name: Pasta King
description: Pizza and many pasta dishes, done very well. Pasta in two serving sizes, around ₱179 or 319. The small one will be enough for most people, perhaps with a soup or salad if you are quite hungry.

name: Roti Boss
description: Indian and Malay food. Small, no a/c, a limited menu, and rather slow service. It is well worth putting up with these minor annoyances, though, since the food is good and prices moderate.
directions: near southeast corner of the park

name: Halang Halang
description: Excellent Sichuan food, authentic so much of it is very spicy.
directions: on San Juan, corner of Santa Catalina, behind Bo's Coffee

name: Fish153
description: Korean restaurant and grocery store. Neighborhood has a few other restaurants and some guesthouses.
directions: on street running inland from ferry terminal

name: Panda Ice Cream House
description: Locally-produced fresh fruit ice cream. Try the fried ice cream! This is a chain with several locations in Dumaguete and a few in nearby towns.

name: Flip-Flops Restobar
description: Large shaded patio, big TV with sports, live band Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Open mic on Tuesdays, acoustic performances or karaoke other nights.
directions: a bit east of Lee Hypermart

name: Happy Jack's Restobar
description: Restobar serving cold drinks and both Asian and Western food. Full meals plus a mix and match bar snack menu. Billiard and poker tables plus live music on a couple of nights.

name: Katz Restobar
description: Pool table, darts, sometimes live music.

name: Octagon Sports Bar
description: Big-screen TV mostly showing sports. Live music and ₱250 all-you-can-eat BBQ on weekend evenings.

name: Pastry Dream
description: Offers wide a variety of European pastry, like eclairs, fruit tarts and French macarons. They also have refreshments and coffee.

name: Senorita's Mexican Grill
description: Tex-Mex food, done well.

name: Hayahay Bar
description: Large and popular. Often has live music, reggae every Wednesday. There are several separate places selling food within the complex; one has good pizza and another offers fine Jamaican food.

name: Lantaw
description: A large place with upmarket Filipino food, much of it seafood. Popular with prosperous locals and with seafood-loving foreigners. Possibly the best place in town to take a Filipina out to dinner; she will probably both like the food and be impressed by the decor.
directions: Corner of Flores and EJ Blanco

name: Cafe Racer
description: A diner in the style of mid-20th century America. Decor includes some old cars and a gorgeous motorcycle; the bar is built inside an old VW van. Menu to match; decent burgers, small but excellent milkshakes, etc. Live music sometimes.

name: Low & Slow
description: A fairly large place with nice decor, offering both American and Filipino styles of barbecue. Prices are reasonable. BBQ is good, burgers decent but nothing special. Margueritas are awful; have a milkshake or ₱50 beer.

name: Tarbush
description: Two Lebanese brothers running a small place for Middle Eastern food. Good shawarma and juices.

name: Cafe Mafioso
description: Another Italian place, good quality and cheaper than most of the others, with pasta dishes around ₱140.
directions: Plaza Escano, along the beach north of EJ Blanco

name: Ayla's Breakfast Restaurant
description: A good variety of breakfast dishes, including some less common ones like eggs benedict or biscuits & gravy, plus a few other things like chile con carne. They rent the space from the municipality which sets limits on their prices, so they have the cheapest beer in the region at ₱40.

name: Pacos
description: A tiny stand with a few tables and good Mexican food, owned by Americans. Ayla's will not complain if you sit at one of their tables and buy beer from them but get food from Paco's.

name: La Cocina by Beth
description: Run by a Filipino chef who trained in Mexico . If you like flavorful food, there are Mexican dishes. Cold drinks and margaritas, fresh lemonades, the only air conditioned restaurant in the town with a perfect view.

name: Kamalig
description: A large semi-outdoor (covered patio) place with live music, Filipino BBQ and some other food, and beverages.
directions: E side of Hibbard, N of EJ Blanco

name: Tiki Bar
description: A large place with a patio and often live music.

name: Avenue Park Hotel
description: Fan single with common bath/ fan double with common bath/ air-con single with common bath, cable TV/ air-con double with common bath, cable TV.

name: Harold's Mansion
description: Popular backpacker hotel. Rooms are spacious and clean with a/c or fans. Free coffee all day & rate includes a small breakfast in the upstairs cafe. Free Internet/Wi-Fi. This is where many of the foreign tourists stay, especially divers. If you are travelling out to Apo island you can leave your large bags there safely. Harold himself is extremely friendly and helpful. Harold is happy to have Peace Corps volunteers visit. There is also an attached massage place that is clean and cheap. Dive shop in the same building, tours arranged.
price: single ₱400 and up; bed in dormitory: ₱300

name: Negros Lodging House
description: In particular, the single rooms with fan are quite cheap for Dumaguete.
price: Single ₱130 (shared WC, fan), double ₱300 (own WC, fan), twin ₱350 (own WC, fan)

name: Piapi Beach
description: A beach area with several budget places
directions: along the coast, north of downtown

name: J & J Hotellier
description: free Wifi.
price: single en suite ₱600 with air-con but no window. Has cable TV

name: Crisfils Lodge
description: All rooms have TV.
price: Double ₱200 (shared WC, fan), ₱350 (shared WC, air-con), ₱425 (private WC, air-con)

name: RM Guesthouse
description: Wi-Fi available.
address: 2F RM Building, North National Highway corner East Rovira Road, Bantayan

name: Vintage Inn
description: A decent budget option in the center of town. Has fan and AC single/double rooms all rooms have own bathroom. Free Wifi.

name: Worldview Pension Plaza
description: AC single room with hot water bathroom and cable TV.

name: Moriah Pension Inn
description: AC double room with own hot water bathroom. Cable TV. Free Wi-fi. Has a nice garden to sit in. Can buy breakfast.

name: OK Pension House
description: AC double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Hotel Camila
description: AC double room with own bathroom and cable TV. Free Wi-fi.

name: Gabbys Bed and Breakfast
description: AC single room with own bathroom and cable TV free breakfast, free Wi-fi.

name: White Knights Inn Main
description: A/C double with queen size bed good for 2 with cable TV and free Wifi.

name: New White Knights Inn two
description: A/C queen size bed good for two with shared bathroom all rooms have cable TV and DVD player. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Joraville Pension House
description: A/C double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Dastraum Guest House
description: Fan single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Bethel Guest House
description: Don't let the name fool you, this is a five-storey, squeaky clean, modern building with a whip-cracking management style that can shame the Swiss. Flunky to open the door to the large and comfortable lobby and its own large generators to power the air-conditioning during frequent brown-outs. Well equipped, en-suite shower rooms and free, cooled, filtered water. 1270 m from the port terminal. This is a non-smoking, no-liquor hotel and pets are not allowed.

name: Check Inn
description: 50 air con spacious and clean rooms in this hotel. Cable TV, free Internet in rooms, laundry, restaurant.

name: GoHotels Dumaguete
description: Local location of a national chain. Set in a colorful, low-rise building, Go Hotels Bacolod is 1 km from the 18th-century Dumaguete Cathedral, 5 km from Ang Tay Golf Course, and a 3-minute walk from Robinsons Place Dumaguete shopping center. Brand new budget hotel with 102 rooms (60 Queen, 42 Twin, some without windows) 16-22 m², free Wi-Fi, Asian Gourmet & Cafe
address: Dumaguete Central Business District Calindagan, cor Negros South Road, Dumaguete, 6200 Negros Oriental

name: Honeycomb Tourist Inn
description: 16 air-conditioned rooms, with hot & cold shower, cable TV, PABX telephone, Wi-Fi in the Coffee Shop, ample parking area and 24/7 standby power generator. With Restobar and Coffee Shop offering food, music and nightly fun! Complementary Filipino breakfast.
address: Rizal Boulevard, corner Dr. V. Locsin St.

name: Hotel Nicanor
description: A/C, free Internet, hot & cold showers.

name: Hotel Palwa
description: Near international ATM.

name: Plaza Maria Luisa Suites Inn
description: 22 air-con rooms. Clean and modern interior, local breakfast, internet, money change
directions: on park square near Rizal Blvd

name: The Bricks Hotel
description: Opened in 2018 in a renovated building.

name: Coco Grande
description: Rooms are nice, all with fridge, Wi-Fi and shower. Price includes Western or Filipino breakfast, OK but by no means great.The same company have a beach/diving resort called Coco Grove on the nearby island of Siquijor, and the Apo Island Beach Resort on Apo Island. They have several vans for moving customers around, mainly between those.

name: La Residencia Almar
description: Spanish-influenced style, very central. The building includes three upmarket restaurants (one Spanish, one Filipino and one Japanese) and a moderately-priced burger bar.

name: Bravo Golf Course
description: (listed under #Do) has a hotel with rooms from ₱2200.

name: Loly's Place
description: Built on two floors with all modern-day amenities. It has four spacious bedrooms each with a private balcony, a large living room, a modern gourmet kitchen, ample parking, and an outside garden. Amenities include free high-speed WiFi, TV, Netflix, hot/cold shower, air conditioning, and utilities. The home can accommodate 8 guests. Other services can be arranged such as airport transfer, on-site chef, restaurant recommendation, grocery pickup, rental transportation, laundry service, and child care.
directions: across from Florentina Hotel/Gabby's Bistro, next to the Mormon Church

name: DND Suites
description: Good hotel for longer-term stay, central location. Large rooms with a/c, cable TV (not many channels), free Wi-Fi, fridge (but no cooking facilities), bathroom and shower (with hot water in some rooms, not in others). Rooms are on 2nd and 3rd floor and there is no elevator. No laundry facilities but nearby Silliman Road has both a do-it-yourself laundromat and a do-it-for-you laundry place.Weekly & monthly rates are not always available; when it is busy they will rent only by the day. For weekly or monthly stays, electricity bill is extra.
directions: Above the Frozen Throne Internet cafe

name: Dumaguete Studio Apartments
description: Furnished, with A/C, Internet, cable TV, microwave & gas stove, swimming pool. No children. Strictly no smoking, anywhere in the compound. Inhabited mostly by retired western men with Filipina wives or girlfriends. Rent includes fast Internet and a motorcycle.

name: Hermogina
description: Apartments from studio to three bedroom. Fully furnished, free wired Internet, in a walled compound with security guards and parking. They have a second location further from the city, to the south, with only studio units.
directions: just off the highway, south of Robinson Mall

name: Villa Prescilla
description: Furnished apartments, owned & run by a Swedish/Filipina couple. Rent includes Internet connection, cable TV, and access to laundry area and swimming pool. There is a small eatery next to the pool.

name: Dumaguete Springs Apartments
description: Swimming pool plus access to the beach at the company's resort in Bacong. High-speed Internet available for 1400/month.

name: Andy's Private Garden
description: On the beach. All rooms studio type with queen size beds, stove, fridge, aircon, hot water shower, wifi, cable TV. Water included, and electric up to 2000 pesos per month. All rooms have their own electric meters. Kids two years plus accepted, pets possibly depending on size. Has a resto/bar with a fairly simple menu, Western and Filipino food. Great expat breakfasts.
directions: Turn towards the sea at the Shell Gas Station, go to the end of the road, right side with red gate.

name: Marina Spatial
description: A condo development with units from 20 to 64 sq m (220 to 740 sq ft) at prices from 1.94 to 6.29 million pesos.

name: Valencia Forest Camp
description: Accommodation includes a backpacker dormitory, treehouses and nipa huts. Has two swimming pools.

name: Tejero Highland Resort and Adventure Park
description: A development with ziplines, ATVs, Segways, slide, and natural pools, a ₱12 Jeepeny ride from downtown Dumaguete.

name: Harold's Eco-lodge
description: This place has the same owner as Harold's Mansion in downtown Dumaguete; you can book and arrange transport there.

name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Church
description: The main Roman Catholic church in Dupax del Sur, built in the Baroque style during the 18th century and declared a national cultural treasure in 2001. Beside the convent is a souvenir shop and museum showing church antiquities. The courtyard also features a centuries-old acacia tree.
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Dopaj, Dupax del Sur

name: Spanish Flagpole
description: A red-brick flagpole built in 1873.
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Dopaj, Dupax del Sur
directions: in front of Dupax del Sur Plaza and beside the "Dupax del Sur" sign

name: Dampol Bridge
description: A 19th-century red-brick bridge built over a creek and still used by motor vehicles. The roadway itself is modernized, but its original structure is still intact and can be seen after borrowing a key from caretakers at Saint Vincent Ferrer Church to unlock a gate leading the bottom of the bridge.
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Dopaj, Dupax del Sur

name: Sea of Clouds
description: A stretch of upland rural highway leading to Quirino province, so-called because the low-lying clouds appear to inundate the area in the mornings.
address: National Road, Binuangan, Dupax del Norte

name: Bundok Pag-ibig
description: Meaning "Love Mountain" in Filipino, it is more of a grass hill that somewhat resembles the iconic Windows computer screen, particularly when the rainy season turns the surface green.
address: Maharlika Highway, Gabut, Dupax del Sur

name: Mount Susong Dalaga
description: Meaning "Maiden's Breast", it is the highest peak, with a height of 1650 m, inside the Pantabangan-Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve, a protected area with that straddles the boundary between Dupax del Sur and the towns of Carranglan and Pantabangan in Nueva Ecija.

name: Dupax Watershed Forest Reserve
description: An ecotourism site in the forested foothills of the Caraballo mountains leading to panoramic vistas over the surrounding valley.

name: Dupax del Sur Public Market
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Domang, Dupax del Sur

name: Dupax del Norte Public Market
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Malasin, Dupax del Norte

name: Green Oasis of Dupac
description: A farm-to-table restaurant serving fusion Filipino and Mediterranean cuisine.
address: Aritao-Quirino Road, Mangayang, Dupax del Sur

name: Mount Romelo
description: A 300 m peak surrounded by multiple waterfalls. Most hikes to the mountain combine a stop with the Buruwisan Falls.

name: Balangiga Massacre
description: Every 24 September, the locals in Balangiga town celebrate the 1898 massacre in which the native Balangigans rose up and attacked the abusive American soldiers stationed in their town. The celebration includes a reenactment of the massacre. After the uprising, the sole surviving American soldier made his way back to nearby fort Base (American fort). The Americans immediately dispatched a regiment to Balangiga and inflicted a violent reprisal which resulted in many of the native population seeking refuge in nearby hills.
directions: Bus from anywhere in Samar or Northern Leyte

name: Calicoan Surf Camp
description: It offers Thai, Balinese, and Filipino architecture accommodation rooms, all of which have an air-conditioner, a satellite TV, and a mini-bar. Some of its amenities include a 300 sq m infinity pool with a view of the Pacific Ocean, and a Yacht for island hopping, deep-sea fishing, and “Surfaris”. While staying here, you can visit some interesting places like Santa Monica Caves, and Menasnge Park.
price: Best rates on official website start at ₱6150

name: El Nido Airport
description: Air Swift. . has flights to and from Manila and Cebu. It is best to book via their website. The airport can accommodate only small aircraft, so the prices tend to be much higher than to Puerto Princesa.

name: El Dive
description: This small dive center will offer you relaxing and long dives (departure at 8AM, come back at 4:30PM) among the colourful aquatic life of Bacuit Bay. The Japanese Yoshi Ohtsuka is the manager, he is the one who will welcome you there. He has about 20 years of experience in the diving industry, so he knows what he is talking about. The staff can speak at least English, French, Tagalog and Japanese. On Facebook.

name: Deep Blue Dive Seafari
description: Jose and Diana from Deep Blue Seafari are the founders of the El Nido to Coron dive seafari. This 4-day trip includes 14 dives, camping on the exotic beaches and bonfire nights. Besides the seafaris, Deep Blue also offers fun dives and PADI courses.

name: El Nido Adventure Scuba
description: SSI and PADI open water and advanced dive courses are offered.

name: Island Hopping
description: There are many island hopping tour companies throughout El Nido. They all offer similar tours and prices; therefore it is not necessary to shop around for the best tour company or price. You may want to check a few different companies to see how empty or full their boats are. All tours leave between 8 and 9AM.

name: Island Hopping & Kayak Tours
description: The El Nido Boutique & Artcafe is a kayak tour operator and rents out kayaks, stand up paddle boards, snorkel equipment and bicycles.

name: Palawan Divers
description: Palawan Divers was the first certified PADI dive resort in town. Professional and friendly staff serving beginners to experienced divers.

name: Submariner Diving Center
description: Submariner Diving Center is a diving center operated by the German PADI master scuba diver trainer, Ronny Oliwka. Submariner is a certified PADI Dive Resort and certified Aqualung Partner Center that offers a high standard in diving and education as well as diving gear branded by Aqualung and APEKS. The staff is highly qualified to international standards. Habibi Restaurant & Shisha Cafe is on the first floor of the building.

name: El Nido Boutique & Artcafe
description: El Nido T-shirts printed in their own artshop, souvenirs, handicrafts, postcards, books, photo supplies and cameras, snorkel gear, swimming clothes and beach wear, sarongs, dresses, jewelry, suntan lotions and drugstore items, wine and liquors, bags and backpacks, hammocks.

name: Botanica Cafe
description: A third wave coffee shop popular for its coffee and its breakfasts. It has an in-house bakery making cakes, pastries, cookies, and bread.
directions: tell your tricycle driver to stop in front of Amakan hostel

name: The Beach Shack
description: American and Filipino cuisine, beach snacks, and cocktails.
directions: tell your tricycle driver to drop you in Vanilla Beach, go through the line of stores into the beach area, turn left past Marimegmeg Beach Club

name: La Tienda Delicatessen
description: Make your own deli sandwich or buy groceries for food.

name: Art Cafe
description: A beautiful, well-established restaurant with very good food such as seafood, salads, steaks, pizzas, spaghetti, homemade bread, cakes and fruit shakes and very good coffee. They have live music several nights a week. Free Wi-Fi all day.

name: Habibi Restaurant & Shisha Cafe
description: Good food and beverages, and they are the only shisha bar in Palawan. Drinks are made with fresh ingredients, pizzas are also popular. The full bar offers all varieties of premium drinks. The owner frequently visits the local market to find the best/freshest fish available. Free Wi-Fi, widescreen projection television, and games. The vibe is warm and friendly. The restaurant is ideal for groups wishing to enjoy the freshest fish. The fish are presented to you for selection, and prepared to order.

name: The Alternative
description: Offers tasty & health-conscious food at good prices. Also has a pair of scenic beach-perched "nests" available for dining.

name: El Nido Corner
description: Great beachfront restaurant with a Danish owner. Try the fresh catch of the day.
address: North end of the beach in El Nido

name: El Nido Sands Inn
description: Dorms and privates available. Common area over the water.

name: Relucio Traveller's Pension
description: Bay view terrace, free coffee.
directions: left end of the main street

name: Tay Miloys inn
description: Fan single/double room with common bathroom.

name: Sitio Danat
description: You can pitch a tent for free in the public shelter at Sitio Danat, a small village along the highway, some south of El Nido. Just ask for permission at the convenience store. There is also a small canteen next to the shelter (mains ₱70.) There is absolutely nothing to do in Sitio Danat except for enjoying tranquil village life.

name: Gemini Travelers Lodge
description: All rooms feature air conditioning, hot and cold shower, TV, free Wi-Fi internet; there are laundry servicers, and an outside seating area too.
address: Fishermen Street, Barangay Buena Suerte, El Nido

name: Anang Balay Turista
description: A small friendly place with good air-con rooms.

name: Cadlao Resort & Restaurant
description: Beautifully located on a trail just outside of El Nido, with view over El Nido bay and Cadlao island. Exceptional restaurant and bar. Has battery backed-up solar cells and private generator.
price: ₱5500 for economy room, ₱6500 for air-conditioned room

name: Cliffside Cottage
description: It is slightly away from the center but set in a quiet setting with porches facing the garden.

name: Edleahs Inn
description: Small budget guest house with sea view. The host is really nice and helpful. The Internet connection is poor, but that's the case for all places here. Coffee is provided in the morning.
directions: after the Art Cafe near the dock

name: El Nido Beach Hotel
description: All rooms have hot water, TV, mini fridge and free Wi-Fi.

name: El Nido All Seasons Beach Resort
description: All rooms are equipped with air-conditioning, TV with cable channels, hot shower, private balcony, private toilet and bath. It also provides island hopping tours, airport transfers, massage service, room service and laundry service.
directions: 3 km or a 3- to 4-minute ride from the town center

name: Islandfront Cottages and Restaurant
description: Rooms are equipped with air-conditioning, high-speed Internet access, and daily breakfast.

name: Kalinga Beach Resort
description: It is along Calaan beach, and has 8 cottages and beach villas available.

name: La Salagane
description: Two locations, both seafront; offers a variety of accommodations at different prices.

name: Lagen Resort
description: It has 50 rooms and caters à la carte meals and buffet. A clinic, library, boutique, a swimming pool, and a game area are some of the facilities offered here.

name: Lally & Abet Beach Resort
description: A Dept. of Tourism accredited hotel, it has 34 rooms with an A/C, telephone and shower, a laundry service and foreign currency exchange is also provided here. For leisure they also have sports facilities for badminton and volleyball games. Major credit cards are accepted here.

name: Lorenzo
description: Nice basic bungalows in front of the beach. Free hot water, mosquito net, free hot water and friendly owner.
directions: Ask any tricycle driver for Lorenzo

name: Lualhati Cottage
description: A/C rooms. Comfortable family-run accommodation at the edge of town.

name: Marina Garden Beach Resort
description: In center of town on the beach.

name: Miniloc Resort
description: Has 51 rooms. Aside from being a resort, they also offer snorkeling facilities, and they have kayaks, aqua bikes and other water sports equipment available for rent.

name: Og's beach pension
description: Three-story building with rundown rooms but a great view right on the beach. Happy Hour from 5PM to 7PM with ₱40 beer. Divers should seek out one of the staff named Mator as he often does private trips.

name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
description: Floridablanca's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the 19th century and repaired following World War II bombing.

name: White House
description: A two-story private, white-painted mansion built during the Spanish era.
address: Rizal corner San Jose Streets, Poblacion

name: Bale Kastila
description: A 19th-century Spanish-era residence with an extensive balcony that used to be the estate house of a sugarcane hacienda. It fell into neglect and was used as a shooting location for domestic horror films before being restored to its original Victorian and Art Nouveau design complete with tiles in 2024. There are plans to convert the house into a bed and breakfast and event venue.

name: Nabuclod Mountains
description: Part of the Zambales Cordillera, it provides views of the Central Luzon plains up to Mount Arayat.

name: Sumuclab Lagoon
description: A freshwater lagoon.

name: Palakol Summer Place
description: A shallow point along the Gumain (Telesiko) River set in the backdrop of the 150 m high SCTEX Gumain viaduct that is a favorite swimming place for residents. Cottages can be rented from the owners, who are mostly from the local indigenous Aeta community.

name: National Shrine of Our Lady of the Visitation of Guibang
description: A Roman Catholic shrine dedicated to a venerated image of the Virgin Mary found in the barrio in 1905 and believed to be miraculous. The church celebrates its feast day on July 2, during which the highway in front is closed to motor vehicles and non-visitors are directed to use a bypass road skirting the center of Guibang.

name: Cathedral of Saint Michael
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Ilagan, built in 2000. It formally replaced a Spanish-era building in neighboring Ilagan that reverted to being Ilagan's parish church in 2003. Formerly dedicated to Saint Ferdinand, its patron saint was changed to Saint Michael the Archangel in 2013.

name: Saint Rose of Lima Parish Church
description: Gamu's Roman Catholic parish church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in the 18th century.

name: Poor Clare Monastery
description: A nunnery run by the Order of Saint Clare that opens to pilgrims seeking to fulfill vows to pray in seven to 14 churches as part of the Visita Iglesia ritual during Holy Week.

name: Xentro Square Gamu
description: An unfinished mall with a functioning produce market.

name: Piazza Zicarelli
description: Hotel with restaurant and bakeshop.
directions: in front of Shell gas station

name: Hotel Vercida
directions: in front of Camp Melchor dela Cruz

name: Montañosa Hotel
directions: in front of Camp Melchor dela Cruz

name: Tagpuan sa Lumang Gapan
description: Meaning "Meeting-Spot in Old Gapan", it is a cluster of well-preserved colonial-era houses concentrated around two perpendicular cobble-stoned streets beside Gapan Church. During major holidays, the street is closed off to vehicles and becomes a pedestrian-friendly zone complete with stalls.
address: Delos Reyes corner Jacinto Streets, San Vicente

name: Gapan Church
alt_name: Minor Basilica and National Shrine of La Virgen Divina Pastora
description: Gapan's main Roman Catholic church. Built in 1872, it is the oldest church in Nueva Ecija and is one of the few remaining Spanish-era structures in the province. It also hosts a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.
address: H. Malgapo corner Delos Reyes Streets, San Vicente

name: Gapan City Plaza
description: Gapan's main public space, featuring civic monuments, trees and a Ferris wheel. A fine spot for recreational activities, finding some shade from the weather or just people-watching. On weekends, the area hosts a night market.
directions: in front of Old Gapan City Hall

name: Casa Batik
description: A 7 ha garden and farm filled with (mostly) bougainvilleas and other flowering plants, some of which are also on sale. There is also a cafe onsite. Also a popular venue for weddings and photography sessions.
price: ₱100, ₱80 concessions for senior citizens and disabled persons and ₱50 for students, free for children below 3 ft

name: Gapan City Public Market
address: Santo Niño De Praga Street, San Vicente

name: Truffle Cafe

address: Divina Pastora Building, E. Jacinto Street, San Vicente

name: Asia Jem Hotel
directions: at the back of Novo Department Store

name: La Victoria Hotel and Resort
description: An out-of-the way accommodation in the fields southeast of downtown Gapan.

name: Gasan People's Park
description: The largest park in Gasan, this is where the town's annual passion play is staged every Black Saturday, as well as the Gasang-Gasang Street Dancing Festival every Easter Sunday. The Gasan Public Library is located inside the park.

name: Gasan Sea View Park
description: Also known as the Gasan Baywalk, fairs are often held here. A wooden suspension footbridge—the only one of its kind in Marinduque—connects the park to neighboring Barangay Dili.

name: Kawilihan Park
description: Located on the highest point in Gasan, it has a commanding view of the town center, with giant ipil-ipil trees being the park's main attraction.

name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish
description: Located on the second-highest point in Gasan, the church has a viewing platform with wonderful views of the town center below. A grand new church—believed to be the biggest in Marinduque—has replaced the old church (which was converted into an auditorium), with a large altarpiece at the end. While substantial work is complete, the church is not yet finished, and the church accepts donations for its eventual completion.

name: Talao Cave
description: 6 km from the town center, this is a series of twelve caves in the middle of the forest which are only accessible on foot along three mountain trails emanating from the main road.

name: Tres Reyes Islands
description: A chain of three islands off the coast of Gasan, they are named after the Three Kings of the Nativity. Unlike the black, rocky sand and dark waters along the coast of mainland Gasan, the Tres Reyes Islands have white sand beaches and blue waters, and the islands' ecology is ideal for diving.

name: Balthazar's Tavern
description: Opened in May 2012 and run by a U.S.-trained chef, it serves Western and Filipino dishes. As it is on the top floor of the town's tallest building, it has a commanding view of the town and the sea. The restaurant also has an all-you-can-eat buffet on Sundays for ₱175.
address: 4/F DJ Plaza, Bonifacio cor. San Jose Sts., Barangay Uno

name: Barbarossa Pub and Restaurant
description: Run by a German, it is the town's most famous restaurant, on the old site of the Gasan Public Library. The restaurant is as known for its repertoire of dishes as it is for its well-stocked bar.
address: Gomez cor. San Jose Sts., Barangay Dos

name: Ristorante d'l Jose
description: Gasan's only Italian restaurant, it also serves Filipino and Chinese dishes.

name: Tita Laida Food House
description: Gasan's best halo-halo is served here, as well as other Filipino dishes. The restaurant also serves pizza, and is particularly known for its pancit.

name: Luxor Resort and Restaurant
description: Beach front resort on the national road 1.5 km north of Poblacion Gasan. 7 air-conditioned chalets with one bedroom each, with cable ready flat screen LED TV, and en suite bathroom with hot and cold shower. Function hall and beach cabana available for conferences/, conventions, seminars, weddings, parties and other events. Ideal for garden wedding.

name: Raqueno Apartment
description: Raqueno Apartment is available for daily (transient) and monthly rates at very reasonable price. Located at Sitio Bagongbayan, Dili. Contact Tatay Danding at +63 9987472152 or Nanay Luz at +63 9216520402 .

name: General Santos International Airport
description: Opened in 1996, it has the third longest runway in the Philippines and serves daily domestic flights from Manila, Cebu and Iloilo using a mix of medium and large jets.

name: Mount Matutum
description: An active volcano, approximately 5.7 km from Acmonan, Tupi, South Cotabato. Adjacent volcanic edifices are Landayao, Tampad, and Albulhek to the west of the volcano, and Magolo to the north. There is a well-preserved 320-m-wide crater at the volcano's summit. The crater is breached by three gorges and has a 120-m-deep, densely forested floor. The great view of Matutum is seen in Barangay Pagalungan, Polomolok, with some plantation of pineapples and Barangay Mabuhay and San Isidro in General Santos City.

name: Klaja Ecopark
description: An ecological preservation park 15 km (9.3 mi) off the central business district on the north-east side of city in Barangay Conel. Klaja Karsts Land derived its name from “Kalaha” ("frying pot") as it looked like one due to the surrounding towers of karsts formation naturally formed millions of years ago. It produced natural waterfalls and caves. Opposite is the ranch and camping ground of Nopol Hills, which borders Barangays Conel and Mabuhay. Nopol Hills offers visitors a wide scenic overview of the entire city, as well as the Sarangani Bay and parts of South Cotabato and Sarangani Province.

name: Gen. Paulino Santos Museum
description: In the Notre Dame of Dadiangas University, it is the first formal museum in the city. It showcases the memorabilia of General Paulino Santos and the first settlers of the city who flocked to the area now known as General Santos City. It also features cultural artifacts of South Cotabato province.

name: Sanchez Peak
description: 800-foot high mountain peak accessed by trails with panoramas of General Santos City.

name: Baluan Balut Park
description: Good place to eat balut with family. The ambiance is good. A 5-minute drive from city proper.

name: Manny Pacquiao Mansion
description: Tourist attraction.

name: Queen Tuna Park
description: Lawned city park on Sarangani Bay with beachside cabanas & a number of trees for shade.

name: Kalilangan Festival
description: General Santos City celebrates the Kalilangan every month of February. "Kalilangan" means festival, festivity or jubilation. It is a social gathering marked by exchanging of amenities among traditional leaders, elders, allies and subordinates in varying tones. In a broader perspective, Kalilangan projects a positive and dynamic meaning for it engulfs the artistic, humane and altruistic aspects of social interaction that takes place in any occasion or celebration. Kalilangan is a noble tradition. It is a complete work of art nourished and nurtured by rich cultural heritage that has withstand the test of time from generation to generation. The festival is being Spearheaded by the Mindanao State University upon which have garnered awards as the countries best native or local festival three years in succession.

name: Tuna Festival
description: Thanksgiving and festivities are being celebrated annually through its Tuna Festival during the Last week of August and the first week of September highlighting on its main industry which is the Tuna fishing. This is also in line with the celebration of the city's charter anniversary which falls every 5 September and is also being set as the culmination day for the Tuna Festival. Aside from parades and showcases, numerous culinary competitions are being held to promote sumptuous tuna-based cuisines and other delectable meals made from fresh sea food.

name: Yaman Gensan
description: Yaman Gensan is an annual event in Gensan that celebrates and promotes local entrepreneurs. It is celebrated in July. Tuna products, T'nalak, Malong and other tribal objects are shown and sold.

name: Paskuhan sa Gensan
description: The city celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, in this event. It is celebrates from December 17 to the countdown of New Year, Colorful lanterns, giant Christmas tree and Gensan Barangay Christmas House competition are in the event as are Paskuhan sa Gensan Street Dancing, choir group and Christmas Dance.

name: Sto. Niño Patronal Fiesta
description: This one-day celebration in the city is celebrated every 15th of January. It is the same as the Sinulog Festival in Cebu City. Colorful amphibians, Sr. Santo Niño's Grotto and street dancing. This annual and patronal festival is celebrating in Barangay Bula.

name: Mount Cagua
description: The only active volcano in northern Luzon, it is a 1133 m peak in the Sierra Madre mountains that last erupted in 1907 and has a 1.5 km wide caldera. It is home to hot springs, fumaroles and some endemic plant and animal species such as the cloud rat.

name: Rumang-ay War Memorial
description: A small obelisk along the beach commemorating the spot where Japanese forces conducted the first amphibious landings on Luzon during their invasion of the country on December 10, 1941 at the start of the Pacific theater of World War II.

name: Matara Reefs and White Sand Beach
description: A partially-secluded stretch of beach on the boundary with Santa Ana, whose white sands contrast with the grey beaches in the rest of Gonzaga.

name: Tallag Beach and Rock Formations
description: A row of large rocks eroded by the wind and waves, resulting in peculiar formations, caves and tidal pools.

name: Liban's Farm and Nature Park
description: An ecotourism venue with camping and fishing grounds, a natural spring pool, and overnight accommodation.

name: G Farm
description: A family-run farm that offers fruit and vegetable picking to guests.

name: Betis Church
description: The Baroque parish church of Betis district. The original structure was built in 1660, but was damaged by fire and rebuilt in the 1770s. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2001. The church's interior is likened to that of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City. Flash photography is discouraged.

name: Immaculate Conception Church
description: The massive parish church of Guagua proper, with its cupola looming across town. The present barn-style Baroque church and belfry dates to 1772, after the original 1587 building was destroyed by fire. Unlike Betis Church, its interior is painted in austere white, with only the pulpit and altarpiece giving away its Spanish origins.
address: Aurelio Tolentino Street, Plaza Burgos, Poblacion
directions: past Plaza Burgos, at the back of the Municipal Hall and Rufino Cardinal Santos Catholic Center

name: Lopez Mansion
description: Built in 1929 as the residence of a sugar magnate, Don Alejandro Lopez, it is the first concrete house in Pampanga. The house later fell into a long period of neglect caused in part by family squabbles and lahar flows caused by the Mount Pinatubo eruption, which is why some locals refer to the place as the “Haunted Mansion” when asked for directions. The house was repaired in 2016 and is now used as a wedding and events venue, retaining much of its elegant interior.

name: Guagua Municipal Hall
description: Built in 1937, it is one of the few remaining civic buildings in the Philippines to survive World War II.
address: Gil Puyat Avenue, Plaza Burgos, Poblacion

name: Plaza Burgos
description: Guagua's main square, featuring civic monuments, a gazebo and trees. A fine spot for recreational activities, finding some shade from the weather or just people-watching. It is also the de facto main transport terminal for most jeepneys in Guagua.

name: Araullo Ancestral House
description: A private residence built in 1928. Despite the perimeter walls, its two storeys are visible from outside.

name: Bale Pinaud

name: Apag Marangle
description: A restaurant serving Kapampangan cuisine since 2008. Some of their more exotic delicacies include crickets (camaru), fried and stuffed frogs, and Tinolang Tugak (frog s in a thin soup with vegetables).
address: Jose Abad Santos Avenue corner Dalan Betis, San Juan Nepomuceno, Betis

name: Rural Bar & Cafe

name: Fabrika Villas
