address: Santa Clara Road, Santa Ines, Betis

name: Balaan Bukid Shrine
description: Hike to the 14 stations of the cross. Take a ferry bound for Jordan Wharf in Ortiz Port (Iloilo City). From Jordan Wharf, take a tricycle ride to the foot of Balaan Bukid. It's a 30-45 min hike to the top. During the Holy Week (Easter), there are special trips that transport visitors directly to the foot of Balaan Bukid.

name: Guisi Light House
description: From Guisi Beach, follow a trail 15 minutes uphill to the Guisi Lighthouse for a great view of the beach. At the top of the hill are the ruins of a Spanish-colonial outpost and the rotting remains of the metal lighthouse structure.

name: Trappist Monastery
description: An ornate cross-shaped church, with sections both for the monks (in the middle) and lay visitors (on the sides). A gift shop sells souvenirs and sweets.
directions: On the road between San Miguel and Nueva Valencia.

name: Roca Encantada
description: A summer house built on top of a huge rock, possessing a magnificent architectural design, overlooking the Legendary Seven Isles or Siete Picados and fascinating beautiful seascape of the northern part of Guimaras Strait. It was built as a pledge of the great Lopez matriarch, Doña Precentacion Hofeliña Lopez in 1910. It was declared by the National Historical Institute as a Heritage House or one of the National Historical Landmarks on August 14, 2002.

name: National Mango Research and Development Center
description: If you want to learn more about the sweetest mangoes of Guimaras, go here. The ideal month to visit it towards the end of summer where the mangoes are ripe and they offer picking activities. The arrangement of the mangoes are also very good for pictorials.

name: Capitoguan Beach
description: Guimaras has a number of secluded beaches without road access, and Capitoguan is one of them. To get there,The beach operators charge a 50 pesos per person admission fee. If you have packed a tent with you, you pay 200 PHP fee to set up the tent overnight. There are also a few simple cabins which can be rented for 1500-2000 pesos per night. Amenities include a water pump, and a toilet which can be flushed with the water you bring from that pump. Several sari-sari stores sell packages snacks, drinks, and basic meals. One can also buy charcoal (uling) to cook on a charcoal grill. Actual swimming is somewhat challenging, since the beach is separated from the ocean by a small coral reef, which becomes exposed at low tide.When leaving the beach, it may sometimes be possible to hire a pump boat to take you to the nearby Singcalang Beach (about 1 km to the north), which is just outside of Barangay Balcon Melliza, where tricycles are available to take you back to Jordan or elsewhere.
directions: Take a tricycle from Jordan Wharf to Balcon Maravilla (150 pesos, or 200 if the driver takes you off-road a bit closer to the beach), and then walk about a mile on the forest trail.

name: Immaculate Conception Church
description: The most beautiful church in the island of Samar. Built solely by manual labor, this edifice of adobe stone is indeed a cultural heritage. Inside, one can find uniquely carved icons as a Spanish Baroque altar. This 400+-year-old Catholic church, inspired by the Spanish colonizers that came to the Philippines after the Magellan expedition, also features chiseled doorways and has a classical façade. This church was restored by the NCCA following Typhoon Haiyan.

name: Guiuan Church Tower
description: A monumental to native labor, it is the tallest existing tower in the municipality. Two thirds of its height was said to have been destroyed by earthquakes many years ago. The imposing belfry is a comforting sight for an exhausted overland travellers that come from various points of the country via Borongan, the provincial capital of Eastern Samar.

name: Pearl Island
description: This is a quaint coral islet developed by BFAR. It is devoted to experimental round and blister pearl culture and giant clams project and is ideal for scuba diving and underwater sports.

name: PAGASA Radar Station
description: A sophisticated weather forecasting instrument. One of the PAGASA stations in the country. Located on top of a hill, and offers a panoramic view of the town, the Leyte Gulf and the vast Pacific Ocean.

name: Tubabao Island
description: Served as the former International Refugee Organization (IRO) campsite for 6,000 displaced White Russians from 1949-1952.

name: 3149 US Naval Base
description: On December 1, 1944, a fleet of LCT's Liberty Ships and barges poured into the Guiuan Bay to unload machines that was to transform Guiuan into one of the biggest naval bases in the Far East at the time.

name: Pray at the Shrine of St. Anthony of Padua
description: This picturesque barrio is famous for its Shrine of St. Anthony of Padua whose miraculous attributes devotees and visitors from afar and wide.

name: Surf
description: Declared as the surfing capital of the Visayas in 2001, by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. This is an ideal place for surfing during the months of September to December due to the presence of big waves by the northeast trade winds.

description: A small maritime terminal serving travelers to and from Alabat Island, across from Lamon Bay. There are plans to expand the facility to accommodate motor vehicles and larger passenger ferries.

name: Gumaca Cathedral
description: Gumaca's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1690. It is also the headquarters of the Diocese of Gumaca.

name: Kutang San Diego
description: A Spanish-era coastal watchtower built in the 18th century to defend Gumaca against raids by Moro pirates and other foreign invaders such as the Dutch. The site was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2020.
address: Nava Boulevard corner Quezon Street, San Diego

name: Museo ng Gumaca
description: A local history museum.

name: Gumaca Municipal Hall
description: Built during the American occupation in 1921, it is one of a few civic buildings in the country to survive World War II.

name: San Diego de Alcala Park
description: A small recreational space built on top of a limestone hill overlooking Lamon Bay. Its highlight is a monument to Gumaca's patron saint, Didacus of Alcalá.

name: Inaclagan Falls
description: A cascade in the hinterlands of Gumaca.

name: Bosque Cave
description: A set of two caves.

name: Gumaca City Coast Hotel & Restaurant
description: Mixed-use hotel, restaurant and commercial complex with a convenience store and gas station.

name: National Shrine and Parish of Saint Anne
description: Hagonoy's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style and retaining its exquisite ceiling art and religious sculptures. It also has an ecclesiastical museum.
address: M.H. del Pilar Street, Santo Niño

name: White House
description: A white-painted colonial era residence.
address: M.H. del Pilar Street, San San Sebastian

name: Don Francisco Sebastian Ancestral House
description: A colonial-era residence.

name: Santa Monica Chapel
description: A rare Spanish era village chapel.

name: Nuestra Senora del Santissimo Rosario Parish Church
description: A gothic-like Roman Catholic church hosting a venerated Marian image of Our Lady of the Rosary dating from the late 18th century.

name: Bilaran ng Tibaguin
description: After a boat ride to one of Hagonoy's isolated coastal barangays, visitors can learn more about the community's relationship with the water and get the chance to buy seafood in this open-air space for drying fish (bilaran means a place to leave things out to dry).

name: Habibi Resort and Sizzling House
description: A resort complex with swimming pools, karaoke rentals and a grill restaurant.

name: Hagonoy Public Market
description: The town's main fishport.

address: Santa Elena Road, Purok 4, San Pablo

name: Mount Atugu
description: A mountain ridge marking the boundary between the barangays of Bitu and Anao that is said to resemble the silhouette of a partially-laid down woman. Hikers climb to the summit to enjoy the views during sunrise.

name: Umalbong Rice Terraces
description: A functioning rice terrace complex used by the surrounding village.

name: Hungduan Rice Terraces
description: A rice terrace complex lining the Hapao River valley in the barangays of Hapao, Nungulunan and Ba-ang. It is one of five rice terrace complexes in Ifugao included in the UNESCO World Heritage List, but is overlooked by tourists in favor of the more accessible ones in Banaue. There is a panoramic viewdeck along the Tinoc-Hungduan-Banaue Road in Hapao.

name: Bacung Rice Terraces
description: A spiderweb-like rice terrace complex in downtown Hungduan.

name: Lion's Head
description: A small lion's head carved into the rock at a curve along the highway.

name: Mount Napulauan
description: The second highest mountain in Ifugao after Mount Pulag, with a height of 2642 m. Climbers risk the extraordinarily difficult climb to view the sunrise at its summit, as well as its mossy forests. The mountain was also used as a headquarters by Japanese general Tomoyuki Yamashita during the final days of World War II in 1945.

name: Bogyah Hot Spring
description: A hot sulfur spring.

name: Hungduan Eco-village
description: A collection of traditional houses showcasing indigenous Ifugao culture.
directions: at the back of the municipal hall

name: Balentimol Falls
description: A cascade at the foot of Mount Napalawan.

name: Iba Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in Zambales, built during the Spanish era in the 18th century.
address: Olongapo-Bugallon Road corner Lesaca Street, Zone 5 Poblacion (Bano)

name: Zambales Provincial Capitol
description: The seat of the provincial government of Zambales, built with a slightly neoclassical façade.

name: Iba Town Center
description: A small mall.

description: Pastry shop with sit-down tables and menu that includes cakes, burgers and soup.

name: Frenzel Inn
address: Paulien Subdivision, Purok 4, Zone I Poblacion (Libaba)

name: Saint James the Apostle Parish Church
description: Iguig's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1787.

name: Calvary Hills
description: An 11 ha park overlooking the Cagayan River with a replica of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his companions. The site can get crowded during Holy Week.

name: Poor Clare Monastery
description: A monastery and pilgrimage site run by the Order of Saint Clare.

name: Utto Falls
description: An 80-100 ft cascade.

name: Dabbay Falls
description: A step-ladder like cascade.

name: Gayle's Kitchenette
description: Restaurant serving Filipino cuisine.

description: 4 buses and 2 return trips daily. Buses depart from Sampaloc, Manila at 2:30PM, 4PM, 6:30PM, and 7:45PM, and arrive at Ilagan at 12:57 midnight, 2:27AM, 4:57AM, and 6:12AM. Return trips depart at 4PM and 6:30PM.
price: About ₱790, not including food stop at Nueva Vizcaya

name: G.V. Florida Transport
description: One departure daily from Sampaloc, Manila

name: Ilagan City Central Terminal
description: A consolidated terminal for buses, jeepneys and other PUVs.

name: Bonifacio Park
description: Houses a statue of Andres Bonifacio. It is also a common site for demonstrations.

name: Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Ilagan plant
description: There are guided tours where visitors can see the mechanized process of how Coca-Cola is produced.

name: Giant rocking chair
description: This, the largest in the world, was constructed within 29 days with a cost of ₱175,000.

name: Ilagan Japanese Tunnel
description: 40 m tunnel, once used as a Japanese army headquarters.

name: Saint Ferdinand Parish Church
description: Formerly the seat of the Diocese of Ilagan, it houses the oldest bells in the province. The church, save for its belfry, was gutted by fire in 2024 and is undergoing reconstruction.

name: Queen Isabela Park
description: In front of the Provincial Capitol, it hosts concerts and various booths during the Bambanti Festival and has a pond, an amphitheater, and a monument to Queen Isabella II of Spain, after which the province was named.

name: Isabela Provincial Capitol
description: A monumental office complex. In the courtyard is a statue of the province's longest serving governor, Faustino Dy Sr. At the back is the governor's official residence, known simply as Balai (House).

name: Isabela Museum and Library
description: Housed in the old provincial capitol building, the museum has a collection on the province's history and culture.

name: Ilagan Sanctuary
description: 819 ha national park. Activities include hiking, mountaineering, spelunking and birdwatching.

name: Ilagan Sports Complex
description: A large modern sports center opened 2015 to replace the older Paguirigan Memorial Sports Complex. It has badminton, basketball, tennis, and volleyball courts, an 8-lane swimming pool, and an IAAF-certified track and field.

name: Isabela Sports Complex
description: A massive stadium with a track and field course. During the Bambanti Festival, this hosts the street-dancing competition involving teams from the different municipalities of Isabela.

name: Capital Arena
description: A stadium with a seating capacity of 10,000. Opened in 2024, it hosts national-level competitions for indoor sports such as basketball and volleyball.
directions: at the back of Ilagan Central Terminal and Northstar Mall

name: Aggaw na Ilagan
description: May 4. Celebrates the city's founding as a town.

name: Bambanti Festival
description: An annual festival celebrating Isabela's culture. Most major events are held at the amphitheater at Queen Isabela Park.

name: Ilagan Public Market
description: There are some carinderias outside. Meat section may smell like cigarette smoke due to many vendors openly smoking.

name: Northstar Mall
description: Two-story mall with a cinema, a Savemore supermarket, a McDonald's, and a hotel (see #Sleep. While air-conditioned, it may feel hot though inside.

description: Shopping mall.

description: One of the best Pansit Guisado in the City of Ilagan, Isabela. Superior Restaurant serves also delicious Pinoy recipes like Igado, Pork Adobo, Adobong Pusit, Lechon Kawali and more.

description: Food served in a garden atmosphere.

description: Filipino restaurant.

description: City-owned. AC rooms. Free laundry. No free meals.

description: Now closed to commercial service since the opening of Laguindingan Airport.

description: Receives buses headed for Iligan from Cagayan de Oro. Better organized, with a building housing shops and ticketing offices and bus bays. Modern jeepneys headed downtown are available.

name: Iligan City Integrated Bus and Jeepney Terminal – West
description: Buses coming from or headed for the west (Ozamiz, Pagadian, Dipolog, Zamboanga City) use this basic terminal. Vans and jeepneys from Marawi also use this terminal. Transfer to jeepneys bound for downtown are also available. There is a building housing the waiting area, but to get on or off the bus, jeepney or van involves a walk through dirt and gravel.

name: Macaraeg-Macapagal Ancestral House
description: The only house in Mindanao where two Philippine Presidents resided: the father-daughter Presidents Diosdado Macapagal and Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. In 1994, upon the instigation of Diosdado, the lot where the house stands and a two-hectare cocoland nearby were donated to the City Government of Iligan for the purpose of developing the place into a tourist destination with a memorabilia of the Macaraeg-Macapagal Family.

name: Bank of the Philippines Islands
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM. Maximum withdrawal ₱20,000.

name: Iligan Galaxy Express Mart

description: Hawaiian cheese ₱36. Ham egg ₱40. Bacon egg ₱40. Cheese burger with egg ₱40.

Features and amenities: 24-hour reception, 24-hour security, 24-hour room service, daily housekeeping, flatscreen cable TV, free Wi-Fi, free luggage storage, free parking, intercom.
address: Champaca Street, San Miguel Village, Pala-o
directions: at the back of Philippine Independent Church

description: A/C double rooms with own bathrooms and cable LCD TV. 12/24 hours. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Flor-al Mansion
description: A/C rooms with own bathrooms and 40 inch cable TV. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Plaza Alemania Lodge
description: A/C double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV, free Wi-Fi.

name: Island hop and Snorkel in Hundred islands
description: Rent a motor banca (pump boat) for the day, hop between islands and snorkel to your hearts content

name: Quirino Skyline/Tirad Pass
description: designated a National Shrine, this pass was the site of a battle led by a young general named Gregorio del Pilar against revolutionary forces led by hero Emilio Aguinaldo

name: Experience Dinagyang
description: Step up to the beat, enjoy the sound of drums and bare feet stomping into the pavement in perfect unison, and join the locals dancing in the streets with a bottle of beer. The Dinagyang Festival is celebrated every 4th Sunday of January in Iloilo.

name: Paraw Regatta
description: Claimed as the oldest traditional craft in Asia, the Paraw Regatta is a race among seafarers on colorful sailboats called Paraws in the Iloilo Strait between Guimaras Island and the city of Iloilo. The present-day paraw managed to maintain its original design from the sailboats of the first settlers from Borneo who were in search of a peaceful home in 1212 AD. Surviving centuries, the paraws have become a vital part of the Filipino seafaring life. The first race started in 1973 with the mission to preserve the historic value of the paraws. It is held every 3rd weekend of February at Villa Arevalo District in Iloilo City. Today, the event has grown from being a boat race to a festival with various interesting and exotic activities.

name: Iloilo International Airport
description: Located about 19 km northwest of the Iloilo City proper.

name: Parola Wharf
address: Fort San Pedro Drive, Iloilo City Proper

name: Fort San Pedro Terminal
address: Fort San Pedro Drive, Iloilo City Proper

name: Iloilo Fastcraft Terminal
address: New Iloilo Ferry Terminal Access Road, Lapuz

name: Jaro Metropolitan Cathedral
alt_name: National Shrine of Our Lady of Candles
description: One of the most significant religious sites in the Visayas. It houses the miraculous image of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria (Our Lady of the Candles), the only Marian image in the Philippines crowned by a pope and Vatican decree, Pope John Paul II in 1981. Across the street stands the iconic Jaro Belfry, which was originally a watchtower before being converted into a bell tower.

name: Jaro Belfry
description: One of the few belfries in the country that stands apart from the church. It was constructed by the Spaniards to serve as a watchtower to monitor Muslim invasion from Mindanao. The colonial structure was ruined by an earthquake in 1948 and was restored decades later, in the mid-1990s.

name: Molo Church
description: Built in 1831, this Gothic-Renaissance church stands as one of the most iconic landmarks of Iloilo. Known as the “feminist church” for its 16 statues of female saints, Molo Church features twin spires, a coral-stone façade, and a magnificent altar. It was visited by Jose Rizal on his way to exile in Dapitan, Mindanao.

name: San Jose Church
description: Founded in 1607 by the Jesuits and later turned over to the Augustinians, it is considered the first church in Iloilo City. The church houses the replica of Santo Niño de Cebú, the patron saint of the Dinagyang Festival.

name: Calle Real
description: The city’s historic street, lined with late 19th and early 20th-century neoclassical and art deco buildings. The street has been famous since the Spanish era and once served as the city's main shopping center for more than a century. Eusebio Villanueva Building, a neoclassical building built in 1927, stands as one of the most iconic landmarks along Calle Real. Many other structures are also under heritage conservation.
address: J.M. Basa Street, Iloilo City Proper

name: Casa Real de Iloilo
description: The building, formerly the seat of the provincial government of Iloilo, has undergone numerous renovations and additions since it became the seat of the civil government in 1901. It was used as a military garrison by Japanese Imperial Forces during World War II. The building also hosted the Vin d'honneur (wine of honor) for the 117th Philippine Independence Day, led by President Benigno S. Aquino III—the first Vin d'honneur held outside Malacañang Palace.

name: Iloilo Customs House
description: Built in 1916, it is a neoclassical structure designed by American architect Ralph Harrington Doane. It stands as the second largest and second oldest American-era customs house in the Philippines, following those in Manila and Cebu.
address: Muelle Loney Street cor. Aduana Street, Iloilo City Proper

name: Molo Mansion
description: A neoclassical-art deco heritage mansion built in 1926 by Doña Petra Lacson, a matron of the Lacson clan, and Estanislao Yulo Yusay, a prominent lawyer and judge from Molo. The property has been restored and is now owned by the SM Group, housing several cafés, restaurants, and souvenir shops, including Kultura.
directions: in front of Molo Church, across Molo Plaza

name: Nelly Garden
description: Built in 1928 by the Lopez family, this Beaux-Arts mansion is one of Iloilo’s most elegant heritage houses. The property features sprawling gardens, neoclassical architecture, and preserved interiors showcasing the lifestyle of Iloilo’s early 20th-century elite. The mansion is not entirely open to the public and requires a tour or event reservation to enter, but visitors can still admire its grandeur from outside the gate.

name: Lizares Mansion
description: Built in 1937 by sugar baron Don Emiliano Lizares, this Beaux-Arts mansion features hardwood floors, elegant staircases, and classic architectural details. During World War II, it was occupied by the Japanese army. Today, it houses Angelicum School Iloilo and is occasionally open to visitors. The mansion is particularly popular during Christmas, when it is beautifully illuminated.

name: Camiña Balay Nga Bato
description: It was built in 1865 and was designed by the first parish priest of Molo, Anselmo Avanceña, for Don Fernando Avanceña and his wife, Eulalia Abaja. It is now operates as a living museum and restaurant, serving traditional Ilonggo cuisine including tsokolate tablea and local delicacies.

name: Casa Mariquit
description: The 200-year-old ancestral house of Doña Mariquit Lopez, the matriarch of the Lopez clan of ABS CBN. It also serves as a museum of the late Vice President Fernando Lopez, the husband of Doña Mariquit and the patriarch of the Lopez clan. Considered the oldest surviving house in Iloilo City, it is preserved as a museum showcasing furniture, photographs, and artifacts from the Spanish colonial period.

name: Old Iloilo City Hall
alt_name: University of the Philippines Visayas Main Building
description: Formerly the seat of the city government of Iloilo, the building now serves as the main building of the Iloilo City campus of the University of the Philippines (UP) Visayas.
address: General Luna Street cor. Infante Street, Iloilo City Proper
directions: inside the University of the Philippines Visayas - Iloilo City Campus

name: Museo Iloilo
description: Built in 1971, this provincial museum was the first government-sponsored museum in the Philippines outside Metro Manila. It houses a collection of artifacts, historical items, and exhibits on local culture, as well as temporary art and cultural displays. It’s an excellent place to explore Iloilo’s history, traditions, and artistic heritage.

name: National Museum Western Visayas
description: Housed in the former provincial jail, built in 1911, the museum features five galleries on its lower floor and an open gallery on the second floor, showcasing artifacts from across the Western Visayas region.

name: Museum of Philippine Economic History
description: The national museum narrates the evolution of the Philippine economy, highlighting major industries, historical developments, and Iloilo City’s role as the second-most important city in the Philippines during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
address: J.M. Basa Street cor. Ortiz Street, Iloilo City Proper

name: Museum of Philippine Maritime History
description: The national museum highlights the Philippines’ maritime heritage, featuring shipbuilding, trade, port activities, and Iloilo’s role as a major trading hub.
address: Muelle Loney Street cor. Aduana Street, Iloilo City Proper
directions: ground floor of Iloilo Customs House

name: Iloilo Museum of Contemporary Art
description: A three-floor art museum full of avant-garde artistic atmosphere. Compared with ordinary artworks, the works here incorporate the contemporary artists' ideas to express to the public. It has five exhibit halls and highlighting works from 42 different artists.
address: Festive Walk Road cor. Taft Street, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

name: Brandy Museum
description: It is the first and only museum in the Philippines dedicated to brandy.
address: Festive Walk Road cor. Taft Street, Mandurriao

name: Iloilo River Esplanade
description: A -long well-landscaped linear park along the banks of the Iloilo River. It is considered the longest linear park in the Philippines
directions: along the banks of the Iloilo River

name: Plaza Libertad
description: Also known as Plaza Alfonso XII, this central park in Iloilo City Proper is a National Historical Institute site for its role in the Philippine liberation. Surrounding the plaza are key landmarks, including the City Government Center, San Jose de Placer Church, heritage buildings like the Masonic Temple and Lacson Ancestral House, the Botica Lacson ruins, Iloilo Plaza Hotel (now LandBank), and nearby historic sites such as the Ker & Company Heritage Building and Ynchausti Mansion.

name: Graciano Lopez Jaena Park
description: One of the largest district plazas in the city, it is part of the Jaro Cultural Heritage Tourism Zone, alongside Jaro Cathedral, Jaro Belfry, and surrounding heritage ancestral houses. The plaza features several monuments and memorials, including a new shrine of Patrocinio Gamboa, the World War II Memorial Monument, and the Graciano Lopez Jaena Monument.

name: Molo Plaza
description: One of the six district plazas in the city, it features statues of Greek goddesses and a monument of Maria Clara. Like Jaro Plaza, it is surrounded by Molo Church and heritage ancestral houses such as Molo Mansion.

name: WaterWorld Iloilo
description: The first and largest waterpark in Western Visayas, it offers a fun and refreshing getaway for families and friends. It features thrilling water slides, wave pools, and play areas for kids, making it an ideal destination for all ages.
address: Datu Sumakwel Street, Alta Tierra Village, Jaro

name: El Dorado Waterpark
description: A family-friendly waterpark with pools designed for both kids and adults. Guests are welcome to bring their own food and drinks, making it perfect for picnics and casual weekend outings.

name: Vertex Bouldering Iloilo
description: The first indoor climbing gym in Iloilo City, it offers a challenging yet beginner-friendly space for those who want to experience the thrill of wall climbing. It’s a great place to train, exercise, and meet fellow climbing enthusiasts.

name: Iloilo Golf Driving Range
description: A relaxing spot to practice your golf swing, this driving range caters to both beginners and seasoned players looking to sharpen their skills in a laid-back environment.

name: Iloilo Golf and Country Club
description: Known as the oldest golf course in the Philippines, this beautifully maintained 18-hole course offers scenic greens and a peaceful atmosphere. Although located outside Iloilo City, it’s easily accessible via jeepneys, taxis, and private vehicles, making it a convenient escape for golf enthusiasts.

name: Deca Wakeboard Park
description: It offers an exciting wakeboarding experience for both beginners and pros. It’s situated just outside Iloilo City but remains easily accessible by public and private transport. The park also provides training sessions and a relaxing area for spectators.

name: The Boat Club Iloilo
description: A riverside leisure spot where visitors can dine, relax, and enjoy scenic cruises along the Iloilo River. Private boat rentals and chartered trips are available, including leisure cruising and selected trips toward the Iloilo Strait and Guimaras.

name: SM City Iloilo
description: The largest shopping mall in Iloilo City under the SM Supermalls chain, featuring a wide range of local and international retail stores, a department store, supermarket, cinemas, food courts, and numerous dining options. It serves as a major lifestyle and entertainment hub, conveniently located near the Iloilo Business Park and transport terminals.

name: Festive Walk Mall
description: A modern lifestyle mall within the Iloilo Business Park, known for its open-air Festive Walk Parade, high-end shops, cafés, and nightlife spots, managed by Megaworld Lifestyle Malls.

name: Robinsons Iloilo
description: A major shopping mall in the downtown area, offering a department store, supermarket, cinemas, and a wide selection of shops and restaurants, managed by Robinsons Malls.

name: SM Delgado
description: A smaller, centrally located SM mall in the downtown area, popular for quick shopping, groceries, and easy access to the city’s historic core.
address: Delgado Street cor. Valeria Street, Iloilo City Proper

name: MaryMart Center
description: A shopping center in the downtown area known for small retail stalls and affordable local boutiques, frequented by locals.

name: Gaisano City Iloilo
description: A shopping mall offering budget-friendly shopping, groceries, and basic dining options, part of the Gaisano Capital Group.

name: Robinsons Jaro
description: A shopping mall in Jaro with retail stores, a supermarket, a department store, cinemas, and dining options, managed by Robinsons Malls.

name: Nato & Helen Native & Seafood Restaurant

name: Waterfront Seafood & Cocktails
description: Combines fresh seafood with a lively, modern dining atmosphere, perfect for groups and nightlife vibes, with access to the Iloilo River Esplanade.
address: General Luna Street, Iloilo City Proper

name: The Granary

address: Richmonde Hotel Iloilo, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

name: Ramboy's Lechonan and Restaurant
description: Famous for its crispy lechon manok and a variety of Filipino comfort foods.

name: The Mango Tree Restaurant
description: A garden-themed restaurant offering a serene dining experience with a menu featuring Filipino and international dishes.

name: Theo's Restaurant and Bakery

name: Bavaria German Restaurant & Inn
description: A popular spot for families and gatherings, this restaurant serves authentic German flavors, including dishes like sausages and schnitzels.

name: Patpat’s Kansi House
description: Known for its version of the Ilonggo dish kansi, a sour beef soup, in a casual setting inside an ancestral house.

name: MO2 Ice Bar
description: A vibrant place for karaoke, billiards, dancing, drinks, and food, catering to both small groups and families.
address: Glicerio T. Pison Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

name: JLK Music Bar
description: Known for its lively atmosphere, neon lights, and a wide selection of drinks.
address: San Jose Street, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

address: City Times Square, Gaisano Iloilo City Center, Mandurriao

name: Bourbon Street Bar and Grill

address: The Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

name: Drink SLS
description: A chic lounge with stylish interiors, curated cocktails, and a lively atmosphere. It's a go-to spot for those seeking a sophisticated night out.
address: Festive Walk Parade, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

name: Bottle Ground
description: A dynamic resto-bar known for its vibrant ambiance, affordable cocktails, and a nostalgic playlist featuring '80s and '90s hits.
address: Festive Walk Parade, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

name: Madge Café
description: A historic café known for its traditional brewed coffee, since 1940.

name: Glory's Café
description: A traditional brewed coffee since 1948, now run by its third generation.

name: Bluejay Coffee & Co.
description: A contemporary café known for its specialty coffee, minimalist design, and a selection of baked goods.
address: Pacencia L. Tijam Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

name: Monkey Grounds Coffee
description: A hip café with a jungle-themed interior, serving specialty coffee and light bites in a relaxed setting.

name: OYO 562 Northview Inn

name: Battle of Alapan National Monument
description: Houses a giant flagpole with the Philippines flag. This site commemorates the Battle of Alapan, where the Philippine flag was first raised during the Philippine Revolution.

name: Diocesan Shrine and Cathedral Parish of Our Lady of the Pillar
description: Built during the Spanish era, it is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic church in Cavite and houses a venerated image of the Virgin Mary that is regarded as the most sacred in Cavite. Around the plaza are a few surviving colonial era structures such as the old municipal building and the ancestral residence of Daniel Tirona, whose fierce criticism of Andres Bonifacio during the Philippine Revolution triggered the civil war that split the Katipunan and culminated with Bonifacio's execution in 1897.
address: Imus Plaza, General Castañeda Street, Poblacion III-A

name: Isabel II Bridge
description: One of the few surviving Spanish-era bridges in the Philippines, it was the site of one of the earliest victories of the Katipunan against the Spanish during the 1896 revolution. In the middle of the bridge is a memorial plaque designed after the façade of Imus Cathedral with benches. At the approach beside Camp Pantaleon Garcia, the headquarters of the Cavite Police, is a monument to the battle.
directions: beside Camp Pantaleon Garcia/Cavite Provincial Police Office

name: Andres Bonifacio Monument
description: Andres Bonifacio went into hiding in Indang from the Magdalo faction of the Katipunan, but he was captured in 1897 at the barrio of Limbon following an encounter where his brother Ciriaco was killed and another brother, Procopio, was also captured. A monument and a historical marker is erected at the approximate location where Bonifacio was during his capture.

name: Indang Church
alt_name: Saint Gregory the Great Parish Church
description: Indang's central parish church, dating back to 1625. It was originally a chapel, and the present Baroque church, which has galvanized iron roofing and exquisite ceiling and wall paintings, dates back to 1953, rebuilt from the original destroyed during the Philippine Revolution.

name: Old Municipal Hall
description: One of the few surviving municipal buildings from the 19th century, it was where Andres Bonifacio and his brother, Procopio, were detained immediately after their capture from Barrio Limbon in 1897 before being transferred to Naic. It is now a local history museum.

name: Laya at Diwa
description: Meaning "Freedom and Spirit", it is a granite monument depicting a grouping of upright nude figures at the entrance to Cavite State University and surrounded by a wide park that is the only area of the campus open to the public.

name: Saint Anthony Falls
description: A two-tier waterfall that was partially dammed upstream to create rock basins for swimming.
directions: from the highway, travel along a short, unpaved road for 200 m

name: El Paseo
description: A mini-mall with a drugstore and Jollibee.

address: 025 H.Ilagan St. (formerly Plaridel street), Brgy. Poblacion 1

name: Sabangan Island
description: A quiet space surrounded by many trees as well as mangroves. You can lounge around the sand or play beach volleyball. On some areas, cooking is allowed so visitors can bring food without paying a corkage fee.

name: Balaki Island
description: Ideal for snorkeling, camping and swimming. And since this is a private island, getting access requires coordination with the Infanta Tourism Office and budget set aside for the gasoline of the boat and meals for the boat crew but the stay is free. The marine life in the vicinity is rich and healthy proof is the presence of seagrass around the island. Also the waters aren't too deep and the currents are calm so guests can enjoy they stay all day long.

name: Saint John the Evangelist Parish Church
description: Infanta's main Roman Catholic church.

name: Bubble Premium
description: Waffle and bubble tea.

name: Philtranco
description: Has two buses a day from Manila to Maasin via Legazpi and Tacloban.

name: Davao Metro Shuttle
description: Hourly buses between Sogod and Ormoc, passing by Inopacan

name: Bamboo beach Conalum
description: Beach resort with rooms. European/Asian restaurant with great view on the Cuatro islas. Rental service for motorbike and kayak. It is in the middle of many tourist hotspots. Beach terrace is available for venue.
directions: on the national road from Baybay to Maasin

name: Gaisano Grand Mall
description: Has a Gaisano supermarket.

name: Maris Bakeshop and Restaurant
description: Best in pastries and fast food.

name: Coffee Mari
description: Serving gourmet coffee with classy ambience.

name: Maris Rotisserie
description: Delicious lechon.

name: Pinoy's Chicken Inato
description: Sells "Fried Chicken Take-Out Treat" at ₱199. Or try its Chicken Inasal.

name: Iriga City Central Terminal
description: Opened 2005, it is a spartan structure serving all buses arriving at Iriga, as well as jeepneys coming from nearby towns. From there, you can catch a tricycle into the downtown.

name: Iriga Station
description: Philippine National Railways (PNR) operates a once-daily train between Naga and Legazpi. Bicol Commuter train 500 arrives at 5:51AM and the return trip (1720) at 6:58 PM.

name: Mount Iriga
description: An extinct volcano, its last recorded eruption was January 4, 1614 which formed Lake Buhi. It has an elevation of with Ilian Hill sits toward the bottom a few kilometers above barrio San Nicolas. After the 1614 eruption, a deep gully from the summit was formed. Wild berries and local pine trees (agoho, pronounced ah-goo-HAW) grow abundantly due to the rather cold environment.

name: Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
description: Once the supposed home of a witch (aswang) later became the place where the reenactment of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ in the hill of Calvary hence the name Calvario. During World War II, the Japanese Imperial Army took advantage of its strategic location of having a good view of the town proper, used it as a garrison. It is here where countless Irigueños who opposed their presence suffered imprisonment, torture and death.; The grotto provides a panoramic view of downtown Iriga and the surrounding barrios. In the early 1970s the hill was slowly developed, using the stone bricks from blasted boulders to build the Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes to its present grandeur.

name: Tinagba Park
description: Built to honor and commemorate the Lady of Lourdes. What was used to be the old children's park just below the church, became this beautiful park designed for everybody but more so for the children, the future of Iriga.

name: New Social Hall
description: Local farmers sun-dried their rice grain prior to milling. Local and neighboring basketball teams competed every summer. Special events and social gatherings as New Year's Eve masquerade balls were held here for many years. But during the monsoon season one could almost go swimming.; This new, sheltered building, hosts the same activities and more, sporting activities, social gatherings, special events, seminars and workshops, except rice drying.

name: Ilian Hill
description: At the bottom of Mount Iriga in Barangay San Nicolas, this promontory provides a panoramic view of Iriga City, Baao and Bato Lakes.

name: Inorogan Chapel
description: The chapel was built by a local philanthropist to commemorate the miraculous escape from the death and destruction by inhabitants during Mount Sumagang's eruption in 1614. The miracle is attributed to the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary whose image as Our Lady of Angustia was said to have been found at the present chapel site by Agta hunters.

name: Sampaguita Tourist Inn
description: Fan/a.c. single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Cathedral of Santa Isabel de Portugal
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Basilan and Prelature of Isabela, built in 1960s modern-art style with a distinctively Classical Roman mosaic for an altar wall.

name: Kaumpurnah Mosque
description: Historic seat of Islamic faith and teaching in Basilan, can be seen as you enter the Isabela Channel.

name: Alicia Church
alt_name: Our Lady of Atocha Parish Church
description: An 18th century heritage church.

name: Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park
description: An extensive protected area covering a large swathe of the Sierra Madre Mountains from the boundary with Cagayan to San Mariano town. Home to the indigenous Agta/Dumagat tribes, endemic species such as the Philippine crocodile, the Philippine eagle, the Isabela oriole, pitcher plants and virgin forests, in addition to 2000 m peaks that have never been named or climbed by humans.

name: Dunoy Lake
description: An isolated lake reachable only by a four-hour hike or by motorcycling on a single-lane trail, it is home to the endemic Philippine crocodile, which was rediscovered in the area in 1999. An observation tower provides sightseeing opportunities for the reptile as well as endemic birds.

name: Magat Dam
description: Opened in 1983, it was deemed the largest dam in Southeast Asia at the time and created a reservoir that displaced numerous communities in neighboring Ifugao. Since then it is one of the main sources of irrigation and electricity in the Cagayan Valley Region. The complex and its surroundings have become a favorite recreation spot for residents as well as day-trippers from Santiago. Fishing activities are also available at the reservoir.
address: Burgos-General Aguinaldo Road, Barangay General Aguinaldo, Ramon

name: Bambanti Festival
description: An annual festival celebrating Isabela's culture. Most major events are held at the amphitheater at Queen Isabela Park.

name: Isulan Public Transport Terminal
description: Buses and UV Express (minivans) all pick up and drop off passengers here. There are nothing much inside the terminal, except for noisy vendors.

name: CityMall
description: Mall with restaurants and an arcade.

name: Isulan Central Plaza
description: Little two-storey department store and supermarket with a Mang Inasal and Landbank ATM outside.

name: Carlito's
description: Fine Filipino dining.

name: Namaskar Ji Isulan
description: Indian cuisine.
directions: near the bus and van terminal

name: Inko's Grill
description: T-bone steaks, chicken inasal and silog. Serves alcohol.

name: Antonia's Hotel
description: Two-storey hotel with A/C rooms, but lacks a restaurant. Food available only by contract.

name: Jovinaj Traveller's Inn
description: Two storey hotel with A/C rooms, but lacks a restaurant.

name: Cavaywan Lake
description: A lake surrounded by reddish soil.

name: Santa Maria de Mayan Parish Church
description: Itbayat's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1872 but was reduced to ruins following an earthquake in 2019 and subsequent typhoons later that year and in 2025. The ruins can still be seen pending a proposed reconstruction.
directions: in front of the town plaza

name: Torongan Cliff
description: A cliff facing the Pacific coast where the first settlers to Itbayat are believed to have landed in 4000 BC. There is an indigenous Ivatan stone tomb called Axurud dating back to the precolonial era. It also has Torongan Cave, whose mouth was blocked by a typhoon and rendered inaccessible to visitors.

name: Mount Karoboboan
description: The highest point in Itbayat Island, with a height of 280 m. A viewdeck provides panoramic views over the island and the surrounding islets, while residents swear they can see city lights from Kaohsiung in Taiwan at night.

name: Mavulis Island
description: The northern-most island in the Philippines, home to native vegetation, coconut crabs, and a garrison of the Philippine military that forms the only human population, albeit on a rotational basis.

name: Rapang Cliff
description: A cliff facing the Pacific coast on a jagged series of finger-like promontories known as Karapangan, with a background of grass and rock. Nearby is the Stone Bell, a flat stone that creates a distinct sound resembling a ringing bell when hit and was used by the residents as an alarm clock, warning signal in case of invasion, and to call in their livestock.

name: Tachimus Port
description: A promontory on the Pacific coast home to a much-photographed Arius tree that continues to grow despite its truck being continuously bent by Itbayat's ferocious winds.

name: Paganaman Port
description: A sheltered cove facing the South China Sea. As the waves are calmer in this side of the island, it is used as a mooring area for the town's fishing fleet and is one of the few seaside areas where residents can swim, although the waves may still be to rough for outsiders. There are tidal pools and a subterranean cave known as the Blue Hole for the color of its waters.

name: Mount Riposed
description: A peak that dominates the southern half of Itbayat Island. The summit offers views reaching up to the uninhabited island of Dinem on the Pacific coast.

name: Mauyen Cliff
description: A series of 100 m drops at the southern coast of Itbayat that loom over Mauyen Port.

name: Yawran
description: A village composed of houses built in the indigenous Ivatan style called jinjin. Unlike the more famous stone houses in Batan Island and Sabtang, the ones in Itbayat are made of wood and thatched roofs.

name: Mount Ugu
description: At the boundary with Nueva Vizcaya, the 2150 m high peak offers trails that pass through native communities of the Kalanguya tribes and is becoming a favorite mountaineering destination among outdoor enthusiasts.

name: Saint Charles Borromeo Parish Church
description: Itogon's main Roman Catholic church, somewhat resembling a small chalet.

name: Binga Dam
description: A massive hydroelectric complex built in 1960 to control the waters of the Agno River. There is a viewdeck on site.

name: Mount Ulap
description: A 1846 m peak with grassy slopes on the boundary with Tuba. On a clear day, hikers can expect a sea of clouds below the summit.

name: Mount Pigingan
description: A 1328 m high peak.

name: Mount Bidawan
description: A 1120 m high peak. Along its trail is a shrine to the Virgin Mary called Ave Maria.

name: Mount Kotkot
description: A 1600 m high peak.

name: Balatoc Miner Statue
description: A small monument to the town's mining industry at one of the first exploited areas of Itogon, featuring a statue of a miner in his work attire carrying his tools.

name: Crosby Park
description: A popular recreational and picnic spot with pine groves.

name: 1300 Level Swimming Pool
description: A hot spring-fed watering hole

name: Mt. Camisong Forest Park and Events
description: An extensively-developed high-end mountain resort.
address: Benguet-Nueva Vizcaya Road, Sitio Peday, Loacan

name: San Vicente Port
description: An alternate, though less used port serving Sabtang.

name: Radiwan Port
description: The main port in town, servicing the faluwa ferries to and from Sabtang.

name: House of Dakay
description: The oldest house in Batanes, built in 1887 in the traditional Ivatan way of using stones and thatched roofs.

name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
description: Ivana's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1795.
directions: in front of the old port and across from the Honesty Store

name: San Jose Bridge
description: A rare Spanish-era arched stone bridge that remains in use.

name: Ivana Lighthouse
description: Built beside Radiwan Port, it guards over the strait separating Batan Island from Sabtang.

name: Maydangeb Beach
description: A secluded stretch of white sand near the boundary with Mahatao.

name: Toblerone Hills
description: A series of moss- and grass-colored limestone hills named after its resemblance to the logo of the Swiss chocolate brand.

name: Honesty Store and Coffee Shop
description: Probably Ivana's most famous landmark, it is a store with a self-service cafe next door deliberately left without attendants, leaving its components to the mercy of the customer's moral scruples. Payment its deposited in a box, while you may have to knock next door if you need change. The fact that it has a generally stellar record of not being robbed is a testament to Batanes' low crime rate and Ivatan honesty.

name: Honesty Homestay
description: An accommodation run by the owners of the Honesty Store.

name: Metro Bank
description: It has a Mastercard and Visa card ATM.

name: Idea Pension House.
description: fan single/double room with own bathroom.

name: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish Church
description: Jalajala's main Roman Catholic church.

name: Mount Sembrano
description: An extinct 745 m volcano at the head of the Jalajala peninsula that is frequented by hikers due to its proximity to Metro Manila and its commanding views of Laguna de Bay into Talim Island and as far as Mount Makiling, on the southwestern shores of the lake.

name: Dragon Wellness Farms
description: An agritourism site featuring a dragonfruit farm.

name: Jolo Airport
description: Bangsamor Air from Zamboanga and Cotabato.

name: Bud Dajo
description: Volcanic cinder cone and the highest point in the province of Sulu. Site of a battle in 1906; see Mindanao#Understand.

name: Jovellar Underground River
description: Dry caving and underground river adventure experience. Short hike are expected. There are caves and rock formations. Life jackets, local guides and boatmen are available.

name: Detour Computer Rentals and Services
address: La Zona Dorada Bldg. Guanzon Street

name: Gaisano Mall of Kabankalan
description: Has a supermarket.

name: PNB Bank
description: Has a Visa Card ATM.

name: BPI Bank
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: Dexter's Pizza
address: La Zona Dorada Bldg. Guanzon Street

name: Breadbox Bakery
address: La Zona Dorada Bldg. Guanzon Street

name: The Happy Cup
description: A coffee shop that also has beer.

name: Hans Guest house
description: AC double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Perico Pension House
description: AC double with own bathroom. All rooms have cable TV.

name: South Gate Inn
description: AC room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Mount Pulag
description: At 2928 m, it is the second highest mountain in the Philippines, and the highest in Luzon. It also forms the triboundary between Nueva Vizcaya, Benguet and Ifugao.

name: National Museum of the Philippines - Kabayan
description: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, featuring artefacts on Cordilleran natural history, art, ethnography and culture. It was built to find a suitable location for the study and preservation of the mummies of Kabayan from looting, and has one mummy on display.

name: Timbac Caves
description: A series of caves used as burial sites for the mummies of Kabayan. Having been extensively damaged by looters, access to the site is partially restricted to protect the remaining mummies interred in situ.

name: Lake Tabeyo
description: Part of a grouping of four lakes in the area collectively known as the Four Lakes of Kabayan, it is the most accessible lake and has a campsite and ranger station.

name: Lake Incolos
description: Part of the Four Lakes of Kabayan, although it is actually more of a peat bog than a lake. Even if it looks dry, avoid walking over it lest you sink into the quagmire.

name: Lake Latep-Ngapos
description: Part of the Four Lakes system, located in a secluded forest trail.

name: Lake Ambulalakaw
description: The cleanest among the Four Lakes, with swimming prohibited to maintain water quality.

name: Junior Pulag
description: A section of the Tabeyo Trail leading to the Four Lakes and Mount Tabayoc named after its resemblance to the grass and moss-covered summit of Mount Pulag.

name: Mount Tabayoc
description: The second highest mountain of Luzon and the fifth highest in the Philippines. It also forms part of the boundary between Kabayan and the municipality of Tinoc in Ifugao province.

name: Opdas Cave
description: An ossuary reminiscent of the Catacombs of Rome or Paris.

name: Saint John the Baptist Parish Church
description: The church was built in the 18th century but was neglected through much of the 20th century when it was downgraded into a chapel due to the government's decision to move the town center of Kalayaan from Longos to San Juan. After recovering its parish status in 1996, the church was gradually repaired. The church's façade, partially covered by moss complimented by the shrub-lined plaza in front, gives off a garden-like air. Its doors and carvings have been preserved from the Spanish era, while its interior has also been preserved save for the roof, which was rebuilt following typhoon damage in 2006. Among the interior's highlights is the botafumeiro or thurible, the ornate altar, and the bas reliefs in the baptistery. The church is also frequently used as a shooting location for domestic films and television series.
directions: not to be confused with the modernist-looking structure located along the highway in Barangay San Juan that is dedicated to Saint John the Evangelist

name: Kalayaan Twin Falls
description: A set of waterfalls with four other minor cascades that is a favorite swimming spot for locals during the summer months.

name: Kalayaan Balete Tree
description: An imposing strangler fig tree along a cliffside road.

name: Plaza Lagumbay
description: A small square and recreational space with civic monuments and a Hollywood-like Kalayaan sign.
directions: in front of Kalayaan Municipal Hall

name: Kalayaan Welcome Marker
description: A cliffside spot at the boundary between Kalayaan and Lumban overlooking the Caliraya power plant that offers panoramic views over Laguna de Bay into Mount Sembrano in neighboring Rizal province.

name: Caliraya Lake
description: A man-made reservoir created in 1939 following the damming of the Caliraya river. A favorite spot for watersports, fishing and camping activities, with an increasing number of Metro Manilans setting up retirement homes along the shore. The lake is shared by the municipalities of Cavinti, Kalayaan and Lumban.

name: Kalibo International Airport
directions: 2 km east of Kalibo and 68 km from Caticlan port

name: Ceres Liner and Ceres Transport
description: Buses arrive at Kalibo from Manila, Caticlan, Roxas City, Iloilo City, and San Jose de Buenavista. description: The fifth longest cave in the country at . name: Aguinaldo Shrine
description: The sprawling house, built in 1849, is the ancestral home of Emilio Aguinaldo, the first President of the Philippines. It is now a museum. It is where independence from Spain was declared on June 12, 1898. The house’s balcony is where the Philippine president annually raises the Philippine flag on Independence Day.The basement has an exhibition dedicated to Aguinaldo’s life and role in the Philippine Revolution, while the upper floors, which contain Aguinaldo’s living quarters, focus on how the Aguinaldo family lived. The grounds of the house is lush with greenery bordered by a river on the east and backed by a fish pond to the south. Aguinaldo's grave lies at the backyard. A nearby outhouse sells souvenirs. Expect hordes of field-tripping schoolchildren from Metro Manila and nearby places on some days. In front of the house is Aguinaldo Park, which has an equestrian statue of Aguinaldo and stalls selling snacks and refreshments.

name: St. Mary Magdalene Church

name: Baldomero Aguinaldo Shrine

name: Bottleground Bar & Lounge

name: Victoria Court Las Piñas
description: Mid-range option for overnight stays, but has a reputation as a "short-time" hotel hosting illicit sex. Rooms have modern designs, with cable TV, and a few has indoor hot tubs. Has free breakfast and WiFi. Filipino-Japanese fusion ramen dishes are served, starting at ₱150.

name: RedDoorz Plus near Bamboo Organ Las Piñas
description: Kind of like a business hotel.

description: Practical hotel with wifi and a/c.

name: Mella Hotel
description: Full-service hotel with restaurant, outdoor pool, gym, massage service, and kids lounge.

directions: near SM City Legazpi and Ibalong Center

name: Philtranco
description: Three daily buses leave Pasay every 6:30PM, 7PM, and 8PM. They also have buses going south as far as Davao and Cagayan de Oro via Tacloban and Butuan, which stop at Daraga.

name: Amihan
description: Philtranco's sister bus line, with a similar schedule, but with departures from Cubao.

name: Raymond Transportation
description: Has a daily trip from Cubao.

name: Superlines
description: Three departures from Cubao every 6:30PM, 10:30PM, and 5:30AM.

name: Passenger Terminal Building PMO-Legazpi
description: Has boats to Rapu-Rapu, and is being developed as a cruise terminal to serve domestic and foreign cruises.

name: Bicol Heritage Park
description: Has a statue of General Simeon Ola. Site at the Camp Simeon Ola headquarters featuring monuments, including one of General Ola.

name: General Jose Ignacio Paua Statue
description: Paua is the only pure-blood Chinese who supported the Katipunan during the Philippine Revolution.
address: Lerma Street corner Emilio Jacinto Street, Barrio Bañadero

name: Legazpi City Museum and Library
alt_name: Albay Provincial Library and Information Center
description: Deals with the history of Legazpi. Well-maintained place with a high standard. The sculptures, paintings, historical photos and dioramas are especially interesting.

name: Liberty Bell
description: Housed on a concrete dome structure. This bronze bell was a gift from the Americans (the 158th Infantry Regimental Combat team of the US 6th Army) command led by Brig. General Hanford Macnider and Captain Hoomer Mcgee) in 1945 after the liberation of the city from the Japanese occupiers. A side note within is inscribed "Whenever oppression knocks at your door, feel free to ring this bell".

name: Peñaranda Park
description: Has a statue of Jose Maria Peñaranda, the first governor of Albay. Around the park is Legazpi City Hall, Albay Capitol and St. Gregory the Great Cathedral.

name: Pinarik Viewdeck
description: Offers a truly breathtaking experience that captures the essence of natural beauty. Nestled amidst lush landscapes and towering trees, this vantage point provides an unparalleled panoramic view that leaves one speechless. The vast expanse of rolling hills and valleys is adorned with vibrant hues, creating an awe-inspiring canvas that changes with the light of the day. The serenity of the surroundings invites introspection, making it a perfect spot for those seeking solace in nature's embrace. The well-maintained facilities and thoughtful amenities enhance the overall experience. Whether you're an avid photographer, a nature enthusiast, or simply in search of tranquility, the Pinarik Viewdeck promises an unforgettable encounter with the wonders of the natural world.

name: St. Gregory the Great Cathedral
description: The episcopal seat of the Diocese of Legazpi, it was first built by Spanish missionaries as a wooden chapel in 1581. The present church, designed by then governor Don Jose Ma. de Peñaranda, was built in 1839 using volcanic rocks.

name: Karangahan Falls
description: Has a deep catch basin ideal for swimming.

name: Battle of Legazpi Pylon
description: A high monument built to commemorate the defeat of Filipino fighters by American forces in 1900. The pylon marks the site of a bloody battle during the Philippine-American War and World War II.
directions: At the corner with Rizal Street

name: Headless Monument
description: It is dedicated to the unknown heroes who died in the Japanese occupation of Legazpi City during World War II.

name: Ibalong Heroes Monument
description: A monument named after the complete Bicolano folk epic Ibalong. Based on another Asian epic the Ramayana and was allegedly narrated by an ancient sage called Kandunung. The three heroes of the story, Baltog, Handyong, and Bantong are featured as relief with their names in the ancient Baybayin characters on each post.
directions: at the junction of Bicol 630 and Quezon Avenue and near a college school

name: Kapuntukan Hill
description: Provides a view of the Embarcadero, the Port District, Albay Gulf, and Mayon Volcano.

name: Legazpi Boulevard
description: A picturesque seaside road along the city's southern coastline with wide promenades, bike lanes, monuments such as the statue of Miguel López de Legazpi, JCI Legazpi Tourism Marker and the Freemason Obelisk, restaurants, cafés, and pubs.

name: The Obelisk
description: A monument which is built as a joint project between the city government and Masonic Lodge No. 61.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe Shrine (Legazpi City)
description: It features life-sized depictions of Stations of the Cross and a huge statue of the Virgin of Guadalupe at the summit.

name: St. Raphael the Archangel Church
description: The original church was built in 1834 under the auspices of Pedro Romero, but was destroyed during the liberation of Legazpi by Allied forces in 1945. A more modern church was rebuilt in its place. Notable features include an altar table made of a single block of hardened lava rock.

name: Plaza Rizal
description: It has a fountain and a monument to José Rizal, the country's national hero, sculpted by National Artist Napoleon Abueva in 1966.
directions: In front of Saint Raphael Church de Legazpi

name: Sawangan Park
description: Very nice place to relax, just do a simple walk or jog around the area. The park is so clean. No mosquitoes and smells good even if the area is near the port. There are food kiosks and you can enjoy eating with your friends or family

name: Albay Gulf Landing Monument
description: Built in 1995 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Landing of the Allied American Forces in Legazpi City.

name: Albay Park and Wildlife
description: A picnic grove and a zoological park combined. Quaint city park hosting a diverse array of wildlife, including crocodiles, pigs & eagles.

name: Ligñon Hill
description: Pronounced leeng-YAWN, it is a peak with a nature park at its summit offering panoramic views of the city and Mayon Volcano, and adventure activities like ziplining.

name: Giant Statue of Nuestra Señora de Salvacion
description: A towering religious monument dedicated to Our Lady of Salvation, a patroness celebrated for protection and blessings among local devotees.

name: Padang Memorial Cross
description: A monument dedicated to the victims of Typhoon Durian ("Reming") in 2006, which destroyed parts of the city. The location is right beside the highway. There are no parking spaces available except for the highway's shoulder. Visitors should take extra precaution alighting from their vehicles as there are lots of fast moving vehicles on the highway. There are no trees at all to hide under when the sun gets too hot or any covered areas should it rain.

name: Our Lady of Fatima Church de Legazpi City
description: A modern church with a semi-circular nave built in 1999.

name: Imelda Park
description: Has pavilions, a playground, and a basketball court. Also at the park is Mag-Ilusyon, a metal sculpture by artist Eduardo Castrillo, commissioned in 1976.

name: Our Lady of Perpetual Help Parish Church
description: It is also known as the Redemptorist Church and Our Lady of Perpetual Help is the patron.
directions: near the Marison hotel opposite side of the hotel

name: A. Bichara Silverscreens and Entertainment Center
Ibalong Festival
description: This non-religious festival based on the Ibalong Epic is held in August. It celebrates the epic story Ibalong who was accompanied by three legendary heroes, namely Baltog, Handyong, and Bantong. People parade in the streets wearing masks and costumes to imitate the appearances of the heroes and the villains, portraying the classic battles that made their way into the history of Bicol. The Ibalong Festival aims to express warmth and goodwill to all people; visitors and tourists are encouraged to celebrate with the Bicolanos.

name: Embarcadero de Legazpi
description: A marina-inspired waterfront lifestyle hub, commercial and entertainment center in the city's port area. It also hosts the first Duty Free Philippines store in Bicol.

name: Pacific Mall

name: Yashano Mall Legazpi

address: Rizal St., corner Imperial & Marquez Sts., Old Albay District, Legazpi City

name: Albay Pili Nut

name: 1st Colonial Grill
description: A well known restaurant in the area that is famous for inventing the Sili ice-cream, a chili-infused ice-cream that is a core part of Bicol cuisine. There are three branches in Legazpi: SM Legazpi, Pacific Mall, and near the Bicol University College of Education.

name: BIGG'S Diner
description: A famous fast food chain in the Bicol region serving various comfort Western and Filipino foods.

name: Sol at Hotel Areca
description: A high-end restaurant that is part of Hotel Areca, serving both high quality local and international cuisine. Hotel guests have a 10% discount.

name: Catalinas Lodging House

It offers rooms completely furnished with a 32-inch LCD television set with satellite cable TV connection, high-speed internet access, NDD/IDD telephone, in-room safe, and an electronic door lock system. Amenities include Essences Spa, Salon Mye, a fitness center, and a kiddie activity room.

name: Fantasy World
description: 300 ha theme park, though incomplete and closed to the public. It has been once used in some local fantasy-themed television dramas in the 2000s. This is, however, a common stopover for picture-taking by tourists travelling from Tagaytay to Taal.

name: Casa Corazon Motorcycle Museum
description: A private collection with many bikes and some classic cars. Lots of BMW machines including one from World War II with a machine gun mounted on the sidecar. The complex also includes a restaurant, hotel and some park areas.

description: Lemery's main parish church, it dates back to 1887, and used to have a Neoclassical façade with two belfries. It was badly damaged by aerial bombing at the end of World War II in 1945, and the façade was replaced by a modernist one in 1968, with the belfries demolished.

name: Jamocha Cafe & Bistro

description: A/C rooms with cable TV, gym and heated shower rooms.

name: Orlando's Beach Resort

name: San Juanico Bridge
description: This spans the San Juanico Strait from Tacloban to Santa Rita on Samar Island. At 2.16 km long, it was the longest bridge spanning a body of seawater in the Philippines until the Cebu-Cordova bridge opened in 2022.

name: Agas-Agas Bridge

Matabungkay

name: The Coral Beach Club
description: Less than 2 hours drive from Manila. European and Asian cuisines, a pool and jacuzzi, a hot stones massage, and a hair salon are available on premises, and the Calatagan Golf Club is nearby.

name: Bulalacao Hill

name: Kawa-Kawa Hill
description: Kawa-Kawa (or formerly Lunad) is a hill with a crater, that looks like a giant cauldron, or kawa in the local language of Albay Bikol, and serves as both an ecotourism site and a pilgrimage site. People who climbed this hill described it as a huge amphitheater, a sliced coconut, or a hill without a top. From a distance, it looks like an ordinary hill, but up there, you'll feel its uniqueness with the calm winds and breezes blowing through it, and you can also get a full view of the city. The hill is also a pilgrimage site, with a Way of the Cross (Via Crucis) featuring images created by a sculptor from Paete, Laguna. The Via Crucis here is unique as it follows a walkway up the hill, where the first six stations are placed, with the remaining 8 forming the path circling the crater.
directions: It is 2 km from downtown as the crow flies but is a 30-minute drive.

name: Malison Spring Resort

name: Berman Ice Cream Haus
description: Halo-Halo ice cream (ice cream sandwich), Banana split, halo-halo, tapsilog, and pancit are available.

address: Entrances:9th corner Gat Tayaw Streets and 8th corner San Juan Streets (for vehicles), Mabini Street (for pedestrians only), Barangay Pag-asa

name: Heritage Houses
description: Liliw retains a sizeable number of houses from the colonial era, some of which have been converted into restaurants or commercial outlets. These are concentrated in the town center, particularly in San Juan, Gat Tayaw, Plaza Rizal, and P. Burgos Streets.

name: Liliw Church of Christ
description: A white-painted, Gothic inspired church that is one of the oldest Protestant places of worship in the country, established in 1904.

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people.

name: Bukal Falls
description: A waterfall at the boundary of Majayjay and Liliw that is claimed by both municipalities.

name: Pamilihang Bayan ng Liliw
description: The town’s central market

name: B.N. Badong Footwear Trading
description: One of the oldest footwear stores in Liliw, in operation since the 1960s. Also sells purses.

name: Arabela
description: Italian dishes, not limited to pasta and pizza, and a selection of cakes and pastries at their bakery. Location rather quite has too low headroom (approximately 5′3″), as the dining area used to be the basement of a colonial-era residence.
price: House style pasta: ₱270-300; pesto: ₱280-320; pizza: ₱290-405 (depending on size and thickness)

name: American Ribs & Wings
description: A chicken wings and pork ribs chain offering meals paired with rice. Group-sized platters are also available.

name: Caffè Lilio
description: A restaurant serving coffee, pastry, pasta and sandwiches inside a converted heritage house.

name: Mang Larry's Artisanal Distillery

name: Tree Farm
description: A/C rooms with hot water shower. Has a swimming pool, basketball and volleyball court, gym, and strawberry farm.

name: San Fernando El Rey Parish Church

name: Urduja House

name: Casa Real

name: Lingayen Cathedral

description: Shopping mall.

description: Filipino restaurant.

description: Italian restaurant.

El Jardine Fastfood And Catering Services

name: Bergamo Hotel
description: A 3-minute walk from the Basing River, this relaxed hotel is 3 km from both Lingayen Beach along the West Philippine Sea and Lingayen Airport.

name: Lipa City Grand Terminal
description: A large bus station opened in the early 2010s, and also serves some jeepneys and UV Express. Buses arrive at the front, and jeepneys and UV Express at the back. The terminal is built over one of SM City Lipa's parking areas, which is moved above to provide space for the structure. While large, it is rather functional, but there are also a few food kiosks and a small Alfamart store.

name: Robinsons Place Lipa Passenger Terminal
description: Serves as terminus for the Batangas City-Lipa (BN-02), and Calamba-Lipa via Tanauan routes, as well as UV Express coming from Calamba, San Pablo, and Ibaan.

name: Lipa-Rosario jeepney terminal
description: Serves the jeepney routes coming from Rosario and San Juan

name: Casa de Segunda Katigbak
description: The ancestral home of prominent Batangas family, the Casa is a typical "Bahay na Bato" (stone house). It is Spanish Colonial in style, yet tropical in ambiance. It was named after Segunda Katigbak, reputed to be the first love of Dr. Jose P. Rizal, the Philippines' national hero. Casa Segunda was declared by the National Historical Commission as a heritage house for having harbored generations of artists, poets and persons of learning and distinction.

name: San Sebastian Cathedral de Lipa
description: A reconstruction of a 19th century church that was bombed out in World War II, serving as the seat of the Archdiocese of Lipa. It has a narrower nave and higher ceiling than most churches. Its highlights are the cupola, the high altar and the ceiling frescoes loosely based on the Sistine Chapel.
address: C.M. Recto Avenue corner G. Solis Street

name: Mary Mediatrix of All Grace Parish
description: Church and monastery complex, site of the 1947 Marian apparitions that was not recognized by the Vatican, which has not discouraged a faithful following in Batangas and is supported by the Archdiocese of Lipa, which continues to gather evidence of the apparitions in the hopes of persuading the Holy See to reconsider.
address: Lipa-Padre Garcia Road, Antipolo del Norte

name: Marian Orchard
description: Serene Roman Catholic pilgrimage site in the middle of rainforest, most frequented every Holy Week as part of Visita Iglesia itineraries. There is a chapel, Stations of the Cross, Our Lady of Lourdes grotto, carillon bell, and rows of statues of various saints. Souvenirs and food are available near the chapel and carillon bell.

Amenities and attractions restaurant, swimming pool, replica Buddha, themed cottages, hanging bridge and zipline. Resort also provides views of Taal Lake. name: Shercon Resort and Ecology Park
