name: The Suites at Mount Malarayat
address: Mount Malarayat Golf and Country Club

name: Loboc Church Of San Pedro
description: Built in 1734

name: Loboc River Cruise
description: A river cruise lasts about 90 minutes. In addition to a buffet lunch, the cruise will dock alongside stations on the river that feature ethnic dance and music performances. On-board, a prevalent scam features a photographer offering "free photographs." However, despite using simple point-and-shoot or outdated DSLR cameras, the act of taking the photo is the only free aspect; the emailed JPEG alone starts at ₱2000 without haggling and you may not be permitted to leave without agreeing on a price.
directions: at the bridge across from San Pedro church
price: ₱850 with buffet lunch. {₱100 for soft drinks. Tipping is expected for the dancers.

name: Loboc Ecotourism Adventure
description: Cable car (420 m) and zipline (520 m).

name: Angel's Burgers
description: Buy one take one. They also sell soft drinks and coffee.

name: Loboc Backpackers Inn
description: fan dorm with two beds. shared bathroom

name: Fox & The Firefly Cottages
description: Dorm beds and rooms.

name: Nuts Huts
description: Dorm and rooms.

name: Maria Makiling
description: A diwata, (equivalent of a fairy or goddess) who has been the guardian spirit of the mountain since long before the Spanish arrived. There are many legends about her; in some she is Dian Masalanta, the ancient Tagalog goddess of love, pregnancy and childbirth, while in Christian versions she is named Maria and attends church often.

name: University of the Philippines, Los Baños
description: Primarily a university of agriculture. There are some places of interest within its administered area:.

name: Makiling Botanic Gardens
description: Little streams and rivulets cut through the demonstration garden.

name: UPLB Museum of Natural History
description: Biological & zoological exhibits. Hopefully it won't be a field trip day for all the Metro Manila schools.

name: International Rice Research Institute
description: On a large (252 hectares, 620 acres) experimental farm. In the 1960s and 1970s, the facility pioneered the development of fast-growing and large-yielding "miracle rice" varieties, along with controversial genetically-modified produced.

name: Mount Makiling Forest Reserve
description: Formerly a national park, now a reserve administered by the university's forestry department. It is adjacent to the campus and, like the campus, includes some sites of interest.

name: National Arts Center
description: A school for young artists managed by the Cultural Center of the Philippines. Perhaps what stands out most though are the truly exceptional views of Lake Laguna.

name: Boy Scout of the Philippines Campground
description: A campsite at the foot of Mount Makiling

name: Paciano Rizal Shrine
description: Jose Rizal's older brother, Paciano, became a general in the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American War. When peace came, Paciano moved to Los Baños and bought a plot of land from which he built a house in 1927 and did farming. The private residence is still owned by Rizal's heirs and is open only by prior arrangement, but contains a museum dedicated to Paciano's life complete with personal effects.

name: Immaculate Conception Parish
description: The main Roman Catholic church in Los Baños, dating from the 17th century, although its appearance has been significantly altered by modern cement renovations.

name: Dampalit Falls
description: Small waterfall
directions: at the back of the National Arts Center

name: General Yamashita Memorial Monument
description: In 1946, General Tomoyuki Yamashita, the "Tiger of Malaya", was executed by hanging at this site following his conviction for war crimes committed by Japanese forces during World War II, including the conversion of UPLB into a concentration camp. A small shed housing a simple tombstone with Japanese inscription now stands at the site. A few meters to the back is a similar shrine to General Masaharu Homma, who was hanged after being held responsible for Japanese atrocities during the Bataan Death March in 1942.

name: Magnetic Hill
description: An elevated site where an optical illusion makes it appear that cars move on their own or in the opposite direction.

name: Mount Makiling
description: Fine hiking destination, not only to the peak but also en route through the UPLB-owned Mount Makiling Forest Reserve. Birding and sightseeing opportunities avail (as in big views of surrounding territory). But take ample water, watch out for leeches, and be prepared to come back sticky and withered after completing the 3200 ft (Peak 2 being the highest point) ascent and back. Takes about 4–5 hours each way, so plan to make it a full day outing. Some sites associated with the trek are Flatrocks (river cascade), Mudspring (often mistaken as volcanic crater of Mt. Makiling)
directions: start from gate at end of Makiling Rd on UPLB campus next to Makiling Center for Mountain Ecosystems

name: Batong Malake Public Market
description: A nearer public market to UPLB.

name: Seoul Kitchen
description: Good for if you need a Korean fix.
address: F.O. Santos st, corner Pearl St

name: Spice Jar Restaurant
description: Good Mexican food plus a few Filipino dishes, pizza, donuts, & expensive steaks. No guacamole or margueritas.
directions: about a block from Robinson's, same side of street

name: The Crunch
description: Homemade cakes, pastries, and specialty coffee.
address: 2nd floor of Vega Center, in front of UPLB gate

name: Splash Mountain Resort Hotel
description: Pool with slides and lazy river, spa, gym.

name: Hillspa Resort
description: Pool, waterslide.

name: La Roca De Trinidad
description: Casa Florentina 1, 2, 3 for groups

name: Makiling Onsen Hotel and Restaurant
description: Japanese style resort with onsen (hot spring) where you can even put on a yakuta (kimono).

name: Splash Oasis Hotel
description: More pool/spa bliss, with a restaurant.

name: Diosdado Macapagal Museum and Library
alt_name: NHCP Museo at Aklatan ni Diosdado Macapagal
description: It was built behind the bahay kubo where Diosdado Macapagal, the 9th President of the Philippines, once lived. Inside the museum are historical photographs of Macapagal and other memorabilia, and a replica of the Office of the President's desk.

name: San Agustin Church
description: The oldest parish church in Pampanga, it has a neoclassical façade and a stone brick structure. The church building and belfry that stands today dates back to 1638. It was declared a National Historical Site in 1952, and an Important Cultural Property in 2013. As of 2026, access to the interior is restricted due to renovations and repairs to undo damage caused by a 2019 earthquake.

name: Museo ni Jose B. Lingad
description: A museum about the life of Jose B. Lingad (pronounced “ling-gad”), a Kapampangan politician who held senior positions in the provincial government, the executive branch and the national legislature before being assassinated in 1980 when he was a political opponent of President Ferdinand Marcos and his martial law dictatorship. The complex, which converted Lingad's simple two-story ancestral house into exhibition space, also features a monument of Lingad set in a spacious park.

name: Plaza Lubao
description: Lubao's main square, featuring a bust of President Macapagal, trees and a Hollywood-like sign of Lubao.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Pradera Verde Golf Club
description: A golf course set in an eponymous tourism and luxury residential estate. The complex also has its own airfield, and hosts the annual Lubao International Balloon and Music Festival.
address: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Barangay Prado Siongco

name: Lubao Bamboo Hub & Eco-Park
description: An ecotourism park on the Lubao wetlands featuring an extensive bamboo grove. As of 2026, the complex is closed for renovations.

name: Santa Cruz Public Market
address: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Barangay Santa Cruz

name: Hermano Pule Monument
description: A shrine to Apolinario de la Cruz, better known as Hermano Pule, who founded the Cofradia de San José, who fought for religious and civil rights during the Spanish colonial era. Pule lead a rebellion from 1840 until his execution in 1841.
directions: Near the junction to Majayjay, Laguna

name: Kamay Ni Hesus Healing Church
description: Roman Catholic pilgrimage site on the foot of Mount Banahaw, frequently visited during Holy Week. It houses a replica of Noah's Ark, a healing church, family park and pond. Group tours can be organized from Lucena.

name: La Casa de Doña Ana
description: A large Bahay na Bato (stone house) built in Neoclassical style by a local couple. Among the ancestral homes in town, only the Casa is designed with that style.

name: San Luis Obispo Parish Church
alt_name: Lucban Church, St. Louis of Toulouse Parish
description: A Baroque 18th century church that has a bone relic of its patron saint.

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people. On the slopes of the mountain covered by Lucban is Banahaw de Lucban, a parasitic cone that protrudes from the main landmass.

name: Mortuary Chapel Ruins
description: These are what remains of the old mortuary church of Lucban Public Cemetery. built in the late 1700s on top of a hill overlooking the town, this church features two belfries and a magnificent ornately designed façade which is quite unique for this type of church. although the church is now in ruins the exterior is still well preserved, though weathered.

name: Buddy's Restaurant
description: The flagship branch of a restaurant chain that began in Lucban in 1985 and has since spread across the Calabarzon region and Metro Manila. It serves Lucban and Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
address: 99 Rizal Avenue corner San Luis Street, Barangay 8
directions: in front of Plaza de Revolucion

name: Kalesa Inn
description: Home stay in the Poblacion, having A/C rooms with basic amenities

name: Samkara Restaurant and Garden Resort
description: A farm-themed hotel, resort and restaurant complex in a rural setting, along the border with Majayjay, Laguna.

name: Lucena Grand Terminal
description: Central bus station serving as terminal for buses headed for Lucena, as well as a stopover for some long-distance buses. There are two departure areas: one to the west for services within Quezon Province, Alabang (on AB Liner and P&O), Batangas City and Bicol, and another for services to Manila (Pasay or Cubao) and Alabang (on Dela Rosa Express). Buses unload at curbside in between the departures areas. At the arrivals area and the intra-provincial departures area is a food court with kiosks and pasalubong shops, and on the Manila-bound departures are a Jollibee and Chowking, a cafe, a BPI ATM and food kiosks.

name: Dela Rosa Express
description: Regular AC buses run from Alabang South Station to Lucena via South Luzon Expressway and Maharlika Highway.

name: Superlines
description: Bus services between Manila, Bondoc Peninsula, and Bicol. Buses either AC or "ordinary" non-AC, with on-board restrooms.

name: P&O Transport
description: All-AC bus services from eastern Quezon (Calauag, Tagkawayan, Guinayangan), Ragay (Camarines Sur), and Santa Elena (Camarines Norte) to Manila (via Maharlika Highway) and Batangas City (via Eco-Tourism Road), with some trips terminating at Lucena.

name: Supreme
description: Buses come from Batangas City, via Ibaan, Rosario, San Juan and Candelaria. Fare is at around ₱133 for a regular AC bus (₱119.25 for ordinary).
directions: Terminal/depot near St. Alphonsus Seminary and in front of Seaoil. Local transportation through the City Proper-Isabang, Tayabas jeepney route

name: Dalahican Ferry Terminal
description: Montenegro Shipping Lines (with M/V Marie Kristina) and Starhorse Lines (with M/V Virgen de Peñafrancia) operates ferries to and from Marinduque island. Getting there: There are jeepneys from downtown Lucena, and takes 5 minutes. Some buses from Manila terminate here.

name: Quezon Provincial Capitol
description: A grand Neoclassical building that houses the provincial government offices of Quezon province. It dates back to 1908, and is a National Historical Site. Perfect place to get your photo with Quezon marker sign.

name: Lucena City Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Lucena, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1882.

name: Governor's Mansion
description: The official residence of the governor of Quezon, built during the Spanish period.

name: Lucena Perez Park
description: Small green space honoring former governor Don Filemon Perez with stone monuments and a playground.

name: Heroes' Lane
description: Tourist attraction.

name: SM City Lucena
description: Has a supermarket.
address: Maharlika Highway corner Dalahican Road, Ibabang Dupay
directions: Provincial buses terminating at Dalahican port stop here

name: Pacific Mall-Lucena City
description: Has a Metro Gaisano Supermarket.

name: Lucena Fish Port Complex
description: Fresh seafood wholesale.

name: S&R Membership Shopping Lucena
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.

name: Señoritas Mexinoy Kitchen - Lucena
description: A beautiful restaurant with a great atmosphere!
address: Villa Señoritas Garden, Pearl St. Pleasantville Subd

name: La Casa de Cafe
description: Foods are affordable and delicious, Pasta, Baby Back Ribs, Fries, etc.

name: Pleasant Grill
description: Great Mediterranean/Filipino street food.

name: Special Lomi Batangas
description: This place offers quick-served, hot, tasty Lomi Batangas. It is a big and affordable serving of noodles, egg, meat, topped with chicharon, all in a thick, viscous and seasoned soup.

name: Bosschito Roasted Chicken
description: Grilled Porkchop and Grilled Liempo are equally delicious! Serving size was fair, price was affordable, and grilled aroma was very appetizing.
address: Old Manila South Road corner Bonifacio Drive

name: Virgie's Native Lechon
description: Best lechon in Lucena City.
address: 1560 Quezon Avenue Extension, Purok Maligaya, Cotta,

name: The Green Bowl
description: Green Bowl refreshingly offers healthy food choices in a city where vegetable dishes are hard to find.

name: Pares ni Peso sa Lucena
description: Value for money. Delicious.

name: DadBod
description: Hamburger restaurant.

name: Kentouka
description: This is a good place if want to try to experience Japanese ramen. Have the Tonkotsu and Tantanmen a try and you'll definitely like it.

name: Isaiah's Kitchen
description: Japanese restaurant.

name: Queen Margarette Hotel - Downtown
description: Set 3 km from the Pan-Philippine Highway, this straightforward hotel in a colorful commercial district in the city center is a 13-minute walk from the Gintong Yaman ng Quezon Museum, and 1 km from Lucena Botanical Garden.

name: Jaelle Residences
description: clean and comfy. spacious bathroom, strong water pressure. has a pantry area outside the room with utensils, mugs, microwave that you can use.

name: Okazu Garden Resort & Restaurant
description: A popular water park.

name: The Star Garden Tower Hotel
description: On a bustling street with shops and eateries, this informal hotel is 6 minutes' walk from the Dumacaa River, 14 minutes' walk from Lucena Botanical Garden and 3 km from the Pan-Philippine Highway.

name: Lucena Fresh Air Hotel and Resort
Hulugan Falls

address: Fabricante corner Estrellado Streets, Zone I

name: Aliw Falls
description: A 25 m cascade.

name: San Sebastian Parish Church
description: Lumban's Roman Catholic church was built in the late 16th century but was finished in its present form during the early 20th century. It features a partially plastered facade colored in orange. Its interior is largely plastered, without much ornamentation.

name: Lumban Welcome Marker
description: A Hollywood-like signage at a cliffside spot at the boundary between Kalayaan and Lumban overlooking the Caliraya power plant that offers panoramic views over Laguna de Bay into Mount Sembrano in neighboring Rizal province.

name: Lumban Municipal Hall
description: A rare civic building from the American period.

name: Caliraya Lake
description: A man-made reservoir created in 1939 following the damming of the Caliraya river. A favorite spot for watersports, fishing and camping activities, with an increasing number of Metro Manilans setting up retirement homes along the shore. The lake is shared by the municipalities of Cavinti, Kalayaan and Lumban.

name: Burdang Lumban Festival
description: A festival showcasing Lumban's main products, particularly its textiles and embroidery.

name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria Parish Church
description: Luna's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style in 1690. It houses the venerated image of Our Lady of Namacpacan, a 6 ft statue of the Virgin Mary that arrived in town when the ship transporting the image to its original destination in Vigan was repeatedly forced to seek shelter in town due to storms along the South China Sea in 1871. The church was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.
address: Luna-Bangar Road corner Namacpacan Road, Victoria

name: Baluarte Watchtower
description: A stout, Spanish-era watchtower meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

name: Luna Pebbles
description: A stretch of beach known for its pebbled composition.

name: Bahay na Bato
description: Meaning "stone house", it is a beachside house and art gallery featuring local history artefacts and works by Korean sculptor Bong Kim, who also designed the house using rocks, wood and pebbles collected along the beaches of Luna.

name: Darigayos Beach
description: The most famous beach in Luna, featuring white sands along a cove and ideal surfing conditions.

name: Occalong Falls
description: A 10 ft cascade.

name: USAFFE-NL Military Shrine and Park
description: A beachside memorial to the time when Darigayos Beach hosted Camp Spencer, the operational headquarters of American and Filipino forces during the Battle of Bessang Pass in 1945 during World War II.
directions: at the back of Darigayos Beach

name: Dupag Rock Formations
description: A limestone formation in the Marag Valley with boulders reaching up to 8 ft in height. It has variously been described as resembling a jagged maze and labyrinth, a mangled honeycomb, a human brain, or Swiss cheese.

name: Manacota Underground River
description: A 700 m long underground waterway in the Marag Valley with crystal-blue waters reaching a depth of up to 40 ft and looming cave formations.

name: Lussok Cave
description: A cave with looming rock formations and an underground lagoon. Its name derives from a local term for the natural light that manages to penetrate its chambers and bounce off the stalactites and stalagmites.

name: Bayugao Falls
description: A 3-tier cascade with a height of 30 m.

name: Apayao Eco-Tourism and Sports Complex
description: A recreational space and sports complex with accommodations run by the provincial government.
The only convenience store of its kind in Apayao.
directions: at the junction with Kabugao-Junction Luna Road

name: Apayao Brew
directions: at the back of JL Fuel gas station

name: Casa Lacuesta
description: A bed and breakfast.
directions: at the back of the provincial capitol complex

name: Bicol International Airport
description: This airport serves Legazpi in Albay, southern Luzon.

name: Laoag International Airport
description: This airport serves Laoag in Ilocos Norte, northern Luzon.

name: Metro Gaisano
description: Has a Gaisano supermarket and a food court.

name: Metrobank
description: Has a 24-hour Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: PNB
description: Has a 24-hour Visa Card ATM.

name: Alberto's Pizza
description: very good low cost pizza.

name: GV Hotel
description: 43 single and double rooms each with an electric fan or air conditioning, en suite and cable TV.
directions: the Maasin port is beside the GV hotel

name: Ampil Pensionne
description: Fan single, fan double, a/c double.

name: Southern Comfort Pensionne
description: Air-conditioned single and double rooms of different sizes all with own bathrooms and cable TV.

name: DW Pensione
description: Large fan room with balcony.

name: Bad Smell Cave
description: Due to bat guano and urine.

name: Cayaso Cave
description: 2,222m long.

name: Crystal Caves
description: Nice gardens with plenty of shade trees have three pavilions where you can leave your bags and gear and use clean toilets. The cave is about 150m walk over rough karst and through sheltering trees. Since the cave atmosphere has pretty well 100% humidity you might want to pause for a few moments to cool off before you enter. There is an iron walkway at relatively high level of about 140m from the cave entrance and artificial lighting. The formations are interesting and extremely varied, but of a uniform whiteness except where they have been contaminated. Many will be interested to see the rhinoceros bats hanging from the ceiling, but watch where you place your hands because of guano deposits. The air is not foetid or unpleasant despite the lack of any air currents. For many the highlight may well be the opportunity to get very close to tiny Balinsasayaw swifts nesting in the ceiling about 1m above your head. (The caves have to be kept locked to prevent the theft of their valuable nests that are prized for making birds' nest soup. The nests built, with the birds saliva, have high levels of calcium, iron, potassium, and magnesium and can fetch about ₱40 per gram. According to traditional Chinese science, these soups are believed to help maintain skin tone, balance qi {"life energy"}, help digestion, alleviate asthma, boost the libido and reinforce the immune system.)
directions: 10km south of Mabinay township on the south side of the highway towards Bais and well signed in brown
price: ₱215 includes a hard hat and the services of a guide

name: Kabugan Cave
description: Large colonies of three different species of bat and an opening that allows a shaft of sunlight to penetrate.

name: Odloman
description: At a length of some 8,870m, this cave system is the second longest in the Philippines after St Paul's Underground River in Palawan's National Park. It's not a cave for casual visitors since it can only be accessed by swimming 20m across an underground torrent of by rappelling down from a squeeze in the roof. Seasoned spelunkers will be rewarded with large galleries, narrow corridors, and some pretty extreme water challenges.

name: Pandalihan Cave
description: Contains the "Berlin Wall".

name: Panligawan Cave
description: The most accessible of them all.

name: Andrew's Diner
description: Cafeteria style with outside tables set in a tranquil garden with artificial waterfall.

name: Econotel
description: Unfortunately this roadhouse suffers from the common cycle of tourism decline in the rural Philippines: infrequent guests mean that maintenance and modernisation is reduced which, in turn, reduces patronage. In Jan 2015 the restaurant was not open and there was no running water or refrigerated drinks. 3 Motel style units surprisingly well furnished but with tiny shower rooms where anybody seated on the WC has an intimate encounter with the pedestal of the wash hand basin. Bizarrely for an establishment with no running water in the rooms, one corner of the bedroom - where normally you might expect to encounter a writing desk - is very fully occupied by an ivory-coloured two person spa bath! Grounds are pleasant and sufficiently removed from the cloying dust of the (perpetual?) roadworks on the highway (which have been "in progress" for more than 6 years now).

name: Anilao Outrigger Resort
description: The resort provides complete diving equipment and houses a restaurant and bar. There are about 185 steps down to the resort from the parking lot. Porters will carry your luggage up and down, but you have to climb all of those stairs, which can be strenuous.

name: Sea's Spring Resort
description: Air-conditioned rooms, with cable TV, hot water and views of the beachfront or the mountains. Cottages are also available. There are also an outdoor swimming pool with slides, and natural hot spring baths.

name: Mayumi Resort
description: Small Filipino-themed beach resort. Scuba diving available on site.

name: Balincaguin River
description: Balincaguin River is open to everyone at any time of any day and is ideal during hot summer days. There has been news of development of a Swim-Bike-Row tour but until then, guests are free to lounge and relax.

name: Santo Rosario Cave System
description: If you're a fan of cave adventures, exploring the Santo Rosario Cave System is for you. Though visitors are required to crouch down and carefully navigate themselves past the cave’s small entrance. Bats are flying around and the path inside changes in every few steps so visitors need to be cautious. You may get scrapes and bruises but mini-waterfalls, the clear pool of water and the enchanting rock formations are the rewards so it will be all worth it.

name: Cacupangan Cave
description: The Cacupangan Cave System proudly features four kilometres of stalagmite and stalactites beautifully carved by nature for centuries. In order for visitors to enter the cave, they have to carefully trek through a rough road and avoid the slightly jagged rocks and the slippery mud trails along the way. Once you're inside the cave, the rocks smooth over and are stable but guests still need to be cautious of not waking the bats, scorpions and snakes residing within, and that they have to be ready to get soaked because of the water level inside the cave which may vary depending on the season.

name: Yabite's Cafe
address: Stall no.5 @ Caberto Promenade (across KmC-mart Grocery), Purok Uno Brgy. Calzada

name: Nuestra Señora de Candelaria Parish Church
description: Mabitac's Roman Catholic church was largely rebuilt following damage from World War II and earthquakes, resulting in an austere look, with only the belltower and altar hinting at its Spanish origins. The church was built on top of Kalbaryo (Calvary) Hill, the highest point in the town center with vistas of the surrounding valley, Mount Sembrano, the Sierra Madre mountains, and Laguna de Bay. While the church is accessible by vehicle through a gentle ramp leading from the Battle of Mabitac monument, many devotees instead climb the short but steep 126 steps leading from Mabitac Rural Health Unit.

name: Battle of Mabitac Monument
description: A colorful monument commemorating a rare victory by Filipino forces against the Americans during the Philippine-American War in 1900.

name: Balete Tree
description: A towering old strangler fig tree along the national highway.

name: Kota Paradiso
description: An upland resort offering forest bathing and ecotourism activities, a coffee farm and a cafe.

name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church
description: Macabebe's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Baroque style in 1904 after it was burned by nationalist forces during the Philippine-American War in 1899. The arson also saw the massacre of 300 residents accused of treason, which explains Macabebe’s subsequent support for the Americans. Despite its relative youth compared to other colonial churches, the place retains a dated air and much artifacts and ornaments expected of an old church, including the pulpit.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Macabebe Ecopark
description: An extensive nature complex at the very edge of Macabebe marking spot where the Pampanga River empties into Manila Bay. It has wetland formations and a small beach, though the estuarine waters are not recommended for swimming.

name: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish Church
description: Masantol's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Renaissance style in 1932 with a façade somewhat resembling a trident.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Caduang Tete Public Market
description: A small market serving a barangay of Macabebe.

name: Casa Palmera Resort and Events Place
Governor's Rapids Nature Park
description: Maddela's main tourist draw, it is an undisturbed section of the Cagayan River that was named after a Japanese officer who drowned in the area during World War II. It is a popular swimming, rafting and caving venue.
directions: take a junction from Maddela-Echague Road

name: Maddela Eco-Tourism Park
description: Another natural park complex west of town. Its highlight is Maddela Falls, a seven-tier cascade, with a natural crystal-clear pool at its base.

name: Maria Angela Falls
description: A 15 m cascade in a secluded hiking trail named after a local politician.

name: Panagsasalog Festival
description: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

name: Buddies Place
directions: at the back of Total gas station

name: Medy’s Noodle House and Restaurant
description: A restaurant serving noodle dishes.

name: Aldine's Pastry and Food Hauz
directions: in front of Total gas station

name: San Bartolome Apostol Parish Church
description: Magalang's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present style in 1866.

name: Heliograph Tower
description: An obelisk-like structure built by the Spanish to serve as a "sun telegraph" that transmitted Morse code messages using the sun's rays. It is one of a few remains of an extensive Spanish military communications and watchtower system in Central Luzon and was later used to store and manufacture sugar.

name: Magalang Municipal Hall
description: One of a few civic buildings in the Philippines that survive from the American occupation, dating back to the 1920s.

name: Banal A Bunduk Dalan Ning Krus
description: Meaning "Holy Mountain, Way of the Cross" in Kapampangan, it is a religious complex at the foot of Mount Arayat that attracts pilgrims during the Lenten season for its 14 Stations of the Cross laid out across a 1.6 km trail that culminates in a 35 ft statue of a risen Jesus Christ.

name: Plaza Magalang
description: One of the better-designed and maintained town squares in the Philippines, featuring a large gazebo, civic monuments to local heroes and other noteworthy achievements, and a statue of a carabao.

name: Feliciano Ancestral House
description: A colonial-era residence converted into a clinic.

name: Don Cayetano Rivera House
description: A colonial-era residence.

name: Don Antonio Luciano House
description: A colonial-era residence inside a secluded compound that was also used as a filming location for some domestic period films.

name: Aquino-Gueco House
description: A Spanish-era residence belonging to a minor branch of the Aquino political dynasty in neighboring Concepcion, Tarlac. The view is partially obscured by mango trees.

name: Ordonez-Calma House
description: A colonial-era residence whose ground floor has been leased out to commercial establishments.
address: Angeles-Magalang Road corner Morales Street, Santa Cruz

name: Camaru Festival
description: Magalang's annual festival, coinciding with the feast of its patron saint, Bartholomew and dedicated to the local delicacy, crickets (camaru in Kapampangan)

name: Angeles City Flying Club
description: The main recreational aviation club in Central Luzon, offering short flying, paragliding and related activities. The club's facilities also include a cafe and swimming pool.

description: Cafe with cakes and snacks.

name: Altezza Cabins
description: Hotel with eponymous cafe and restaurant.

name: Gibalon Historical Shrine
description: Marked as the historic site of the first Christian mass in Luzon.

name: Saint Mary Magdalene Parish Church
description: Magdalena's Roman Catholic church was built in the Baroque style and features an austere and unplastered facade and interior, along with a statue of Saint Mary Magdalene seemingly bleeding through her eyes while she holds a skull. Its main claim to fame is being a convalescent home for Filipino revolutionary hero Emilio Jacinto during the war of independence against the Spanish, with a small monument in the adjacent convent showing where drops of his blood fell, although the stains have faded away. The church faces the town plaza and the municipal hall, both of which have been preserved from the colonial era.The front steps leading to the church may be too steep and narrow for some visitors. An alternative option is to approach the building from the jeepney terminal at the back of the structure and walk past Magdalena Mini Park, where the ground is flat, towards the church’s side entrance.
directions: in front of the town plaza

name: Magdalena Town Plaza
description: An extensive public square with a small garden, a monument to national hero Jose Rizal, and a busts gallery of former mayors in front of the municipal hall. Flanked by the Spanish-era parish church and the American-era municipal hall, the grounds were laid out according to a design established during the colonial era, which explains why the area is a favorite filming shoot. There is a Walk of Fame commemorating actors who visited Magdalena, but the plaques containing their names have faded away due to neglect.

name: Magdalena Municipal Cemetery
description: The town's cemetery, built in 1938, is also a common filming location due to its old design and the original arch at its entrance.

name: Magdalena Mini Park & Children's Playground
description: A small park with a Hollywood-like sign of Magdalena, statues of superheroes and animals, including Monstro the Sperm Whale from Pinocchio.
directions: at the back of Magdalena Church

name: Balanac Dam
description: An irrigation dam along the Pagsanjan River that is a favorite swimming spot for locals during the summer months.

name: Magdalena Public Market
address: Burgos corner Bernardo Streets, Ilayang Butnong

name: Saint William the Hermit Parish Church
description: Magsingal's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish period in 1827. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

name: Magsingal Municipal Hall
description: The seat of local government in Magsingal, built to resemble a Spanish-era government building.

name: Magsingal Belfry
description: Magsingal Church's belfry predates the actual church building by about 100 years. It also functioned as a watchtower guarding against pirates and foreign invaders. The belfry and the adjoining convent are part of the National Museum-Ilocos Region and was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

name: Puro Pinget Island
description: Not really an island but rather a round peninsula connected to mainland Magsingal by the narrow Puro Sandbar. It contains white sand beaches and a large concentration of beach resorts.

name: Ichthus Beach Resort
description: Resort near the Puro Sandbar.

name: Majayjay Transport Cooperative
description: Majayjay's central terminal, though crude-looking, is well-organized and offers services to Lucban, Luisiana, Santa Cruz via Magdalena, and Nagcarlan via Liliw. Be prepared to wait for the jeep to fill up.
directions: beside EcoOil gas station and in front of the municipal cemetery

name: Minor Basilica and Parish of Saint Gregory the Great
description: The only Catholic basilica in Laguna and a national cultural treasure, Majayjay's church burned several times during the Spanish era, with the last being in 1711. Instead of razing the structure, its priest instead ordered the ruins to be encased inside a 3 m-thick layer of brick and plastered in pink, resulting the façade exuding a fortress-like aura. The interior contains an ornate altar and an upper-level catwalk that rings the space. Unlike most Spanish-era churches in the Philippines, the basilica was built in the Romanesque style. The parish office sells some souvenirs.

name: Tulay Pigi
description: In the 19th century, a Spanish priest ordered his parishioners to build a bridge connecting Majayjay and Magdalena over the Pagsanjan River. He treated his workers badly and frequently whipped them in the buttocks, hence its name (Tulay Pigi literally means Buttocks Bridge, while Puente del Capricho literally means Bridge of Caprice). This ultimately backfired, and the bridge was left unfinished as Majayjay was depopulated by residents fleeing from the priest's abuses. The bridge's overgrown state and missing span, which was later filled with a steel contraption, is best admired from the bottom of the structure.
directions: the main entrance is at Ordoñez corner Limquico streets beside the town cemetery, but involves passing through a closed but still malodorous dumpsite and a steep descent along a narrow, secluded and overgrown trail. For a safer experience, enter through Majayjay-Magdalena Road at the back of the barangay hall of Talortor, on the other side of the bridge, where you can be in earshot of residents in case of an emergency

name: Taytay Falls
description: The most visited waterfall in Majayjay, with a height of 15 m.

name: Dalitiwan Stream
description: A cold stream running from Mount Banahaw. At the gorge surrounding Dalitiwan Bridge are two resorts allowing access to the stream and partially channeling the waters to create man-made cascades and rock pools.

name: Nuestra Señora de la Porteria Chapel
description: An 18th-century chapel containing a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.
address: Arellano corner F. Blumentritt Streets, Poblacion

name: Old Presidencia
description: Majayjay's colonial era municipal hall burned down sometime in the 20th century and was abandoned in favor of a new site near Majayjay Church. Nevertheless, the old building's shell remains as an imposing ruin, with the stairs and parts of its portico still intact.

name: Nuestra Señora de Porteria Grotto
description: Placed beside the Olla (Santa Cruz) river, this was where the Nuestra Señora de Porteria image was originally thought to have been placed before the chapel in the town center was built.

name: APA Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Park
description: A privately-owned zoo with more than 900 animals in the woods outside town.
price: Adults: ₱345, concessions: ₱295, group discounts also available

name: Bukal Falls
description: A waterfall at the boundary of Majayjay and Liliw that is claimed by both municipalities.
directions: from Bukal Barangay Hall, hike for 30-40 minutes

name: Sprite Falls
description: Another set of waterfalls upstream from the Dalitiwan Bridge.
directions: from Piit Barangay hall, hike for 15 minutes

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people.

name: La Triccias Resort Hotel, Events and Restaurant
Ayala Station
description: Serves Ayala Center. Station is connected by overhead walkways to One Ayala, the BGC Bus Ayala terminal and SM Makati. There are some food kiosks before the turnstiles.

name: Buendia station
description: Connects with Buendia stop on the EDSA Carousel and jeepneys headed for the CBD from a terminal outside the Bel-Air gated community. Escalator and stairs are present on site. No food establishment at the station but there's a nearby Shell with Jollibee and Mercury Drug store as their landmark.

name: Guadalupe station
description: Connects with the Guadalupe stop of the EDSA Carousel under the MRT bridge immediately north of the station. Jeepneys to Poblacion are available from nearby terminals at Guadalupe Market (aka "Guadalupe ABC") and Bernardino St

name: One Ayala
description: A three-story city bus station, serving as a connecting hub for several city bus lines terminating at the CBD. Direct connection to EDSA Carousel southbound and the MRT is available. Transfer to EDSA Carousel northbound or BGC Bus requires crossing through MRT Ayala station.

name: Guadalupe Ferry Terminal
address: Epifanio de los Santos Avenue corner J. P. Rizal Avenue

name: Greenbelt Chapel
alt_name: Santo Niño de la Paz Chapel
description: The church is popular for church-goers, most people find it relaxing though because of the park around it. The church is surrounded by trees and a fish and lily pond is on the side of the chapel. The Greenbelt Chapel might be the most relaxing chapel in the Philippines. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is also found here.

name: Nuestra Señora de Gracia Church
description: Built by the Augustinian friars and is inspired by European Baroque. It is named Nuestra Señora de Gracia in honor of the miraculous image of the Virgin Mary that can also be found inside.

name: Philippine Stock Exchange
description: One of the two stock exchanges in the Philippines, it is known to have Asia's shortest trading times which lasts only for two hours. Nearby the PSE is the Ninoy Aquino Monument.
address: Tower One & Exchange Plaza, Ayala Triangle Gardens, Ayala Avenue

name: Ninoy Aquino Monument
description: Erected in honor of the late Filipino senator, Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino, who was the husband of late Philippines president. Corazon Aquino.

name: Nielson Tower Historical Marker
description: The Nielson Airport was built by Laurie Reuben Nielson, a businessman born in New Zealand. It was built in 1937 and served as the control tower and passenger depot of the city's airport. Until 1948. The Nielson Airport was built on a 42-hectare piece of land owned by Ayala y Cia. During World War II, commercial flights were relocated so that Nielson could serve the U.S. Army Air Corps.

name: Sultan Kudarat Monument
address: Makati Avenue corner Paseo de Roxas Avenue

name: Ayala Museum
description: Showcases the rich and vivid history of the Philippines from the earliest times of the Mactan battle to the struggle of democracy in EDSA. Also present are some famous paintings by Filipino painters such as Fernando Amorsolo, Juan Luna and Fernando Zobel. Guided tours are available if booked in advance for large groups.

name: Yuchengco Museum
description: The museum was created to house the art collection of Secretary Alfonso T. Yuchengco, and highlight his distinguished career as a businessman, diplomat, collector, philanthropist, patron of the arts, and advocate for education in the Philippines. The museum’s primary goal is to foster a greater public appreciation of the finest in Filipino and Filipino-Chinese visual arts and creativity. The Yuchengco Museum houses paintings by Fernando Amorsolo, Juan Luna and Carlos “Botong” Francisco.
address: RCBC Plaza, Corner Ayala Avenue and Senator Gil J. Puyat Avenue

name: Filipinas Heritage Library
description: Has an astounding collection of books that date back to the Spanish period. Serious scholars of the time period will love it, but anyone with even a remote interest in old books and history should give it a visit.
directions: inside the old Nielson Airport tower

name: Makati Museum
description: Old colonial building displaying some local historical artifacts & photos.

name: Greenbelt Park
description: Greenbelt Park is a small park designed to be a complement to the surrounding Greenbelt Malls. An artificial duck pond and stream can be seen here, as well as the Greenbelt Chapel for Catholic services. Greenbelt Park is also a good place to sit, people watch and see the more multicultural side of Metro Manila.

name: Ayala Triangle Park
description: Behind the Philippine Stock Exchange, the Ayala Triangle Park is surrounded by restaurants and cafes.
address: Paseo De Roxas Avenue corner Makati Avenue corner Ayala Avenue

name: Legazpi Active Park
description: A small, well-kept park along Legaspi Street. On Sunday mornings the Legaspi Market opens, where you can get fresh organic foods, delicacies, sweets and other assorted souvenirs.

name: Salcedo Park

name: Washington Sycip Park
description: Compared to Legazpi Active Park this park is far more tranquil with a lot more greenery. The trees are quite lovely, the pond is quaint, plenty of spaces to sit & eat a meal; plus, large enough for a moderate paced walk.

name: Power Plant Mall
description: A four-level complex in the heart of Rockwell Center that has shops, international and local restaurants, and cinemas.

name: Salcedo Weekend Market
description: In the heart of the Business Center District is the Salcedo Park. Every Saturday, vendors take over part of the park to sell their specialty items. There are ornamental plants, organically grown vegetables, bakery products, lechon from Cebu, etc. Be sure to come early for the full experience.

name: Yellow Cab Pizza

name: Sbarro

description: It is what it is. If thin crust is your taste, head here. Dine in, take away or delivery.

Though the prices (₱410 average starter; ₱670 average sandwich; mains from ₱690 for Mango BBQ Chicken, to ₱3,550 for the Steak Frites) come out on the high side of mid-range dining options, Apt. 1B is well worth it.

name: Circles Event Café

Each unit has an air conditioner, one double-bed with towels and linen (one bed, sleeps 2 people), a refrigerator, a 24" LCD TV with cable, a living room set, dining room set, an electric kettle, a private bath with hot and cold shower, kitchen utensils, an electronic vault/safety deposit box, fans and a telephone/intercom (free calls within Metro-Manila). Wi-Fi is free. Utilities included. Daily housekeeping provided. All-female, friendly staff. Very clean, safe and inexpensive.

No phone.There is no in-house restaurant or room service, though they can provide a few things like coffee and sandwiches on request and there is a vending machine for soft drinks. However, there are plenty of restaurants nearby, including at least three Japanese restaurants and a pizza place in the building. The surrounding area has many more places, mostly Japanese: at least a dozen restaurants, plus bars and nightclubs.
address: Mezzanine Floor Creekside Mall, Amorsolo St. cor VA Rufino St., Legazpi Village

name: Franchise One Inn

name: The Clipper House Makati
description: Hotel in an old art deco building in Makati, near the red light district and the Powerplant Mall. It's a budget hotel, but annoyingly they do not show their rate on the website.

name: LPL Suites Greenbelt
description: Studio and bedroom suites, all equipped with air conditioning, cable TV and Wi-Fi Internet access. Facilities and services are safe deposit box, travel and tour assistance.

name: Guijo Suites
description: Deluxe room, junior suite and premier suite, all equipped with flat screen LED TV with cable channels, Wi-Fi Internet access and safe. Facilities and services are Lobby Restobar, daily housekeeping services and 24-hour CCTV security.

name: Jupiter Suites

name: The Picasso Boutique Serviced Residences
description: Offers air-conditioned rooms with 32-inch flat-screen LCD TV with cable channels, kitchenette with electric stove and microwave oven, and Internet connection. Some of its amenities include Qi Wellness Spa, salon 119, and gym.

name: CEO Flats

name: A.Venue Hotel Suites

name: I'M Hotel
description: I’M Hotel is a 5-star hotel in the Poblacion district and houses the largest onsen spa (as of 2018) in the Philippines. The hotel's architecture and rooms are designed by Singapore-based architects. It features 434 rooms including 182 suites equipped with an Electrolux-fitted kitchenette, living room, and dining area. The hotel also has an infinity pool, which can be seen upon entering the lobby as one looks up because it is acrylic-bottomed. The hotel's Common Good Food Playground features nine upscale dining outlets offering various international cuisines.

name: Discovery Primea
description: In the Makati Central Business District, this upmarket hotel is a 9-minute walk from the Ayala Museum and a 12-minute walk from Greenbelt Park. Ninoy Aquino International Airport is 6 km away.Airy rooms feature Wi-Fi and loaner smartphones, as well as flat-screens, coffeemakers, and floor-to-ceiling windows with city views. Some offer balconies, while chic suites add kitchens and living/dining areas. A bi-level 2-bedroom apartment sleeps up to 4 guests. A breakfast buffet is available. Other amenities include 2 restaurants and 2 bars, as well as a lobby lounge. There’s also a gym, a spa, and an outdoor heated infinity pool with a bar.

name: Somerset Millennium Makati
description: In a modern glass-fronted building, this high-end urban hotel is 1 km from a metro station, 7 km from the SM Mall of Asia, and 11 km from the aquarium and live shows of Manila Ocean Park. Featuring quilted headboards and natural tones, the polished rooms and suites come with free Wi-Fi and flat-screen TVs. Most have kitchens, and some offer living rooms. Room service is available.Parking and breakfast are complimentary. There's a restaurant and a bar, as well as an outdoor pool and a fitness room.

description: Opens in 2024.

name: Evolution
description: Malapascua's only 5-star Instructor Training Facility rating from TDI. Evolution offers a full range of TDI tech classes. Day trips and local dives are run 365 days a year by a professional team. Evolution is a full service resort with 16 rooms and a well-known restaurant on site and is owned and operated by a seasoned Irish and English duo. In 2015 Evolution became a Green Fins top member having the 6th least environmental impact of dive centres audited in Asia and is the only dive centre resort on Malapascua to make the list.

name: French Kiss Divers
description: French Kiss Divers is a small diveshop who offers SSI courses from open water to Instructor and a panel of specialties such as Nitrox, Deep, Night, and Wreck, a very good knowledge of the dive sites. The dive group doesn't exceed 4 people. They often organize day trips in surrounding islands like Kalanggaman or Carnaza.

name: Malapascua Exotic Dive & Beach Resort (IDC Centre)
description: Offers all in one - accommodation, restaurant, bar, diveshop, travel service. This eco-friendly resort has its own recycling plant and 24-hour generator. This PADI 5-star Instructor Development Resort is the only National Geographic Center in Malapascua. Courses range from beginner through to Instructor (100% pass rate) and technical diving courses. They cover more than 22 dive sites around Malapascua, have daily dives to see the thresher sharks, as well as Nitrox, Wreck and Night dives.

name: Sea Explorers
description: Located at the center of Bounty Beach beside Ocean Vida Resort with a bar on the island. In the Visayas since 1989, offering all PADI recreational courses from beginner up to Instructor courses.

name: Thresher Shark Divers

Regular trips include morning thresher shark dives at Kimud Shoal, local reef and macro dives, Gato Island, night dives and wreck dives. Open Water divers may be able to join some shark dives with instructor supervision; deeper or overhead-environment sites require suitable experience and certification.
address: Bounty Beach, Logon, Daanbantayan, Cebu 6013 Philippines
directions: on the main beach, they can arrange your transport from Cebu
hours: 8am-7or 8pm, dive schedule confirmed the day before

More 10 years experience on Malapascua and Divemasters. Eco-friendly resort, Dives to see the thresher sharks Monad Shoal, Kimud Shoal, Kalanggagamn, Gato Island,

Since 1998, the National Museum has been the regulatory and enforcement agency of the National Government in the restoring and safeguarding of important cultural properties, sites and reservations throughout the Philippines. Swirl a pair of these wooden half disks over your incense sticks so they catch the smoke and then throw them to the floor. Identical faces means "NO" while opposing figures means "YES". Kuang Kong is the patron of Scholars and Martial arts as well as the God of War; it is known as the protector of Quan Yin; the Goddess of Mercy.

name: Rizal Park (Luneta)
description: Nearest railway station: United Nations (LRT-1). Manila's green lung, this large urban park stretches from the Quirino Grandstand in the west to Taft Avenue in the east, with the historic walled district of Intramuros bordering it to the north. The park's most famous landmark is the Rizal Monument, a stone obelisk with bronze statuary erected near the site of Philippine national hero José Rizal's execution in 1896. All distances in the Philippines are measured from the large flagpole near the monument, which serves as the country's Kilometre Zero. Other prominent features include a statue of Lapu-Lapu (the native chieftain who repulsed Magellan's expedition in 1521) and a giant relief map of the Philippines (set within a reflecting pool near the Taft Avenue end). Well-known landmarks within the park's boundaries include the Museum of the Filipino People (inside the old Finance Department building), the Department of Tourism building, the Manila Planetarium, and the National Library. Many locals (including taxi drivers) still refer to the park by its old name: Luneta.
