description: Rice in a bowl Pork-chop, Fried Chicken, Grilled Liempo/Burger/Fries/Coffee/Shakes.

name: F3's Riverside Food Park
description: This is a simple drinking and billiards place in Naga City. Cheap beer, cheap Billiards table, friendly staff. Chill ambiance.

name: Cellar Wine Bar Kitchen Deli
description: Quaint little resto tucked away from busy Magsaysay Avenue. Good steak and reasonably priced wine.

description: This hotel has more facilities than most hotels in Camarines Sur. It has gym, sauna and function rooms.

Nagbukel Viewdeck

name: Nagcarlan Underground Cemetery
description: The only cemetery of its kind in the Philippines, it was built in the 19th century on an octagonal layout, it retains its Spanish-era chapel containing a sculpture of the dead Christ, and its underground crypt with the remains of Nagcarlan's high society still inside. Beside the entrance to the compound is a small but informative museum about the concept of death in Philippine culture. An urban legend claims that the cemetery is connected underground to the parish church, Mount Banahaw and even to Pagsanjan, 41 km away. The cemetery was declared a national historical landmark in 1981.

name: San Bartolome Apostol Parish Church
description: A Spanish colonial church built in a Baroque style with Moorish-inspired crenellations, and supporting exterior pillars that seemingly wrap around the structure like a cast. Look for the ornate altar and painted wooden carving of the Final Judgement made by carvers from Paete.
address: J. Lirio corner Mabini Streets and J. Coronado corner E.A. Fernandez Streets (for pedestrians only); P. Zamora Street (for vehicles), Barangay Poblacion III
directions: drop off at Nagcarlan Town Plaza or Municipal Market

name: Nagcarlan Municipal Hall
description: Built in 1941, it is one of the few remaining civic buildings in the Philippines to survive World War II.

name: Bunga Falls
description: Twin waterfalls system with a drop of 10-15 m.

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people.

name: Nagcarlan Public Market
address: E.A. Fernandez corner J. Coronado Street, Poblacion I

name: Telang's Cafe
description: A cafe with rice meals.
directions: in front of Nagcarlan Underground Cemetery

Landingan Viewpoint
description: A stretch of the highway overlooking the Cagayan River valley that offers views of the town and a flower garden surrounding it.

name: Siitan Nature Park
description: A nature preserve along the Cagayan River featuring rafting, swimming and boating facilities.

name: Bimmapor Rock Formation
description: A much-photographed and looming limestone formation along the Cagayan River named because of its resemblance to the stern of a ship (bapor in Filipino).

name: Masug Falls
description: A cascade located within Aeta ancestral grounds.

name: Junuan Falls
description: A roadside cascade downstream from Masug Falls.

name: Diamond Cave
description: A cave with looming rock formations and underground streams.

name: Penenkakasisit Festival
description: The town's annual celebration of its foundation date, featuring local dances and costumed parades by its indigenous residents.

name: Oh Pares Ko
description: Restaurant specializing in beef pares (tendon).

name: Naic Church
alt_name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of the Immaculate Conception Church
description: Naic's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era and containing an exquisite altarpiece and interior. At the front is a pedestrian mural showing a map of Cavite.
directions: in front of Naic Public Plaza

name: Casa Hacienda de Naic
description: One of the few surviving friar estate manors from the Spanish era. It was also used as a headquarters for the Philippine revolutionary government led by Andres Bonifacio in 1897.
directions: inside Naic Central Elementary School and beside Naic Church

name: Torres Farm Hotel and Resort
description: A resort and hotel complex whose main draw is a collection of miniaturized landmarks from around the world.
price: ₱260 for a picture-taking tour, ₱290 for tour with usage of swimming pools, valid for seven hours. Separate rates apply for accommodation and other rentals.

name: Pawikan Festival
description: A celebration of Naic's natural resources and biodiversity. The highlight of the event is the release of captive sea turtle hatchlings (pawikan) into Manila Bay.

name: Fortune King Central Mart
address: Antero Soriano Highway corner Governor's Drive, Ibayo Silangan

name: The Stadium
description: A shopping complex resembling two conjoined stadiums.

name: Lolo Claro's
description: A branch of a Maragondon-based restaurant offering fried chicken. Group meals are also available.

name: Mikay's Kitchen Restaurant
description: A Filipino-Western restaurant with a boodle-style option.

name: Verdance Cafe and Kitchen
description: A cafe and restaurant serving all day breakfasts and a mix of Filipino, western and Asian dishes.

name: Arena Island
description: This resort in Puerto Princesa offers two type of rooms which are: first the "Casita" (maximum adults: 4, maximum children: 1) and it is equipped with air conditioning, minibar, private toilet and bath, queen bed, hot and cold shower. The second room offered is: "Pavilion" (maximum adults: 10, maximum children: 1) and it is equipped with private toilet and bath, electric fan, hot and cold shower. Some of its facilities and services are tree house and hammock, floating veranda for cocktails and Al fresci dining areas.

name: Sulvec Watchtower
description: The remains of a Spanish-era watchtower and fortifications meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

name: Narvacan Church
description: Narvacan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style.

name: Paraiso ni Juan
description: Meaning "Juan's Paradise", it is a grotto built on top of a protruding rock off Sulvec Beach, itself a popular swimming spot, marking the spot where the Spanish conquistadores who first arrived in Narvacan were shipwrecked. It is a picturesque venue for sunsets, but the site itself is only accessible during low tide.

name: Mount Noah
description: A towering hill with views over Sulvec Cove, the Cordillera Mountains and downtown Narvacan.

name: Northern Luzon Heroes Hill National Park
description: A 1316 ha ridge that is popular among hikers and motorists for the dramatic coastal views along Manila North Road. While most of the park is located in Santa, its southern tip lies at Barangay Sulvec in Narvacan.

name: Tangadan Tunnel
description: A road tunnel cut through a stretch of the Cordillera Mountains to bypass the narrow treacherous stretch of the Abra River Gorge. The tunnel marks the approximate boundary between Ilocos Sur and Abra provinces and has rest stops on the Ilocos Sur side.

name: Sangaan Rolling Hills
description: A series of symmetrically shaped rolling hills at the boundary with Abra province

name: Narvacan Tobacco Farmer's Tourism Park & Commercial Complex
description: A sprawling mixed-use commercial and tourism complex featuring a farmers' market, civic monuments, a dancing fountain, and a replica of the shipwrecked vessel carrying the Spanish conquerors of Narvacan.

name: Narvacan Farmers Market
directions: inside Narvacan Tobacco Farmer's Tourism Park & Commercial Complex

name: Letong's Grill & Restaurant
directions: at the back of Narvacan Church

name: Nasugbu Landing Monument
description: It commemorates the landing of American liberation forces on January 31, 1945.

name: Saint Francis Xavier Parish Church
description: A Romanesque parish church dating back to 1852. Spanish era church. Looks amazing from the outside.

name: La Iglesia de la Nuestra Señora de la Escalera
description: Old Church Ruins under a Balete Tree (Banyan Tree).

name: Mount Batulao
description: This mountain is a must-visit for beginners. The scenic views and beautiful mountain range made the experience unforgettable. Highly recommended for those looking to start their hiking journey.

name: Fortune Island
description: The island is owned by José Antonio Leviste, a former governor of Batangas. Leviste opened the Resort Club on the island in 1995. It was a bad investment (also due to lack of fresh water on the island). In the end the idea of the resort was abandoned. What has left are remnants of the beach cabanas, swimming pool and an acropolis with Grecian pillars and statues on the edge of the island overlooking the sea. Great place for swimming and snorkeling. Visiting is not cheap though.

name: Nasugbu Beachfront
description: Nice views and you can see Fortune Island at a distance.

name: Waltermart - Nasugbu
description: Mall, Supermarket.

name: Mang Kulas Lomi House
description: Do yourself a favor and visit this lovely restaurant in batangas. The service is unmatched. The staff and owners truly cares about your experience. The food is absolutely amazing – big serving, great for sharing and flavorful . Absolutely the best meal we had while in batangas. Highly recommend!
address: Wawa Port Road corner Evangelista Street

name: El Cocinero by Chef Arnaldo
description: Filipino food, Spanish food restaurant.

name: L’Bulalo Restaurant - Nasugbu
description: Filipino food restaurant.

name: Canyon Cove Resort
description: Accommodations equipped with coffee/tea maker, mini-bar, cable TV, and electronic safe. Some of its facilities and services are swimming pool, massage and spa services, game room, children's playground and a beach.
address: Far East Road, Piloto Wawa, Nasugbu

name: Chateau Royale Hotel Resort and Spa
description: Chateau Royale Sports and Country Club stands on fifteen hectares. Accommodations are in log cabins.

name: Club Punta Fuego
description: Club Punta Fuego is in Nasugbu.

address: located at Terraza de Punta Fuego Main Phase

address: Pico de Loro Cove, Hamilo Coast

description: Navotas' main Roman Catholic church, built in the 1890s.
directions: alternate entrance at Los Martires Street

name: Navotas Fisheries Port Complex
description: Seafood market.

name: Agora Market
description: Wet & Dry goods.

name: Masskara Festival
description: A big annual Mardi Gras like event celebrated every 3rd week of October in Bacolod. Each of the city's barangays (districts) joins the competition for the fiercely competitive best costumed group. Lots of food and handicraft stalls, street dancing and beer at the Bacolod city plaza area. "Masskara" means "Mask" in Hiligaynon and Tagalog. The use of colorful masks with large smiles represent the nickname for the city, "City of Smiles". The masks are usually the icons for the festival and sometimes for Bacolod.

name: Christian Ventures Bookstore
description: This bookstore, which has stores at Terminals 1, 2 and 4, sells novels, travel guides, maps and periodicals in addition to Christian literature.

name: Cora Jacobs
description: Known as the "pioneer of Philippine handbag design", its airport store has a variety of items from its collection on sale.

name: National Book Store
description: The Philippines' largest bookstore has two stores in Terminal 3: one each at the International and Domestic Wings. It has a good selection of books and periodicals, and has a nominal school supplies section.

name: Mixed Lifestyle
description: A trendy clothing store in Terminal 3, it carries Team Manila merchandise, which make good souvenirs.

name: Preclaro's Souvenirs
description: This souvenir shop has a variety of Filipino souvenirs, but it is better known for the giant, purple morion (a localized Roman soldier found in Marinduque) statue standing outside the entrance.
directions: underneath the escalator going down to the gate area

name: Tesoro's Philippine Handicrafts
description: A famous retailer of Filipino handicrafts and souvenirs, it has stores at Terminals 1 and 3.

name: Belmont Hotel Manila
description: One of two mid-range options among the four hotels in Newport City, it has standard rooms, deluxe rooms and suites. No free breakfast.
directions: opposite Terminal 3, between Runway Manila and the Shrine of Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus

name: Holiday Inn Express Manila Newport City
description: Formerly the Remington Hotel, it is the largest and cheapest of the four hotels in Newport City, equipped with standard and deluxe rooms. No free breakfast.
directions: opposite Terminal 3, across from Resorts World Manila

name: Marriott Hotel Manila
description: The Philippines' first Marriott Hotel, it is one of two mid-range options for hotels in Newport City. Rooms have a panoramic view of either the airport or the Villamor Golf Course, and the hotel has its own casino. No free breakfast.
directions: opposite Terminal 3, beside Maxims Hotel and Resorts World Manila

name: Maxims Hotel
description: The most expensive hotel in Newport City and the first six-star hotel in the Philippines with 171 all-suite rooms which are all equipped with kitchens, bar facilities and a massage room, as well as individual in-room Wi-Fi and a personal butler. Unlike the Marriott, Belmont and Holiday Inn, there is free breakfast.
directions: opposite Terminal 3, between Marriott Hotel Manila and Resorts World Manila

name: Go Hotels Manila Airport Road
description: Go Hotels Manila Airport Road is a budget-friendly hotel strategically situated in Pasay City, Philippines. Located 10 to 15 minutes from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminals 1, 2, 3, and 4, the hotel offers convenience for travelers seeking quick and stress-free airport access. Its prime location also provides easy access to Metro Manila’s prominent shopping centers, lifestyle hubs, dining establishments, entertainment venues, and gaming destinations, making it a popular choice for both leisure and business travelers.
address: 608 Quirino Ave, Tambo, Parañaque, 1701 Metro Manila

name: Saint Andrew the Apostle Parish Church
description: Norzagaray's main Roman Catholic church, which burned down multiple times since the Spanish era but has continuously been rebuilt in its original style.

name: Angat Dam
description: Built in the 1960s, it is the largest of the three dams along the Angat River system and is the highlight of the Angat Forest Watershed. While access to the dam itself is restricted, the complex provides wide views of the Sierra Madre mountains.

name: Ipo Dam
description: The oldest of the three Angat River dams, built in 1935, and the scene of a battle between Allied forces and Japanese stragglers during the closing stages of World War II in 1945. While access to the dam itself its restricted, a viewdeck provides vistas of the surrounding watershed.

name: Pinagrealan Cave
description: A cave that served as a refuge for revolutionary leader Emilio Aguinaldo during the war of independence against the Spanish in 1897.

name: Bitbit Bridge
description: A road bridge offering stunning views of the upper reaches of the Angat River valley.

name: Angat Watershed Forest Reserve
description: A popular birdwatching site and a biodiversity hotspot containing most of the remaining closed-canopy forests in Central Luzon. The site also covers parts of the city of San Jose del Monte, and the towns of Doña Remedios Trinidad, Angat, San Rafael, and San Miguel, as well as parts of Rizal, Quezon, Aurora and Nueva Ecija provinces.

name: Bitbit Ecopark
description: A popular recreational and swimming spot in the Angat Watershed.

name: Casay Festival
description: The annual festival celebrating the establishment of Norzagaray as a municipality.

name: Bakas
description: A popular swimming spot along the Norzagaray River with rock formations smoothly polished by the currents.

Noveleta Tribunal

name: Noveleta Plaza

description: This church was established in 1905 by General Pascual Alvarez and is as one of the old existing Aglipayan churches in the country, although its current structure was built much later. It houses an image of the Virgin Mary locally called "Nanay Paz" (Mother Peace), based on the one in Antipolo, and is venerated by Aglipayans and Roman Catholics alike.
directions: near the junction with Magdiwang Highway

name: Noveleta Public Market
description: Wet section bustling with seafood vendors every morning. Quite noisy and smelly.
directions: At the back of Noveleta Municipal Hall and in front of Noveleta Tribunal

name: Malen's
description: Hearty Filipino food.
directions: In front of Puregold, beside Noveleta Diversion Bridge

name: One Serenata
description: AC rooms with car port, WiFi, TV and study table. Food and beverages available for purchase.

name: Baliwag Transit
description: Operates air-conditioned coaches from Cubao to Cabanatuan, Cabiao, Cuyapo, General Tinio, Jaen, Licab, Pantabangan, Rizal, San Jose and Santa Rosa via the Maharlika Highway. Sister company Golden Bee provide similar service to Cabanatuan, Cabiao, Lupao, San Jose and Zaragoza, also on regular AC buses. Baliwag buses are painted green, while Golden Bee buses are yellow.

name: Bagabag Airport
description: Has charter flights from Clark on Platinum Skies.

name: Kayapa Quad Peak
description: A nice loop hike that goes over the ridgeline of the four peaks in the area - Mt. Tugew, Mt. Kuban, Mt. Cabo, and Mt. Sadjatan. The hike is around 13 km long and takes approximately 5-6 hours, excluding breaks. The starting point is at the Alang-Salacsac Barangay Hall. A guide, available at the barangay hall, is required, in addition to the entry and environmental fees. The barangay also provides some food after the hike, for a price.

name: Oas Church
alt_name: St. Michael the Archangel Parish Church
description: The main Roman Catholic Church in Oas, built in the 19th century but with a façade spruced up and incongruous with its surrounding structures.

name: Gabbi's Bistro
description: available for dine-in, take-outs, and catering service

name: Obando Church
alt_name: San Pascual Baylón Parish and National Shrine of Nuestra Señora de la Immaculada Concepción de Salambáo
description: Obando's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Spanish-era design following World War II destruction. Unlike most churches, it is dedicated to three patron saints, namely St. Pascual Baylon, St. Claire of Assisi and the indigenous Our Lady of Salambao.The Obando Fertility Rites are performed on Sundays following the 8AM Mass and the feast day of Our Lady of Salambao on May 19. Following the performances, the staff will offer free eggs, a symbol of fertility associated with St. Claire. There is also an ecclesiastical museum on the second floor of the convent building and a souvenir store.

name: Obando Fertility Rites
description: Literally meaning "Dance in Obando", the practice is believed to have been a Hispanicized version of a precolonial fertility ritual whose subject of veneration was transferred from animist deities to the patron saints of Obando Church. The practice was discouraged and even banned by clergy on multiple occasions due to its syncretic origins, but has since been accepted by the church as an integral aspect of Catholic faith in town. The ritual is commonly celebrated on Sundays, but its biggest edition is on the feast days of Obando's three patron saints in May, during which pilgrims seeking to bear children flock to the church while massive processions are held in the streets to the tune of a theme song dedicated to Saint Clare, which is also a popular children's song in the Philippines.

name: Puregold Obando
address: Plaridel corner Kapitan Vililla Streets, Catanghalan

name: Olango Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A wetland area with many water fowl, very popular with bird watchers; close to a hundred species are found here, about half of them migratory and half permanent residents. It is listed by the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, especially as Waterfowl Habitat. See Ramsar sites.Facilities are minimal; the sanctuary office sells coconut juice and provides a bathroom, but there are no restaurants or accommodation on-site.
directions: South end of the island, in Barangay San Vincente

name: Olango Reef
description: A government-protected fish sanctuary with good snorkelling, located south of Olango around the smaller islands of Nalusuan and Hilutungan. It is one of the largest reef areas in the Visayas, about 4.5 km².

name: Triponia's Homestay
description: Somewhere between a normal homestay and a small resort hotel; guests are in a separate wing but the rest of the compound is inhabited by locals. Rooms on land have solid walls, a/c, & private bathroom with cold water shower. Others are built over the water with woven bamboo walls, electric fan, shared bathroom, & the sea visible through gaps in the bamboo floor at high tide. Some travellers find the sound of waves very relaxing Not much else except a large patio area; no restaurant but they can provide Filipino food if asked. Nearby shops have drinks and snacks.

name: Sagastrand Beach Resort & Restaurant
description: A pleasant establishment between Santa Rosa and the Wildlife Sanctuary. Nice swimming pool, rocky not-very-nice beach, tennis court, a small playground with swings etc., restaurant with both western and Filipino food. Rooms all have a/c, shower, hot water, fridge, TV. Apartments available for long-term stays.

name: Talima Beach and Dive Resort
description: A large place with a swimming pool, massage service, dive center, reasonably good but expensive food.
directions: The road is appalling; come by boat if possible.

name: Nalusuan Island Cebu Resort and Marine Sanctuary
description: Aqua sports activities like wave runners, jet skiing, scuba diving, and water skiing.

name: Casa Blanca by the Sea
description: As the name implies, this is a white building. It is large and looks rather like an antebellum plantation from the American South.

name: Island and Sun Beach Resort
description: 25 rooms, 25 villas, all A/C with cable TV, refrigerator, bathtub, private toilet and hot and cold water.

name: Ulo ng Apo Monument
description: A monument of a head of a chieftain in the middle of a roundabout in Rizal Avenue. According to local folklore, the area was once ruled by a benevolent chieftain who was known as "Apo" who was beheaded by rival tribes. The monument features the namesake of Olongapo (particularly from the phrase "Ulo ng Apo" or Apo's head).

name: Marikit Park
description: A park beside the SM City Olongapo Central. At its entrance is a concrete mural/relief dedicated to Filipino workers, and a model of a RA-5 Vigilante aircraft. The park also has a children's playground.

name: The Dove Monument
description: Historical landmark.

name: Fort Wint
description: Ruins of an American fort in Grande Island.

name: Bat Stop II
description: A hotspot for seeing bats, The best time to visit is sunset.

name: Hellships Memorial
description: It’s a nice memorial to read about its history. The memorial does a great job conveying the history.

name: The Hands that Freed the Nation
description: A historic monument, commemorating the Magnificent 12 Senators of the Republic of the Philippines who stood up and said "no" to the military bases in Olongapo and ended the foreign military presence in the country.

name: Children of the Sun Returning
description: Symbolises the past event on how the volunteers saved the Subic Bay from the Mount Pinatubo eruption, transforming the former Navy Base.

name: Spanish Gate
description: The old Spanish Gate at Subic is the remnant of the naval installation established by the Spanish colonial authorities in 1885. Two cannons straddle the gate as a reminder of its military past. Two markers are installed on both sides of the gate giving information about its origin. One can visit the gate with no special permission needed and it is generally open to the public.

name: SFEX Twin Tunnels
description: Nice forest and mountain green views along the way.
address: N Luzon W Expy, Subic Bay Freeport Zone, Bataan

name: Port Of Subic Bay
description: Sign.

name: Waterfront Park
description: Morning or evening walk, jog, bike, picnic, play frisbee or badminton, etc. This is definitely a good place to be.

name: Boardwalk Divers
description: Run by George AngDyPay, an experienced TDI and PSAI technical rebreather instructor. Set up to cater to both recreational and technical divers it has quickly become the dive center of choice for most tech divers. Guiding is done by local staff members who are all trained as divemasters and technical wreck guides. Accommodation is at the nearby hotels, Herbie's Mansion, Boardwalk Inn, and Mango Valley.

name: Scuba Tech Philippines
description: Runs PADI and TecRec technical courses from a luxury dive boat based in Subic Freeport Zone. The instructor, Andy Davis, is a highly qualified and experienced UK-trained instructor with PADI, SSI, BSAC, and DSAT TecRec. Daily scuba diving trips are offered to the wrecks and reefs of Subic Bay. These trips can be tailored to fulfill diver requirements at any level. Accommodation can be booked at any hotel inside SFZ, with pick-up/drop-off included.

name: JEST Camp
description: Jungle survival training. Learn how to survive the harsh jungle environment through the courses that they offer.
address: J.E.S.T Camp, Upper Mau, Cubi-Triboa, Subic Bay Freeport Zone

Scuba diving

directions: located in The Cliff Seagrapes Royale Subic

description: Formerly known as 'Olongapo City Mall', the SM City Olongapo is a mid-sized flagship shopping mall by SM Supermalls in Olongapo.
address: Magsaysay Drive cor Gordon Avenue, Asinan
directions: by Bus: Saulog Transit (Terminal is beside the mall), By Olongapo City Color-coded jeepneys: Yellow, Red and Orange, By Olongapo City color coded tricycles, (Orange), by Freeport Taxi or by Private Vehicle (Parking Space available on the upper mall floors)

name: Royal Duty Free
description: The biggest department store in Subic. They carry imported and local housewares, cooking items, snacks, and branded clothing. Most of the items are surplus so they're actually cheaper. Has an extensive selection of cigarettes and perfumes.

name: Ayala Harbor Point Mall
alt_name: Harbor Point or HP or Ayala Subic
description: The first Ayala Mall development in the province of Zambales. This sprawling mall offers a wide variety of shopping, dining and entertainment choices. It also has its anchor stores such as Puregold Supermarket, Timezone (gaming arcade), Abenson Appliances, and four Ayala Cinemas. VIP lounges are available to special members so they could take a quick rest in the middle of their shopping or while they wait for their movie schedules. The Riverwalk area is a green park concept where people could enjoy the riverside park along with a dancing fountain. Shops and restaurants also dot this area. The mall has both indoor and outdoor activity areas where special exhibitions, shows, and bazaars are held. The mall also offers weekend and holiday sales usually extending up to the wee hours of the night.
address: Rizal Highway, CBD, Subic Bay Freeport Zone

name: Royal Duty Free Hypermarket
description: A mini version of Royal Duty Free which is a stone's throw away from Harbor Point, this store offers duty free grocery items, clothing/apparel and other imported goods.

description: A casual bistro style restaurant that serves breakfast, lunch and dinner The cafe is known to serve Italy's no. 1 coffee, Lavazza, and is famous for its unique collection of Italian menu.

description: Subic Bay's beloved restaurant that offers a variety of Filipino and international dishes. Famous for its Pineapple Rice. The place is always full so always be ready to go there early to save a seat.

description: Rooms are cozy with warm lighting fitted with wooden furniture and modern decor.

name: Playa Papagayo Beach Inn and Restaurant
description: One of the popular hotels & resorts in Olongapo and Subic.

name: By The Sea Resort Hotel
description: Pared-back rooms feature free Wi-Fi and cable TV. Most offer hot water; some have cold-water bathrooms. Upgraded rooms offer bay views and/or minifridges. Suites add sitting areas. Room service is available. There's a casual bar/restaurant offering views of the bay and live music on the weekend. Other amenities include an outdoor pool and covered picnic areas. Activities consist of water sports, volleyball, badminton and table games. Massages are offered.

name: Central Park Reef Resort
description: Warmly decorated rooms provide Wi-Fi, TVs and safes, plus minibars. All have balconies, some with bay views. Some rooms sleep up to 6 people. Suites add whirlpool tubs, kitchenettes and/or living areas. Room service is available 24/7. Amenities consist of a diner and a casual rooftop restaurant, as well as outdoor infinity pools. There's also direct beach access and secured parking.

description: Amid the nightlife district of Barretto. Seconds walk away from beachfront restaurants and bars as well as the famous go-go bars of Subic.

description: This casual hotel in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone is an 8-minute walk from SBMA Beach, 3 km from Inflatable Island water park and 11 km from Subic Bay International Airport.

name: Minor Basilica and Shrine Parish of Our Lady of the Rosary of Orani
description: Orani's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Baroque style following the 1938 fire. Since 2019, it is the only basilica in Bataan and houses a venerated Marian image of the Our Lady of the Rosary, also known locally as Our Lady of Orani.

name: Archdiocesan Marian Shrine of the Birhen sa Cotta
description: Locally known as the Cotta Shrine. A shrine dedicated to Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception and of the Triumph of the Cross of Panguil Bay, locally known as the Birhen sa Cotta. The shrine is located at the south wall of the Fuerte de la Concepcion y del Triunfo and is a known pilgrimage destination in the city.

name: Fuerte de la Concepcion y del Triunfo
description: Called "Fort of the Conception and of the Triumph" in English. Established in 1756, this fort is the oldest structure in the city. Inside in the fort is a garden, with a museum displaying artifacts from the fort and the city. On the southeast bastion is a lighthouse.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
description: Built from the remains of the original parish church after the earthquake of 1955. This cathedral was designed by National Artist for Architecture, Leandro Locsin. His simple style of squares, circles, and half circles are evident throughout the external and internal designs of the church. Alterations to the façade of the cathedral were performed later. The cathedral is home to the wooden image of the Birhen sa Cotta.

name: Immaculate Conception Pipe Organ
description: The only existing pipe organ in Mindanao, and one of only a few anywhere in the Philippines. It was Father Sean Lavery, an Irish-Columbian priest in charge of music at the cathedral, who first thought of the idea of an organ at Immaculate Conception. Funds were raised through donations and a musical extravaganza, organized by the parish, to buy the pipe organ. Father Lavery requested the aid of a German priest, Father Herman Schablitzki S.V.D., in designing the organ. Father Schatblitzki visited Ozamiz to take measurements to give to the organ builders back in Germany. Father Schablitzki himself, assisted by one carpenter and one electrician, assembled the organ in six weeks, and it was completed on May 31, 1967. It was inaugurated on July 16, 1967.
address: inside the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception

name: Bukagan Hill
description: At the top of the hill is a bell tower that houses four great bells, named "St. Peter", "St. Marien", "St. Joseph", and "St. Michael". They were originally purchased by Bishop-Prelate Patrick Cronin, D.D. for the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception. However, the bells weigh 7 tons and were found to be too heavy and too large for the cathedral's belfry. Given the recent costs of installing an organ at the cathedral, it was commonly thought that the installation of the bells would prove too expensive but, through the efforts of then Mayor Fernando T. Bernad and Jesus Y. Varela, the bells were finally given a place at Bukagan Hill.

description: Locally known for their grilled foods with unlimited rice.
address: Circumferencial road cor. Don Anselmo Bernad Ave.

name: Shanghai Boy
description: The restaurant is locally known for Chinese food.

name: Timfanel Garden and Ornamental Plant Farm
description: Formerly known as Naomi's Botanical Garden and Tourist Inn. The garden has now become one of Ozamiz’s attractions. The nursery of Timfanel Garden has grown to become one of the biggest supplier of plants used for landscaping in Mindanao. The environment afforded by the greenery surrounding the building has made it a favorite venue for different community activities, conferences and weddings. It now has three reception halls for these events.

name: 67th Boulevard Pension House
description: Single rooms with own bathroom.
address: Cebedo St. (in front of Banco de Oro)

name: GV Hotel
description: A/C single and double rooms with own bathrooms and cable TV. The GV Hotel Ozamiz has 62 rooms.

name: Rosales Travellers Lodge
description: Nice size fan single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV. Free Wi-Fi. cheapest single rooms in town.
directions: over the street from The Country Lodge

name: Tatlong Krus
description: As suggested by its name, the site features three white crosses which was patterned after the cross in Mount Calvary.
address: Juan Tinawin Street, Brgy. Nueve (9) Ibaba del Norte

name: Saint James the Apostle Parish Church
description: A Roman Catholic church built during the Spanish colonial era, featuring a Baroque brickwork with Asiatic-like jagged ridges on top. Inside the church are murals by local artist, Luciano Dans namely Langit, Lupa, Impiyerno (Heaven, Earth, Hell) and large murals of Saint Christopher. The murals are designated as national cultural treasures, although some of them are in urgent need of repair due to termite damage and humidity. There are also statues of saints whose limbs can be moved like puppets. This is usually done during religious processions for events such as Holy Week.
address: Juan Tinawin Street, Barangay. Nueve (9) Ibaba del Norte

name: Museo Ac-ac
description: A museum featuring works by acclaimed carver Luis Ac-ac.

name: Wawa Park
description: Board on motorboat rides to Laguna de Bay at the Wawa Park.

name: Ukit-Taka Festival
description: An annual festival honoring Paete’s signature heirloom industries: (wood)carving (ukit) and taka (paper-mache toys).

name: Kape Kesada
description: Small coffeehouse which also features paintings and artworks by local artists. A patio overlooks the Paete River.

name: Pagadian Airport
description: Cebu Pacific and Philippines airlines has daily flights from Manila. Cebu Pacific has flights from Cebu.

name: Pagadian Rotonda
description: It is a park within a large roundabout between two of the city's major streets. Every night, the park has dancing fountains which are accompanied by music, and during the Christmas season, it hosts illuminated Christmas displays, with themes that change annually.
directions: a few meters away from the bus terminal

name: Gaisano capital mall & Gaisano Supermarket.
description: Has a McDonald's and Jollibee.

name: Robinsons Supermarket
address: Fs Fajares and J P Rizal avenue

name: Brew 'n Bake
description: Brunch, coffee, and pastries.

name: Brown Butter Café
description: Healthy eats and comfort treats.

name: La Pergola Cafe
address: Mercedes Street, F. S. Fajares Ave

name: Bo's Coffee
address: C3 City Commercial Center, Rizal Avenue, Corner F.S. Pajares Avenue

name: Mardale Hotel and Convention Center
description: Hotel and convention center.

name: Lexx Pensionne
description: A/C double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.
address: corner Datoc street and Rizal aveune

name: JRC Grand Hotel and Restaurant
description: A/C double with own bathroom for 12 hours. A/C double with own bathroom for 24 hours. Has 36 rooms. Cable TV in all rooms. Free Wi-Fi.

name: GV Hotel
description: A/C single and double rooms all with own bathrooms and cable TV. The GV Pagadian has 50 rooms. There is also a GV Hotel in Ipil which has 33 rooms and rates from ₱450 a night.

name: Napsally Pension House
description: A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Pagsanjan Falls
description: It is a moderate-sized waterfall (perhaps 15-20 meters) upstream from the town, but very pretty. The trip there is mostly through wild jungle in a deep canyon. Very scenic. If you are fortunate you may even see monkeys in the jungle along the canyon walls. The falls are also claimed by the municipality of Cavinti, hence its alternate name.

name: Diocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe
description: The town's Roman Catholic church, it was rebuilt in its original Spanish colonial-style minus its dome after sustaining heavy damage from World War II-bombardment. It houses a venerated image of Our Lady of Guadalupe that was donated by Mexico. A side chapel contains funeral plaques of residents from the colonial era. A side room to the left of the entrance leads to a parish store selling themed memorabilia.

name: Pagsanjan Arch
description: One of the few-surviving town gates in the Philippines from the Spanish era, the three-portal structure is a designated National Cultural Treasure that sits directly on the highway from Santa Cruz.

name: Heritage Houses
description: Despite heavy bombing during World War II, Pagsanjan retains a sizeable number of houses from the colonial era, some of which have been converted into restaurants or commercial outlets. These are concentrated in the town center, particularly in J.P. Rizal, Mabini and P. Caballes Streets.

name: Pagsanjan Public Market
address: Calamba-Pagsanjan Road corner F.T. San Luis Avenue, Barangay Biñan

name: Areza Mall and Shopping Complex Pangsanjan
BDO Pagsanjan
address: Rizal corner F. de San Juan Streets

name: Aling Taleng's Halo-Halo
description: In operation since 1933, it serves Filipino dishes and delicacies in group-sized portions. The highlight is the halo-halo, which includes sweetened heart of palm (ubod). It also sells takeaway Filipino snacks such as banana chips and biscuits.
directions: Turn right from Calamba-Pagsanjan Road over the Balanac bridge leading to Cavinti.

name: Calle Arco Restaurant
description: Set in a 1950s house full of antiques and souvenirs from the owners' travels abroad, it serves Laguna dishes based on recipes passed down by the owners' family.

name: Dragon Hotel
description: Choice of A/C or non A/C rooms, starting at ₱300 and ₱200, respectively. Has free WiFi.
address: KGA Building, Dita Road, Biñan Road

name: La Corona de Pagsanjan Resort and Training Center
description: Houses an obstacle course (High Altitude Ropes Course Challenge) and a 2-hectare camp site. It also offers 35 cottage-style rooms, 2 swimming pools, function rooms, and various sports facilities.

name: Casa Marina Bed and Breakfast
description: A hotel set inside a converted heritage house. Also organizes tours of Pagsanjan Falls and other natural attractions in eastern Laguna.

name: GV Florida Transport
description: Offers sleeper buses with built-in toilet going to/from Manila via Laoag.
directions: at the back of the Mormon church

name: RCJ Bus Lines
description: Earnshaw cor Lacson St. Manila +63 2-7819306

name: GMW Buses
description: To/from Laoag and to/from Tuguegarao.

name: Saud White Beach
description: Heart-shaped cove popular with both national and international tourists, movie producers, and travel writers with its emerald water and breathtaking views.

name: Bantay Abot Caves
description: Verdant seaside knoll that, on account of seismic and wave pressures, developed a tunnel that is frequented by swallows and the sea at times.

name: Timmangtang Rock
description: Timmangtang rock stands majestically a few meters away from Bantay Abot caves along the shoreline. You cannot separate Bantay Abot Cave from the Timmantang Rock for they are believed to be lovers, the former being the female and the latter the male. They are collectively termed as "Lover's Rock". This rock is bell-shaped, hence the name Timmantang and affords views of the calm blue sea.

name: Nacatnagan Cliff
description: Cliff marked by virgin forest with rare ferns and wild orchids growing below. Some mountain climbing opportunities. From the top, you can glimpse panoramic views of Pasaleng Bay, Maira-ira Point, Sitio Gaoa, and even Babuyan Island on a clear day.

name: Malingay Cove (Blue Lagoon)
description: Half-moon bay tucked away below Maira-ira Point with Nacatnagan Cliff to the east and Dos Hermanos in the north. Here thick forest meets crystal blue waters and fine white sand.

name: Dos Hermanos Islands
description: Sea stacks with caves noted for seaweed "gamet" harvesting and tropical fisheries.

name: Kabigan Falls
description: Enchanting waterfall surrounded by thick forest and well-known for its concavity.
directions: 1.8 km south of AH26 via marked roadway.

name: Saguigui Falls
description: Small relatively unknown waterfall 3.5 kilometers away from the national highway.

name: Patapat Viaduct
description: Elevated viaduct hugging the cliff of the North Cordillera Mountain Range along the sea that is sometimes referred to as the "French Riviera of the North". Along the expanse is Mabugabog Falls used for hydroelectric power. The viaduct is part of the Manila North Road (AH26).

name: Bolo River
description: Some kayaking opportunities around Dampig, Tarrag, and Poblacion 1.

name: New Pagudpud Public Market
description: Has a bus terminal for travelers coming to and from Laoag.

name: Maria Exaltacion Lodge
description: 8 multi-colored rooms; (6 m² wide, fully air-conditioned, with 2 double beds, cable TV, bathtub, heated shower, free Wi-Fi and back-up lighting generator.

name: Madrid Beach Resort
description: Off and mid peak season rates: ₱800-2500.

name: Palm Grove Saud Holiday Complex
description: Palm Grove Saud Holiday Complex and beach resorts close to famous Saud white sand beach in Saud, Pagudpud.

name: Terra Rika Beach and Dive Resort
Northridge Beach Resort
description: Single/double with own bathroom and TV.

name: Saint Peter of Alcantara Parish Church
description: The church was built in the 18th century and features elaborate Baroque carvings in its plastered, cream-colored exterior. Its interior consists of an ornate altar, a holy water font carved with a resemblance to a gargoyle, an old painting of the Final Judgement made by artisans from neighboring Paete, and folksy, vibrant ceiling frescoes inspired by Sistine Chapel and the town's devotion to Our Lady of Turumba, a venerated painting of the Virgin Mary that washed up in the town. The second floor of the adjacent convent houses the Turumba image itself, while the ground floor contains a museum about the Turumba and a souvenir store.
directions: in front of Pakil town plaza, across the old municipal hall

name: Mount Ping-as Pilgrimage Park
description: A hilltop Roman Catholic pilgrimage site featuring the Stations of the Cross and a Hollywood-like Pakil sign.

name: Turumba Spring Resort
description: Pakil prides itself on its pristine spring waters coming from the Sierra Madre, such that even local floods sometimes produce a blue-green rather than mud-brown color. The resort, which is supplied by natural spring water, is also said to have therapeutic and even miraculous powers, with pilgrims to the Turumba Festival also coming to bathe or drink the waters to bolster their experiences.

name: Estaca
description: A small wharf over the Pakil River with panoramic views of Laguna de Bay and Pakil town itself.

name: Turumba Festival
description: Regarded as the longest religious festival in the Philippines, lasting from April to October, although in practice the festivities are only done on 11 occasions between those said months. It is held to honor Our Lady of Turumba, a painting of the Virgin Mary regarded as miraculous and involves participants dancing and singing as the image is taken from Pakil Church to the streets for a procession.

name: Clemente Campsite
description: An upland resort nestled in the Mount Sembrano range.

name: M & W Townstore
address: Tavera corner V. Rarela Streets, Baño

name: Palanan Airport
directions: at the western edge of downtown

name: Aguinaldo Shrine
description: A small memorial to Emilio Aguinaldo and Palanan's heyday as the last capital of an independent Philippines fighting against the American occupation. It was built on the site of Aguinaldo's residence, where he was also captured by the Americans on March 23, 1901, a day after his birthday.

name: Saint Mary Magdalene Parish Church
description: Palanan's main Roman Catholic church. It retains three bells from the Spanish era.

name: Dicotcotan Beach
description: A 3 km stretch of white-sand beach facing Palanan Bay. Its name derives from the soft sand light enough for human feet to sink through.

name: Diago Beach
description: A less-visited white sand beach directly facing the Pacific Ocean, on the other side of the peninsula on where Dicotcotan Beach is located.

name: Palanan Lighthouse
description: A lighthouse guarding the promontory separating Palanan Bay from the open waters of the Pacific Ocean. It also marks the easternmost point of northern Luzon.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: A pristine blue-colored lagoon curiously situated further south from downtown Palanan, at a significant distance inland from the coast. There is no visible outlet, although there are fishes living inside of it apart from a spillway that channels some of its waters towards the Palanan River.
directions: take a 20-minute tricycle ride from downtown Palanan

name: Diddadungan Beach
description: A stretch of white-sand beach facing the Pacific Ocean.

name: Digoyo Point
description: In July 1972, the ship MV Karagatan, which was carrying weapons destined to the New People's Army from China, ran aground on the reefs surrounding the area and was intercepted by the security forces. This incident later became the reasons Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos cited in his subsequent decision to impose his Martial Law dictatorship two months later. The wreckage of the ship is a highlight of diving activities in the area, alongside the adjacent coral reefs.

name: Culasi Beach
description: A stretch of black-sand beach facing Palanan Bay that forms a sandbar at the mouth of the Palanan River.

name: MacArthur Landing Memorial National Park
description: A protected area that commemorates the historic landing of U.S. General Douglas MacArthur at the start of the campaign to recapture and liberate the Philippines from Japanese occupation on 20 October 1944.

name: Palo Cathedral
alt_name: Palo Metropolitan Cathedral, Metropolitan Cathedral of Our Lady of the Transfiguration
description: This Roman Catholic cathedral was built in 1596 by the Jesuits. It served as a military hospital during World War II, and in 2013, was badly damaged by Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda). Palo Cathedral also hosted Pope Francis' visit to the Philippines, also dedicated to the victims of Typhoon Haiyan.
address: San Salvador Street corner F. Sevilla Street

name: Palo Public Market
description: The municipality's central market, destroyed during the onslaught of Typhoon Haiyan, but was rebuilt.

name: Acacia
description: Mostly meat dishes. They also serve wine.

name: Kandingan/Bulaloan ha Palo
description: Home-cooked bulalo and goat (kanding) dishes.

name: Seafood and Ribs Warehouse
description: Grilled seafood dishes and spareribs.

name: The Oriental Leyte
description: Rooms are locally themed. There is free WiFi and rooms have a TV. Better rooms have dining areas and balcony views of the beach. Some rooms that can accommodate up to 10 people have hot tubs and kitchenettes. Amenities are a pool, spa, Asian fusion restaurant, ballroom, infinity pool and a poolside bar. Free breakfast and laundry.

name: Hutton Lodge
address: Corner Evangelista and San Francisco St

name: Chiong Bed & Bath
description: a/c double room with cable tv. free wifi.

name: Love Travellers Inn
description: fan/a/c single/double rooms. free wifi. some rooms have cable tv.

name: Grants Building Travellers Lodge
description: a/c 12 bed dorm. free wifi. double room ₱700.

name: Cham's Inn
description: a/c single/double and dorm.

name: Churches of the province
description: Pampanga is host to many old and beautiful churches. The oldest and largest of which is the Lubao Church, which was built in 1570 and boasts a fine altarpiece. The most beautiful, however, is the Betis Church which is often tagged as the "Sistine Chapel of the Philippines" because of its painted wall and ceilings, and its sumptuous retablo. The Bacolor Church is famous for being buried up to its ceiling by the lahar flows from Mt. Pinatubo. Minalin Church is famous for its ornate altarpiece-like facade Other notable churches include San Luis Church, Guagua Church, Sta Ana Church, Apalit Church, Arayat Church, Sta Rita Church, Angeles Church, and San Fernando Cathedral.

name: Trek Mt. Pinatubo
description: Mount Pinatubo erupted in 1991 and is now open for tourism. It has an elevation of 1,485 m (4,872 ft) and a beautiful crater lake where you can swim. This trek can be done as a day tour if you leave very early on the morning.

name: Bird watching at Candaba
description: The best time to go bird watching is on the early morning, around five to seven in the morning when bird activity is at its peak and the heat is not intense. Late afternoons are also a good time for this. Must brings are hiking footwear and clothes, and a good pair of binoculars or telescope. The avid birdwatcher might also want to bring his or her field notebook, pencil and camera. Expect to pay a fee at the bird sanctuary of at least ₱150. Migratory birds are best seen in the marsh from November-February. The marshland is flooded during the rainy season, usually September-October, when the bird sanctuary becomes submerged and inaccessible.

name: Kamp Hayahay
description: It is highlighted as a potential ecotourism park featuring natural scenery and a relaxing environment for visitors looking to unwind.

name: KOME kome
description: Selling noodles.

name: Fruits
description: The city is famous for bananas and pomelos.

name: Residencia de Cristita
description: Air-conditioned rooms with cable TV, refrigerators and WiFi. Safe parking.

name: Jams Apartelle
description: A/C rooms with own bathrooms and cable TV.

name: Santa Monica Parish Church
description: Panay's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1884. Its main highlight is the church bell, which at 10 tonnes, is dubbed as the heaviest in Asia. There is also an ecclesiastical museum.
address: Iloilo East Coast-Capiz Road, Poblacion Ilaya

name: Pawa-Buntod Beach
description: A 3 km stretch of black sand along the barangays of Pawa and Buntod.

name: Napti Island
description: An uninhabited islet surrounded by white sand beaches and coral reefs.

name: Mangrove Forest
description: The largest mangrove forest in Panay Island, with an area of 371.03 ha. It is situated at the mouth of the Panay River and covers the barangays of Lat-asan and Buntod.

name: Nuestra Señora dela Natividad Parish Church
description: Pangil's Roman Catholic church was largely rebuilt following World War II destruction in a more modernist style, resulting in an austere and smooth look. It is known for hosting the Nuestra Señora de la O, a rare venerated image of the Virgin Mary in her pregnant state, and Santo Niño de la O, an equally venerated image of the Christ Child. At the side of the building is a memorial to Charles III and his supposed exile in Pangil.

name: Ambon-Ambon Falls
description: A cascade along the Pangil River that literally means "Drizzle-Drizzle" in Filipino.

name: Buntot Palos Falls
description: A cascade along the Pangil River that literally means "Eel's Tail" in Filipino.

name: Saint Mark the Evangelist Parish Church
description: A Spanish-era looking church.

name: Panguil River Eco-Park
description: An extensive ecotourism site covering the Pangil River watershed and much of the Pangil highlands including forests and waterfalls. It also provides overnight accommodation.

name: Bohol–Panglao International Airport
description: A new airport, large enough for international flights using large aircraft. It is expected to handle many charter flights for package holiday companies. Until this airport opened Cebu Airport was the only one in the country close to beach resorts and capable of handling these flights.

name: Hinagdanan cave
description: There is a tiny lagoon inside a coral cave. Enjoy a dip in a fresh water. The cave is completely dark, the guides have a flashlight. The admission is around ₱20. To get here, you can take a bus or mini van towards Panglao island from Tagbilaran. If you tell them you are going to Hinagdanan cave, they will know what intersection to drop you off at.

name: Momo Beach
description: Small quiet beach on the north west of the island. Coral reef is situated only a couple of hundred meters off shore, it's a good location for snorkelling straight from the beach.

name: Seashell museum
address: J Teofilo St, Poblacion, Panglao town

name: Momovillage
description: Specious studio/rooms (30m2) for rent in an exotic tower overlooking the tropical rainforest, 350 meter from Momobeach, 6.1 km from Alona.

name: Panglao Princess Suites
description: Family-owned vacation home. 3 two bedroom, 2.5 bath suites, dining room and kitchen with on-site management, professional security, internet and a car & driver. Each unit has a lanai with views of the ocean.

name: Pantabangan Old Town
description: The old site of Pantabangan was razed by bulldozers and dynamite before it was submerged by 50 m of waters from Pantabangan Lake, but since the 1980s it has reappeared as an island on five separate occasions coinciding with extremely low water levels caused by drought and the El Niño, the most recent being in 2026. During such occasions, there is a higher volume of tourists from outside town seeking to reach the island by boat, along with long-time residents trying to sate their nostalgia. Among the highlights are the remains of the old civic monuments in what used to be the town center, and a huge cross that was left behind at the ruins of the old Saint Andrew Parish Church.
hours: March-May, if the water levels are low enough

name: Pantabangan Dam
description: One of the largest dams in the country, it is a 107 m high structure with a length of 1615 m holding back 9174658 m3 of water from the upper reaches of the Pampanga River, sustained by the Pantabangan–Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve that covers the Caraballo mountain range in the towns of Pantabangan and Carranglan in Nueva Ecija, and Aritao, Dupax del Sur and Alfonso Castañeda in Nueva Vizcaya. There is a viewdeck at the eastern edge of the dam providing panoramic views of the reservoir and the structure itself.

name: Mount Susong Dalaga
description: Meaning "Maiden's Breast", it is the highest peak inside the Pantabangan-Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve, with a height of 1650 m.

name: Mount Kaanducian
description: A grass-covered peak overlooking Pantabangan Lake.

name: George Point
description: A dinosaur-themed nature park with large animatronic dinosaur statues, swimming pools, children's playground and overnight accommodations.

name: Lake Farm de La Marre Park
description: An agritourism-themed resort with spa and overnight accommodation.

name: Highland Bali Villas Resort and Spa
Montana del Sol Farm
description: A farmstay.

name: Paoay Church
description: A monumental church built in a mix of Baroque and Javanese architecture that took three centuries to complete. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1993

name: Malacañang of the North
description: President Marcos' official residence in Ilocos Norte, with a veranda overlooking Paoay Lake. Sequestered by the government following his overthrow in 1986, it was turned into a museum about him and his living conditions, although the exhibits mention nothing about his regime's abuses.

name: Paoay Sand Dunes
description: A stretch of sand dunes on the arid coastal plain stretching to Laoag that has also been used as a shooting location for desert scenes in domestic movies.

name: Paoay Lake
description: A natural lake with no connecting rivers said by folklore to be the site of a sunken community. It has been a national park since 1969.

name: Paseo de Paoay
description: A Baroque-themed two-story commercial building containing souvenir stores and restaurants, with a colonnaded arcade for those seeking shelter from the scorching Ilocos sun.

name: Kusina Valentin
description: Serves Ilocano and Filipino fare. Its main specialty is Pinakbet Pizza, which was invented by the restaurant and features pizza topped by the ingredients of the signature Ilocano vegetable stew, including fermented fish paste (bagoong). Also has a Sunday breakfast buffet.

name: Ulot Watershed Ecotourism Loop
description: An exciting river ride.

name: Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange
description: Pronounced either as an initialism, or increasingly as PEE-tehckss, it is one of the three common bus stations being built to replace the scattered company-owned bus stations throughout Metro Manila; this one aimed on trips to southern Luzon and interisland routes that once depart from Pasay. Connection to the LRT Line 1 is available.

name: Baclaran Church
alt_name: Redemptorist Church, National Shrine of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
description: This Modernist Romanesque Catholic church completed in 1958 is an important landmark for Baclaran, and provides a serene atmosphere away from the area's gritty side. Every Wednesday, devotees to the Our Lady of Perpetual Help and the international Redemptorist movement flock this church to pray.

name: Parañaque Cathedral
description: The original church was founded 1580, but were torn down in preparation of the invasion of the Chinese pirate Koxinga. The present cathedral was rebuilt somewhere in the 18th century.

name: Battle of Don Galo monument
description: Parañaque locals led by Don Galo, who became the namesake of the barangay nearby, helped the Spaniards to ward off an attack by the Chinese pirate Limahong off Manila Bay, but the waters nearby is now buried by land reclamation since the 1970s.

name: Manila Memorial Park
description: Founded in 1964, it is the first cemetery in the Philippines to open to cremations after the Catholic ban was lifted. Among the most notable buried here are Ninoy Aquino, who was assassinated in 1983 upon arrival at Manila International Airport, which was eventually renamed in his honor, Corazon Aquino, the first female president of the Philippines and also of Asia, who died in 2009 due to colon cancer, and Benigno Aquino III, the 15th president of the Philippines, who died in 2021; both lie together at a common tomb at a block off Bouganville Avenue.

name: DreamPlay Manila
description: The characters from DreamWorks films feature at this state-of-the-art center for kids' activities.

name: GG 999
description: I didn’t expect to enjoy this game so much It’s simple, fun, and actually pretty addictive.

name: Las Piñas-Parañaque Critical Habitat
description: A rare thing, natural habitat extant in these parts. Here you can find a mangrove trail and marine views.

name: Solaire Resort & Casino
description: Opened in 2013 as the first resort and casino constructed in Entertainment City. Solaire Resort and Casino houses 5-star hotels and a casino, as well as a theater and other entertainment facilities.

name: City of Dreams Manila
description: It was planned as the Belle Grande Manila Bay. It is the second resort and casino to be built in Entertainment City. It houses six five star hotel buildings and a casino, as well as an animated movie-oriented theme park named DreamPlay Manila built with collaboration with DreamWorks Animation.

name: Okada Manila
description: It houses a large fountain and a man-made indoor beach.

name: SM City Sucat
description: The first mall by the SM mall chain at the south of Manila, it has two buildings, connected together by a skybridge across C-5 Road Extension. Building A has a SM Hypermarket, and is larger, while Building B houses the anchored department store.
directions: Jeepneys stop at Building A eastbound, and at front of Avida Towers Sucat westbound.

name: Duty Free Philippines Fiestamall
description: Duty Free Philippines' flagship store, sits just 200 meters from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 1. This shopping haven boasts an extensive selection of foreign items, including chocolates, cigarettes, liquor, electronics, sporting goods, and supermarket items.

name: Ayala Malls Manila Bay
address: Diosdado Macapagal Blvd. corner Aseana Ave

name: WalterMart Sucat
address: Dr Arcadio Santos Ave, San Isidro

name: Robinsons Townville BF Parañaque
address: Aguirre Ave. cor. Elsie Gaches St

name: WalterMart Bicutan
address: East Service Rd. cor. Mañalac Ave., Brgy. San Martin de Porres

name: The Alley
address: 3F Ayala Malls Manila Bay, Diosdado Macapagal Blvd, cor Aseana Avenue

name: Amber Restaurant
address: 8278 Dr. A. Santos Ave. Lopez Sucat Brgy. San Isidro

name: Cozee Monkey Backpackers Manila
description: Four- to ten-bed fan or a/c dorms. Fully equipped Kitchen. Free Breakfast. Free Wi-Fi. Near the Manila airport. If you check in from 1AM till noon you pay ₱150.

name: NomadsMNL
description: Cozy homestay with wifi, a/c, and free breakfast. Rooms a little snug.

name: Casa Joaquin BnB
description: Garden-like homestay with free breakfast, wifi, and a/c. You can relax a bit from the city noise here.

name: Manila Backpackers
description: Kind of basic lodging but the host is friendly and rooms are clean. Has wifi, a/c, and flat screen TV.

name: Hop Inn Hotel Aseana City Manila
description: Restaurant, wifi, a/c. New clean hotel tower with cool blue tones.
address: Lot 9 Block 5, near corner of Bradco Ave and Macapagal Blvd

name: Lourdes Inn
description: Whitewashed guesthouse with friendly service and fulfilling breakfast (eggs, toast, etc).

name: Red Planet Manila Aseana City
description: Modern highrise with wifi and a/c and breakfast (surcharge).

name: 47 Long Beach
description: Just another guesthouse with complimentary coffee and tea, wifi and a/c, and a nice garden.

name: Okada Manila Resort and Casino
description: A snazzy casino resort that sort of looks like a glass parabola lying on its side. Plenty of ways to indulge yourself here with restaurants and pool and gaming.

name: Azure Urban Resort Residences
description: This definitely has a resort feel - lots of pools and play areas.

name: Nobu Hotel, City of Dreams Manila
address: Aseana Blvd, cor Diosdado Macapagal Blvd

name: Nüwa Hotel
address: Aseana Avenue corner Roxas Boulevard, Entertainment City

name: Hyatt Regency Manila, City Of Dreams
Pasacao Port
description: The main ferry terminal for travelers heading to Burias Island in Masbate.

name: Cultural Center of the Philippines
description: Straddling the boundary with Manila, this building complex showcases Filipino performing arts and culture. The area is also popular for jogging, and families often have picnics here, especially on weekends.

name: Tanghalang Pambansa
description: A giant Brutalist theater building that is the center of the CCP complex. It was built in 1969, and the architecture was designed by Filipino architect Leandro Locsin. It houses four theatres for different performance genres.

name: Harbour Square
description: Surrounded by a variety of dining shops, offering a diverse culinary experience. Visitors can enjoy a picturesque view that showcases yachts from the Manila Yacht Club against the stunning backdrop of the Manila skyline. A perfect spot for relaxation and appreciation of the city's charm.

name: GSIS Building
description: A significant landmark hosting both the Senate of The Philippines and the Senate Museum. Art enthusiasts can see the GSIS Museo ng Sining (GSIS Museum of Art), which showcases a diverse collection of artworks by Filipino artists from the colonial to contemporary period. The museum not only displays historical pieces but also serves as an exhibition space for contemporary Filipino artists.

name: Philippine International Convention Center
description: the venue of the 1994 Miss Universe Beauty Pageant in Manila.

name: Coconut Palace
description: Coconut lumber & shells were used for this octagonal government building & some of its furniture.
address: F. Ma Guerrero Street, PICC Complex

name: The Dessert Museum
description: Offbeat museum showcasing large, colorful sculptures of dessert items, plus sweets to sample.

name: SM MOA Eye
description: Riders of this huge Mall of Asia Ferris wheel with night lighting can take in city & bay views.

name: J.W. Roadway Bridge
description: Go here during the morning and the afternoon for the stunning view of the area.

name: Two E-Com Center
description: one of the beautiful buildings in the Philippines.

name: Mall of Asia Arena
description: A large outdoor arena that serves as an alternative venue for Philippine Basketball Association (PBA) games, most concerts, and theatrical performances.

name: SM By the Bay
description: This amusement park offers a delightful experience with a Ferris wheel, bumper cars, and other thrilling rides. Adjacent to it is an esplanade overlooking Manila Bay, providing a stunning view for witnessing the sunsets. Along the area, visitors will find a plethora of dining options to savor, making it an ideal destination for a fun-filled day with scenic views and delectable meals.

name: Star City
description: The only indoor, air-conditioned amusement park in the Philippines, with over 30 attractions and rides including rollercoasters such as the Star Flyer - the first inverted coaster in the Philippines. Plus, enjoy the country's largest permanent ice entertainment area, Snow World. Within the amusement park complex, you can also find the Aliw and Star Theatres.
address: Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex
directions: alight on LRT-1 Vito Cruz station
price: Ride pass + Snow World = ₱859; Ride pass only = ₱699

name: Manila Bay Breakwater
description: Stunning view of Manila Bay, Roxas Boulevard's Skyline, Bataan Province.

name: Cartimar Shopping Center
description: Similar to Manila's famous Divisoria, this bustling shopping area specializes in selling imitation products of well-known brands, primarily shoes, often imported from China. Here, visitors can explore a plethora of shops offering a wide range of affordable options. Besides the imitation goods, the area also hosts pet stores and plant shops, catering to those in search of even the most exotic supplies.

name: SM Mall of Asia
description: This enormous mall was constructed on reclaimed land. As of mid-2026 Wikipedia ranks it the largest in the Philippines and sixth largest on Earth. It features a wide array of mid-range and high-end stores and restaurants. In addition to shopping, the mall offers various attractions, including a large arena that frequently hosts concerts, a science museum with numerous interactive exhibits, a convention center, and even an ice skating rink. Behind the mall, overlooking Manila Bay, you'll find the theme park 'MOA by the Bay'.

name: Newport Mall
description: This mall offers a high-end shopping experience with luxury shops and dining. Located within the mall is the Newport Performing Arts Theatre, known for its musicals and various events. Additionally, there is a casino for those who enjoy gaming. Surrounding the mall, you'll find prestigious hotels such as Marriott, Hilton, and Sheraton. Conveniently, these hotels are connected by a bridgeway, allowing you to move between them without having to step outside and experience the heat, as the entire area is air-conditioned for your comfort.

name: DoubleDragon Plaza at DD Meridian Park
MET Live
address: Metro Park, EDSA Extension corner Pres, Diosdado Macapagal Blvd

name: Blue Bay Walk
address: Metropolitan Park Bldg., Macapagal Boulevard corner EDSA Extension

name: Varona Vegetarian Health Foods
description: A canteen that caters to vegetarians and vegans, offering plenty of delightful options. With a focus on plant-based cuisine, visitors can indulge in a variety of vegetarian and vegan-friendly dishes. Additionally, they also boast an extensive selection of high-quality mock-meats, providing a diverse range of meat alternatives for those seeking a flavorful plant-based experience.

name: Seaside Dampa
description: a popular seafood market, visitors can explore the market and purchase their desired seafood. For added convenience, there are nearby restaurants that offer cooking services, allowing you to have your freshly bought seafood prepared to your liking. Moreover, the area boasts some lively bars and KTV spots, providing ample entertainment options for a fun-filled evening after indulging in delicious seafood delights.

name: The Singing Cooks & Waiters Atbp
description: At this restaurant, you'll be immersed in an ambiance of joy and constant singing from the passionate cooks and waiters, creating a truly unique and lively atmosphere. Indulge in delicious Filipino cuisine that tantalizes the taste buds and showcases the country's rich culinary heritage. The staff goes above and beyond, frequently joining guests on the floor, singing, and dancing, epitomizing the genuine Filipino hospitality.

name: Ellipsis
description: This nightclub is a hotspot among college students, particularly those from the nearby De La Salle University. This vibrant venue comes alive on weekends and days leading up to holidays, drawing crowds seeking an exciting and lively nightlife experience.

name: Copacabana Apartments
description: Copacabana Apartment Manila Hotel is the pioneer in the serviced apartment industry. Established in the early 1970s, this Manila hotel carries with it a long history of quality service and dedication to excellence. Light sleepers should be warned: the EDSA Extension is one of the major highways in the southern Metro area and motor traffic will be audible even on the top floors, particularly on weekends.

name: The Heritage Hotel Manila
description: A five-star deluxe hotel, it is minutes away from the international and domestic airports, business hubs; convention centres and SM Mall of Asia, the largest shopping mall in the Philippines.

name: Kabayan Hotel Pasay
description: It offers 253 air-conditioned rooms, all equipped with cable TV, private toilet and bath, telephone, and bedside control panel. Some of its facilities and services are restaurants, function/meeting rooms, business center with Internet facility, room service & laundry, and massage service. Near Metro Point Mall.

description: A/C rooms equipped with cable television, private balcony, shower with bathub, hair dryer, phone and wi-fi internet access. Some of its facilities and services are airport and city transportation service, cafe and parking.

name: Park, Bed, and Breakfast
description: It offers 75 affordably cozy rooms, all equipped with air-conditioner, cable TV, mini-bar, Internet access, coffee/tea maker, private toilet and bath, and a telephone. Some of its facilities and services are airport and city transfers, business center, car rental, restaurant, massage service, and valet parking.

name: Pasig City Museum
description: Also found in the city center adjacent to Plaza Rizal, this former colonial mansion has been converted into a museum to showcase Pasig's rich history of culture and arts.

name: Bahay na Tisa
description: Lit. "House of Stone". It is the only remaining "Bahay na Bato" in Pasig City, still owned by the Tech Family and not yet open to public. This house has also been used in many movies relating to Spanish times due to the house's authenticity and rustic appeal.

name: The Victor
description: The Victor is a 60-m steel art installation which depicts the victory of the global Filipino. At night, it can be lit up with various colours & can be seen in the city's northern Barangay Rosario.

name: Maybunga Rainforest Park
description: Visitors can enjoy flower viewing, boating or swimming. As a green space, it offers a respite from the hustle & bustle of the city; it's also where local events are held.
directions: in the east of Pasig City
price: Entrance is free but certain attractions require payment
