name: Old Passi Municipal Hall
description: A town hall built in 1930, and the few buildings that survived the razing of Passi by the Japanese.

name: Plaza Paloma
description: This Spanish-era town square has a pineapple sculpture, its main attraction.

name: St. William Parish Church and Convent
description: A Spanish-era church with a façade that resembles more of a fortress, with large buttresses on the front and back. It was first built in 1612, to replace smaller churches destroyed by an earthquake. The architecture reflects the church's secondary purpose as a Spanish military outpost.

name: Gaisano Capital Passi
description: Has a supermarket, department store, and chain restaurants.

name: Pateros Church
description: Spanish-era parish church, completed in 1815

name: Five Star Terminal
directions: in front of Piat New Market

name: Minor Basilica of Our Lady of Piat
description: The main landmark and destination in Piat, it was established by the Spanish on a hilltop in the early 17th century, but has been drastically altered, rebuilt and expanded over the centuries to accommodate the increasing throng of pilgrims seeking blessings from the Our Lady of the Visitation of Piat, a 17th-century darkwood sculpture of the Virgin Mary that was imported from Macau and is believed to be miraculous. The present structure, which dates from the 2020s, is Romanesque-inspired and features a red-brick façade and white plaster. The church celebrates its feast day on July 2.
address: Our Lady of Piat Avenue, Poblacion I
directions: a one-way traffic scheme is in force when visiting; when entering the town center, don't turn left immediately at the junction leading to Our Lady of Piat Avenue and the Basilica as it is only for departing vehicles; instead, follow the main road then turn left at Our Lady of Piat High School towards Our Lady of Piat Avenue leading to the Basilica

name: Black Water Lagoon
description: More of a brackish pond than an actual lagoon, it forms the nucleus of the People's Integrated Agri-Tourism Center, which serves as the town's municipal park.

name: Cross in the Sky
description: A 16 m built on top of Black Hill. It is accessible following a 50 m climb and offers panoramic views of the town, including the Basilica.

name: Piat Hill Viewpont
description: A Hollywood-inspired sign spelling the town's name, built on top of a hill with panoramic views over the town center.

name: Mapannao Lake
description: An elongated lake that sustains migratory birds through its wetlands.

name: Piat Pilgrim's Inn
description: A small dormitory-like accommodation.
address: Our Lady of Piat Avenue, Poblacion I

name: National Shrine and Parish of San Antonio de Padua
description: Pila's Roman Catholic church was built in 1849. Its gray brick exterior contrasts with the red brick belltower. Its interior features an ornate altar, multiple gravestones on the walls containing the remains of Pila's high society, and an exquisite statue of the Christ Child

name: Pila Historic Town Center
description: One of the few surviving colonial-era town centers in the Philippines, clustered around the town plaza and Saint Anthony parish church and declared a National Historical Landmark in 2001. Contrary to popular belief, only the church was built in the Spanish era, while the houses and municipal hall were built during the early years of the American occupation. Unlike other heritage towns in the Philippines, Pila's houses remain functional residences owned by the same families for generations and are closed to the public. Some of them house businesses at the ground floors.

name: Old Pila Municipal Hall
description: A well-preserved government building from the American era.

name: Pila Town Plaza
description: Pila's main public and recreational space, with views of Pila Church, Municipal Hall and some of the most beautiful heritage houses in the town, a reference to the practice of rich people showcasing their wealth by building their residences on prime real estate, namely the main square.

name: IFI Saint Anthony Parish
description: One of the oldest Aglipayan churches in the Philippines, built in 1932.

name: Pila Elementary School
description: The administrative building of the town's main primary school is an American-era bungalow (commonly known as the Gabaldon) that is among the recognized national treasures in Pila.
address: M.H. del Pilar Street, Bulilan Norte

name: Clinica Napil
description: A 1930s residence owned by the same family that runs the clinic.

name: Pinagbayanan Crematorium
description: The remains of a precolonial burial site where many of Pila's antiquities were discovered. As the site stands on a private lot, access is erratic and on a case-by-case basis with the owners and caretakers.

name: Pailah Festival
description: The town's annual festival, celebrating its agricultural and natural resources.

name: Pila Public Market
address: General Luna Street corner Calamba-Pagsanjan Road, Bulilan Norte

name: Mini Puregold
description: A grocery set inside a heritage house.

name: Alfamart Bulilan Sur
address: Rizal corner Mabini Streets, Bulilan Sur

name: La Cosina Antonio
description: A restaurant serving Filipino and Western dishes inside a converted heritage house

name: Sleepy Knights Castle
description: A towering landmark in Pila that was built to resemble a medieval castle.

name: Flaming Sword
description: This is a landmark depicting a hand holding a flaming sword up in the air, which symbolized the Filipino patriots' courage and gallantry as they face the adversary and threats to their democracy and freedom. The ESPADA was inaugurated on April 8, 1967.

name: Mount Samat National Shrine
description: Also known as Dambana ng Kagitingan or Shrine of Valour, it is a 92-meter-high War Memorial Cross and a national shrine atop Mount Samat, built to honor and remember the gallantry of the Filipino and American soldiers who fought during World War II. Memorial services are conducted every April 9, which is commemorated nationally as Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valour) and known in the province as Bataan Day. Parts of the shrine, including the museum and the cross, are closed for renovation until 2027 to 2028.
directions: Turn at the junction from Governor J.J. Linao Highway
price: P75 entrance fee, P60 for seniors, disabled and students, P75 parking free for small vehicles and P200 for buses

name: Our Lady of the Pillar Parish Church
description: Pilar's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish-era in 1834 using adobe bricks.

name: Death March markers
description: Pilar was the confluence point of Allied POWs from Bagac in western Bataan and Mariveles during the Bataan Death March. Their routes are marked by the life-size white obelisks lining Bataan National Road and Governor J.J. Linao Highway.

name: Dunsulan Falls
description: This is a waterfall located at the foot of Mount Samat, northeast of the National Shrine.

name: IMA Flora's Pamangan
description: A fixture in Pilar since 1979. The family-owned restaurant's strategic location at the junction of two major highways, a buffet of Filipino and Kapampangan dishes for prices less than mall buffet chains and its two expansive mess halls have made it a popular stopover for tourists and regular motorists as seen in the tour buses parked outside. A la carte dining available. Can get crowded at lunch time. Also sells takeaway snacks and pastries.
address: Gov. JJ Linao Highway corner Roman Superhighway, Ala-uli

name: Marres Kitchen
description: Filipino cuisine.

name: Lingling Garden Restaurant
description: Filipino and Chinese cuisine. Their specials are the crispy pata (pork knuckle), fried pork belly and kare-kare (peanut stew).

name: Panumbagan Sandbar
description: A wide white sandbar featuring floating bamboo pods and cottages designed by local artist Milo Naval where you can view fish and snorkel.

name: Pili station
description: A slowly crumbling structure being rebuilt as of 2019, it is served by the Bicol Commuter route between Naga and Legazpi during weekdays. Naga-Legazpi (#500) arrives at 5:20AM and Legazpi-Naga (#1720) at 7:29PM.

name: Saint Raphael Archangel Parish Church
description: A Catholic church dating to 1819.

name: Filipino - Japanese Friendship Landmark
description: A marker erected in 1985 to commemorate the end of Japanese occupation of Bicol and the start of stronger Filipino-Japanese relations.

name: Our Lady of Remedies Parish Church
description: A Catholic church located at the foot of Mt. Isarog.

name: Mount Isarog
description: A dormant volcano and a national park open for trekking and mountain biking.

name: Balang Falls
description: A waterfall at the foot of Mt. Isarog and is the last falls of the "eight falls in one river". It can be accessible through hiking from the Bongcao trail at Barangay Curry.

name: Pililla Wind Farm
description: The first wind farm outside the Ilocos region.

name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of St. Mary Magdalene
description: Home of the ivory processional image of Saint Mary Magdalene. Built in the Spanish era in a Baroque style, its interior features exquisite ceiling frescoes.

name: San Diego de Alcala Parish Church
description: Built between 1599 and 1632 as a chapel of ease. As of August 2026, the church is undergoing renovations and is expected to reopen in October 2026, with masses being held temporary in a nearby covered court.

name: Bahay na Bato
description: A private residence built from stone bricks during the Spanish era
directions: beside the entrance to Pililla Church

name: Lyger Animal Sanctuary
description: Home to some exotic animals, such as the liger.

name: Mount Sembrano
description: An extinct 745 m volcano at the head of the Jalajala peninsula that is frequented by hikers due to its proximity to Metro Manila and its commanding views of Laguna de Bay into Talim Island and as far as Mount Makiling, on the southwestern shores of the lake.

name: Bulawan Floating Restaurant
description: Restaurant serving Filipino dishes.

name: Plaridel Church
description: Plaridel's main Roman Catholic Church, built in its current state by the Spanish in the 18th century in a Baroque style with cream-colored plaster in its facades and gravestones in the interior walls.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Simborio Chapel
description: A rare 19th-century octagonal chapel. Built on the former municipal cemetery beside the church, it now lies in the middle of a residential block after the cemetery was moved to outside downtown for hygienic reasons.
directions: take the alley from Garcia Street

name: Battle of Quingua Memorial
description: A memorial to the 1899 battle set inside a small, tree-lined park featuring a mural depicting the event.

name: Parola Museum
description: A privately-run museum on local history and culture housed inside a structure that resembles a lighthouse (parola).

name: Primark Center Plaridel

name: Banana View
description: A scenic spot frequently visited for its natural views.

name: JMP Adventure Park
description: A nature resort.

name: E.L. Tordesillas Airport (Balesin Airport)
description: A private airstrip, with a concrete runway which can accommodate propeller and turboprop aircraft. Alphaland Aviation has charter flights for resort guests from Manila and Cavite City, using planes leased from AirSwift.

address: Jose P. Rizal Street, Barangay Poblacion

description: Home to the Clubhouse and Golf Club, owned by DOLE.

Durian Garden

description: Home of the B'laan ikat weaving tradition.

name: Polomolok Town Plaza
description: A plaza beside the town hall that serves as a central gathering point for the community. Various activities, such as sports, can be done here.

name: Gaisano Grand Mall Polomolok
description: The only mall in Polomolok.

name: Megan Buko Halo
description: Specializes in buko halo, meaning halo-halo with coconut as its base.

name: Santa Catalina de Alejandria Church
description: A Baroque church dating to 1872. It was damaged during World War II, but was restored in the 1980s. Its four-storey belfry was reduced to three storeys by an earthquake in 2019.

name: Mount Pinatubo
description: Inevitably associated with the town, the volcano is the biggest draw in the area, particularly its crater lake and the lunar landscapes created along its gullies following the 1991 eruptions.

name: Dara Falls
description: A set of four cascades. Its name was shortened because its last syllables are also the Filipino word for pubic hair.

name: Pio Chapel
description: The first known circular chapel in the Philippines, built in 1861. Damaged by the 1991 Pinatubo eruption and a 2019 earthquake, it was controversially repaired in a DIY manner by locals amid limited funds and lack of advice from conservationists.

name: Miyamit Falls
description: A waterfall on the Mount Pinatubo massif. A permit from the municipal hall is needed before entering.

name: Tutulari Avatar Gorge
description: A gorge named in part because it resembles the setting from the film Avatar (the one with blue aliens).

name: Hacienda Dolores Chapel
description: A Spanish-era Roman Catholic barangay chapel, built in 1838 and repaired following damage caused by the 2019 earthquake.

name: Sandbox
description: Part of the Alviera private development, it has a giant swing and an obstacle course. Being in a relatively dry area near Mount Pinatubo, it can become hot during the months of March to May, so prepare to get sunburned.
directions: At the vicinity of SCTEX Porac Exit

name: Inararo Trail
description: One of many trails leading to Mount Pinatubo and its crater lake, with a duration of 8-10 hours and length of 40 km that is thankfully covered by 4x4 drives through gullies clogged with lahar. Although the trail's jump-off point is actually in Sapang Bato in Angeles City, the majority of the route passes through Porac and usually includes stops at other attractions along the Pinatubo massif such as Puning Hot Springs, Tutulari Gorge and Ana-an Falls. The route also passes through the ancestral domain of the indigenous Aeta communities and provides opportunities for those seeking to combine cultural experiences with the hike, especially as most guides are also resident Aetas.

name: Nasi Ya
description: Restaurant serving Kapampangan, FIlipino and Asian cuisine.

name: Wings City
description: A chicken wings restaurant.

name: Secret Paradise Resort and Nature Reserve
description: In a private, protected bay (Turtle Bay) with crystal clear blue waters, consisting of three white sandy beaches lined with coconut trees and a 3-km long coast-line frontage. Enjoy three beaches in 52-hectare nature reserve, "Sunset Beach", "Turtle Beach" and "Hideaway Beach" which are all accessible within a 15-minute walk of each other. Closest neighbours are 45 minutes walk over the hills.

name: Le Cou De Tou Village Resort
address: Lapu-lapu Street, Port Barton, Palawan, The Philippines

name: Mataguisi Church Ruins
description: The stone shell of the mission church established by the Spanish. Its interior has been partly converted into a chapel.

name: Holy Rosary Parish Church
description: Pudtol's main Roman Catholic church. While the church building itself is a bland modern structure, beside it are the partially manicured ruins of a mission church built by the Spanish.

name: Maton Bridge
description: A bridge along Kabugao-Junction Luna Road overlooking the Maton River, a tributary of the Apayao River, and some picturesque rock formations.

name: Hutungan Hidden Paradise
description: A series of rapids lined by rock formations and a gorge along the Maton River upstream from the Maton Bridge.

name: Agguimangan Agro EcoTourism Farm & Home Stay
description: A farm with homestay and indigenous crafts showroom overlooking the Apayao River

name: Aggapawan Nature Farm Cafe
description: A farm and restaurant serving Isneg cuisine.

name: JAM transit, DLTB and Sikat tourist service
description: Puerto Galera is easily accessible from areas around Manila. Most tourists prefer to take a JAM transit, or DLTB bus from its terminals along EDSA Cubao. These ply every hour between Cubao or Buendia in Manila and Puerto Galera pier. The Sikat tourist service operates one trip per day and is convenient for people staying in Manila close to Ermita. JAM transit, DLTB and Sikat tourist service, ☏ +63 2-7089628. Buses run every hour from the Manila (Quezon city) Cubao bus terminal. JAM transit is among the popular bus services. DLTB too runs buses every about 2 hours. These cost about ₱200 per trip. Sikat leaves at 6:00AM daily from the Citystate Tower Hotel on Mabini Street, Ermita, Manila. The round trip ticket costs ₱1550 and includes both bus and ferry to either Puerto Galera. It reaches Puerto Galera at 11AM.

name: PITX
description: For independent travelers, you can reach Batangas Pier from the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX). From Manila’s international airport (NAIA), you can take a bus or simply get a taxi from anywhere in the city and ask for PITX. Once at PITX, you will find a large terminal with electronic boards and multiple transport options. Look for buses heading to Batangas Pier, purchase a ticket, and board the next available departure. Travel time varies depending on traffic but generally takes around 2–3 hours.

name: Buendia Bus Station
description: Another way to reach Batangas Pier is by taking a bus from Buendia Bus Station. This is an older bus terminal, and travelers may need to ask staff or vendors for directions to the correct bus, as signage can be limited. However, once you ask, someone will guide you directly to the right bus. Unlike PITX, at Buendia Bus Station, tickets are purchased directly on the bus. More buses operate from this station compared to PITX, making it a good alternative, especially during peak travel hours.

name: Coral Garden
description: One of the best snorkeling and freediving spots in Puerto Galera, known for its vibrant coral formations and diverse marine life. The shallow waters are home to colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and occasional rays. The area is part of a marine sanctuary, ensuring excellent underwater visibility and a well-preserved ecosystem. Best explored with a guided boat tour.
directions: near Batangas Channel, accessible by boat
price: Entrance fee may apply for snorkeling tours

name: Muelle Bay
description: A beautiful hidden hideout with a natural harbor where most ferries and boats dock. The bay is lined with shops, bars, and restaurants, making it a great spot to enjoy the scenic waterfront views while having lunch or a romantic dinner. At sunset, keep an eye on the sky—giant flying foxes (fruit bats) emerge from the nearby mangrove forest and take flight in search of food, creating a mesmerizing spectacle.

name: Muelle Pier
description: A scenic harbor area with a small promenade lined with cafés and restaurants, where visitors can see flying foxes (giant fruit bats) emerge from the nearby mangrove forest as they begin their evening search for food.

name: Tukuran Falls
description: Also known as Hidden Paradise, these multi-tiered waterfalls cascade into natural pools surrounded by lush jungle. Visitors can swim in the cool, clear water or relax in the peaceful environment. The journey includes a trek through rice fields, river crossings, and tropical forest, making it an adventure in itself.

name: Tamaraw Falls
description: A scenic multi-tiered waterfall cascading into natural pools. The lower pool, located under a bridge, offers a refreshing swim in cool mountain water. A few meters upstream, visitors can enjoy stronger waterfalls surrounded by lush greenery. Nearby, a small beach area can be found along the road.
directions: 15 km from Puerto Galera on the road to Calapan

name: Underwater Cave
description: A underwater cave, known for its rock formations and marine life. Visitors can explore hidden chambers and natural rock pools.

name: Badladz Adventure Divers
description: A small dive shop known for its friendly instructors and personalized service. They offer PADI courses from beginner to Assistant Instructor level, as well as snorkeling trips, kayak rentals, and beach BBQ experiences.

name: Extreme Sports Puerto Galera
description: An adventure sports park offering a variety of high-adrenaline activities, including ATV rides, paintball, archery, airsoft, and target shooting. A great spot for thrill-seekers looking for an alternative to beach activities in Puerto Galera.

name: Land Bank ATM
description: A reliable ATM in Puerto Galera town, operated by Land Bank. Accepts most local and international cards. Withdrawal limits and fees may apply.
directions: near the municipal area in Puerto Galera
price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

name: PNB Savings Bank ATMs
description: Two ATMs available at this location, operated by PNB Savings Bank. Accepts both local and international cards. Recommended for reliable cash withdrawals, though machines may run out of cash during peak season.
directions: at PNB Savings Bank in Puerto Galera
price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

name: Candava Supermarket
description: A local supermarket offering a variety of groceries, fresh produce, household goods, and snacks.

name: HL Supermarket Golden Conway Holding Inc
description: A local supermarket offering a variety of groceries, fresh produce, beverages, and household essentials.

name: 7-Eleven
description: A convenient 24/7 store offering snacks, drinks, basic groceries, and essential items. A reliable option for quick bites, cold beverages, and travel necessities.

name: Puerto Galera Public Market
description: A bustling local market offering fresh seafood, fruits, vegetables, meats, and a variety of local goods.

name: Mercury Drug
description: A well-known pharmacy chain in the Philippines, offering a wide range of prescription and over-the-counter medicines, personal care products, and medical supplies.

name: Mr.DIY
description: A popular hardware and home improvement store offering a wide selection of household items, tools, stationery, toys, and personal care products at affordable prices.

name: Cebuana Lhuillier
description: Offers currency exchange services. Also provides money remittances, pawnshop services, bill payments, and insurance products. More currency exchange points in Sabang.

name: Robby's Cafeteria Steakhouse
description: A casual steakhouse and cafeteria-style restaurant known for its grilled steaks, sizzling plates, and hearty Filipino dishes. The restaurant also serves pizza and features a small shop selling a wide selection of cheeses, cold cuts, and other imported goods.

name: Buri Beach Resort and Spa
description: A beachfront resort offering private villas, a full-service spa, and an infinity pool. The resort is only accessible by boat.

name: Bahay Isla Inn & Hostel
description: A long-running family-managed budget inn and hostel, set in a quiet compound slightly elevated from the street. The property features small garden areas, an outdoor plunge pool. Offers private rooms (double, deluxe, family) and dormitory beds. On-site bistro and bar serve meals and drinks. Free Wi-Fi and parking available

name: Badladz Adventure Resort
description: Each room comes with A/C, hot water, cable TV and an overview over the yachts at Puerto Galera Bay. There's free Wi-Fi. A diveshop is part of the resort.
directions: at the quiet end of the main tourist pier

name: Puerto Princesa Grand Terminal
description: A bustling large terminal complex serving buses, vans, and jeepneys coming from most points of Palawan. Buses depart from a large shelter near the San Jose public market, and vans (UV Express) depart from scattered terminals nearby. The surrounding area has small shops, a small supermarket, and a public market.

name: Cherry Transport
description: Has trips every two hours between Puerto Princesa and El Nido from 4AM to 10PM. They operate a fully air-conditioned fleet, and a one-way trip costs ₱500.

name: RORO Bus
description: Has four hourly trips from 5-8AM between Puerto Princesa and El Nido. They operate a mix of ordinary and air-conditioned buses with a yellow-green livery. One-way trip from El Nido costs ₱395 (₱445 on ordinary).

name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
description: At over 8 km in length, it is claimed to be the longest underground river in the world. With its crystalline waters and spectacular cave formations, the Underground River is possibly Puerto Princesa's most popular attraction. The site was also declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1999. The winding path of the river is navigable via small pumpboats that depart from Sabang Beach. Travel time from the city proper to Sabang is about 1.5 hours (This can take closer to 3.5 if you choose to ride in a Jeepney, since you have to wait while they deliver goods along the journey.) A permit is now necessary to visit the underground river and only available in Puerto Princesa, though an online system is in construction. As of 2018, you can purchase the tickets in Sabang pier: if you do it yourself it will cost you around ₱600, if you do it through your accommodation they might overcharge you up to ₱1200. You can also ask if you can make the return trip trekking the park and the jungle: you will need to get a guide to do that but the experience is worth your time and money.

name: Honda Bay
description: Consisting of several islets with beautiful beaches, Honda Bay is the place to go to for swimming, snorkeling as well as beach and island hopping. Accessible via the Sta. Lourdes wharf which is 25 minutes away from the city. Pumpboats at the wharf can be hired to take visitors to the various islets on the bay. Arrive before 11AM to go island hopping if you require a small boat (1-5 people) and before 2:30PM if you require a larger boat.

name: Iwahig Penal Colony
description: A good example of a true correctional institute, the Iwahig Penal Colony is more of a farming community rather than a prison. Inmates often live with their families and are allowed to toil their farms to earn a living. Carving out handicrafts is also a common preoccupation and mahogany handcarvings are a good buy for tourists. The colony is about 35 minutes from the city center.

name: Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center
description: Formerly the Crocodile Farming Institute, and still referred to by locals as the "Crocodile Farm," is a tourist attraction and a national research institute devoted to crocodiles. About 30 to 40 minutes from the city center, the Croc Farm also has a mini-zoo, which features some of Palawan's endemic species of wildlife. The place is open from about 8:30AM to about 4:30PM. From Rizal Avenue you can take an 8-person covered pickup truck (labeled "Irawan") for ₱20 and the Croc Farm is the last stop; a tricycle carrying only one or two people will cost ₱100-150. Croc Farm Tickets cost ₱40 for adults and ₱20 for kids. You start with a guided tour of the crocs which last about 15 minutes. After that you wonder around by yourself in the endemic species area, where you have to be careful not to fall through a few rotton and crumbling wooden bridges. Although this is not the best managed wildlife area, the endemic species are nonetheless worth seeing and deserve your support.

name: Butterfly Garden
description: With native Palawan butterflies is about half-way to the Croc Farm (above) and along the same road. Open 7 days a week from 8AM to 5PM. Entry is ₱50.

name: Our Lady of Immaculate Conception
description: A very beautiful church that is decorated in blue and white.

name: White Beach
description: The only beach in town. Not as clean as it used to be and no longer white or pristine. But if you want to meet some of the locals and have a few drinks (alcoholic) then it's a great place. Just walk down and buy a few beers from the take away store and walk around the huts and you will be invited to join a group at a table. Lots of fun for an international traveller - if you have a great time then throw in some money for the table (₱200) or buy a cheap bottle of whatever they are drinking.

name: Ugong Rock
description: A 75-foot (22-m) limestone formation in the middle of farmlands and karst forests located near the Underground River. Main activities in the site include spelunking and zip line.

name: Rizal Avenue
description: Puerto Princesa's main commercial strip where one can find various shops, banks, restaurants, and budget inns.

name: Langogan Reef
description: New Coral reef protected by city ordinance and three falls, the largest of which is around 50 m, 5 km from the barangay.

name: Palawan Heritage Center
directions: Next to the Palawan Provincial Capitol

name: Palawan Museum
description: This is an old museum that is not very well maintained or labeled but which has a number of interesting pieces. It is well worth a visit on a rainy day.

name: Palawan Special Battalion World War II Memorial Museum
directions: on far eastern end of Rizal Avenue, near the airport

name: South Sea Pearl Museum
address: Irawan Watershed Flora and Fauna Reserve. Bgy. Irawan

name: PSU Museum
description: This is a one room museum located inside a university building. You should ask for specific directions at the front gate, because not everyone knows about the existence of the museum. The museum is located in one small room but is clean, organized, and well-maintained, with an enthusiastic and helpful staff member.
directions: about a 10-minute walk from the front gate of PSU, if you know where you are going
hours: Closed from noon to 1PM for lunch

name: Plaza Cuartel
description: Historical place, a must see site. It is the restored ruins of an old garrison where Japanese soldiers burned 143 American prisoners of war inside a tunnel and stands as a grim reminder of World War II.

name: Baker Hill
description: Check out the plants and animal in its natural habitat.

name: Robinsons Mall
description: It has a Robinsons supermarket. There is also a food court, bakeries, and assorted electronics stores.

name: NCCC Mall
description: It has an NCCC supermarket.

name: Unitop Mall
description: It has a small supermarket.

name: SM City Puerto Princesa.
description: A mall with a Savemore supermarket.

name: A&A Seafood Palace
description: Seafood prepared by a Hong Kong chef. Authentic Chinese cuisine.

name: Ditchay's
description: French cuisine and can be a very welcome alternative for those longing to eat something else than local food after a long trip. The little restaurant lets you dine in intimate ambiance while you may chat to both the cook and the owner. The menu includes a variety of French foods like coffee & tea, paté rillettes, confit, soupes, salades, tapenades, grillades, fruits de mer, porc, boeuf, poulet, canard, crépes, patisserie.
address: Manalo Ext. before Island Divers, Bancao Bancao

name: Divine Sweets
description: Great cakes (₱45-90), coffee, shakes, etc. They also serve food (untested). Wifi if you order

name: Ima's Vegetarian Restaurant
description: Very good vegetarian food. Highly recommended

name: Kinabuchs Grill and Bar
description: A sports bar and grill and a magnet for tourists and other visitors. The food is really good and customers can play pool or watch live sports.

name: KaLui Restauran
description: Amazing food and ambiance. Can get quite busy so a reservation can't hurt. Seafood is the specialty and the daily seafood special for two is ₱395.
hours: Opens at 6PM for dinner, closed some holidays

name: Artisan’s
description: Owned by a British expat and his Filipina-American stepdaughters.

name: Carpe Diem Villas & Resort Restaurant
description: Open-air restaurant set in a tropical garden inside Carpe Diem Villas & Resort. Serves French-inspired dishes alongside Filipino and international options, with a daily breakfast buffet, à-la-carte lunch and dinner, and cocktails. Open to both hotel guests and outside visitors. Walk-ins are welcome.
address: F. Ponce de Leon Road, San Pedro, Puerto Princesa, Palawan 5300
directions: Inside Carpe Diem Villas & Resort, near the end of F. Ponce de Leon Road
price: Breakfast buffet ₱750; approximately ₱400–1,500 per person for lunch or dinner

name: Cafe Nori
description: Serves Japanese cuisine with fusion and variety of Filipino and American cuisine. Also available are fruit shakes, coffee & frappuccinos.

name: Reggae Pulse Bar
description: Cool reggae bar serving ice-cold beers, beer towers/buckets, cocktails and mixed drinks. Free WiFi, a stylish & relaxing VIP bamboo lounge.
directions: between Bpi Bank and LBC on the main street Rizal

name: Duchess Pension
description: Not the newest pension anymore but offers clean beds and quiet rooms. Not all are the same, so have a look before checking in. Friendly and helpful staff. Try the sandwich with French baguette. Wifi for ₱50 (for the length of your stay)
price: Fan with common toilet S/D ₱250/₱350, aircon with private toilet S/D ₱700

name: Dallas Inn and Cafe
description: Family run guesthouse. Free Wi-Fi, quiet location, central, 3 min drive from the airport with free pick up if booked in advanced. Dallas Inn has a variety of rooms to choose from according to budget. Fan Doubles ₱600, 4-bed dorm.
directions: Follow Rizal ave towards the pier, once at Chowking turn right onto Lacao st and then take first left onto Carandang St, and walk 200 m from there to number 11.

name: Kuhl-In Pension
description: Perhaps the best address for a monthly accommodation in the city. City location but is in a green area. Monthly rate for a 2-bedroom apartment is ₱15000.
address: Libis Road Ligaya St. San Pedro

name: House of Rose
description: Offers a comfortable and relaxing ambience in their bungalows or semi-native style cottages. Surrounded by trees and situated a couple of meters away from the road, you could almost forget you are in the city. They offer free wireless internet and claim to serve delectable foods at their restaurant. They also have a swimming pool and billiards table.
directions: off Abueg, close to Badjao Seafront Restaurant

name: Aniceto's Pension
description: Fan single/double without a side bathroom

name: Abelardos Pension
description: Clean fan rooms without a side bathroom.

name: Sheebang Hostel
description: Bed in a dorm.

name: Princessa Inn
description: Fan single/double.

name: Tree House Inn
description: Dorm beds.

name: O M G Backpackers
description: Free wifi.

name: Ezy Stay Pension House
description: Free wifi.

name: J L C Hostel
description: Free wifi.

name: Garellano Tourist Inn
description: Fan double room with own bathroom.

name: Mabini Pension
price: Rates start at ₱680 for single with fan and shared bath.

name: Mabini Mansion
description: This hotel offers rooms equipped with kitchen, refrigerator, remote control colored television, individual air-condition unit, telephone with IDD/NDD access and voice mail. Mabini Mansion also offers the following facility and services: restaurant, foreign currency exchange, airport transfer to and from the hotel, daily maid service, business service and room service.

name: Grande Vista Hotel
description: Standard Single, Double and Twin Room, all equipped with Air-conditioning, LED TV with cable channels and Hot and cold shower. Facilities and services are Restaurant, cafe, and bar.
address: Malvar Street, Puerto Princesa, Palawan, Philippines

name: Sunlight Guest Hotel
description: Superior, Deluxe and Penthouse all equipped with air-conditioning, TV with cable channels and Internet connection. Facilities and services are Isabelle Grand Ballroom, conference and meeting rooms, business center.

name: Edgardo's Place
description: All rooms are equipped with air-conditioning, flat-screen TV with cable channels, safe, private toilet and bath. It also provides room service, tour assistance, airport transfer, parking, a standby generator and free Wi-Fi.

name: Casitas de az Pension
description: Standard Single, Standard Twin, and Family or Deluxe Rooms, all equipped with air-conditioning, TV with cable channels and shower with hot and cold water. Facilities and services are Wi-Fi Internet access in public areas and tour assistance.
address: Cayapas Building, Valencia Street corner Bonifacio (A. Abueg) Street, Brgy. Bagong Silang

name: Seasons Guesthouse
description: All rooms are equipped with air-conditioner, hot and cold shower, cable TV, and complimentary wireless internet access. Also offers tour assistance, massage service, vehicle rental, and laundry services.
directions: Near Pilot Elementary School, in front of Skylight Convention Center

name: Palo Alto Bed & Breakfast
description: Homey rooms all equipped with air-conditioner, cable TV, Internet access, refrigerator, and safe. Facilities and services are restaurant and cafe, spa and massage service, car rental, laundry/dry cleaning, and Palawan tours.
address: Kawayanan Street, Libis Road, Barangay San Pedro

name: Villa Leonora Beach Resort
address: KM60, National Highway, Sitio Dacutan, Barangay San Rafael

name: Liberty Park Pension
description: All rooms have A/C, cableTV, intercom, and private toilet and bath. Rooftop bar and restaurant, high-speed Internet, fitness room, and massage service.

name: Hotel Centro
description: All rooms have A/C, cableTV, mini-bar, and coffee/tea maker. Business center with high-speed internet, swimming pool, airport and city transfers.

name: La Charica Inn
description: All rooms have A/C, cable TV, and a private toilet with hot and cold shower. High-speed Internet, restaurant/café, and massage service.

name: D' Lucky Garden Inn, Apartelle & Suites
Dos Palmas Arreceffi Island Resort
description: High end beach resort.

name: The Legend Hotel Palawan
description: Perhaps the most modern hotel in Puerto Princesa. Excursion packages to the various attractions of Puerto Princesa.

name: Puerto Pension
description: Nice rooms, free continental breakfast in the rooftop Tribu Restaurant. Desk staff are helpful, nice views.

name: One Rover's Place
description: 5 min from the airport with 18 A/C rooms.

name: Palawan Village Hotel
description: A/C rooms all with cableTV, a hair dryer, private toilet, bath with hot & cold water, and a balcony/deck.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites Puerto Princesa
address: The Emerald Playa Beach and Nature Park, Brgy. San Jose
directions: From the airport, take a right on Rizal Ave, then left at the National Highway, after the 5 km mark, turn right at Brgy. San Manuel Road then follow the signs.

name: Amerson Pension Place
description: Single, Standard Double, all equipped with air-conditioning, LED TV w/ cable channels and Hot & cold shower. Complimentary breakfast and airport transfer (upon request). With Wi-Fi Internet. Other services include tour assistance and massage service.
address: Pablico Road 5, near North National Highway, Tiniguiban
directions: near Ka Inato Restaurant; 2 minutes away from San Jose Bus Terminal and 4 minutes away from Robinsons Place Palawan

name: Carpe Diem Villas & Resort
description: Small tropical boutique resort in a quiet part of Puerto Princesa, approximately 10 minutes by car from the airport. Accommodation includes pool-access rooms, one-bedroom private-pool villas and two-bedroom family villas. The resort has a tropical swimming pool, swim-up bar, restaurant, massage services and a small fitness room. Airport transfers, local tours and diving experiences can be arranged.
address: F. Ponce de Leon Road, San Pedro, Puerto Princesa, Palawan 5300
directions: Near the end of F. Ponce de Leon Road, approximately 10 minutes by car from Puerto Princesa International Airport
price: Double rooms from ₱3,500; private-pool villas from ₱7,000; family villas from ₱13,500. Rates vary by season and inclusions

name: San Isidro Labrador Parish Church
description: This is where the carabaos during the feast are made to kneel as tribute to their patron saint, St. Isidore the Laborer. This is a 19th-century baroque church located at the Kabayanan or the downtown area (Poblacion). It is also a famous pilgrimage site in Bulacan during the Holy Week or "Kuaresma". The Museo San Ysidro Labrador with its ecclesiastical collection is also situated here.

name: Casanova-Aguirre Ancestral House
description: A well-preserved house built in 1927 and used as a setting for several films.

name: Casa San Francisco
description: A house built in 1929 that was converted into an events venue.

name: Aguirre Centennial House
description: A 1920's house inside the Butterfly Haven Resort, which has a butterfly garden.

name: Casa Balbina
description: A private residence built in 1910 that has the largest veranda in Pulilan.

name: Adriano Salvador Heritage House
description: Dubbed as the "Malacañang of Pulilan", in 1908 this historical house served as the joint municipal seat of government of the two adjoining towns of Quingua (Plaridel) and Pulilan.

name: Pulong Kabyawan Agricultural Farm
description: An 7 ha ecotourism site promoting rural culture, although the view is somewhat spoiled by the presence of industrial warehouses nearby. The complex has a reconstructed colonial-era mansion containing a museum about farm life and temporary exhibitions of folk art.

name: Carabao Festival
description: This festival is celebrated annually. Pulileños celebrate the feast in honor of their saint by parading carabaos (water buffaloes) and making them kneel in front of the church as a sign of respect to Saint Isidore Labrador, patron saint of farmers. Also included in the parade are cows, horses, street folk dancers, marching bands and floats of commercial establishments of the town.

name: Robinsons Townville Pulilan
address: Pulilan Regional Road corner Dona Remedios Trinidad Highway, Barangay Cutcot

name: SM Center Pulilan
address: Plaridel-Pulilan Diversion Road, Barangay Santo Cristo

name: Funnside Ningnangan
address: Doña Remedios Trinidad Highway, Barangay Santo Cristo

name: Yodogawa Japanese Restaurant
description: Japanese restaurant.

name: Leefoo Panciteria
description: Cantonese restaurant.

name: Marahuyo Private Resort
address: Lot 3499, Dulong Malabon, Pulilan-Baliwag Bypass Road

name: Tabon Caves
description: The Tabon cave complex consists of 29 explored caves, but there are 200 caves known on Lipuun Point. They are maintained and managed by the National Museum. Diwata Cave and Liyang Cave are open to the public. The Caves were the discovery site of the Tabon Man, one of the oldest discoveries of human inhabitants found in the Philippines.

name: Tabon Village Resort
description: Fan double cottages.

name: AB Liner
description: Regular bus service from Manila (Alabang or Sampaloc, Manila) to Guinayangan and Tagkawayan via Lucena and Calauag.

name: DLTBCo.
description: Services from Manila to Lucena, and onward to Bicol with stops at towns in Eastern Quezon. Tickets can be purchased on board from the conductor on the Manila-Lucena services, but for services stopping at Eastern Quezon, reservation is required if coming from major stops.

name: JAC Liner and LLi
description: Frequent bus service from Manila to Lucena (Grand Terminal, SM City Lucena and Dalahican port), stopping at most towns and cities from Calamba.

name: JAM Liner
description: Frequent regular AC bus service from Manila to Lucena terminal, and daily service to Mauban via Tayabas. Stops at Tiaong, Candelaria, Sariaya, and Tayabas (Calumpang). Mauban-bound buses stop at Gulang-Gulang (at Lucena) and Tayabas poblacion.

name: P&O Transport
description: Air-conditioned buses run from Manila (Alabang) to Tagkawayan and Guinayangan via the Maharlika Highway and Batangas City to Tagkawayan via San Juan and Eco-Tourism Road.

name: Supreme
description: Run both regular AC and non-AC buses between Batangas City and its own terminal in Lucena, with stops at Candelaria, Sariaya and Calumpang (Tayabas).

name: Superlines
description: Daily runs from Manila (Alabang and Cubao) to Santo Tomas Batangas, San Pablo Laguna, Alaminos Laguna, Catanauan and San Francisco via Pagbilao and Padre Burgos, with a layover at Lucena. Buses either AC or non-AC, with restrooms on board. Reservations required if traveling from their Manila (Alabang and Cubao) or Superlines and own sister company Daet Express bus stations.

name: FOC Transportation
description: Services between Lucena and Northern Quezon via Tayabas, Lucban, and Eastern Laguna.

name: NCR-Rienton Lines
description: Non-AC minibuses between Lucena, Tayabas, and Mauban.

name: Araneta City Bus Port
description: Opened 2018, it is an air-conditioned replacement to the older terminal outside Ali Mall. It serves some northbound and southbound services on ALPS, Amihan, Ceres, Isarog, Peñafrancia, and Philtranco. One of the officially designated provincial bus terminals, this will be spared from the proposed closure of company-owned terminals scattered along EDSA and Aurora Boulevard.

name: ALPS the Bus
description: Frequent trips from Batangas City, Lipa and San Juan in Batangas, and tri-weekly from Iloilo City.
address: Epifanio de los Santos Avenue near corner Ermin Garcia Street

name: Ceres Transport/Gold Star
description: Frequent trips to Batangas City, and bi-weekly service to Iloilo City. Buses to Iloilo, and some buses to Batangas City have a lavatory, but travel may be slower for the latter as they will make frequent stops.
address: New York Street corner E. Rodriguez Sr. Avenue

name: Lucena Lines Inc.
description: Hourly trips from Lucena.

name: Bataan Transit
description: Departures to Balanga every 15 minutes from 2:15 to 8:15PM, and to Mariveles every 20 minutes from midnight to 8:20PM.

name: Genesis Transport/Joy Bus
description: Hourly trips to Olongapo and Baguio, and midnight departures to Baler, Casiguran.

name: Viron Transit
description: Departures to Vigan on 2:30AM, 3:30AM; 4:30AM, 6:30AM, 8:30AM, 1:30PM, 2:30PM, 3PM, 9PM, 9:30PM, and 10PM, to Tayug daily every 6:30AM, and to Bangued daily every 7:30AM.

name: Art in Island
description: Interactive art museum where visitors can pose for a picture with 3D paintings in exhibit.

name: Gateway Museum
description: Museum dedicated to Filipino arts and supporting new artists.

name: Topiary Garden
description: A small secluded garden at the top of the Gateway Mall. Benches and tables are available. See the garden's animal-shaped foliage.
directions: elevator from the Gateway Tower, or stairway from the Gateway Mall cinema

name: Socorro Water Towers
description: Historic concrete water towers built in the 1930s. as of August 2023 Cubao Water Towers is Temporarily closed.
address: 15th Ave, Cor. Col. Bonny Serrano Ave

name: "Christmas is Home"
description: Live Christmas display in Araneta Center, featuring Filipino and Western Christmas traditions and Araneta Center. It was revived in November 28, 2018, after it was held from 1966 to 2002.
directions: At the Times Square Food Park

name: Smart Araneta Coliseum
description: Officially nicknamed the "Big Dome", this is a multi-purpose indoor arena built in the 1960s, and the centerpiece of Araneta Center. The "Thrilla in Manila" match between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier in 1975 was held here; it is also the main venue of Binibining Pilipinas pageants since the 1970s. The arena gets its present name from 2010 when telecommunications giant Smart Communications bought naming rights to the arena.

name: New Frontier Theatre
description: Multi-purpose venue opened in 1967, with fast food chains, upscale restaurants and cafés outside.

name: Ali Mall
description: The oldest standing major shopping mall in the Philippines, built in 1976. It is named in honor of boxing legend Muhammad Ali, who won the famed "Thrilla in Manila" on 1975.

name: Farmers Plaza
description: Shopping mall.

name: Gateway Mall
description: The flagship mall of the Araneta Group. Opened 2006.

name: SM Araneta City
description: One of the oldest malls owned by retail giant SM, but it looks more like its older sister in Makati's Ayala Center, SM Makati. This instead houses a department store and supermarket inside; all other shops and restaurants are outside.

name: Four Seasons Buffet & Hotpot
address: Manhattan Parkview, Ground Floor, General Roxas Ave

name: Popeyes - Ali Mall
address: Ground Level, Ali Mall, General McArthur Ave, corner Times Square Avenue

name: Baker's Fair - Farmers
description: Bake Shop.

name: McDonald's - New Frontier Theater
description: The second Mcdonald's branch in the Philippines, it is located in one of the oldest structures in the area.
directions: located in GF & 2nd Floor of New Frontier Theater

name: Salazar Bakery - Farmers Plaza Mall
directions: located in 2nd floor of the Farmers Plaza Mall

name: Chill Top - Cubao
description: Roofdeck Restobar.

name: Eurotel
description: European-style rooms with basic amenities. Amenities include bar and restaurant, free or valet parking, massage, and safe.

name: Hotel Dreamworld
description: A/C rooms with free WiFi, cable TV and in-room bathrooms

name: Hotel Sogo EDSA Cubao
description: The flagship branch of the nationwide motel chain housed in red and white buildings, with four room classes.

name: Hotel 99
description: Accented A/C rooms with free WiFi and computers. No free breakfast.
address: 18 Pinatubo Street, San Martin de Porres

name: Mariposa Budget Hotel
description: Single rooms with cable TV and free breakfast. Free parking and WiFi available.

name: The Fernandina 88 Suites Hotel
description: Transportation available to and from international and domestic airports. All suites have living, dining, and kitchen areas, internet connection, cable television, air conditioning, hot & cold shower. The rooftop pool and restaurant have a nice ambience, especially if you like looking at a concrete jungle, and a complimentary breakfast buffet is available.
directions: at the back of Ali Mall

name: Novotel Araneta City
description: Has 401 suites, two classy restaurants and bars, and an executive sky lounge providing 360-degree views of Metro Manila. Each room has A/C, cable TV, desk, minibar, and coffee and tea makers.

name: ibis Styles Manila Araneta City (Opening March 2024)
directions: beside The Araneta Colesium, infront of Farmer's Plaza Mall

name: UP Carillon Bell
directions: At Washington SyCip Garden of Native Trees

name: Oblation
description: The iconic statue, sculpted by Guillermo E. Tolentino, that symbolizes the University of the Philippines and its tradition of the Oblation Run.

name: Parish of the Holy Sacrifice
description: Chapel inside the University of the Philippines Diliman campus with distinctive architecture designed by Leandro Locsin, and hosting works from five National Artists. Designated a National Historical Landmark since 2005

name: Quezon Hall
description: The centerpiece and gateway of the University of the Philippines campus

name: Academic Oval
description: Composed of Roxas and Osmeña avenues, this 2.2 km one-way road forming an oval around the University of the Philippines Diliman has space for walking, jogging, and biking, and popular for everyone.

name: UP Town Center
description: Open-air shopping mall built over the former site of U.P. Integrated School

name: Blissful Belly
description: Continental restaurant and café. Very vegan/vegetarian friendly. Cakes, bread and juices are also available.

name: Banapple
description: This once hole-in-the-wall, almost home-run restaurant cum bakeshop serves some of the best cakes and pies in town and serves mostly the intellectual crowd from the nearby universities of UP and Ateneo (who drive over just for lunch/dessert). Be sure to secure seats as a lot of students flock the place (especially during lunch, early afternoon and dinner) to sample their latest cakes (according to season) or to go for their classic Banoffee pie.

name: One Liberty Hotel
description: Basic rooms with free WiFi, cable TV, in-room bathroom, and free breakfast. Has coffee shop on first floor

name: Yuj Inn
description: Basic A/C rooms with cable TV, free WiFi, and free breakfast.

name: Maya Residence Inn
description: Provides anytime check-in, free WiFi and café and pastry shop below.

name: Fersal Hotel Kalayaan
description: It offers fully air-conditioned guest accommodation, cable television, a mini-bar and telephone. Some of its facilities and services are Some of its facilities and services are private toilet and bath with centralized hot and cold shower.

name: The Oracle Hotel and Residences
description: Standard, Superior, Deluxe and Suite Rooms, all equipped with electronic lock system and 24-hour broadband internet connectivity. Ballroom and gym also on premises.

name: Microtel by Wyndham UP Technohub
description: Has free breakfast, swimming pool, laundry, and conference rooms.

name: Iglesia Ni Cristo Templo Central
description: Central Temple of the Iglesia Ni Cristo (Church of Christ). The Central Complex includes the Central Temple, which is an 8,000-seat church with one of the largest pipe organs in the Philippines; the Iglesia Ni Cristo Museum, which showcases the history of the Church in exhibits and artifacts from all over the world, marking its global expansion; the Tabernacle, a large multi-purpose meeting and presentation hall; and the New Era University and College of Evangelical Ministry, which are the flagship educational campuses of the Iglesia Ni Cristo, established in 1979.
directions: Travel northwest on Commonwealth Avenue toward and past Quezon Memorial Circle

name: La Mesa Eco Park
description: A beautiful 5-hectare eco park on the outskirts of Quezon city. A haven for people who'd like to get away from the heat and dust of the city. Quite hard to find though, and there is little public transport going there.

name: Payatas Dumpsite
description: Clearly not for the normal traveller easily shocked by the stench and the poverty, this dumpsite, which receives a third of Metro Manila's waste, is one of the district's local landmarks. This was once an empty ravine until it was converted into a landfill to replace Tondo's Smokey Mountain. Though touring the facility requires advance permission, you can see the life of Payatas's poorer families from roads surrounding this fenced-off pit. There is a monument erected to the northeast, dedicated to the victims of a garbage landslide that killed over 300 on July 10, 2000.

name: Tandang Sora National Shrine
description: A national monument and memorial park dedicated to Filipino revolutionary and centenarian, Melchora Aquino. It covers an area of 1,000 m² and features a 10.67-m bronze sculpture. An art gallery is also hosted within shrine grounds which features paintings and other sculptures dedicated to Aquino. It also has a pavilion and stage for events, and a mini-museum dedicated to Melchora Aquino. It was completed in 2008.

name: Royal Ace Driving Range
description: Golf driving range.

name: Litex Market
description: The wet and dry market frequented by residents of the surrounding slum areas. It is also a metonym for the surrounding area.
directions: At the corner with IBP Road.

name: Ever Gotesco Mall Commonwealth Center
description: The last Ever Mall.

name: Pacific Park Hotel
description: Glassy edifice in the midst of cacophony and concrete with a bathtub type pool. Jollibee's just down the road.

name: Butler's BnB @ Trees Residences
description: An AirBnB place inside a condominium complex with access to an outdoor pool terrace for PHP 150 extra. Accommodation has hot water, Netflix, high speed internet, and kitchen facilities.

name: OYO 108 Spiral Suites
description: Lodging includes on-site restaurant and has a/c, wifi, TV, security system, and kitchen area, though what's probably best is the rooftop patio and the views.

name: OYO 136 Regal Residences
description: A lot like the other OYO property with an outdoor rooftop sitting area, a/c, and wifi, but a little noisier due to its location on a busy road.

name: Eastwood City Walk of Fame
description: The Philippines' answer to Hollywood's, it sports a row of stars used to commemorate famous television, film and radio personalities of the country.

name: EDSA Shrine
description: Opened in 1989, it is a chapel and monument designed by renowned Filipino architect Francisco Mañosa also commemorating the 1986 revolution

name: People Power Monument
description: A monument that commemorates the events in the People Power Revolution in 1986.

name: Dampa sa Libis
description: A fresh seafood market with several restaurants all under one roof, with a dining hall that seats up to 800 people at any one time. Buy some fresh seafood at the market, then have one of the restaurants cook it to your liking for an extra charge.

name: Agezuki Japanese Cuisine
description: Known for their wide variety of sushi and sashimi, in addition to traditional Japanese fare, they serve quality dishes that won't break the bank.
address: A. Francisco Bldg., 83 Katipunan Ave., White Plains

name: Apero
description: A neighborhood cafe with a selection of freshly-baked bread and pastries, coupled with an eclectic menu of French-inspired eats served in large portions.
address: The Club House, Corinthian Hills, Temple Drive, Ugong Norte

description: An unassuming jazz bar with a large selection of cocktails and imported whiskey. Guests can also listen to owner Jay Amante's large collection of vinyl records, with over 10,000 records available.
address: 2nd Floor, White Plains West, 42 Katipunan Ave., White Plains

name: Bantayog Memorial Center
description: Monument dedicated to the people who died during the Marcos dictatorship.

name: 11th World Scout Jamboree Monument
description: Monument created in memory of the 22 Boy Scouts who perished en route to the 11th World Scouting Jamboree in Greece.
address: Timog Avenue and Tomas Morato Avenue

name: Millennium Transmitter
description: The transmitter tower of ABS-CBN, providing strong TV signals around Metro Manila. It is a landmark of the district itself, and is very visible from almost every corner of the Scout Area.
address: Mother Ignacia Avenue corner Sergeant Esguerra Street

name: Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center
description: Houses a zoological and botanical garden, complete with a man-made lagoon for boating activities

name: SM City North EDSA Sky Garden
description: Elevated park with a simulated river and waterfall, part of SM City North EDSA (see #Buy)

name: Pinoy Big Brother House
description: See (#Do)

name: ABS-CBN Broadcasting Center
description: The flagship studio of the ABS-CBN media network, built in 1968 and is the Philippines' most advanced broadcasting center.
address: Eugenio Lopez Jr. Drive, South Triangle

name: ABS-CBN Studios
description: The oldest television studios inside the complex, with 10 studios housing ABS-CBN's popular shows like It's Showtime, Magandang Buhay, TV Patrol, and ASAP.

name: Pinoy Big Brother House
description: Home of the Philippine Big Brother franchise. The façade makes this more of a house, but it also hosts the studios where Pinoy Big Brother is aired. The surrounding area can become very crowded during eviction nights, where thousands of fans wait. The house is generally closed when Pinoy Big Brother is not being broadcasted.
address: 18 Eugenio Lopez Jr. Drive, South Triangle

name: Eton Centris
description: Mixed-used development with a shopping mall, lifestyle strip, and call center buildings

name: Centris Station
description: Indoor mall of the Eton Centris complex, with select restaurants, shops and a SM Hypermarket.
directions: At the corner with Quezon Avenue. MRT station: Quezon Avenue; Bus stop: Quezon Avenue

name: Fisher Mall
description: Mall owned by a fishing business in Malabon, and built over an old bus terminal. This mall has plenty of fast food chains and fast food restaurants, but not as crowded as the major ones.

name: SM North EDSA
description: The second largest mall in the Philippines, one of the world's largest malls, and the first mall of the nationwide SM Supermalls chain, SM North EDSA houses almost 1000 retail stores, services and restaurants within the mall's premises. It was the largest mall in the Philippines from 2008-2011 and 2015-2021.

name: TriNoma
description: Short for Triangle North of Manila, it is a large shopping mall in Quezon City in the Philippines owned by land developer Ayala Land. Opened in 2007, the mall is on the side of Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, near the MRT-3 North Avenue Station in Quezon City, giving significant market competition to the nearby SM North EDSA as one of the largest malls in Manila's metropolitan area.

name: Wil Tower Mall
description: Small upscale mall with a Coffee Project café and All Day convenience store, part of the 46-storey Wil Tower condominium complex.

name: Greens
description: Continental restaurant with many vegetarian and vegan friendly options including cake.

name: Music Match
description: Karaoke bar with disco and a selection of food. Smoking allowed in some rooms

name: Strawberry Hometel
description: Comfortable, affordable inn with air-conditioned rooms and international cable TVs.
directions: just behind Zirkoh Comedy Bar and Mang Inasal at Tomas Morato Avenue

name: Hotel Sogo North EDSA
price: Half-day stay: from ₱1,020 (weekdays) or ₱1,400 (weekends); Overnight stay: from ₱1,290 (weekdays) or ₱1,575 (weekends)

name: Camelot Hotel
description: Castle-themed hotel, with rooms having a royal and European feel. It has five restaurants, one open 24/7, another playing live music, and some with bars.

name: Cocoon Boutique Hotel
description: Has vibrantly colored rooms with free WiFi, cable TV, minibar with coffee and tea makers, and bathtub with hot and cold water. Larger rooms have a living room and an additional bedroom. Its rooftop has a swimming pool providing views of the Scout Area and nearby Cubao. Amenities include a bar, a restaurant, a café, a hair salon, a gym, a business center, and a spa. Free breakfast available.

name: Imperial Palace Suites Quezon City
description: This hotel offers room amenities like air-conditioning, cable television, and kitchenette, complete with daily maid service. However be prepared for possible privations (e.g. no soap/towels, dirty sheets, broken toilet seat, bad TV reception, overall dilapidated conditions).

name: Luxent Hotel
description: All rooms have in-room safety deposit box, mini bar, individual climate control, LCD flat screen with cable and DVD player. Some of its facilities and services are lobby lounge, bar, infinity pool, kiddie pool, gym/fitness center, multi-level parking, Wi-Fi internet connection, in-room suite dining service, laundry/pressing and dry cleaning, wake-up call, 24-hour concierge and security.

name: Santo Domingo Church
alt_name: National Shrine of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary of La Naval de Manila
description: Large, contemporary Catholic church, with a shrine to the Virgin Mary & an adjacent cemetery.
address: 537 Quezon Avenue corner Santo Domingo street

name: Mabuhay Rotonda
description: The name was changed during the 1990s. Built in 1948 during the term of Mayor Ponciano Bernardo. Quezon City had been declared the capital of the Philippines on July 17, 1948 and so the monument was built to welcome people to the capital, hence “Welcome Rotonda”.

name: San Pedro Bautista
description: One of the oldest churches in the country, housing the bones of the patron saint. There is also a catacomb in the basement of the church where the friars of the past were buried.

name: Wensha Spa - Banawe
address: Don Manuel Agregado Street corner Banawe Street

name: Ace Water Spa
description: Indoor swimming pool, Ace Water Spa is a brand of water themed spa. There are many instruments you can use to give you a spa treatment like hot bath, pressurized water that could "massage" you, and sauna rooms.

name: Robinsons Magnolia
description: Large shopping mall with cinema (Robinsons Movieworld) and food court.
address: Aurora Blvd, Doña Hemady St, New Manila

name: Z Square Mall
description: Urban open-air shopping mall housing a supermarket & gym along with restaurants & food stalls.
address: Banawe Street corner Del Monte Avenue

name: Bugis Singapore Street Food
description: Singaporean food.

name: Samgyupsalamat
description: Korean barbeque restaurant, part of Banawe culture scene.

name: Daily Veggie n’ Café
description: Friendly Chinese restaurant for the travelling vegan or vegetarian.

name: JT's Manukan Grille-Banawe Branch
address: 74 Scout Alcaraz Street corner Palanan Street

name: Ahma’s Kitchen
description: Chinese restaurant.

name: The Aristocrat Restaurant - 518 Banawe Branch
description: Filipino restaurant.

name: Robbinsdale Hotel
description: Nestled in a quiet corner but easily accessible from Makati or Manila through various routes.

name: OYO 190 Anglo Residences
description: Pretty typical OYO place, as in it kind of looks as sterile as a lab. Has wifi and a/c.

name: Madison 101 Hotel + Tower
description: Restaurant with breakfast and lunch buffet. Wifi and strong a/c.
address: Aurora Blvd, corner Madison, New Manila

name: Condo Studio Luxe in Princeton Residences
description: Here's a chance to stay in a condominium tower with spacious rooms, kitchenettes, and hot water. Has a pool on the 7th floor and great views of Manila from up high. Surcharge for room cleaning and food but Robinsons mall is not far with food options/entertainment.
directions: next to Gilmore Light Rail station in New Manila

name: Summit Hotel Magnolia
description: Kind of sterile looking rooms but clean with wifi and a/c, breakfast is extra. Sleek lines outside as it fits contours of mall.
address: Doña Hemady Street corner Aurora Boulevard, New Manila

name: RedDoorz Plus @ E Rodriguez Corner Banawe
description: Very sanitized-looking like somebody took a mop to it. Satellite TV, wifi, a/c, restaurant/bar.
address: 447 E. Rodriguez Sr. Ave, cor Banawe St

name: Quezon Memorial Shrine
description: The main attraction of the Quezon Memorial Circle. The Art-Deco monument which is adorned by mourning angels on each of its three pillars is a national shrine dedicated to the late President Manuel L. Quezon. Embedded artworks are also decorates the base of the shrine. At night the monument is illuminated with lights that gradually shifts its colors.

name: Dancing Fountains
description: The centerpiece of the Liwasang Aurora. It is illuminated at light with moving water features accompanied by music.

name: Liwasang Aurora
description: A circular paved plaza decorated in a style of a compass rose. Along with the adjacent stage, the Liwasang Aurora serves as the venue for various events such as concerts held at the Quezon Memorial Circle.

name: World Peace Bell
description: The World Peace Bell, housed in a gazebo, is a donation by the World Peace Bell Association, a Japanese organization promoting awareness on the world peace movement. It was inaugurated in 1994. The World Peace Bell grounds also has other features such as the Peace Wall, a mural and flag poles with names countries at its base (although flags are no longer hoisted). The grounds is also the location of the Agong of Peace dedicated to the Bangsamoro Peace Process.

name: Peace Monument
description: A marker erected to mark Quezon City as a Rotary Peace Community as part of the "Community Peace Cities/Towns" concept conceived by the Rotary Club of Wagga Wagga, Australia.

name: Philippine-Israel Friendship Park
description: A small secluded area beside the Quezon Heritage House which is dedicated to the bilateral ties of the Philippines and Israel. It features a small three-sided monument which commemorates; President Manuel Quezon's "Open Door Policy" to Jews escaping from Nazi Germany, the United Nations Resolution 181 of November 29, 1947 which led to the creation of the State of Israel where the Philippines voted in favor of Israel, and the 60th anniversary of the establishment of formal diplomatic relations between the two countries.

name: Museo ni Manuel Quezon
description: A museum at the triangular base of the Quezon Memorial Shrine, dedicated to the political career of President Quezon. The remains of President Quezon are inside a marble sarcophagus inside the museum. His wife Aurora Quezon is also interred at the site.

name: Quezon City Experience
description: Focuses on the history of Quezon City. The interactive museum is divided into multiple pod buildings which were designed to be green building compliant.

name: Quezon Heritage House
description: A historic house museum which used to be the house of the family of President Manuel L. Quezon and was at 45 Gilmore Street in New Manila, Quezon City. The museum focuses on the personal life of Quezon in contrast to the Museo ni Manuel L. Quezon which focuses on Quezon's political career.

name: Presidential Car Museum
description: Museum featuring land vehicles which were owned and/or used by past Philippine Presidents.

name: Hardin ng mga Bulaklak
description: The Hardin ng mga Bulaklak is a flower garden which is a project of the city government, the Succulent and Cactus Society of the Philippines, and the Philippine Horticultural Society. It features various indigenous flowers and is often a location of gardening and flower shows by various gardening societies of the country.

name: Tropical Garden
description: Garden featuring tropical plants which was inaugurated in October 2012. It features a small pond as well and is another venue for gardening and flower shows.

name: Joys of Urban Farming
description: The urban farm where vegetables are planted in the park is part of Vice Mayor Joy Belmonte urban farming project, "Joys of Urban Farming". A custodian is available within the farm's premises where visitors could learn about growing crops at their own backyard.

name: Charito L. Planas Garden
description: A small fenced garden dedicated to Quezon City Parks Development Foundation head, Charito L. Planas who was responsible for the rehabilitation of the park in the early 2000s.

name: Fern Garden
description: A garden dedicated to ferns, however as of 2016, only a few ferns are present at the garden. Nevertheless, the garden provides a secluded place for park visitors that prefers a quieter place.

name: Cactus Garden
description: In a secluded area behind the Hardin ng mga Bulaklak, the Cactus Garden features cactuses and succulents of various types and sizes some almost as tall as a human. It also has a greenhouse but is usually off-limits to visitors.

name: Quezon City Memorial Circle Zipline
description: For the adventurous and definitely not for the faint-hearted. Zipline from a height equivalent to about four-stories. The path of the zipline crosses the Pedal N' Paddle Pond. One Zipline station is near the Children's Playground and the other near the Joy of Urban Farming.
price: ₱100 (one way) ₱150 (two way); senior citizen rates ₱80 (one way), ₱130 (two way)

name: Circle of Joy
description: A children's playground within the park. The playground features various slides and other attractions such seesaws. The grounds are either covered in concrete or artificial grass which reduces the likelihood of little kids from getting dirty while still having fun.

name: Circle of Fun
description: An amusement park within the park. It features various attractions and rides such as the "Fun Drop" a drop tower ride and the "Sea Dragon", a pirate ship type of amusement ride.
price: ₱30 entrance fee (except children below 3 ft and senior citizens)

name: QMC Bicycle Rental
description: Bicycles and bicycles with side cars can be rented from a station located near the Children's Playground. The use of the rented vehicles are only for a bicycle track which circles around the Children's Playground.

name: Pedal N' Paddle
description: A amusement space featuring bicycle and pedal-powered-boat rentals.

name: Pokemon Go
description: A suitable place for players due to many Poke-stops within the park's premises, although the use of mobile data is highly recommended since the public Wi-Fi is unreliable.

name: Tropical Hut
description: A good place to order burgers. Other food such as chicken and sundaes are also available at this fast-food restaurant.

name: Max's Restaurant
description: A Filipino restaurant popular for its chicken.

name: New Kamameshi House
description: A Japanese restaurant which offers an array of sushi as well as yosenabe or Japanese hot pot.

name: Passenger Terminal Building PMO-Legazpi
description: Has boats to Rapu-Rapu, and is being developed as a cruise terminal to serve domestic and foreign cruises.

name: La Conchita Hotel and Resort
description: It offers a quiet, rustic, and private ambiance. Dining includes an on-site restaurant. It is the only hotel on the frontier island. Its sprawling, secure grounds enclosed by a 10-meter fence. The resort provides 14 air-conditioned rooms.

name: Thunderbird Resort Rizal
description: A/C rooms equipped with mini-bar, cable TV, coffee/tea maker and free wi-fi access. Some of its facilities and services are business center, swimming pool, and casino.

name: Saint Raymond of Peñafort Parish Church
description: Rizal's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1617 in a baroque style using stones quarried from the Matalag River. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001 on account of its age and dual function as a fortress against raids by Kalingas and Isnegs from Apayao.

name: Biuag and Malana Ecopark
description: A pair of mountains separated by the Matalag River and named after two opposing giants in local folklore. Derisively known as Ambush Point as it was a favorite site by NPA rebels to stage attacks on military convoys in the 1970s and 80s, it was redeveloped by the local government into an ecotourism venue containing picnic grounds, a bicycle zipline and a cable car.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: A secluded and pristine freshwater natural pool in the Zinundungan Valley.

name: Mount Annaguan
description: The highest peak in town, at 1400 m. The summit holds views of the town as well as the neighboring provinces of Apayao and Kalinga.

name: Padekat Festival
description: Named after the local term for rice cake, it is the town's annual festival marking the establishment of the municipality on April 26.

name: Casa Carolina
description: A pension house and the only accommodation in town.

name: Wawa Dam
description: an old reservoir

name: Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary Parish Church
description: The town's main Roman Catholic church.

name: Avilon Zoo
description: The largest zoo in the Philippines in terms of land area and collection of animals.
price: ₱800, concessions for children, elderly and disabled

name: Espadang Bato
description: A rock that looks like a big sword.

name: Rodriguez Ancestral House
description: A colonial-era house that used to be the residence of the town's namesake, Senate president Eulogio Rodriguez.

name: Mount Irid
description: A 1467 m high peak near the triboundary with Rizal, Laguna and Quezon provinces that is also claimed by the municipality of Tanay. The mountain is home to a few endemic wildlife including subspecies of orchids, rafflesias, pitcher plants and forest mice.

name: Mount Balagbag
description: A 777 m peak at the boundary with the city of San Jose del Monte in Bulacan province used as a stand-in location for films set in northern Luzon and one of the closest hiking destinations to Metro Manila.

name: Montalban Town Center
description: The only mall in Rodriguez.
address: Rodriguez Highway corner R. Reyes Street, San Jose

name: Primark Center Kasiglahan
address: Block 1, San Jose Plains, Kasiglahan Village, San Jose

name: Robinsons Easymart Birmingham
address: A. Mabini Street, Birmingham Meadows, Burgos

name: Puregold Montalban
address: Rodriguez Highway corner D. Marcelo Street, Rosario

name: Romblon Airport (Tugdan Airport)
description: Served by a thrice-weekly by Cebgo and by AirSWIFT twice-weekly flight from Manila.

name: Romblon Shipping Lines
description: Operates a ferry from Manila and Masbate to Romblon Island.

name: Montenegro Shipping Lines
description: Ferries from Batangas City to Romblon town.

name: 2GO Travel
description: Operates a ferry from Batangas City to Romblon 2/3x weekly, and from Roxas City.

name: Starhorse Lines
description: Operates ferries from Dalahican port in Lucena, Quezon, with stops at Kawit (in Marinduque) to Banton, San Agustin, Romblon town, and Sibuyan Island, twice weekly.

name: Twin Forts
description: at the peak of San Andres and Santiago hill, constructed by the Spanish in the 1640s. It is now a declared National Cultural Treasure under the protection of the Philippine government through the National Museum of the Philippines. There is a strenuous climb up the stairs to reach the forts situated at the summit of the hill; however, the reward is well-worth it as it affords a magnificent view of the picturesque town and bay.

name: Rosario Church
alt_name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary
description: Rosario's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and containing the venerated painting of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary, Queen of the Caracol.

name: Casa Hacienda de Tejeros
description: A partial reconstruction of the friar estate manor where the first provisional Philippine government was established during the Philippine Revolution against Spain on March 22, 1897, although most history textbooks erroneously place the site in General Trias, whose boundary with Rosario lies along the southern perimeter wall of the compound.

name: Caracol Festival
description: The town's patronal festival is held twice a year to commemorate the feasts of Saint Isidore the Laborer and Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary. Both occasions feature a procession of the Marian Caracol image, accompanied by street dancing to the tunes of the pandanggo folk dance at a slow pace resembling that of a snail (caracol).

name: Tinapa Festival
description: An annual celebration of Rosario's signature product, smoked, cured fish (tinapa).

name: SM City Rosario
description: The largest mall in Rosario and part of the SM Malls chain.
address: General Trias Drive corner Costa Verde Access Road, Tejeros Convention

name: Rosario Public Market/Primark Town Center
description: An amalgamation of the town's main market and a department store chain.
directions: at the back of Rosario Municipal Hall

name: Red Planet
address: Block 5, Lot 7-10, Market Avenue, Costa Verde

name: PNB Bank
description: Has a Visa Card ATM.
price: Has a ₱200 fee for overseas cards
