description: Fan single/double with own bathroom

name: Danna Hotel
description: Fan single/double rooms with own bathroom.
directions: over street from Roxas public market

name: Roxas Villa Hotel
description: Fan single/double room with own bathroom.

name: EN Jays Pension house
description: Fan single, fan double.

name: Roxas City Integrated Terminal
description: Roxas City's central bus station, with transfers to jeepneys and trikes to downtown and nearby towns. Just beside it are a few shops and a supermarket. Buses, vans and jeepneys will drop you off on the main road. The bus departures are at middle, jeepneys to the east and vans to the west.
address: Integrated Transport Terminal, Sacred Heart of Jesus Ave

name: Roxas Airport
description: Cebu Pacific (2 flights), PAL Express and Philippines Air Asia flies daily from Manila, all using an Airbus A320 jet.

name: Port of Culasi
description: 2GO Travel has a ferry from Roxas City from Batangas City via Romblon island 3 times a week. Super Shuttle has a direct RORO ferry from Batangas City. To get to the city center, take a tricycle from outside the port gates.
directions: near the Culasi Lighthouse take a tricycle from downtown

name: Barangay Culasi Lighthouse
description: Take a 20-min walk to the base of the lighthouse, which has a viewing deck overlooking the sea and some islets.

name: Ang Panublion Museum
description: The Roxas City Museum was once a circular water tank that has been creatively reused as a museum. It has exhibits about local and indigenous Panay culture, and the tourism office.

name: Santa Monica Parish Church
description: It was built in 1884 on the site of an earlier church. The church is built of coral blocks and is approximately 70 metres long, 25 m in width and 18 m in height; the walls are about 3 metres thick. The church has an unusually large bell, the largest in the country and in all of Asia. It was cast by Juan Reina in about 1884, using sacks of coin given by the people of the town; it weighs more than 10 tonnes.

name: Palina Greenbelt Ecopark
description: Ecological park.

description: Tourist attraction.

description: Fan single/double rooms with own bathroom.

name: RedDoorz Plus @ San Roque Roxas City
RedDoorz near Plaridel Street Roxas City
La Laguna Viewpoint
description: Along the sidewalk that leads between Big La Laguna and Small La Laguna you'll find a narrow path. Follow the path for 20 meters up the stairs and onto the top of a rocky out cropping which has an oddly placed cement pad at the top, as if for a house. From the top of the outcrop, you'll be provided with some lovely views of the surrounding beaches and the surrounding islands.

name: La Laguna beach
description: Located a short walk around the hillock off the upper edge of Sabang beach, this is a short beach (about 300 metres in length) and yet miraculously further divided into Big La Laguna and Small La Laguna beach. The beach is clean, with white sand (unlike the brown sand of Sabang), filled mostly with day tourists, has a few quiet resorts and at least five dive shops as of 2012. It is especially popular with Koreans.

name: Lighthouse Walk
description: Follow the road up past the market to the village of Sinandigan and on to the lighthouse where there is a spectacular view of the Verde Island Passage and Luzon to the north, and on a clear day the summit of Mt Halcon to the south. To the east you can see the City of Calapan in the distance and further on the horizon, the island of Marinduque.

name: Sabang Webcam
description: If you want to see Sabang Beach live, there is a website that has three webcam locations for Sabang beaches, one each for Big La Laguna, Small La Laguna and Sabang. The webcam image frequency is once every 30 seconds so you can see the real-time vista, the weather and the people and boats coming and going.

name: Puerto Galera Reefs
description: A snorkeling and diving destination with coral gardens and diverse marine life, including sea turtles and reef fish.
directions: Various dive shops in Puerto Galera offer trips

name: ABWonderdive
description: A PADI 5 Star Dive Beach Resort owned and operated by Danish couple Alice and Bjørn Askholm in Small Lalaguna. Offering all level of PADI courses – from entry level up to Dive Master, as well as a wide variety of specialties taught in English, Scandinavian, German, French and Tagalog. Accommodation is in their own nicely appointed rooms or in one of the many resorts nearby.

name: Action Divers
description: A smallish dive shop has been in Small Lalaguba but is very proud of its high level of customer satisfaction and safety. They generally run 3 dives a day at 9AM, midday and 3PM. Local guides know all the good spots and understands the tides in the Verde Channel. If you contact them they can put together diving and hotel packages to suit your needs.

name: Asia Divers
description: A reputable dive shop. The divemasters, hailing from Britain, Germany, and Canada, are friendly and dive in smaller groups (usually four divers and one divemaster). They typically run four dives each day, including one night dive, and put together some nice hotel/dive packages with their sister resort, The El Galleon, located adjacent to their dive shop.

name: Atlantis Dive Resort
description: A Five Star PADI Career Development Centers; two of only few dive centers with such a rating in Asia, you will find the highest standard of dive education, first class facilities and world class dive guides.

name: Big Apple Dive Resort
description: The resort is in the middle of Sabang beach. The bar and restaurant are open 24 hr, serving a wide range of food and beverages. With two full size billiard tables in the bar overlooking the bay of Sabang, and a wide range of accommodation to suit all budgets from cottage style fan rooms to luxury air conditioned apartments with standby generators guaranteeing 24-hr power. There is 'Super Sports' Satellite TV showing live sports events from around the world. Fully equipped dive shop adjacent to an excellent swimming pool offering PADI and SSI courses from open water to dive master at competitive rates.

name: Mermaid Resort and Dive Center
description: A world-class resort offering accommodation, nature tours, and diving services. It has over 30 spacious guest rooms and suites. The resort offers international and local cuisine as well as a fully equipped beach-front shop with new and top-of-the-line compressor room.

name: Frontier Scuba
description: Owned and run by Rick Kirkham an instructor trainer. Frontier Scuba is a TDI / SDI 5-Star Instructor Training Facility, one of only a handful in Asia. Packages are arranged including direct private transfers from Manila Airport and excellent resort accommodations. Their partner resort has more than 40 rooms all with hot showers, cable TV, and air-conditioned, and are very reasonably priced. One night aircon accommodation in twin share with full meals and three guided boat dives is US$98 per person. The dive center has trained naturalists as guides. Recreational courses are offered from the Discover Scuba 'try dive', PADI Open Water up to Divemaster and SDI courses up to and including the Instructor Course and Exams. The Technical dive center offers nitrox, Advanced Nitrox, Advanced Wreck, Extended Range, Trimix and Advanced trimix courses as well as Technical Instructor courses.

name: Octopus Divers
description: Very friendly owner Mac and dive masters teach all PADI courses from beginner to professional level, diving all year around, dive safaris all over the Philippines, specially Apo Island and Coron, new equipment, relaxed, good value, can organise accommodation, located in at-cans resort just behind Papa Fred Steakhouse. Also help you with island hopping, trekking tours, go-kart or mud-kart, shooting range, paint ball shooting, power walking tours around Puerto Galera twice a week, wellness and spa.

name: Sea Rider Dive Center
description: 63 29215885994. The cheapest dive and courses rate in the island with excellent macro & pelagic spotter. Berde island trip and night diving are always part of their daily activities. They arrange accommodation and transportation from Manila Intl airport & Clark Field Pampanga Intl airport to Sabang vice versa. Free intro dive for Non Nitrox Divers. Free boat pick up for public commuters from Sabang pier or Muelle pier to Sea Rider.

name: South Seas Divers
description: Friendly and fluent instructors in Jappanese, Korean, Tagolo, Spanish, and French. PADI courses offered at reasonable rates.

name: Puerto Galera Hash House Harriers
description: The local branch of the Hash House Harriers, an international group with clubs on every continent. All you need is a little taste for adventure combined with an enjoyment of the outdoors, when every Saturday afternoon a mixed group of Filipinos and Foreigners follow trails around some of the finest hashing areas in the country, when you will have the opportunity to see some of its most picturesque locations. You do not have to be super fit; the emphasis is more on enjoying the hash, and go at your own speed. If you would like to join in, meet at Capt'n Greggs Dive Resort on Sabang Beach from 3PM each Saturday. Runs depart at 3:30PM sharp. Cost for first time runners is ₱450 for men, ₱350 for women and ₱300 for children which includes a t-shirt, post-hash drinks and transport. If you are already a member (i.e. you are wearing a hash t-shirt) subtract ₱150.

name: Snorkel at Coral garden
description: This can be arranged with any boat operator at Sabang beach. It costs ₱1500 to hire a bangka for the day - usually they take you to a few secluded small beaches on the islands close by, and to snorkel at these places. Coral garden has the best snorkelling in this area - most of the corals are still alive, and the variety of colourful fish is amazing. A warning - the waters sometimes get cool so wearing a thin wet suit is not a bad idea.

name: Maxbank
description: The only ATM in Sabang accepting local and international cards with a 3% commission. In Puerto Galera, the Rural Bank and Allied Bank have ATMs which accept cards on the Megalink and Expressnet networks and at the Allied Bank Visa cards (debit or credit). The nearest banks with international Cirrus/Maestro links are in Calapan or Batangas (including ATMs at Batangas Pier).

name: JE and G Express Payment Center ATM
description: A convenient ATM option in Puerto Galera, accepting both local and international cards. Located near the payment center, making it a useful stop for cash withdrawals and other transactions.
directions: near JE and G Express Payment Center in Puerto Galera
price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

name: The Viewpoint Coffee Bar & Gastro Bar
description: Cafe/bar with Tapas style food. Great view to the west (sunset!).

name: Not Just Coffee
description: A stylish café offering specialty coffee, fresh pastries, and a cozy atmosphere, with an ocean view.

name: Hemingway's Bistrot, Certified Angus Beef Restaurant
description: Located at the West end of Sabang beach. Hemingway's Bistrot featuring traditional German, Filipino and international cuisine prepared by Master Butcher Pfannen Fred and Chef Jake.
directions: at the west end of the beach

name: Vesuvio
description: One of the best wood-fire pizza and coffee in town.

name: SeaShore Resort
description: Tasty Filipino style breakfast right on the beach front, comes with the brewed coffee for ₱100 only. Fast internet and one of the best pork BBQ stick in the area.

name: Toko's Restaurant
description: Atlantis also have a resort in Dauin near Dumaguete, and that also has a Toko's.

name: Sunsplash Resort
description: Sunsplash Resort offers breakfast and lunchtime menus with local and international dishes. In the evening at 5PM Sunsplash offers an all-you-can-eat BBQ buffet for ₱250, with a selection of BBQ meats, salads, local and international dishes to choose from.

name: Capn Greggs
description: With an all wooden decor, and some interesting and punny posters on their walls, this second floor sea facing restaurant serves filling meals. Their vegetable curry with rice is especially delectable. It is also among the few restaurants in Sabang that has newspapers for patrons to read.

name: Cheap Charlies Bar
description: If you're looking for a bar that offers you a genuine local experience with a western touch then Cheap Charlies is the place to go. It is known for its cheap drinks, free karaoke and simple but delicious food. If karaoke is not your thing they turn off the karaoke later in the night and turn up the music. Opens at 4PM and closes around 5AM (or later.) It is located just down the hill from Max Bank, ask any local and they will be happy to show you the way.
directions: Located on the ground floor of the Tropicana Castle.

name: Marti's Bar & Accommodation
description: Has a few rooms to let right above the bar for about ₱600 a night. Rooms have private bathroom and kitchen. After diving, go have a beer with Marti.

name: Angelyns Beach Resort
description: Great value for money makes this one of the best buys in Sabang. 40 air-conditioned rooms complete with TV, hot shower and mini bar. Breakfast is included in the price and the resort has a beach front restaurant and swimming pool. Reservations can be made through Frontier Scuba in conjunction with dive packages and transfers. Rates are from ₱1250-1900 per room per night including breakfast. Unlike other resorts there is no additional service charge or VAT.

name: Big Apple Dive Resort
description: Offers a range of accommodation from budget fan rooms to luxury apartments. Located right on the beach in the middle of Sabang close to all the action, Big Apple has a large outdoor pool, 24 hour restaurant with pool tables and 24-hour sports bar with satellite TV showing all the latest sports action live. Recreational diving, dive packages and PADI dive instruction are available at very competitive rates.

name: Sabang Inn Dive Resort
description: Good value for the money, many packages to choose from. Located right at the beachfront in the quiet area yet just a minute walk away from the nightlife. it is a blend of perfect location with a beach front atmosphere - a friendly staff and, of course diving.
price: Budget room ₱700-1000, standard ₱1000-1300, deluxe to VIP ₱1200-2400

name: Sabang Oasis
description: Sabang Oasis is a modern resort in the center of Sabang. With a rooftop bar and swimming pool giving amazing views acroos the bay. All rooms have hardwired internet access and high pressure solar heated showers, 5* hotel standard mattresses and air-con as standard, refrigerators and safety boxes are also fitted. Nightly rates are ₱1500-1800 with discounts available for longer stays.

name: Reynaldo's
description: Budget rooms, some of them with a beach view.

name: Sergio's Lodge
description: Budget rooms behind Tina's.

name: Tropicana Castle Resort
description: A large and rather posh hotel with a roof-garden restaurant that serves local and international cuisines. The hotel is in the form of a castle and the Austrian owner Paul runs the place with his Filipina wife and family. Nice digs except for hot water problems. Bookings can be made via agoda.com.
directions: on the main street perpendicular to the beach

name: El Galleon Resort
description: Has a nice waterfront location on the point separating Sabang from Big La Laguna. If you are in Sabang to dive, you could easily spend a week and never venture further from El Galleon and its adjacent dive shop, Asia Divers. There are three types of rooms (budget, poolside and ocean view), all are quiet (no roosters or generators nearby), clean and close to the pool. Nightly rates for double occupancy range from $36 - $60 with discounts available with a dive package. Rates do not include service charge and taxes The resort also has a fine restaurant and is one of the few in Sabang that offers waterfront dining.

name: Portofino Resort
description: Has a waterfront location with a pool and a bar just inside the front wall. Restaurant and Bar are good. There are studio, single bedroom and two bedroom apartments which can be self catering. The elevated rooms at the front have a good view. Nightly rates for twin occupancy are posted on their website but could be negotiable when you contact them, so long as it's not Christmas, New Year, Chinese New Year or Easter!

name: Out of the Blue Private Villas
description: Offer the most luxurious villas in Puerto Galera with great views in a quiet environment on the hillside overlooking Small La Laguna Beach. Choose from 10 fully furnished luxurious 1, 2, 3 or 4 bedroom villa suites or 4 private spa villas.

name: Sunsplash and Blueribbon Dive resort
description: Offers beach huts. Nice water front location. Good food and a great dive school also available.

name: Blue Lagoon Dive Resort
description: Faces the waterfront. Offers free rental for diving fins and goggles.
price: ₱2300 and up (but sometimes promotion can be as cheap as ₱400 per night)

name: Campbell's Beach Resort
description: Situated at the far western end of the beach, Campbell's Beach Resort has rooms to suit every budget from ₱990 per night. All rooms are absolute sea frontage with double beds, air conditioning, cable TV and private bathroom with hot showers. Additionally Deluxe and Penthouse Rooms are equipped with refrigerators and safety boxes. The bar and restaurant is a great place to relax and enjoy the sunset and offers a full range of drinks and Thai, Filipino and Western dishes as well as the best Angus Steak on the beach! Private Transfers from Angeles and Manila can be arranged, as can adventure activities, tours and scuba diving.

name: Lalaguna Beach Club
description: In the center of the bay, La Laguna Beach Club is the most up-market hotel on the beach with an emphasis on diving. The resort has 31 rooms, 28 rooms offering air-conditioning and mini bar, cable TV, plus 3 cottages with electric fans. All rooms have private bathrooms and modern comforts including hot water. There are 6 family rooms available, consisting of 1 double bed and a set of bunk beds. (stretcher beds and mattresses available for children.) Popular activities which can be offered by the resort are beach picnics, mountain hiking, golfing and fishing. The Beach Club also offers dive trips to other destinations aboard the live-aboard dive vessel M.V. Rags II.

name: Big La Laguna Beach Resorts
description: Big La Laguna Beach Resorts operate two resorts in Big Lalaguna Bay – Campbell's Beach Resort and Scandi Divers Resort. These resorts offer a variety of beachfront accommodations, from cozy rooms to spacious three-bedroom suites. The area is known for its quiet atmosphere, pristine beach, and excellent snorkeling and diving spots. Scandi Divers Resort features a professional dive center offering PADI dive courses from beginner to instructor level. Guests can also enjoy the Scandi Skybar, which provides a terrace view of the ocean.

name: Swengland Dive Resort
description: On the beach at Big Lalaguna, it caters to holiday makers and recreational divers. There are 14 fully air conditioned rooms each with private en-suite bathroom, queen sized bed and cable TV from just ₱1100 per night and from just ₱900 per night with fan. Enjoy an ice cold beer in the bar as you watch the sunset over the Batangas Channel or have a game of pool on the full-sized billiard table. The restaurant offers Filipino and European cuisine and specialises in authentic Chinese food. Other facilities include cable television, internet access, 24 hour electricity, international telephone and fax service, money changing and travel booking and confirmation.

name: Scandinavian Divers
alt_name: Big La Laguna Beach Dive Resort
description: Small resort with full services right on Big La Laguna Beach which is preferred by everyone for swimming and snorkeling. 8 poolside rooms, and 1- to 3-bedroom waterfront suites. Full diving instruction, waterfront restaurant and a bar named SKYbar. Free wi-fi available to guests and divers.
directions: 15-minute walk from Sabang or 4 minute boat ride

name: Campbell's Beach Resort
description: Quiet all waterfront rooms at the end of the Big La Laguna Beach, a 15-minute walk or a short boat or tricycle ride from Sabang. Restaurant featuring international food with emphasis on Thai food. Guests use pool and dive center 50 meters next door at Scandi Divers. Free Wi Fi.
directions: End of beach walking from Sabang

name: Scandi Divers
description: Scandi Divers is a short walk to Sabang, but quiet and relaxing. It's a great place to come for scuba diving as they have their own fully-equipped dive shop and boat; US$25 per dive. The restaurant is fantastic too, with great-tasting dishes from all around the world.

name: Blue Crystal Beach Resort
description: Air-conditioned rooms and suites that face their private beach are equipped with bath and shower, cable TV, mini-bar and refrigerator, private terrace, and Wi-Fi. The resort has a scuba diving center, swimming pool and offers a wide range of day trips by boat and jeepney.
price: ₱995 per person per night for double occupancy and ₱895 per person per night for multiple occupancy

name: Mary's Beach Resort
description: Good place to relax during the day but the simple nipa huts are extremely rundown inside. Cracks in the floor and let mosquitoes in, a hole in the floor serving as the shower drain did the same. It's cheap and it's got character but is not for the fainthearted. It is perfect for those who just want to take a sleep and enjoy the rest of the day in the beautiful nature. If you prefer to take a bath right after a swim in the see, you can do it easily here.
directions: At the very right of the beach.

name: Daluyon Beach & Mountain Resort
description: A beautiful resort on the beach. Friendly and helpful staff, gorgeous rooms with hot shower, 24-hour electricity, AC, minibar, TV, DVD player (ask front desk for available DVDs), room service breakfast included, very nice pool with outdoor shower facilities. Restaurant is open for walk in guests: very good quality!

name: Sheridan Beach Resort & Spa
description: A beautiful beach resort, with a backdrop of hills and forest. Over 90 modern guestrooms and suites with a touch of Asian culture - fully fitted and fully furnished. 24-hour electricity. It features great restaurant with a buffet dinner for ₱620 (tax included), exceptional wellness spa, gym, very large pool with kiddie pool, outdoor jacuzzi and outdoor shower, poolbar, lobby lounge with gift shop.
directions: a few meters away from the Sabang Wharf fronting the Sabang Beach.

name: Dab Dab Resort
description: Turn left once you hit the beach. The owner has an arty flair and built some funky cabins including a treehouse style. with own bathrooms. Bring your own insect repellent, and torch is a must.

name: Roberts Beach Resort
description: Cottages with fan and own bathrooms

name: Taraw Beach Resort
description: Fan cottages with own bathrooms.

name: Penao Beach Cottages
description: Cottage with fan and own bathrooms.

name: Bambua Nature Cottages
description: Lovely place in the middle of the rainforest away from the hustle and bustle from the beach. Run by a Filipino family that has been here for 30 years. Offers budget rooms for backpackers as well as private cottages for families. There's a small bar and a restaurant that serves breakfast and dinner. Has its own pond and is surrounded by rice paddies. Power runs from a generator from 10AM to midnight.
address: Sabang main road before the beach
directions: Ask the van/jeepney driver to drop you off at Bambua before reaching Sabang beach

name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church
description: Sabtang's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1785.

name: Sabtang Lighthouse
description: An 18 m structure overlooking the northern part of the island and watching the ferries heading to and from Batan Island.

name: Chavayan
description: The main draw in Sabtang, it is a community (barangay) composed of houses built in the traditional Ivatan way and composed of stone and thatch roofs in the southern part of the island. It is where most postcard images of Batanes are taken.

name: Santa Rosa de Lima Chapel
description: Chavayan's Roman Catholic chapel, built with a Baroque facade and a thatched roof during the Spanish era.

name: Chamantad-Tinyan Viewpoint
description: An elevated sport along the National Road with views of the surrounding cliffs, coves and roaring ocean, set amid a background of rolling hills and grasslands. Beware of droppings from grazing goats and cattle.

name: Savidug
description: Like Chavayan, it is a barangay in the east-central section of Sabtang composed of traditional stone houses that also forms the typical postcard pictures of Batanes.

name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Chapel
description: Savidug's Roman Catholic chapel, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era.

name: Savidug Idjang
description: The idjang is an Ivatan word for the elevated and fortified settlements that existed in Batanes before Spanish colonization. The one in Sabtang, situated on a triangular-shaped hill, has been the one most extensively studied by archaeologists.

name: Morong Beach
description: A stretch of white sand on the northeastern shores of the island.

name: Mayahao Arch
description: A naturally-formed rock arch along Morong Beach that is the most photographed natural attraction in the island.

name: Nakabuang Cave
description: A low-ceilinged chamber along Morong Beach.

name: Ivuhos
description: A large grass-covered island west of Sabtang inhabited only by free-roaming cows and goats.

name: Mount Kiltepan
description: A popular hiking spot to see the sunrise.

name: Hanging Coffins
description: A set of coffins precariously perched on a cliffside.
directions: Walk from the St. Mary Church through the Calvary Hill (Mission Compound) Cemetery

name: Sumaguing Caves
description: A large and extensive cave system with jagged rocks, boulders, stalactities and stalagmites.

name: Bokong Falls
description: A 6 m cascade.

name: Bomod-ok Falls
description: A larger 200 ft cascade.

name: Lumiang Cave
description: A cave that is also used as a burial site featuring hanging coffins, usually combined with a tour of Sumaguing Cave.

name: Mount Ampacao
description: A 1889 m mountain with panoramic views of Sagada and the surrounding mountains.

name: Saint Mary's Episcopal Church
description: The main church in Bontoc, built during the American period and a reminder that of the Protestant dominance in this part of the Cordilleras.

name: Sagada Underground River
description: A 300 m cave with running water.

name: Lake Danum
description: A pristine lake visited by hikers for its sunset views.

name: Sagada Weaving
description: Store for local and handwoven products are one of the more popular souvenir shops in Sagada. It is one of Sagada's biggest employers and you can visit the weaving looms to view how intricate the weavers go about in producing the handwoven raw materials. Very affordable prices too.
directions: 10 minutes walk from the center of the town towards the direction of St. Theodore's Hospital

name: ATM
description: There are three ATMs: a PDB in the tourist center, at the Sagada Rural Bank (downstairs around the corner) and one at the 3rd floor of the Eduardo Gaudan Longid Center building at the main junction (probably no credit card).

name: Yoghurt House
description: A popular and excellent restaurant. They serve meals from breakfast to dinner. Specialties include varied yoghurt dishes and fresh local produce.
directions: Go down the main road from the municipal hall

name: Bilig Cafe
description: Excellent rice meals, pancakes, fantastic coffee, and more. Check out the cool postcards on the ceiling.
directions: in the basement of the municipal hall; if you are facing the hall, look for stairs at the side of the building

name: Salt & Pepper
description: The restaurant has good vegetarian options, Filipino specialties and picnic baskets to take out for a hike! The friendly staff also take orders for late dinner (beyond the curfew hour) and early (before 6AM) breakfast or packed meal. Wifi available. The restaurant also offers tour meal packages for a cheaper price. Contact the number above for inquiries.
directions: on the main road down the municipal hall

name: St. Joe's Cafe
description: Inconsistent food, but the sizzling plates are quite good, and the building feels like a ski lodge.

name: Bana's Coffee
description: Serves native coffee and excellent breakfasts on a ledge overlooking the valley.
directions: two-story building after Yogurt House, the cafe is below street level

name: Kimchi Restaurant and Bar
description: In the center of town, when most of the places close down, and the lights go out, this is the only place still open late into the night. Nice music. They close up when people stop drinking. The Korean food is also very good. The owner lived in Korea for 15 years.

name: Treasure Rock Resto Bar and Inn
description: Overlooking a Hanging Coffin or 2 at the end of the main Sagada road before you cross the bridge in the direction of the big cave. Jerry the owner will light you a bonfire while you watch the sun disappear from the front of the bar, and if you're lucky his wife will cook some tasty fried chicken too. has no official closing time. Difficult to find, look for the hand-painted sign and climb upwards then to the left for 2 min.

name: George's Guesthouse
description: Try getting the penthouse rooms. You will have a balcony where you can hang out at night, lay out mats to check out the stars, have a cool view of Sagada. The owners are extremely helpful. No wifi.

name: Masferre Country Inn and Restaurant
description: Masferre Country Inn and restaurant offers hotel-like amenities including a full service restaurant. It also houses the world-renowned photographs of the father Philippine photography, Eduardo Masferre. Wifi.

name: Canaway Resthouse
description: with hot water bathrooms.

name: Sagada Homestay
description: Quiet location on a side street up from the center. Nice rooms, views over the valley, a fire pit and wifi.

name: Green House
directions: on a hill over the south road

name: Misty Lodge
directions: 15 min walk east out of town.

name: Himogaan River
description: Residents call that place as the Himoga-an River Overflow that is located at Barangay Puey, Sagay City, Negros Occidental. The Himoga-an River is the longest river of Sagay City. It was wide and clean so you would not wonder why most people living near that area usually take a bath and wash their clothes there.

name: Inangtan Hanging Bridge
description: "Inangtan" in local dialect means "to connect". The Inangtan Bridge connects the Barangay Maquiling proper from its rural half that is separated by Himoga-an River.

name: Saguday Eco-Tourism Park
description: A 4.7 ha recreational space with farms, cottages and gardens.

name: Saguday Municipal Hall
description: One of the oldest buildings in town, dating back to the 1960s.
directions: at the back of the municipal park

name: Pagay Pagay Festival
description: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

name: LJ's Panciteria, Resto Bar and Grill
description: A noodle (pancit) restaurant.

name: Hearty Harvest Cafe
description: A quaint roadside coffee shop that has a relaxing vibe.

name: Saint Catherine of Siena Parish Church
description: Samal's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish period in the 17th century.
directions: at the back of the municipal hall

name: Pilis Falls
description: A 120 ft cascade along its eponymous creek located in the slopes of Mount Nagpali.

name: Bataan National Park
description: A 23000 ha protected forest area covering Mount Natib, a dormant volcano with a wide caldera encompassing most of northern and central Bataan.

name: Samal Museum and Library
description: A local history museum with library that also houses the municipal tourism office.

name: Miss Piggy K Store
description: A Korean grocery store.
address: Bataan National Road corner Daang Bago, East Daang Bago

name: Mr. Brewsko
address: JP Laurel Street corner Daang Mestizo, West Bagong Daan

name: San Juanico Bridge
description: One of the longest bridge in the Philippines.
address: between Tacloban, Leyte and Sta. Rita, Samar

name: Anawangin Cove
description: The most famous and visited cove in town featuring white sand beaches and an agujo grove. The place can get crowded with campers from Metro Manila on weekends.

name: Nagsasa Cove
description: A less crowded alternative to Anawangin with scant phone signal. There is also a shallow creek entering the cove near its southern edge.

name: Capones Island
description: A picturesque island with white sand beaches, stunning views of the mainland mountains and an equally picturesque lighthouse.

name: Casa San Miguel
description: A house inside a mango orchard built in 1921 and now hosting a museum on local history, culture and art.

name: Nagsasa Falls
description: A small cascade near Nagsasa Cove.

name: Mount Pundaquit
description: A highlight in the hiking trail from Pundaquit to Anawangin Cove overlooking Agnain and Diego's Coves.

name: Silanguin Cove
description: The farthest of San Antonio's coves. Unlike the other coves, its beaches are of the gray sand variety. At the mouth of the cove is an eponymous island.

name: Talisayen Cove
description: An less-visited cove between Anawangin and Nagsasa Coves.

name: Camara Island
description: A smaller island with rock formations and a small white sand beach.

name: Mount Capalngan
description: A mountain with commanding views extending to the neighboring town of San Marcelino. Also has an eponymous waterfall.

name: Bigfoot Restaurant & Rest House
description: Restaurant serving Filipino dishes. Their main draw is the halo-halo.

name: Peopes Park
description: A nice park to walk around has a board walk over looking the sea.

name: Gaisano Mall
description: Major chain with malls in many cities. Has a Gaisano supermarket

name: Metro Bank
description: Mastercard/Visa card ATM.

name: PNB Bank
description: Visa card ATM.

name: Jollibee
description: Breakfast 07:00-11:00

name: Yoyongs Travellers Inn
description: Fan double rooms with outside bathrooms or a/c double rooms with own bathroom. All rooms have free WiFi and cable TV.
directions: 5 mins walk from the port and city plaza.

name: Dragon Inn
description: Fan and ac double rooms with own hot water bathroom and cable TV.

name: F B Travelers Inn
description: Economy fan or a/c double with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Mom's Hotel and Restaurant
description: Air-con double room with own hot water bathroom. All rooms have cable TV and free Wi-Fi. It's best to call to book a room.

name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
description: Largest Catholic church in the Philippines during the late 18th century, founded in 1773, but had to be rebuilt in 1890.

name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church

name: Ambulong Island
description: Ambulong Island is a 30-km² island with fine beaches, cliffs and abundant coral formations. It is characterized by white sand beaches, cliffs along pillars jutting out of the water, and underwater caves. Coral gardens and tropical fish are abundant in several coves. An islet called Grace Island is located at a limestone cove at the southern tip of Ambulong. A fisherman's village is located at the sheltered side of the island. Ambulong Island is also a jump-off point to some of the dive spots in the area, such as the Iling Point, Baniaga Reef, Ambulong Bank, Dungan Reef, Sardines Reef, Apo Reef, and Manadi Island. These dive sites are about an hour away by pumpboat from the Caminawit Port.

name: Ilin Island
description: Ilin Island has a village of shell divers, being abundant in shells and coral reefs. There are ancient burial caves of early Chinese traders, ethnic fishing villages, and numerous dive sites from which to view many tropical fishes. Lush foliage encircle the clear blue waters of the South China Sea. There are scuba diving facilities, a 6.8 CTM compressor, seaport facilities, diveboats, and PADI and NAUI-certified instructors. Kweba Cansubong is a popular destination in the island apart from its white beaches, estuaries, rock formations, etc. Inasakan Beach, located at the far side of Ilin, is a small stretch of powdery white sand. It has been proposed to declare the island's timberland a conservation area for its natural fauna and flora. The Philippine teak, an endangered Philippine tree, is found only in Ilin and Batangas. Meanwhile, an endangered fauna called the cloud rat (or cloud runner/Ilin Island cloud runner) is found only in San Jose, Occidental Mindoro particularly in the island of Ilin. The cloud rat is the biggest and one of the most beautiful rats in the world.

name: White Island
description: White Island has a long powdery beach where buried turtle eggs are occasionally found. It has an almost mile-long beach with smooth and powdery white sand. The tranquil and peaceful island is an ideal place for swimming, scuba diving and fishing. Turtle eggs are occasionally found buried in the sand, and visitors are cautioned to keep them undisturbed.

It is a sanctuary for the 'tamaraw' (Bubalus mindorensis), an endemic species of buffalo found only in Mindoro. It provides a nice eco-tourism, trekking, or mountaineering alternative to beach/dive resorts. However, a part of the tamaraw genepool which is also a part of the national park is at the boundaries of Rizal and San Jose, more or less 50 hectares are in the territorial jurisdiction of the municipality.

name: San Luis Gonzaga Parish Church
description: San Luis's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a mix of Baroque and Renaissance styles. The turreted and unplastered brick façade itself is unlike the typical flat church exterior found elsewhere.

name: Luis Taruc Monument
description: Placed on a road junction next to the municipal park, it is memorial depicting a sculpture of a peasant family. It is dedicated to the town's most famous resident, Luis Taruc, a peasant leader who founded the Hukbalahap, the country's largest guerrilla organization fighting against the Japanese in World War II, and then the Philippine government when it reneged on its promises to grant land reform after independence in 1946. Taruc surrendered in 1954, but dissenters within the movement regrouped themselves into the New People's Army in 1968, continuing one of the world's longest leftwing insurgencies. Taruc himself was imprisoned but was eventually amnestied and rehabilitated before dying in 2005 aged 92. Taruc's ashes are interred at the base of the monument.

name: Hukbalahap Monument
description: A monument built in 2023 at the entrance of a private cemetery to honor the Hukbalahap (an abbreviation of Hukbong Bayan Laban sa Hapon; translated as People's Anti-Japanese Army) movement founded by Luis Taruc, who was born in what was then the rural village of Santa Monica in 1913. It features concrete statues depicting Taruc and two of his comrades in the Huk movement. Its construction, along with that of Taruc's solo monument in the downtown, marks the rehabilitation of the Huks as agrarian nationalist heroes after being vilified for decades as communist bogeymen in the political paranoia caused by the Cold War.
directions: inside Garden of Peace Memorial Park

description: San Miguel's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 19th century and used as a garrison by opposing sides during the Philippine Revolution against Spain. It houses a statue of Saint Michael the Archangel that was found in the forests outside town and is believed by residents to be miraculous. It is one of a few churches in the Philippines whose belfry is built above its façade. There is a souvenir shop in the convent.

name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
description: A sprawling 2117 ha national park that also covers parts of the neighboring towns of Doña Remedios Trinidad and San Ildefonso. Famous as the site of the Biak-na-Bato Republic during the Philippine Revolution, it also contains caves, rivers and forested highlands of the Sierra Madre that belie the misconception of Bulacan as a largely flat province.

name: Banal na Bundok
description: Meaning "Holy Mountain" in Filipino, it is a hillside monument/park filled with monuments to Jesus Christ and other key figures in the Bible. It is a popular pilgrimage site during the Lenten season, when visitors clamber to pray atop the various hilltop shrines.

name: Mount Manalmon
description: A 196 m peak that is popular among hikers in Biak-na-Bato National Park. It also contains Madlum Cave and forms one side of a gorge along the Madlum River that is also shared with Mount Gola, another popular hiking destination. The area is also claimed by the municipality of Doña Remedios Trinidad.

name: Tecson House
description: A residence built for the Tecson family, whose members included an officer in the Philippine Revolution.

name: Komikero Komiks Museum

name: Lake Sampaloc
description: The largest of San Pablo's seven lakes, of volcanic origin. Around the lake are Dagatan Boulevard, a lakefront park, floating cottages, and various civic monuments such as that of a giant tilapia fish.

name: Saint Paul the First Hermit Cathedral
description: An adobe Romanesque Roman Catholic cathedral that forms the center of San Pablo and serves as the seat of the namesake Roman Catholic Diocese of San Pablo which oversees the entirety of Laguna. Built in 1714, it was damaged during World War II, and its façade been restored to its original. Its dome is a landmark of the city.

name: Doña Leonila Park
description: A tree-filled park filled with fountains and neoclassical and Filipino-themed statues, it is a favorite recreation hub among residents. It sits on a promontory overlooking Dagatan Boulevard and provides views of Sampaloc Lake.
address: Trece Martires Street co. Dagatan Boulevard

name: Fule-Malvar Mansion
description: A prominent landmark, the mansion was built in 1915 in the beaux-arts and Art Nouveau style that was typical of the American period for the first city mayor of San Pablo, Potenciano Malvar, and his wife, Eusebia Fule, both of which came from prominent families. Visiting presidents and dignitaries were often hosted here. Since then the house has changed ownership multiple times and as of 2025 is being used as a civic center by the city government.
directions: beside San Pablo Central School and the ornate, white painted stone pedestrian footbridge, across the street from the red-brick Philamlife building and a gasoline station.

name: Doña Prudencia D. Fule Ancestral House
description:
A Spanish-era bahay na bato last inhabited by a scion of the Fule family known for her devotion to the education sector. In the 1930s, she donated the house and the adjoining plot to build a high school that now bears her name. The house was at times used as a school building before falling into neglect and becoming inhabited by squatters claiming to be Doña Prudencia's heirs. Following a legal battle to remove aforementioned squatters, the house was restored in 2019 and now contains a school museum. On the other side of the highway, at the elementary school also named after Prudencia, is one of the few Gabaldon school bungalows in the Philippines that dates back to the American period.

To avoid confusion with the Fule-Malvar Mansion, Prudencia is located outside downtown, on the highway running between the city and Alaminos, and is painted in strips of ocean-green and white with a red roof.
address: Prudencia D. Fule Memorial National High School, Maharlika Highway, Brgy. San Nicolas
directions: By Jeep: Take the one running from the city center to Brgy. San Nicolas and ask the driver to drop you off at Prudencia. By other vehicles: Beside an under-construction overpass connecting two schools on both sides of the highway. The house lies directly along the highway and is a landmark in the barangay.
hours: Museum for Industrial Arts and Economics: Open Mon-Fri during school hours. Otherwise ask caretakers for permission.

name: Old San Pablo City Hall
description: Built in a neo-classical style, this imposing structure is one of the few surviving civic buildings in the Philippines from the pre-World War II era. It contains a small museum on the history of San Pablo.

name: Pio Conducto Ancestral House
description: A private residence built for one of San Pablo's well-to-do residents in 1924, it became known as the setting of the 1988 classic Filipino horror film Tiyanak featuring a demon-baby from Filipino folklore and has since become a stereotype for a haunted house, lightened somewhat by the grotto of the Virgin Mary in the yard. Only the semi-cylindrical exterior and ornate window grills can be seen on the outside, but if one is lucky enough to be invited in, expect to see the interior of an American period house complete with custom-made furniture from that era. There are plans to restore the house, which has not been directly inhabited by its owners for some time, to its former glory.
directions: between Villa Lozada Subdivision and Saint Peter's College Seminary

name: Twin Lakes
description: Two of San Pablo's Seven Crater Lakes, situated in close proximity to each other and separated only by a narrow isthmus. These lakes are the most suitable among the seven for recreational activities, including swimming, and offer pristine unspoiled waters. There are camping accommodations nearby.

See if you can spot the small sphinx sculpture in the front lawn.

name: Dalton Pass
description: It is a rugged piece of terrain where a part of the Caraballo Sur reaches south and joins the Sierra Madre. Because of its strategic importance as the only access between Nueva Ecija and Cagayan Valley, the pass became the scene of much bloody fighting during the final stages of World War II. Japanese Shobu soldiers headed by General Tomoyuki Yamashita tried to hold their positions while Filipino and American soldiers under the leadership of Colonel Robert Lapham, were determined to dislodge them from February to March 1945. By the close of hostilities, the blood of almost seventeen thousand Japanese fighting units and the US-Filipino allied forces mingled with the soil. Markers that commemorate their sacrifice stand by the road’s highest point, with good view into the highlands. The shrine is a reminder for Gen. James L. Dalton who was killed by a sniper’s bullet during the end of World War II. At above sea level, Dalton Pass is the gateway to Cagayan Valley.

name: Salacsac Pass
description: The site of a World-War II battle fought in conjunction with the Battle of Dalton Pass. Unlike Dalton, the site sits on a higher altitude and is a newly-developed site that was opened following the concreting of the Pangasinan-Nueva Vizcaya Road in the early 2020s. There are stalls selling coffee and agricultural goods and a war memorial. On a clear day, the mines of Itogon in Benguet province can be seen to the west, as well as the Central Luzon plains as far south as Nueva Ecija and Tarlac. However, the area is claimed by both the provinces of Nueva Vizcaya and Pangasinan, which views the area as part of the municipality of San Nicolas.

The park is built with Filipino values in mind, and not just for amusement and thrill-seeking. Go ride the Wheel of Fate and see the wide views of the city and surrounding area, spin around in the Space Shuttle roller coaster, get wet at the Jungle Log Jam, drive a go-kart on their tracks, or take pictures with the park's mascots Eldar and Princess Victoria.
hours: Mon Tue closed, Wed Thu 11AM-7PM, Fri noon-7PM, Sat 11AM-9PM, Sun 10AM-9PM

name: Santa Rosa Arch
description: 19th-century welcome arch based on Paris's Arc de Triomphe, with the current arch being Art Deco, built in the 1930s. It is a local symbol, found in the city's official seal.

name: Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church
description: The main Roman Catholic church in the city, built in 1796.

name: Balibago Complex
description: The traditional commercial heart of the city, which also hosts the bus terminals.

name: Paseo Outlets
description: Lifestyle mall, part of the Greenfield City private township which spreads into neighboring Cabuyao. Shops and restaurants are spread out in 9 buildings, with their own parking lots.

name: SM City Santa Rosa
description: A huge two-storey mall with a vast collection of shops and restaurants, cinemas, a department store, and supermarket. Since 2017, it hosts tower blocks housing call centers. Also at the mall grounds is the SRIT (see #Get in).
directions: about 3 km from the bus terminal; most jeepneys traveling the National Highway stop here

name: Robinsons Santa Rosa
description: Three-storey mall, with fewer shops and restaurants. Has a supermarket and cinema, but no department store. Used to be frequented by locals before the opening of its rival, SM City Santa Rosa.
directions: past the junction leading to the old downtown; UBE Express buses from NAIA stop here

name: S&R Membership Shopping Nuvali
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.
address: Lot 1, Block 13, Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Nuvali, Santo Domingo

name: Landers Superstore Nuvali
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.
address: Nuvali Boulevard corner Evoliving Center Drive, Don Jose

name: WalterMart Santa Rosa
address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road corner San Lorenzo, Balibago

name: WalterMart Santa Rosa Bel-Air
address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz
directions: beside Wilcon Depot and in front of CW Home Depot

name: Puregold Santa Rosa
address: Pearl Road corner Amethyst Street, Balibago

name: El Cielito Inn
description: The El Cielito Inn, a member of the respected family of Philippine low-cost, high-quality inns, is conveniently located near the Convention Center and SM City.
address: Sta. Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz

name: Seda Nuvali
description: Part of chain of luxury hotels owned by Ayala. Rooms have cable TV, iPad docks, a small bar, and tea and coffee makers. Amenities include outdoor pool, laundry, free breakfast, kids playroom and restaurant. The rooms provide a view of Nuvali and surrounding area. There is a bus connection from Ninoy Aquino International Airport, and also free parking if you drive. Its location is not too far from the other tourist draws of Nuvali, which stretches into Cabuyao and Calamba.

name: Hotel Sogo Santa Rosa
description: Part of motel chain with distinctive red and yellow buildings. A/C rooms with cable TV, bathroom and WiFi. Parking is available, and you can also order meals inside.
address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz

name: Ambucao Beach
description: An extensive stretch of cream-colored sand running to Biak na Bato aka Mapisi Rock, a rock formation marking the boundary with the town of San Esteban.

name: Santiago Cove
description: The town's main draw, a horseshoe-shaped bay surrounded by Sabangan Beach, stretch of white-sand beach dubbed the “Boracay of the North”.

name: St. James the Greater Parish Church
description: Santiago's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style by the Spanish during the late 18th century on a hilltop. It also functioned as a fortress against pirates and foreign invaders at the time.

name: Mapisi Rock
description: A rocky promontory with a walkway and viewdeck at the top.

name: Sabangan Watchtower
description: A stout, Spanish-era watchtower overlooking Santiago Cove meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

name: Vitalis Villas
description: A luxury accommodation overlooking Santiago Cove and architecturally inspired by the houses of Santorini in Greece.

name: Santiago Cove Hotel and Restaurant
description: A resort overlooking Santiago Cove

name: Corals, Sand and Shells Beach House
Calvary Hills and The Chapel of Transfiguration
description: The place offers a pilgrimage venue for the Holy Week where life-size Stations of the Cross are presented from the foot of the hill going all the way up to the top where a Chapel was so designed to face the rising sun. The Chapel of Transfiguration offers pilgrims a commanding silence befitting a place of worship and can also be utilized for masses and retreat venues. A life-size image of Our Lady of La Salette also stands at the site, facing the City.

name: Balay Na Santiago
description: This used to be a barangay hall called Palacio del Barrio located at Calao West. Balay na Santiago houses the city museum and city library. This also serves as a multi-purpose function hall for art and music exhibitions and different occasion. The building itself is of the bahay na bato style popular during the Spanish colonial era.

name: Santiago Concrete Water Tank
description: This concrete water tank has been a landmark in Santiago City since the early 1970s. It is almost 30 meters high, and towers over the whole city, visible from almost anywhere. It was constructed through the help of then Congressman Delfin Albano of the lone district of Isabela, and under the leadership of then Mayor Dodo Miranda. It was turned into a colorful mural and is now considered a City Heritage Treasure.

name: Museo de Pattaradday
description: This museum at houses collection of artifacts, relics, dresses and antique furniture showing the culture and traditions that are typical in this region of Northeastern Luzon. Temporary closed as of September 2023.

name: Magat Dam
description: Opened in 1983, it was deemed the largest dam in Southeast Asia at the time and created a reservoir that displaced numerous communities in neighboring Ifugao. Since then it is one of the main sources of irrigation and electricity in the Cagayan Valley Region. The complex and its surroundings have become a favorite recreation spot for residents as well as day-trippers from Santiago. Fishing activities are also available at the reservoir.
address: Burgos-General Aguinaldo Road, Barangay General Aguinaldo, Ramon

name: Robinsons Place Santiago
description: Has a nice food court on the 2nd floor.

name: Xentro Mall Santiago City
address: Maharlika Highway corner Four Lanes Street

name: Gwapigs Porkchop-Estrella's Cafe
description: Filipino restaurant.

name: Katerina's Homemade Goodies
description: Has a wide variety of cakes and pastries that suits everyone's taste.

name: Gorio’s Yakiniku - Alfresco
description: Korean barbecue restaurant.
address: corner Alvarez Street and Sacristia Street

name: Chang Noi Food House
description: Thai restaurant, Very tasty, flavorful and authentic Thai food. The prices are very reasonable.

name: Makkhan Boodle Restaurant
description: Filipino restaurant.

name: Jubilee Hotel
description: A/C double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV for 12 hours.

name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
description: Santo Domingo's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a baroque style in 1740. Diego Silang, who later led the biggest anti-Spanish revolt in the Ilocos Region in 1762, served as a bell ringer at the parish.

name: Unknown Citizen Park
description: A small monument dedicated to the anonymous citizens of the municipality.
directions: in front of the Municipal Hall

name: Rizal Park
description: The main recreational and green space in town, featuring a monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal, that was erected in 1972, and Monumento ti Pagulidanan, an obelisk-like contraption built to celebrate unity and notable residents.
directions: at the back of the municipal coliseum and beside Santo Domingo Church

name: Sived Beach
description: A 6 km stretch of gray sand in the northwestern side of town ideal for surfing.

name: Puerto Beach
description: A stretch of sand along the southwestern side of town. It has the ruins of a jetty built by the Japanese during World War II.

name: Santo Domingo Public Market
address: Manila North Road corner A. Bonifacio Street, Vacunero
directions: in front of Shell gas station

name: General Miguel Malvar Shrine
description: Houses a statue and a museum on Miguel Malvar, Filipino general of the Tagalog Republic during the Philippine-American War.

name: Parish and International Shrine of Saint Padre Pio
description: A Roman Catholic shrine and parish devoted to St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina, with buildings built to local styles. Built as a small chapel along Maharlika Highway, it is now a large complex frequented by devotees around Batangas and surrounding provinces, as well as Metro Manila. It was recognized as an international shrine by the Vatican in 2026.
address: Gov. Antonio Carpio Avenue, San Pedro
directions: About 2 km away from Maharlika Highway

name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Parish
description: There is little known about the church's early history, but it dates back to around the 17th century, when Santo Tomas town center was established. The old church was destroyed by American artillery bombardment during World War II in 1945, and was replaced by a modernist church building and belfry. There is a memorial to the 15 Holy Spirit Sisters, mostly Germans, who died.

name: Mount Makiling
description: A towering inactive volcano and prime hiking destination shared with the town of Los Baños in Laguna.

name: S&R Membership Shopping Santo Tomas
description: A members-only warehouse grocery.
directions: in front of SM Santo Tomas

name: The Lifestyle Strip
description: Strip mall with various restaurants and coffee shop.

name: Rose & Grace
description: A restaurant serving bulalo (beef bone soup) since 1970.

name: Microtel Inn & Suites
description: A/C rooms equipped with cable TV and radio clock. The inn has a swimming pool, meeting room and Wifi connection.

name: Balay Anito Falls
description: Meaning "House of the Spirits", it is a cascade that drops down to a 20 m deep pool.

name: Puy-ocan Falls
description: A secluded cascade whose crashing waters produce a mist-like effect.

name: Simminublan Falls
description: A cascade whose name derives from the cooking pot-like shape of its basin.

name: Lengsad Falls
description: A cascade leading down to the Amburayan River.

name: Sasaba Rice Terraces
description: A terraced farming complex on the slopes of the Cordillera Mountains.

name: Meditation Cross
description: A large concrete cross overlooking downtown Santol that is commonly visited during Holy Week.

name: Santol Green Market
description: The town's main marketplace.

name: Supreme
description: Frequent service between Batangas City and Lucena via Rosario, San Juan, and Candelaria. Buses either AC or "ordinary" non-AC.

name: Gala-Rodriguez Ancestral House
description: It is an Art Deco mansion built by the renowned Filipino architect Juan Nakpil for the opulent Gala and Rodriguez families in 1935. It is one of the three houses in Sariaya declared a Heritage Home in 2008.

name: Natalio Enriquez Mansion
description: A 19th-century Beaux-Arts mansion built by a former governor of Quezon, Natalio Enriquez. It is declared a Heritage House by the Philippine government in 2008.
directions: At the corner with Rizal Street, near the church

name: Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church
description: A Barn-style Baroque church that forms the center of Sariaya's historic downtown. It was first built in 1599; the present stone church building was built in 1748, to replace one destroyed by earthquakes and flooding.
directions: Across the street from Rizal Park

name: Villa Sariaya
description: The ancestral home of Don Catalino Rodriguez, built in Bahay na Bato (stone house) style. It was built in 1922.

name: Mount Banahaw
description: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people. At the side of the mountain covered by Sariaya is the breached crater wall whose collapse in 1734 triggered the emptying of Banahaw's crater lake and a massive flood that destroyed Sariaya and forced its relocation to its present site.

name: Agawan Festival
description: Annual harvest festival held every May 15. Among the highlights is the Pinagong-eating contest, involving the rapid consumption of Quezon's own notoriously hard bread.

name: V&V Pizza
description: Pizza (house special, ham and cheese, Hawaiian, and pepperoni), sisig and shawarma. The location is small, and orders are done in a kiosk.

name: Buddy's Restaurant
description: A branch of a provincial restaurant chain based in Lucban serving Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
address: Maharlika Highway corner Pablo Street, Poblacion

name: Sariaya Bread House
description: A bakery operating since 1982 that sells local delicacies such as pinagong, a hard but sweet bread, and broas, a meringue-like contraption sold in large metal cans.
address: Maharlika Highway corner Rizal Street, Poblacion

name: Balai Sadyaya Resort
description: Has a restaurant open 9AM-10PM.

name: Villa del Prado Resort
directions: Follow the signs along Eco-Tourism Road

name: Santa Lucia Parish Church
description: Sasmuan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era and extensively modified over the succeeding years while retaining its façade and pineapple-looking cupola.
directions: beside the public market and before the pedestrian bridge leading to Barangay San Pedro

name: Sasmuan Coastal Wetland
alt_name: Sasmuan Bangkung Malapad Critical Habitat and Ecotourism Area
description: A protected area of the Pampanga River delta on the southern edge of Sasmuan facing Manila Bay. It is a critical habitat for various flora and fauna, particularly birds, spanning 3500 ha across four barangays of Sasmuan and was internationally recognized as a Ramsar Site in 2021.

name: Sasmuan Public Market
directions: beside Sasmuan Church and before the pedestrian bridge leading to Barangay San Pedro

name: Sasmuan Delicacies
description: A store selling popular delicacies and sweets from town such as polvoron and turrones de casoy, a nougat made from cashew nut. Although they do not have a physical store in Sasmuan itself, they have branches in major cities in Pampanga such as San Fernando and Angeles.

name: Sayak Airport
description: The island's main and only airport in the town of Del Carmen. Its only runway was able to accommodate 19-seater jets, but has since been expanded to allow flights using larger planes.

name: Fat Lips Surfshop
description: Offers new/used/rental surfboards, apparel, and surf accessories. They also arrange island hopping and other tours.
directions: midway between Cloud 9 and General Luna

name: Tagpuan Cafe
description: Here you can have some shrimps or crabs.
directions: in Dapa, just east of ferry landing on waterfront

name: Wayfarers Cloud 9 Restaurant & Residences
description: Fan double rooms with own bathrooms.

name: Siargao Surf Resort
description: Set in the heart of the Siargao Island Surf community.
directions: Located between the busy Cloud 9 and the town of General Luna

name: Malipaya Siargao
description: Malipaya Villas offers beachfront glamping tent accommodations along Tourism Road. Each spacious 30-square-meter tent includes two queen-sized beds, air conditioning, and a private bathroom. The tent area features an outdoor lanai that can serve as a lounge or dining space. Guests have access to a private swimming pool and direct beach access.

name: Lake Balanan
description: This is a scenic mountain lake in a protected wildlife area, in Siaton Municipality a few km inland from the town.

name: Tillys Sail Tour
description: A sailing family residing in Tambobo Bay, offers sailing tours as well as boat repair for world cruisers.

name: Tonga Sail Inn Retreat
description: Extremely basic accommodation. Good Western restaurant.

name: Cove Sands Beach Resort
description: A beach resort located on its own secluded bay. Personalized service. Fan cottages and air-con rooms. Private bathrooms, hot water showers, Free Wi-Fi and morning coffee and bottled water in all rooms.

name: Antulang Beach Resort
description: High-end place with swimming pool and library, a/c in all rooms, breakfast included.
directions: South of Tambobo Bay, across the peninsula

name: Aw-asen Falls
description: The main tourist draw in Sigay, it is the tallest waterfall in Ilocos Region, with a height of 110 m gushing through a vertical rock face. Access to the site is restricted to pre-organized tour groups for safety reasons.

name: Mount Tuwato
description: A 1802 m peak along the Bessang Ridge shared with the municipality of Cervantes.

name: Mount Monserrat
description: A 1763 m high peak along the Bessang Ridge.

name: Mount Longon
description: Another mountain in the Bessang Ridge, often climbed as part of the Tuwato-Monserrat circuit.

name: Namempengan Falls
description: An overlooked but similarly picturesque terraced waterfall system gushing along a shredded-looking and gently sloped rock face on the other side of town.

name: Sigay Viewdeck
description: A panoramic viewdeck on the boundary with Suyo with vistas over Sigay's valleys.

name: Erjohn and Almark
description: Bus station near Monteluce, on barangay Lalaan 1.

name: Lucsuhin Natural Bridge
description: It is a natural bridge formation between Barangay Lucsuhin and Kalubkob in Silang, Cavite. The formation crosses the Ylang-Ylang River and is the first, large natural bridge reported in the country. The bridge and cave is not a protected area.
directions: From the town proper: follow Silang-Banaybanay Road for about 1.8 km west from the Aguinaldo Highway and J. Rizal Ave. junction to the barrio of Lucsuhin, past the road to the Riviera Golf & Country Club, past the bridge over Ylang-Ylang River to barangay Calubcob. From Calubcob proper, take F. Belen Drive for about 400 m before turning right. From either point, hike.

name: Silang Church
alt_name: Our Lady of Candelaria Parish Church
description: A typical Baroque church dedicated to the Virgin of Candelaria. The original parish church and its attached school was completed 1595 by the Franciscans, but were destroyed by fire in 1603. A new church was built in 1637-39, and dedicated in 1640, and its belfry was damaged by earthquakes in 1880 and repaired in 1989. It became a Spanish Civil Guard (Guardia Civil) outpost against a local uprising by Filipino general Vito Belarmino during the Philippine Revolution in 1896.

name: Perlas ng Silang
description: Meaning "Pearl of Silang", it is a 3.5 ha flower farm featuring an assorted number of flowering plants, manicured gardens and lawns, and sculpted horticultural images.

name: Riviera Golf Course and Country Club
description: 36 holes, has a Korean restaurant. The course's terrain is flat, but challenging due to winds, but the weather is generally clear and temperatures are cooler.

name: Acienda Designer Outlet
description: Opened 2018, this open-air outlet mall houses a collection of 100 designer clothing shops in four European-themed sections. Its main catch is that most items are 70% off the tag price, all year round. There is also a small foodcourt and a branch of Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, a domestic coffeeshop chain.
directions: near Balinsasayaw. Many southbound buses headed for Tagaytay stop here

name: Ilog Maria Honeybee Farm
description: Large assortment of products sourced from the farm's honeybees such as soap, propolis and royal jelly, shampoo, and Honey Cider vinegar. Their throat spray is quite effective for smokers.
directions: From Manila: Take Aguinaldo Highway toward Tagaytay. If you pass Santis, you've gone too far. From Tagaytay Rotonda: Take Aguinaldo Highway to Manila, if you pass the Adventist compound, you've gone too far

name: Santis Delicatessen
description: A branch of a Metro Manila-based delicatessen store. They also sell ready-to-ear deli sandwiches and sweets.

name: Silang Public Market
address: M. Belen Street, San Miguel II

name: WalterMart Silang
address: Aguinaldo Highway corner Biluso Road, San Vicente II

name: Balinsasayaw
description: They serve good Filipino food inside bahay kubo cottages, with fly and mosquito netting, fans, and power outlets. The restaurant has a second branch at the junction with Aguinaldo Highway and J. Rizal Street in Barangay Lucsuhin leading to Silang town proper, beside Premier Plaza.

name: Aling Tonya's Seafood Palutuan
description: A seafood restaurant that has operated since 1974 and serves fresh seafood despite its inland location by keeping live specimen to be cooked upon order.
directions: Beside Acienda Outlets, with direct access to its carpark at the back

name: Mrs. Saldo's
description: Thai-inspired dishes.

name: Marius B&B and Hostel
description: Rooms are air-conditioned, and the in-house restaurant has good food.

name: Monteluce
description: There are four buildings, with all-air-conditioned rooms and an outdoor swimming pool. Parking is free.
directions: Near the Erjohn and Almark bus station

name: Bacolod-Silay Airport
description: Served by the two airlines and connects Silay and the whole of Negros Occidental with Manila, Cebu and Davao. Cebu Pacific: Manila, Cebu, Davao. Philippine Airlines: Manila, Cebu.

name: Bernardino-Ysabel Jalandoni Ancestral House
description: Besides from European architecture, what special about the house is that it has been turned into a museum and displays an expensive doll collection, and century-old objects like telephones, chandeliers, etc.

name: Manuel Severino Hofilena Ancestral House
description: The ancestral house is home to the world's smallest doll. It also displays ancient artifacts from the 15th century and a collection of Ramon Hofilena.

name: Balay Negrense
description: Home of the French descent family; the Gaston family, who helped in experimenting Sugar cane production in the province. After the death of their father; Victor Gaston, the family abandoned the house and fell into ruins but during the 1970s concerned people showed their support and repaired the house. The architecture is a typical example of "Bahay na bato" or House of stone, with American-European colonial influences. Today it is a museum containing antiques.

name: San Diego Pro-Cathedral
description: The only pro-Cathedral church outside Metro Manila, its birth was in the 1700s, the church was still made of nipa-palm, bamboo and grass, in the 1800s the church was then made into a wood and stone structure, finally in the 1900s the structure was made into what it is now, the architecture; Lucio Bernasconi (an Italian architect) took churches in his native Italy as an influence and model of the church. It was finished on 1927 also inaugurated in the same year.

name: Cinco de Noviembre St.
directions: located at the back of the Silay Public Plaza, near a supermarket named Lopues.

name: Silay Public Plaza
description: The center of the city. If you are a family, this place is the best place to walk and enjoy with ease.

name: St. Theresita's Academy
description: A private school.
directions: can be found nearby the Rizal Street.

name: Mt. Patag
description: A hiking/mountain climbing adventure you can experience with some resorts you can stay.

name: The Mansion
description: A well-preserved heritage house wherein antique materials can be found.

name: Savemore Silay
description: 8am-8pm

name: El Ideal Bakeshop
description: Inside an old Silay building, serves Filipino/international cuisine (try the lumpiang ubod) as well as offering baked goods like piaya, meringue and barquillos. You can also find the famous Guapple Pie, made of guavas, the local version of apple pie.

name: Mang Inasal
description: Also serves its grilled chicken here, and customers who dine on the second floor get an excellent view of some of Silay's heritage architecture.

name: Silayushi Japanese Restaurant
description: The only Japanese restaurant in Silay City, serving sushi and other Japanese cuisine.

name: Masjid Sokah-Bulan
description: Mosque.

name: Masjid Shiekh Karimul Makhdum
description: The Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque building dates from the 1960s. Four old mosque pillars found within the mosque are from the 17th century. According to local lore, the original mosque, built in the indigenous sacred Moro pagoda architectural style, was established in 1380, making it the oldest mosque in the Philippines and in Southeast Asia.

name: Papa Bull’s Park
description: Papa Bulls in the swampy mangrove area within the municipal complex of the Municipality of Simunul. This crocodile is now a major tourist attraction where several people come to view it.

name: Bagid Beach Resort
description: During the American period, a group of soldiers arrived here only to be bewildered by its natural beauty. Inspired by the tropical landscape, they composed a song titled “Tawi-Tawi Beach”. It’s a popular site for picnic goers with its crystal-clear waters.

name: Zara's Food Hub and Catering Services
Minor Basilica of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino
description: Sinait's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period in the 17th century in the Baroque style and housing the venerated image of the Santo Cristo Milagroso.

name: Santo Cristo Milagroso Chapel
description: A chapel built by the cove where the Santo Cristo Milagroso was said to have washed up in 1620 from Japan, where it had been hidden away by Christians being persecuted by the Tokugawa Shogunate. At the same time, a twin image of the Virgin Mary, known as the Virgen Milagrosa, washed up in the neighboring village of Paguetpet, part of Badoc, and is also venerated in that town’s basilica. The cove was subsequently named in the Virgin's honor.

name: Cabangtalan Beach
description: An underdeveloped white-sand cove.

name: Cabulalaan Hills
description: A series of rolling foothills of the Cordillera Mountains that have become a popular hiking destination.

name: Manna Pension House
description: Fan and A/C double rooms, a good places for backpackers to stay.

name: Langub Pension
description: Fan single/double room with own bathroom.

name: Driftwood Village
description: Dorm and double rooms.
directions: Sugar Beach is about 5 km from Sipalay town

name: John Aldrin Beach
description: this serene white sand beach is about an hour's drive from the town proper and features bamboo rafts (balsas), picnic areas, and swimming.

name: Bella Ciao by Chef Eldon
description: Selling pizzas.

name: Tourist information center
description: Readily provide tourist information, sell souvenirs. The tourist police office can also be found in the same building.

name: St. Francis of Assisi Catholic Church
description: With Siquijor Belltower right next to it.

name: Siquijor Beach
description: Several white sand beach resorts dot the coastal areas.

name: Capilay Spring Park
description: A natural spring fed swimming pool in the centre of San Juan. A favourite with the locals at weekends.

name: San Juan Beach
description: Lots of beach resorts and great for snorkelling and scuba diving.

name: Lugnason Falls
description: Nice waterfall close to San Juan.

name: San Isidro Labrador Convent
description: Reputed to be the biggest and one of the oldest convents in the Philippines, the Spaniards started construction in 1887 and was completed in 1894. Declared as a historical landmark by the Philippine Historical Commission.

name: Cambugahay Falls
description: Impressive 3-tiered waterfalls just outside Lazi. Great for swimming.

name: Century Old Balete Tree
description: Supposedly enchanted old tree covered in hundreds of roots and vines.

name: Kagusuan Beach
description: Noted for its picturesque seascape and rock formation, it is situated below a cliff and accessible by concrete staircase.

name: Our Lady of the Divine Providence church
Salagdoong Beach
description: Favourite with the locals and great for swimming and snorkelling. There are also water slides and places to dive into the sea. On the way to the beach you'll be passing Salagdoong Forest Reserve, which a manmade forest with Molave trees.

name: Mt. Bandilaan National Park
description: It hosts the highest peak in the island. It takes about 5-10 minutes to get to the top of the mountain from the road. The path is not well maintained. On the way there are a couple of Stations of the Cross.

name: Butterfly Sanctuary
description: Sign-posted from the main road.

name: Cantabon Cave
description: Takes 1.5 hr to walk through and you need to register in the town before venturing inside. Local guide required (they hang around the cave) as the cave is locked up.

name: Aberration Dive Club
description: Offers filled scuba tanks (₱650 each) for certified divers and easy diving without dive center connections.

name: Villa Marmarine
description: 3 km north of Siquijor going towards Larena. Good food, maybe the best on the island.

name: Kawayan Holiday Resort
description: 2 restaurants; main restaurant touts international cuisine next to the "Infinity" swimming pool and lounge area around the pool.

name: Jollibee Restaurant
description: Air-conditioned restaurant. Breakfast till 10:30AM.

name: C Zars Place
address: Just outside San Juan. The other side of the road from the beach
price: Double rooms with bathroom for ₱500 per night

name: JJ Backpackers Village
description: Restaurant with good food. Cottage rooms with queen-sized beds and outside bathrooms. All rooms have fans.
price: Dorm bed ₱350, camping ₱250, double room from ₱500

name: Das Traum Guest House
description: Double fan rooms, some with and some without en suite bathrooms. Cable TV. Nice Garden. Good budget place to stay.
directions: Just behide the Siquijor town Hospital, 10-minute walk to town

name: Buhisan lodge
description: Ordinary room with fan.

name: North Haven lodge
description: Fan double room with outside bathrooms.

name: Casa Miranda
directions: on road to San Juan just south of JJs

name: Diocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
description: Sison's main Roman Catholic church.

name: Sohoton Cove
description: Sohoton Lagoon and Caves is a more than 600 hectare Eco-reserve situated in the isolated south of Bocas Grande island. Accessible only on lower tides, this pristine sanctuary offers a grand experience. The trip is conducted by boat and is required most of the day.
directions: 1½-2 hour boat ride from Gen Luna

name: Club Tara Resort
description: Club Tara in Bucas Grande Island offers rooms equipped with air conditioning, minibar, hairdryer, shower, balcony/lanai/terrace, jacuzzi, coffee/tea maker, refrigerator and complimentary bottled water. Some of its facilities and services are bar, restaurant, meeting facilities, poolside bar, garden, jacuzzi, swimming pool, airport transfer and room service.
directions: on the west side of the island

name: Agas-Agas Bridge and Adventure Park
description: The main attraction of the town is the country’s tallest viaduct. The Agas-Agas Bridge zipline or what they call "Zipline Leyte" is a twin zip line and one of the longest in the country gliding diagonally above the bridge and the riverine below it.

name: Cainting Cave and Falls
description: This site, which forms part of the lush Sogod Rainforest served as meeting point of 3 rivers which offers a scenic junction of a natural pool.
