The presence of leeches locally known as “limatok” thrive on its waters. The area can be reached after a 5-km walk from the road in barangay Pancho Villa to the barrio of San Francisco Mabuhay. Pancho Villa is a 20-minute habal-habal ride from Doctor Gonzalo Yong Bus Terminal in the poblacion. It is also accessible via a feeder road in barangay Kahupian which connects it from the sitios of Lubong Sapa, Silao Bato, Kabernal and Hagna. The latter, which is the farthest of the sitios and under the territorial jurisdiction of barangay San Francisco Mabuhay, is the location of the cave and falls.
directions: in the northern mountainous area of the town

name: Magsuhot Park
description: The 500-hectare forested Magsuhot National Park is 3 km from barangay Mahayahay. It has four 20-meter high waterfalls falling into a common basin.
directions: in the barangay of Maria Plana

name: Metro Bank
description: Has a Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: Gaisano Capital Mall
description: Has a Gaisano supermarket.

name: G V Hotel
description: Fan/a.c. single/double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Solano Transport Terminal
description: A small and simple bus and jeepney station, with a single shelter for jeepneys. Boarding for buses is at the parking area; jeepneys depart from the single shelter. Tricycles are available, waiting along the street
directions: Around the Poblacion North barangay hall

name: Heroes' Park
description: A small park housing a preserved World War II cannon.

name: St. Louis Beltran Parish Church
description: Solano's central Roman Catholic parish church is not very special architecturally, but it houses a replica of the Black Nazarene.

name: Bangaan Rolling Hills
description: A hidden paradise, beautiful hill formations, view of the town and full of grass. Due to an increase number of visitors the pathway was widened, making the hills less elegant.

name: TGIF Resto
description: Good Food presentation and great combinations.

name: Deodato's Pizza Solano
address: A. Luna corner Bonifacio Streets, Roxas

name: キクハナ kikuhana
description: Japanese restaurant.
address: W. Ongtao Building, Maharlika Highway, Roxas

name: AM-PM Lodge
description: Clean fan double rooms with own bathroom and cable TV. Free WIfi.

name: Balai Gloria Hotel
description: Hotel/Function Room/Wellness Center with restaurant, Cafe Angelo.

name: Governor's Garden Hotel
address: J. Manzano St., Barangay Poblacion North

name: Sorsogon City Grand Terminal Bus Stop
Sorsogon Provincial Museum and Heritage Center
description: There are guides on each station who will explain to you what's in the gallery (they're not experts as most of them are interns from senior HS or college doing immersion.

name: Sorsogon Rompeolas
description: Sign.

name: SM City Sorsogon
address: Maharlika Highway, Barangay Balogo, East District, 4700

name: LCC Supermarket
description: There is also an LCC Expressmart.

name: Nono's Bakery - Yema Buko Pie
description: A must-visit bakeshop in Sorsogon if you’re a fond of cakes and pastries. Try their Yema Buko Pie, it’s one of the best. It’s really appetizing and I’m sure you’ll love it too.

name: The Chancery Coffee Shop, Bookstore & Religious Store
description: Right beside the Fatima Church is this well decorated and good coffee shop in town. The price is affordable, and you have a good venue to chat and talk small or big talk topics.They are also selling supported locally produced products on display.

name: Capisaan Caves
description: The fifth longest cave in the country at . It has layers of cave network including Lion and Alayan Caves with rare calcite formations and a subterranean river which doubles as a passageway to the best part of the cave. Brgy. Capisaan is about four hours by jeep from Solano on feeder and clay type soil road carved out of mountain sides. Tours can be arranged with the Sang-at-Salug Mountaineering Group or the Provincial Government of Nueva Vizcaya.

name: Kayapa Quad Peak
description: A nice loop hike that goes over the ridgeline of the four peaks in the area - Mt. Tugew, Mt. Kuban, Mt. Cabo, and Mt. Sadjatan. The hike is around 13 km long and takes approximately 5-6 hours, excluding breaks. The starting point is at the Alang-Salacsac Barangay Hall. A guide, available at the barangay hall, is required, in addition to the entry and environmental fees. The barangay also provides some food after the hike, for a price.

name: Mount Ugu
description: At the boundary with Benguet, the 2150 m high peak offers trails that pass through native communities of the Kalanguya tribes and is becoming a favorite mountaineering destination among outdoor enthusiasts.

name: St. Peter the Martyr Parish Church
JamPoy's Snackbar
address: 1 Padilla Street (in front of Sual Public Market)

name: Cinco Picos
description: A massif with five peaks in the Subic Peninsula that is regarded as a sacred spot by the Aeta people, with a height of 881 m.

name: Pinaglabanan River
description: A stretch of pristine freshwater in the Subic Peninsula reachable by hiking from Sitio Cawag.

name: Pacaoan Sea of Clouds
description: A highland roadside viewdeck along the Pacaoan Ridge named for the waves of clouds that form around it on foggy days.

name: Sugpon Bridge
description: A bridge connecting Sugpon with Sudipen with panoramic views over the Amburayan River valley.

name: Balled Falls
description: A twin cascade.

name: Les-eng Rice Terraces
description: A rice farming complex built on a mountain slope.

name: Bachelor Express
description: Buses connect to Butuan (3 hours), Tandag (4 hours), and Davao (10 hours, 10 times daily between 8AM and 6PM).

name: Philtranco
description: Buses run the Manila-Davao City route via AH26. The bus from Manila leaves from Pasay at 3PM and arrives at 4:30PM, one day after, while the return service leaves Davao City at noon and arrives at about 8:45PM.

name: Mapawa Cave
description: Unique rock formations approximately 20 feet high stand out against a backdrop of dense coconut trees and nipa palms (Nypa fruticans) and covers an area of 1 hectare. Also a known burial ground. Not too distant is another rock formation called tamulayag that resembles a giant vase with trees perched on top.

name: Sukailang Waterfalls
description: Cascades at 50 feet high near the village of Sukailang.

name: Manjagao Mangrove Forest
description: A vast mangrove forest around Manjagao Island is a sanctuary to various species of fish, marine life, birds and bats.

name: Buenavista Cave
description: A three kilometer cave with three entrances located in Hikdop Island. From the main entrance in Pagkawasan, Buenavista, visitors wiggle through a collapsed boulder into a grand chamber complete with what locals call the Kings Throne. A knee-deep pool culminates the subterranean trek approximately 100 meters from the main entrance. It has an array of impressive stalactites and stalagmites and is home to some unique species of cave bats and snakes.

name: Surigaonon Heritage Center
description: A small collection of ancient burial coffin jars and antique Chinese kitchenware are showcased in this museum. Some of the artifacts were unearthed at an archeological dig in Panhatungan, Placer. It also contains a significant collection of various rocks and minerals found in the province.

name: Bitaugan Whirlpools
description: These maelstroms of various dimensions are almost all occurring during ebbtide. They have a characteristic behavior to pull, twirl, and suck into their vortices anything that comes near them. They are called magic whirlpools due to their peculiar behavior to appear and disappear at certain nature-designated time intervals. The appearance of Pahibongan, as they are called locally, are usually followed by almost inaudible explosions and just as quickly vanish after the explosions.

name: San Pedro Cantiasay Footbridge
description: This wooden footbridge is among the country's longest at 391 meters, connecting Sibale and Nonoc Islands.

name: Luneta Park
description: Host to annual events, gatherings, and concerts for over a hundred years, it is a Spanish-style park with few acacia trees fronting the Surigao Cathedral. The new Children's Park Playground is under rehabilitation in May 2018 and publicly opened in June.

name: Jannex Pension and Restaurant
description: A/C single and double rooms with common bathroom. Cable TV.

name: Dexter Pensionne
description: Fan single rooms with outside bathrooms.

name: Conching Apartelle
description: Clean double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Tavern Hotel
description: Over-priced clean air-con double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Mount Tapao
description: A mountain that served as a Japanese garrison during the Battle of Bessang Pass for the commanding views at its peak and is now a forested bird sanctuary.

name: Bantay Kalbaryo
description: A highland pilgrimage site for followers of Paltiing, an obscure religion based in the Ilocos Region. It also has a demonstration farm operated by the municipal government.

name: Sangbay ni Ragsak
description: Meaning "Falls of Happiness" in Ilocano, it is a 6-7 ft cascade.

name: Suyo Eco-Mountain Resort
description: A mountainside resort complex along the Suyo River run by the government.

name: Pansipit Bridge
description: Connects Taal and Lemery.

name: Flying V
description: The intersection where the bypass swings off the main highway which leads from Taal toward Lipa and Batangas City. It is called "Flying V" even in Tagalog; that was the brand name of the gas station on the corner. It is now gone, replaced by a Jollibee. People arriving by bus and bound for Taal usually get off at this intersection and take a tricycle into Taal; there are usually several trikes waiting. People bound for Lemery stay on the bus since the terminals are in Lemery.

name: The Heritage Town of Taal Welcome Arch
description: Oldest sign going to proper town of Taal.

name: The Heritage Town of Taal
address: Taal Municipal Building, Calle MM Agoncillo, Corner of Calle J.W. Diokno

name: Taal Municipal Plaza
description: An open area with the municipal hall on one side and other town services such as the police station and post office on another side. It becomes quite busy during festivals with music, other entertainment and food stalls.
directions: across the street from the basilica

name: Old Taal Church Ruins
description: A Statue of St. Martin de Tours now stands on the site of the “Old Taal Town” along the lakeshore.

name: Maliputo Landmark
description: It is at the edge of San Nicolas town. It offers a great viewing point for Taal Volcano and the eponymous lake.

name: Taal Basilica
alt_name: Basilica Minor of St. Martin of Tours
description: A fine old church built in Spanish times to replace the one in San Nicolas that was destroyed by a volcanic eruption. The front has a neoclassical facade with lots of columns; the back of the building has high windowless stone walls and looks more like a medieval European fortress than a church. A sign in front of it says it is the largest Catholic church in Asia.

name: Shrine of Our Lady of Caysasay
description: A pilgrimage site just north of the heritage town containing a venerated image of the Virgin Mary. It is on a low ground; one can descend to it from the historical center city over the with a flight of 125 steps (San Lorenzo Ruiz Steps). The church reopened in 2024 following a major restoration program to undo damage caused by earthquakes and the 2020 Taal Volcano eruption, with the drab modern facade replaced in favor of its original colonial-era frontage made of coral stone. To access the Virgin Mary, take the stairs at the back of the church leading to a small chapel, where devotees hold their prayers and touch the glass screen protecting the image.

name: NHCP Museo nina Marcela Mariño at Felipe Agoncillo
description: The birthplace of Marcela N. Agoncillo who was known as the maker of the first official Filipino Flag during the Philippine revolution against the Spanish authorities. The different flags of the revolution are also prominently displayed at the site. It is also one of the few places in the country where the Philippine flag must be hoisted 24/7 by law.

name: Casa Villavicencio
description: Heritage home owned by Gliceria Marella Villavicencio's family, and a site of a meeting of the La Liga Filipina with Jose Rizal and Andres Bonifacio. Open by prior reservation.

name: Villavicencio-Marella House
description: Heritage home beside Casa Villavicencio. It was built as a wedding gift to a son of Gliceria. Unlike the main house, this is open to walk-in visitors.

name: NHCP Museo nina Leon at Galicano Apacible
description: Leon and Galicano Apacible Museum has 6 galleries depicting the lives of brothers Leon and Galicano. First was lawyer, judge and military commander against the Spanish. The other was political activist and diplomat. The visitors may hear theirs stories in a specially prepared film to be watched right upon the entry. Museum is located in nice 19th-century ancestral house. Upper floor showcases elegant Art Deco furniture and other items from the family’s collection.

name: Goco Ancestral House
description: It was built in 1876 in bahay-na-bato style. It is the ancestral house of former Ambassador Raul Goco, son of Juan Cabrera Goco, who was a Treasurer of the Filipino Revolutionary Movement. This house is only open by special arrangement with a minimum of four people needed for a visit, with a Filipino-themed lunch, afternoon snacks and a heritage tour included in the admission.

name: Ylagan - Dela Rosa Ancestral House
description: This house, in Bahay na bato style, was restored by Dr. Martin Ylagan-de la Rosa and his wife in 1995-1997. Since it is a private house, visits must be by special arrangement only. Temporarily closed as of October 2023.

name: The White House (Taal)
description: The stately American colonial “White House” contains a collection of beautiful hardwood antique furniture and personal artifacts. The house is in very good shape. It is preserved by Don Gregorio Agoncillo Foundation in honor of Gregorio’s daughter, Corazon Agoncillo. It seems closed but when you stand in front of the gate long enough, a caretaker appears, let you in and guides you through the house.

name: Galleria Taal
description: Heritage home, turned to a museum with exhibits of old photographs of the Philippines, and vintage cameras

name: Taal Public Market
description: There are many food stalls serving both local delicacies (see #Eat) and other Filipino food. The north and east sides of the market have many stores catering to the tourist trade with embroidered goods, wood carvings and assorted souvenir items.

name: Krisdale Supermarket
description: Not a large or remarkable store; Taal residents generally go to SM or Robinson's malls in Lemery for serious shopping. Krisdale is useful for routine items and as a landmark for some tricycle or jeepney journeys.

name: Paradores del Castillo
description: Paradores del Castillo looks more of a heritage house than a hotel, except for modern comfort like A/C. Rooms provide a view of the historical downtown. There are food and laundry service available on site. The hotel also handles tour reservations for some heritage houses such as Casa Villavicencio.

name: Casa Punzulan
description: A heritage house that the heirs have turned over to a historical society. The hotel is mostly run by volunteers; you may arrive to find no-one on duty to receive you, but there is a phone number posted by the door that will set a volunteer scurrying to help. Free TV & Wifi.

name: Taal Imperial Resort and Hotel
description: Mansion-like resort with private swimming pool. Option of shared rooms with double-deck beds or deluxe rooms with twin beds. All rooms have A/C.

name: Casa Cecilia
description: Air-conditioned rooms, with an option of single or double bed. Laundry service available. Has a function room and gazebo.

name: Balai Sofia
description: All rooms have air conditioning, beds are comfortable, and bathrooms have shower heaters available, but there are no free meals or an in-house restaurant.
price: Official rate is ₱1300, though it is possible to pay just ₱900 (including taxes and fees).

name: TDM Space Rental
description: Units have a single bed, living room and sink, but are fan-only.

name: Club Balai Isabel
description: Rooms also have good views of Taal Lake and the volcano. All rooms air-conditioned. There is a swimming pool, buffet, pizzeria and bar. There are some problems however, with the trash-filled lakefront and bathroom cleanliness.

name: Villa Khristalene
description: All rooms have air-conditioning and terraces providing views of Volcano Island and the lake. Better rooms have tubs and a small refrigerator. One suite has a balcony overlooking the volcano and lake. In-house restaurant serves Filipino cuisine, including Batangas regional specialties. They also have a bar, a swimming pool, karaoke rental, and a kids' playground. Parking is free.

name: Talisay Lakeside Villa
description: A two-storey house converted into a homestay for overnight visitors to Volcano Island. A part of the lakefront is turned into a swimming pool with inflatable slides.

name: Tabaco City Central Terminal
description: It has a quite spartan layout, with two open bus shelters, and a lot for jeepneys headed for downtown Tabaco and nearby towns.

name: A. Bragais Transport
description: Daily trips from Cubao and Pasay using non-air-conditioned buses

name: ALPS The Bus
description: Operates 2-2 seater air-conditioned "executive" buses from their Cubao base. Two trips depart from Cubao, with 2 return trips every 7:30AM (with stops at Calamba and Makati) and 5:45PM (with a stop at Calamba and Alabang).

name: Philtranco
description: Three daily trips depart from Pasay.

name: Amihan
description: Philtranco's sister bus line, with a daily trip to Tabaco from Cubao.

name: TAWTRANSCO
description: One daily trip departs from Starmall Alabang in Muntinlupa.

name: Angela Manalang Gloria House
description: An old two-storey house that was once the residence of Angela Manalang Gloria, a poetess who was born in Guagua, Pampanga in 1907 and died in Tabaco in 1995.

name: Tabaco Church
alt_name: San Juan Bautista Parish Church, St. John the Baptist Parish Church
description: Completed 1750, it is one of the two heritage churches in Albay that are designated as National Cultural Treasures.

name: Mayon Skyline
description: A view deck that features a planetarium.

name: Ishi Aya
description: Specializes in Japanese cuisine, but they also serve Filipino, Malaysian and Indonesian cuisine and fusion dishes.

name: MEACO Royal Hotel Tabaco
directions: Near Novo and LCC Market Plus

name: Hotel Fina
description: Has a rooftop pool and views of Mayon Volcano to the south.

name: Gardenia Hotel
description: The rooftop has a garden on top, and views of Mayon Volcano as well, but you need to ask permission to access it. All rooms air-conditioned. Free breakfast.
directions: A few meters from Tabaco City Mall

name: JSpazio Apartelle
description: Rooms come with 2 floors, and there is a cafe on the 3rd floor of the building.
directions: Next to the Tabaco City Social Security building

name: Odiongan Port
description:
Main seaport of the island. It is serviced by multiple ferry lines from:
Batangas: Daily overnight ferries (8–10 hours) via 2GO Travel, Montenegro, or Starlite Ferries. ₱900-2500.
Caticlan: 3 hours travel time via 2GO Travel. ₱600-1200.
Roxas: 3 hours travel via Montenegro, or Starlite Ferries. ₱400-900.

name: Santa Fe Port
description:
Southernmost seaport of the island. It is serviced by pump boats from:
Caticlan: 2 hours travel.

name: Looc Fish Sanctuary
description: The marine protected area located at the heart of Looc Bay features a floating raft hut where visitors can snorkel and rent a kayak to observe schools of fishes within the crystal-clear waters.

name: Blue Hole of Tablas
description: an underwater hole 10 meters below the surface where you can scuba or freedive

name: Binucot Beach
description: A pristine beach offering crystal-clear waters, perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and beach picnics.

name: Tinagong Dagat
description: Literally translates to "Hidden Sea", This stunning salt-water lake is surrounded by beautiful limestone formations and is remote enough that you could have the whole lake to yourself.

name: Victory Liner
description: Has daily trips from their Manila terminal. There are two terminals, one at Bulanao and another at Dagupan Oeste.

name: Naneng Heritage Village
description: The oldest barangay of Tabuk, it served as the town center during the American era. It is one of the few settlements in the Cordilleras with a mostly intact colonial center with two-story houses made of wood mostly dating from the 1920s, with the Chico River and the Cordilleran peaks as a backdrop. Expect to be invited to participate in the traditional rituals and chores of the Kalinga villagers and be encouraged to buy handicrafts, textiles and other items made by the community.
directions: Drive 45 minutes west from Bulanao and find the junction with a large welcome arch to Naneng

name: Nambaran Cemetery
description: Established in 1986, the cemetery is a stopover for motorists coming from Tuguegarao who are attracted by the various and sometimes wacky sculptures and artworks on top of the graves to commemorate those interred, ranging from everyday tools to signify the deceased's occupation to beloved pets and even liquor bottles to commemorate their favorite vices.
address: Sitio Ileb, Barangay Nambaran, Mountain Province-Tabuk-Enrile-Cagayan Road

name: Saint William's Cathedral
description: The seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Kalinga, built in an austere modernist style with a triangular facade.

name: Patiking Tunnel
description: An arch blasted through solid rock along a curve of the highway overlooking the gorges of the Chico River.

name: Chico River Dam
description: A scaled-down version of the otherwise ruinous Chico Dam project of the Marcos regime that provides irrigation for the region. While access to the dam itself is restricted, a viewdeck along the highway provides panoramas of the structure and the surrounding river valley.

name: Saint Joseph Parish Church
description: The oldest church in Tabuk, built during the 1920s.

name: Dalimuno Half-tunnel
description: A section of highway blasted the side of a limestone hill, with views of the Chico River on one side and a rock ceiling directly above in a semi-arch.

name: Patiking Tunnel
description: A section of highway blasted through the side of a limestone mountainside to create a hollowed-out arch.

name: Gessang Tunnel
description: A section of highway blasted through the side of a limestone mountainside to create a hollowed-out arch.

name: Tree Tops Tabuk
description: A forested resort with spring-fed swimming pools.

name: Daguitan Kan Tangkib Eco-Village Agri Farm
description: An agritourism resort with coffee plantation and swimming pool.

name: Ayuman Aggani Training and Assessment Center
description: A 16 ha farming estate with agritourism facilities.

name: PRAJ Pasalubong Center and General Merchandise
description: A shop selling Kalinga souvenirs and handicrafts.

name: Xentro Mall Tabuk
description: A mall built as part of the redevelopment of the Bulanao Public Market.

name: Ethnic Bothique Café Grill and Restaurant
Alberto's Pizzeria and Ristorante
description: Fusion western and indigenous Kalinga cuisine. The restaurant also makes their own pizza dough by hand.

name: Cornelius Farmville
description: A fruit farm on a steep mountain slope. They also sell home-made smoked meats (kiniing, kussassut and etag).

name: Tasty Pastry
description: A bakery known in the province for its egg custard pie.

name: Golden Berries Hotel and Convention Center
yKalinga Hotel
address: Provincial Road corner Tabuk-Paracelis Road, Bulanao

name: City Tourism Information and Assistance Counter
address: Arrival Area, DZR Airport, San Jose

name: Provincial Tourism Office
address: Leyte Academic Center, Pawing, Palo, Leyte

name: Department of Tourism Regional Office No. 8
Daniel Z. Romualdez Airport
description: This World War II US air base is the main entry point to Leyte (and Eastern Visayas in general) by plane. Tacloban Airport has one runway which can accommodate small passenger jets like the Airbus A320 family. This is badly damaged by Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) in 2013, but has been rebuilt, and in 2015, the airport is the venue of an open-air Mass during Pope Francis' visit to the Philippines.

name: Price Mansion
description: CAP Building served as the residence and headquarters of General Douglas MacArthur for three months.

name: Leyte Provincial Capitol
description: The seat of Philippine Commonwealth in 1944.

name: Philippine-Japan Commemorative Peace Park
description: Stone's throw away from city hall. It was donated by the Tokyo Survivors Associations in honor of soldiers and paramilitary personnel who perished in the area.

name: The Maria Kanon Madonna of Peace Shrine
description: Near the city hall. Carved out of a rare Miyagi rock and fashioned by Japanese sculptor Shiniche Tani.

name: Tacloban City Convention Center
description: Popularly known as the Astrodome.

name: Calvary Hill
description: Larger than life statues of Jesus Christ and other personages, in tableaux, depict Christ's sacrifice and sufferings.

name: Crucified Christ and the Map of Leyte Pilgrim Monument
Santo Niño Shrine and Heritage Museum
Indoor climbing at Bukid Outdoor Shop
San Juanico Bridge
description: It is one of the longest bridges in the Philippines. It connects the city to the third biggest island of the Philippines, Samar. The bridge spans 2.14 km and is one of the major tourist spots in the city.

name: San Juanico Golf Park and Country Club
The People's Center and Library
description: It houses volumes of books from the US and Europe and other countries.

name: Grand Santacruzan
description: May 30

name: Subiran Regatta
description: It is a race of one-man native sailboats with outriggers locally called "subiran" along scenic and historic Leyte Gulf. The race is done without using a paddle but only skills and techniques to manuever the sail.

name: Sangyaw Festival
description: June 29

name: Barrio Fiesta
description: Leyte Landing Anniversary, October 20.

name: Gaisano Capital Department Store and Supermarket.
Gaisano Central Mall
description: Has a Gaisano Supermarket.

name: Puregold Supermarkets
directions: one is near Tacloban City Hospital

name: Calle Z
description: It has a homey ambiance.
directions: Just ask the tricycle driver to bring you to this restaurant.

name: Pindoko's
description: Barbecues at very reasonable prices.

name: J C O Roasters & J C Food Spot
Zaibatsu Cafe Bar
directions: at right going to the provincial capitol from downtown Tacloban.

name: GV Hotel
description: Fan and a.c. single/double rooms with own bathrooms and cable TV. 137 rooms. free wifi.
address: Cnr of Juan Luna and Veteranos

name: Matthews Loding House
description: Fan single/double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Welcome Home Pensione
description: Fan/a.c. single/double rooms with or without own bathroom. Most rooms have cable TV.

name: Cecilias Lodge
description: Single/double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Travellers Suite
description: Fan single room. Shared bathroom. Free wifi.

name: Yellow Doors Backpackers Hostel
description: A hostel with dorm beds and single/double rooms that has its own bar.
address: Cnr of Burgos & Juan Luan St

name: Asia Star Hotel
description: In the downtown area.

name: Leyte Park Hotel
description: This used to be one of Tacloban's well kept charms, now totally destroyed. You will see a bird's eye view of the Canacabato Bay.

name: Hotel Canelsa
address: Realmstar Building, cnr Rizal Ave and P. Burgos St

name: Etsu Hotel
address: GYT Building, cnr Rizal Ave and Tarcela St

name: Baras Bird Sanctuary
description: you can see 7 species of migratory birds, without binoculars. There are 2 pathways to choose from. The easiest and shortest trail can be explored within 15 minutes while the full trail is approximately 30 minutes covering about 2.5 hectares.

name: Genalin Park & Zoo and Rescue Center
Tacurong Public Market
description: This is where you can buy local delicacies, supplies, fresh vegetables and fruits, meat and also purchase local handicrafts and pasalubong like Talakudong hats, Arnis sticks, malongs.

name: Lolo Mauring's Native Chicken
description: Best Sellers : BBQ Native Chicken and Binakol soup.

name: San Agustin
description: Links Tagaytay with Parañaque, Nasugbu, and Balayan. Most buses run from Parañaque to Nasugbu or Balayan, but there are some trips which terminate at Tagaytay.

name: Starliner
description: Departures from Parañaque. Buses are in a yellow, orange and red livery.

name: Tagaytay Jeepney Terminal
description: This terminal has a simple shelter for passengers, but passengers board from the sidewalk. It is served by jeepneys from Balibago, Santa Rosa and Calamba.

name: 11th Airborne Division Marker
description: On February 3, 1945, the 11th Airborne Division of Lt. Gen. Robert L. Eichelberger’s 8th U.S. Army airdropped military supplies and personnel together with the Philippine Commonwealth troops on the Tagaytay Ridge amidst enemy groundfire. Their mission was to secure Tagaytay City and guarantee the easy flow of troops and supplies to Manila, an action later proved as significant to the liberation of Manila. A marker was erected at the Silang Crossing to honor the event.

name: 41st Division USAFFE Marker
description: Tagaytay played a significant role in Philippine history. During World War II, Filipino soldiers and military officers found refuge on its vast forests and ridges. It was used as landing site and sanctuary for the Filipino USAFFE soldiers and paratroopers on their way to liberate Manila on February 3 to March 3, 1945. The 41st USAFFE marker is a place where one can know more about Tagaytay’s rich political history.
directions: at front of Sky Ranch, adjacent to the Metro Tagaytay College of Business and Arts

name: Divine Word Seminary
description: One of the biggest schools of theology in the Philippines in terms of population and land area, it is also one of the oldest religious institutions in the city. It is run by Divine Word Missionaries also known as SVD.

name: The Flower Farm
description: On a windy slope of a hill sprawls a flower farm that keeps Manila abloom whole year round. This five-hectare flower farm has many varieties of flowers, such as chrysanthemums with assorted colors, gerberas, carnations, roses, and anthuriums.
directions: in Barangay Guinhawa, a 10-minute drive from the Aguinaldo Highway

name: Japanese Friendship Garden
description: This 1200 m2 garden was constructed to inculcate the value of freedom, peace and international unity into the hearts and minds of the people. It is in front of Development Academy of the Philippines Conference Center, in Brgy. Sungay East.

name: One Destination
description: This travel spot in the sky city is a strip of fancy restaurants and bars. Being the nightlife hub of Tagaytay, it offers varied cuisine and entertainment to tourists. Some of the noted establishments around are Dencio's Grill, Pancake House, Starbucks Coffee, Yellow Cab, RSM, Leslies, Max's Restaurant, Cliffhouse, Antonio's Grill, and Henlin.

name: People's Park in the Sky
description: A blending of natural and man-made attractions, poised on the highest point of Tagaytay City and the province of Cavite. It stands on a 4516 m2 of solid ground and overlooks four bodies of water – Taal Lake, Balayan Bay, Laguna de Bay and Manila Bay - including nearby mountains. It is located at Dapdap West and Dapdap East, approximately 8 km east from the Tagaytay City Circle. The Palace In The Sky the main attraction of the site was designed to be the presidential guest house of former president Ferdinand Marcos, this complex was never completed. It is, however, now open to the public as a vantage area for viewing the Taal Volcano. The place is a short drive from the Aguinaldo Highway in Tagaytay City. It is 15 minutes' drive from Aguinaldo Highway.

name: Pink Sister's Convent
description: Behind the bars and glass of the Adoration Convent of Divine Mercy are those who answered the call to live in silence. Located at the Holy Spirit Drive in Barangay Maitin in the city, the convent often called the Pink Sisters Chapel has endless visitors carrying their own list of prayers. Also included in their visit is the chance to see nuns praying with them 24 hours a day, seven days a week, although they can only be seen behind the iron grilles of the altar.

name: St. Anne's Shrine
description: The shrine is a small garden where a grotto of the Virgin Mary stands, surrounded by well maintained shrubbery and flower garden. In front of the grotto is a small grass clearing, which is conducive to quiet reflection. From Manila, take BLTB buses that pass by Barangay Silang Crossing to the Tagaytay Marker. At Tagaytay Marker, alight to take a utility jeep leading to Barangay Sungay where the gate of the shrine can be spotted from the road.

name: Sky Ranch Tagaytay
description: 5 ha amusement park opened in 2013, with an assortment of rides, restaurants and souvenir shops. It houses the 63 m Ferris wheel Sky Eye.

name: Tagaytay Picnic Grove
description: Tagaytay's playground is the popular Picnic Grove, a large park that features huts and tables for picnicking, horseback riding, a restaurant, an eco-trail boardwalk, a zipline and cable cars on the gentle slopes of the Tagaytay Ridge. It is a prime location, providing the finest view of the volcano far below.

name: Tierra de Maria
description: A Catholic sanctuary garden known for its 50-foot statue of the Virgin Mary found right beside Tagaytay Picnic Grove. Catholics consider this as the HOME (Haven Of Meditation and Enrichment) of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

name: Puzzle Mansion
description: Museum which is reputed for holding the largest jigsaw puzzle collection in the world according to Guinness. The museum was started by puzzle collector, Georgina Gil-Lacuna.

name: Ayala Malls Serin
description: One of the newer malls, part of real estate conglomerate Ayala's development Serin, beside the Our Lady of Lourdes Parish.

name: Josephine Restaurant
description: Provides authentic Filipino cuisine, best if you are seated at the back, which has great view of Taal Volcano. They also provide catering for large events. The ambiance is good especially for lovers and families too. A very cool place specially starting during the "ber months", from September.
hours: Breakfast: 7-10AM; Lunch: 11AM-2:30PM (weekdays), 11AM-3PM (weekends and holidays); Dinner: 5-10:30PM (weekdays), 5-11PM (weekends and holidays)

name: Neul Borm
description: Korean dining, complete with hot pot and soju.
address: Tagaytay-Nasugbu Road corner C.M. Delos Reyes Avenue, Kaybagal South

name: Breakfast at Antonio's
address: Emilio Aguinaldo Highway, Barangay Tagaytay - Nasugbu Hwy

name: Hello Cafe
address: Lot 2F-8, Polivel Subdivision, Maitim Second East

name: Sip n' Brew by Miara Café
Kapeng Mainit -Tagaytay
address: Mahogany Avenue corner A. Cruz Herrera Maharlika East

name: Amora’s Home
description: Modern well maintained facilities, air-conditioned rooms with cable TV

name: Fat Bill’s Bed and Breakfast
description: Double and Family Rooms with TV and DVD player, and their bathroom has a hot and cold shower.

name: Tagaytay Lake View Villa
description: All rooms are equipped with air-conditioning, TV with cable channels, dvd player, breakfast, hot and cold shower with hygiene kit. Some of its facilities and services are mini-gym, mini-garden, kitchen facilities and housekeeping service.

name: Keni Po
description: In the heart of Tagaytay.

name: Starflower Tourist Lodge
description: Expansive views of Taal Volcano and Lake, rolling hills and greenery; mountain breezes from the balcony.
address: Km 62 Barangay Mendez West, Aguinaldo Highway

name: Tagaytay Econo Inn
description: 17 comfortable and quality rooms, fully serviced and furnished to international standards.
address: Tourism Ave. Hollywood Subd., Brgy. Francisco

name: Gloria De Castros Store.
description: Single/double fan room with own bathroom. Has a restaurant.

name: Alfonso Hotel
description: Each accommodation is air-conditioned and has cable TV and a private toilet and shower.
address: 4 Washington Ave., Royale Tagaytay Estates, Alfons

name: Days Hotel Tagaytay
description: Resorts sit on a ridge 2500 ft above sea level and overlooks Taal Volcano.

name: Hotel Dominique
description: Hotel Dominique is along Aguinaldo Hi-way, a few meters away from the Tagaytay Rotonda. All of their rooms are fully air-conditioned, have a cable tv, telephone with NDD/IDD, and refrigerator. For suites, a bath tub is available. Some of their facilities include swimming pool, spa, game room, bar and restaurant, and a souvenir shop.
address: Km. 55 Aguinaldo Hi-way, Brgy. Maitim II East

name: Emiramona Garden Hotel
description: They have 48 rooms and 2 villas, each has a cable television, DVD Player, night table with lampshade, wardrobe closet with a full-length mirror, refrigerator, safety deposit box, and a balcony, and have the only glass-enclosed indoor pool in Tagaytay, plus an indoor jacuzzi with its gardens and waterfall as a background.
directions: Aguinaldo Highway, near Pink Sisters Convent and Angels Hills

name: Golden Jade Hotel and Restaurant
description: This hotel and restaurant offers rooms equipped with air conditioning, television, private toilet and bath. Some of its facilities and services are bar, restaurant, fitness room/gym, parking and Wi-Fi.

name: Hotel Kimberly Tagaytay
description: Hotel offering 2 swimming pools, playgrounds, lush gardens, games room, free wi-fi.

name: The Lake Hotel Tagaytay
description: Overlooking Taal Volcano Lake. Offers spacious, modern, comfortable rooms and good service.

name: MC Mountain Home Apartelle
description: Each room has air conditioning, a television, deck or balcony, and private toilet and bath with shower. Rates include daily breakfast.
address: Km. 68.9 Tagaytay-Nasugbu Highway (Aguinaldo Highway), Buck Estate, Alfonso

name: Mi-jo Hotel Tagaytay
description: Filipino and American dishes are served in the restaurant and a breakfast selection can be served in the room.

name: Royal Taal Inn
directions: In Front of La Verna House of Pray

name: Tagaytay Wingate Manor
description: It offers 24 rooms, all of which have an air-conditioner, cable LCD television, and a mini-bar. Some of its amenities are 24/7 staffed reception area, swimming pool, and ample free parking. While staying here you can do some leisure activities like picnics, horseback riding, camping, golfing, and zip lining.

name: The Windy Ridge Hotel
description: Offers ten rustic, yet elegant rooms with hot and cold baths and private jacuzzis.

name: 8 Suites By Fat Jimmy’s
description: It provides eight uniquely designed chocolate themed rooms, spacious lobby, dining area, seminar rooms, infinity spa and a sprawling garden overlooking the Taal Lake. Lot 7, Ridge View Subdivision, Barangay Iruhin.

name: Lee Boutique Hotel
description: It offers rooms equipped with air-conditioning, complimentary Wi-Fi Internet access, Private toilet and bath. Some of its facilities and services are Oui Drink Tea Eat Rice Restaurant, free Wi-Fi Internet access, massage service on request.

name: One Tagaytay Place Hotel
description: 120 air-conditioned rooms with LCD TV & DVD player, Wi-Fi, minibar, microwave ovens and free morning newspaper.

name: Summit Ridge Hotel
description: Experience the best view of Taal Volcano and go cloud-watching at the coldest spot in Tagaytay City. Summit Ridge Hotel and Promenade features within it several shopping, dining, and recreational facilities. Summit Ridge is also a venue for meetings and banquets.

name: The Theodore Hotel
description: It offers accommodation rooms namely The Cherry Blossom, The Neo Baroque, The Skyline, The Moorish, The Farm, The Whimsical Garden, The Modern Filipino, The Geometric Room, and The Theodore. It has a lounge area, which is an exclusive recreational and dining area for checked-in guests. It consists of the patio where Chess and other board games are available for guest use. It also has a garden that has a splendid view of the Taal Lake.

name: Anya Resort Tagaytay
address: 4XPC+J47, Buenavista Hills Road, Barangay, Tolentino West

name: Tagbilaran City Tourist Pier
description: Handles more than 5,000 travellers on a daily basis. When leaving Tagbilaran, departing passengers have to pay a "terminal fee" of ₱20. Some boat tickets however already include the fee into the cost of the ticket, so check first before paying.

name: Carlos P. Garcia House
description: The residence of the former Philippine President and his family in Tagbilaran, it has been converted into a museum featuring presidential memorabilia. Much of the house's original furniture has also been preserved, including the former President's bed and work desk. While admission is free, a donation box is set up by the entrance.
address: A. Hontanosas cor. F. Rocha Sts., Poblacion II

name: Casa Rocha-Suarez Heritage Center
description: Built sometime between 1800 and 1830, it is one of the oldest standing structures in Tagbilaran, and one of the few remaining trading villas in Bohol. Owned by the Rocha-Suarez family, it was converted into a museum in 2005, with several of the family's furniture, heirlooms, personal effects and mementos, accumulated over five generations, on display.

name: National Museum of the Philippines, Bohol Branch
description: It was the Escuela La Niña, and then becsme the Provincial Library of Bohol. The museum was opened in July 2008 after moving from the Carlos P. Garcia House. The museum has exhibits on the wildlife, traditions and culture of Bohol, the island's geological history, as well as a room featuring paintings from students throughout the province.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II
directions: beside the Provincial Capitol of Bohol

name: Plaza Rizal
description: Formerly the Plaza del Principe, it is the traditional center of the city. A monument to José Rizal stands in the center, while a monument to Carlos P. Garcia stands to the east. A replica of the Chocolate Hills is located to the west beside the Rizal monument.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II
directions: in front of the National Museum and the Provincial Capitol of Bohol

name: President Carlos P. Garcia Memorial Park
description: The largest park in the city, it fronts the site of the future new Provincial Capitol of Bohol. A large monument to Carlos P. Garcia is located in the park's center.
directions: across from the Bohol Wisdom School

name: Site of the Blood Compact
description: One of the city's most famous tourist attractions. This is a sculpture commemorating the Sandugo (blood compact) made between Datu Sikatuna and Miguel Lopez de Legazpi in 1565, with a wonderful view of the Bohol Sea and coastal mangroves. 100 m to the east is a marker erected by the now-National Historical Commission of the Philippines in 1941 for the same event.

name: St. Joseph the Worker Cathedral
description: The seat of the Diocese of Tagbilaran, it is one of the six original churches of Bohol established by the Jesuits in 1595. The current church structure however dates back to the mid-1800s, after the original church burned down.

name: BQ Mall
description: This four-storey building has a movie theater, a BQ supermarket, several stores, and its own small department store with a large souvenir section.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

name: Island City Mall
description: The largest mall in the city, it has several shops, a movie theater, a department store and a large Alturas supermarket. The mall is also the terminus for a number of jeepney routes within the city and to neighboring towns.
directions: beside the Tagbilaran Public Market and the Tagbilaran City Integrated Bus Terminal

name: Plaza Marcela
description: This mall is the closest shopping center to the airport and seaport. Has a Alturas supermarket

name: Tagbilaran City Square
description: The smallest of the city's malls, it promotes itself as Tagbilaran's version of the Greenhills Shopping Center in Manila. It is built on the site of the old Tagbilaran Public Market, which moved to the city's northern outskirts beside the Island City Mall. The two-storey mall has several computer and mobile phone stores, and wholesale products on the second floor.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

name: Alturas Mall
description: Has an Alturas supermarket.

name: Chicken Ati-Atihan
description: The main competitor to Jo's Chicken Inatô, this open-air restaurant serves Filipino dishes alongside its special grilled chicken.
directions: up the street from the Tagbilaran City Tourist Pier

name: Garden Café
description: This restaurant is owned and operated by the Philippine chapter of the International Deaf Education Association (IDEA), and true to its ownership, most of the employees are members of the local deaf community.
address: Juan S. Torralba Avenue, Poblacion II
directions: beside the St. Joseph the Worker Cathedral

name: JERAC's Pizza
description: This pizzeria is home to Tagbilaran's largest pizza, measuring 22 inches (around ₱600).
address: G/F Gallares Court, Graham Ave. cor. Ma. Clara Wharf Rd., Cogon
directions: beside the entrance to the Tagbilaran City Tourist Pier

name: JJ's Seafood Village
description: Located along the shores of Tagbilaran Bay, this restaurant specializes in several cuisines, though true to its name, it serves many seafood dishes. The "village" also has conference facilities, a pool and a small hotel inside (₱850 for a double room).
address: Knights of Columbus Drive, Poblacion II
directions: beside the Knights of Columbus Wharf

name: Jo's Chicken Inatô
description: This restaurant specializes in chicken inatô, the Cebuano version of the more-well known chicken inasal found on Negros. They also serve Boholano versions of Cebuano delicacies, such as binakhaw (local kinilaw, or vinegared fish), as well as standard Filipino fare.
address: Carlos P. Garcia East Ave. cor. S. Matig-a St., Poblacion I

name: Shiang MaNou
description: Serving mostly traditional Cantonese dishes, this is one of two upscale Chinese restaurants in the city. It however also has a selection of budget meals for ₱75.
address: J. Borja cor. C. Gallares Sts., Poblacion II

name: Sweet Home Café
description: This quiet café is tucked away from the main downtown area. They serve coffee shop staples (i.e. cakes and pastries), and mains.
address: J. Borja cor. Remolador Sts., Poblacion II
directions: across from the Holy Spirit School

name: Club Sphere
description: Run by the Metrocentre Hotel and Convention Centre, it is the only nightclub in Tagbilaran, specializing in dance hits. Visiting DJs play here when they visit the city. The club is small though, with only a maximum capacity of 100 persons.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II
directions: on the ground floor of the Metrocentre Hotel and Convention Center

name: El Portal Inn
description: Located just outside the city center, but still very accessible.

name: Ellens Bed and Bath
description: Single fan shared bath. A/C single shared bath cable TV. A/C double shared bath cable TV. A/C double with own bath, cable TV. All bathrooms have hot water. Free Wi-Fi.

name: G V Hotel
description: Fan double room with own bathroom. Free Wi-Fi.

name: LTS Lodge
description: Single fan rooms with common bathrooms. A/C double rooms with common bathrooms. A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Marbella Leisure Hostel
description: Located very close to Plaza Rizal, this hostel is run by the Metrocentre Hotel and Convention Center.

name: Marcelina's Guest House
description: The closest hotel to the airport, this guest house has air-conditioned rooms with communal bathrooms. There is also a common mini-kitchen with a refrigerator and cooking/dining facilities.
directions: near the intersection with Benigno Aquino, Jr. Avenue and Airport Road

name: Nisa Traveller's Hotel
description: Although located close to Plaza Rizal, some of its rooms are windowless, and others may have a hospital-like feel. However, breakfast is included in the room price, and there is free Wi-Fi in the lounge area. Most of the rooms have a common bath.
address: 14 Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

name: Taver's Pension House
description: Clean, private rooms in the city center, with very friendly staff. All rooms have en suite bathrooms, and Wi-Fi is available in common areas.

name: TR3ATS Guest House
description: Has a 6-bed dorm, double and twin rooms. Cable TV and free wifi. Good place for backpackers.

name: Uptown Lodge.
description: A/C single rooms with common bath. A/C double rooms with own bath. Probably the cheapest A/C rooms in town.

name: Villa Camilla Pension House
description: fan single and double rooms with outside bathrooms.

name: Happy Time Bohol Guest House
description: 8-bed fan dorm & fan double rooms. Shared bathroom, free wifi.
price: Dorm bed ₱250 per person double room ₱400

name: Francesa's Inn
description: Air-con double room with shared bathroom. Cable TV.

name: O M Pension House
description: double air-con room with own bathroom. cable TV.

name: Dao Diamond Hotel and Restaurant
description: This hotel is owned and operated by the Philippine chapter of the International Deaf Education Association (IDEA), and profits generated by the hotel pay for the education of 400 deaf children in Bohol and Leyte. The hotel offers sign language classes and runs a night shuttle (₱15) to the city center.
address: Km 3, Jose A. Clarin Street, Dao

name: Darunday Manor
description: Located very close to Plaza Rizal, it has nine air-conditioned rooms, each with solar-heated showers and baths.
address: 22 Jose A. Clarin Street, Poblacion III

name: Le Pensione de San Jose and Restaurant
description: Close to Plaza Marcela, this hotel has a jazz bar on the ground floor.

name: Panda Tea Garden Suites
description: The closest hotel to the Island City Mall, it has its own restaurant, a keyboard for public use in the lobby, and telephones in all rooms.
directions: Across from the National Irrigation Administration building

name: Soledad Suites
address: J.C. Borja St. cor M. Parras St.

name: Bohol Tropics Resort
description: Located along the shores of Tagbilaran Bay, it has several amenities which are normally found only in the resorts of Panglao Island. A popular local nightclub called Laser Party Club is also located here.
directions: North of the Tagbilaran City Tourist Pier

name: Metrocentre Hotel and Convention Center
description: The only full-service hotel in the city center, it has a total of 72 rooms, including a presidential suite. It has a swimming pool, two restaurants and one of the city's two nightclubs, Club Atmosphere, as well as convention facilities.
address: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

name: Saint Augustine Parish Church
description: Tagudin's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in the 19th century. Its belltower, built separately from the church building, also functioned as a watchtower guarding against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The church's grounds also hold one of two sundials that were built in Tagudin during the Spanish era in 1841 and are the oldest in the country. The other is in the town plaza

name: Tagudin Town Plaza
description: A recreational and civic space surrounded by the town church and the old municipal hall. It contains memorials to the Battle of Bessang Pass, when the plaza was turned into an Allied field hospital, and one of two sundials that were built in Tagudin during the Spanish era. The other is in the yard of Tagudin Church.

name: Farola Lighthouse
description: A lighthouse overlooking the South China Sea built to commemorate the arrival by boat in the area of Belgian missionaries who replaced the Spanish friars in their task of evangelizing Tagudin and the animist highland areas in 1910. The surrounding beach is a mixture of black sand and pebbles.

name: Bimmanga Bangka
description: A small ecotourism venue featuring a creek surrounded by mangroves and other estuarine vegetation.

name: Ilocos Sur Welcome Arch
description: A massive archway marking the boundary between Ilocos Sur and La Union provinces. At the left side of the arch, if coming from the south, is a small visitor center with rest area.

name: Amburayan Bridge
description: A two-lane bridge overlooking the extensive riverbed of the Amburayan River that marks the actual boundary between Ilocos Sur and La Union provinces. On one side is a panoramic view of the river descending from the Cordillera mountains into the coastal plain while on the other side is an equally panoramic view of the river as it reaches the South China Sea. Underneath the bridge are some shacks ideal for those who want to take a swim.

name: Manila American Cemetery and Memorial
description: The largest American World War II cemetery in the World, containing 17,206 graves representing U.S. soldiers who died fighting Japanese forces during the Pacific War. Besides the graves, it contains a chapel, monuments, sculpted gardens and a museum with 25 mosaic maps depicting U.S. battles in the Pacific, making the area well worth a visit. Photo ID is required for entrance.
hours: Daily 9AM-5PM except Christmas and New Year

name: The Mind Museum
description: The top science museum of the Philippines, with stunning architecture and showcasing 5 main galleries with interactive exhibitions.
address: JY Campos Park, 3rd Avenue, Bonifacio Global City

name: Burgos Circle
description: A traffic circle and a public park surrounded by skyscrapers and by alfresco restaurants, cafes and bars, described as a "window to the Parisian lifestyle in the heart of Manila". In the center of the circles lies "The Trees" art installation by Reynato Paz Contreras, and bronze and brass sculpture representing three interlocking trees forming a done.

name: Forbestown Road
description: Linked to the Burgus Circle, Forbestown Road is probably one of Manila's most beautiful and pleasant streets, containing plenty of greenery and mixed used developments with several alfresco restaurants, cafes and bars.

name: Serendra
description: Mixed used development with contemporary decoration and several alfresco cafes and restaurants. It links the Bonifacio High Street to the Market! Market!

name: Uptown Parade
description: Next to the Uptown Mall, a two-floor "dining mall" with several alfresco restaurants and some clubs.
directions: at the crossing between 9th Avenue and 36th Street in Taguig

name: The Fort Strip
description: Building containing several restaurants, bars and clubs.
address: 28th Street Corner 7th Avenue, The Fort Bonifacio, Taguig, 1634

name: Tuscany Private Estates
description: It may sound a bit of joke to have a place named "Tuscany" just next to the "Venice Grand Canal" (and the next project in the area is named "Florence"). Regardless, it is a beautiful mixed used development in Neoclassical style, with plenty of options of alfresco restaurants and cafes facing the Upper McKinley Road.

name: Libingan ng mga Bayani
description: Cemetery for the Filipino soldiers who perished in the World War II, as well as for national heroes and former presidents, including Elpidio Quirino, Carlos P. Garcia, Diosdado Macapagal and Ferdinand Marcos. It contains several monuments, such as the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and memorials to Korean and Vietnamese soldiers who died in the Philippines.

name: Saint Anne Parish Church
description: Church built in Baroque style in 1587. In the old cemetery of the parish lies the Simborio, a dome-shaped funerary chapel build in the 1700s.
address: 18 Gen. A Luna St, Sta. Ana

name: BGC Arts Center
description: One of the few dedicated facilities in BGC for concerts and cultural events.
address: 26th Street corner 9th Avenue, Bonifacio Global City

name: Samsung Hall
description: Indoor theatre and convert venue located at SM Aura Premier (see #Buy).

name: MO_Space
description: Contemporary exhibitions, shows and performances from emerging artists.
address: 3rd floor, MOs Design Bldg, B2 9th Avenue, Bonifacio High Street

name: scatter hitam
description: Good quality contemporary art exhibitions from local and foreign artists.

name: Gondola ride at the Venice Grand Canal
description: Obviously the Venice Grand Canal mall (see #Buy) isn't Venice, but the price of a gondola ride here is also a small fraction of the "real thing". Plus the atmosphere surrounding the fake canal is lively, especially in the evening.

name: Bonifacio High Street
description: An open air shopping mall shaped as a vibrant pedestrian street occupying 3 blocks in the heart of BGC, and one of the area's most popular attractions. Besides a variety of shops, bars, restaurants, and a cinema it contains a park which often hosts contemporary art exhibitions and other events.

name: Fully Booked
description: Fully Booked's flagship store on Bonifacio High street contains 4 floors of books, magazines, and art supplies. Most books are in English, but there is a small foreign language section.
address: Ground Floor, B6, Bonifacio High Street

name: Market! Market!
description: If you think that BGC is all about expensive, high-end shopping you will be blown away when you step in the Market! Market!, a large shopping mall that besides regular shops, has also a fair share of "air-conditioned street shopping" with all sorts of bargains and even products of dubious origin. In the external part of the mall, the Fiesta Market also contains an open air food court and a small amusement park.

name: SM Aura Premier
description: If the Market! Market! is the shopping mall you wouldn't expect in BGC, the SM Aura is pretty much what you would expect - thin crowds and high-end shopping on its finest, although you can still find some affordable Filipino clothing stores. Even if the expensive shopping does not interest you, the curved L-shaped building is a sight to behold on itself. The Samsung Hall is also contained here.

name: Uptown Bonifacio
description: Mall forming a mixed used development with corporate towers, containing a mix of Filipino and international brands. The dancing fountain in the 4th floor is worth checking.

name: Venice Grand Canal
description: A shopping mall that is more like a tourist attraction, the Venice Grand Canal mall contains a replica of Venice's Grand Canal and a sight to behold, leaving far behind any "Fake Venices" you may have seen in Las Vegas or Macau. Besides gondola rides, it contains a small size replica of the Rialto Bridge and hosts free family-oriented performances. Still not many shops around, but the surroundings of the canal are packed with restaurants.
address: McKinley Hill Garden Villas, Cluster B, Upper McKinley Rd

name: BENCH Cafe
description: Cafe in the second floor of the Bench flagship store in Bonifacio High Street. Offers Filipino comfort food with a twist and with affordable prices. Don't expect superb service though. Their Halo-Halos are definitely worth trying.

name: Fiesta Market food court
description: The Fiesta Market located in the external area of the Market! Market! shopping mall contains a food court offering a range of street food.

name: Conti's Pastry Shop and Restaurant
description: The BGC branch of the famous Conti's pastry shop, famous for its mango bravo, sans rival and ensaymada. This branch seems specialised in take-outs so don't expect great service from the sit-in restaurant.

name: Las Flores
description: An authentic Spanish bistro from the popular Andilana group of restaurants in Barcelona, popular for its tapas and paellas.

name: Locavore BGC
description: Locavore is where laid-back Filipino grub meets trendy urban chic. This eatery and watering hole marries a slick industrial charm with an open bar, boasting an array of delectable drinks.

name: Manam Netpark
description: The menu is filled with comfort food and the Filipino classics! Simply delicious!

name: The Alley by Vikings BGC
description: International food buffet.
address: C1, Upper Ground Floor, Bonifacio High Street, Taguig, Metro Manila

name: Indus Modern Indian Kitchen
description: Indus is a veritable oasis of sumptuous Indian cuisine located in the bustling heart of Metro Manila. This fine dining establishment takes pride in offering an authentic Indian dining experience with a touch of modern sophistication.

name: Wildflour Restaurant - BGC
address: Ground Floor Six/NEO 4th Avenue corner 26th Street

name: George and Onnie's - BGC
description: George and Onnie's has got the welcoming service and flavorful Filipino cuisine down to a T, though a touch more culinary wizardry and an indoor pet-friendly policy could push it into the realm of restaurant legends.
address: Ground Floor, World Plaza, 4th Avenue corner 31st Street

name: The Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf - Bonifacio High Street
Tomatito Sexy Tapas Bar
address: BGC Corporate Center, 11th Avenue corner 30th Street

name: Skinny Mike's Bar & Restaurant
address: 2nd & 3rd Floors F&B Bldg. MC Home Depot, 32nd Street corner Justicia Drive

name: F1 Hotel
description: F1 Hotel offers superior room, deluxe king, deluxe double, city suite king and executive suite with air-conditioning, high-definition LCD TV and high-speed internet connection. Its facilities and services include Infinity lap pool, rejuvenation center, 24-hour room service and guest services.

name: Grand Hyatt Manila
address: 8th Avenue corner 35th Street, Bonifacio Global City

name: Shangri-La The Fort, Manila
address: 30th Street, corner 5th Avenue, Bonifacio Global City

name: Ascott Bonifacio Global City
address: 5th Avenue Corner 28th Street, Bonifacio Global City

name: The Resurrected Christ
description: The world's largest wooden rosary.

name: Gaisanao Mall of Tagum.
description: The largest Gaisanao mall in Tagum. Has a KFC.

name: Robinsons Mall & Robinsons Supermarket & South Star Drug
Puregold Tagum
description: Supermarket.

name: PNB Bank
description: Visa Card ATM.

name: Bank of the Philippines Islands BPI
description: Master Card/Visa ATM.

name: Metro Bank
description: Master Card/Visa Card atm.

name: BDO Bank
description: Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

name: Dencio's Kamayan Tagum
description: All you can eat and drink breakfast.

name: Mabini Shrine

description: The Shrine houses the remains and personal belongings of the revolutionary hero and "Brains of the Katipunan," Apolinario Mabini, who was a native of Tanauan. Mabini is known as the "Sublime Paralytic" who, despite his polio-induced paralysis, fired nationalism in the Filipinos and urged them to unite, with the sheer power of his writings. He wrote fiery articles against Spanish atrocities in revolutionary papers. His writings and memorabilia are kept here. His tomb lies at the middle of the site where a replica of the house where he was born also stands.

The library is about 100 m from the national road, jeepneys and tricycles service the area. About 5 to 10 minutes' drive from the town proper depending on traffic. name: Fort Drum
alt_name: "Concrete battleship", originally known as El Fraile Island
description: A heavily fortified sea fort, shaped like a battleship, built by the United States in 1909 as one of the harbor defenses at the wider South Channel entrance to the bay during the American colonial period. It was unique among forts built by the United States between the Civil War and early World War II, both as a sea fort and in having turrets. It was captured and occupied by the Japanese during World War II, and was recaptured by the U.S. after igniting petroleum and gasoline within the fort, leaving it permanently out of commission. The now-abandoned fort was named after Brigadier General Richard C. Drum, who served during the Mexican–American War and the American Civil War, and died on October 15, 1909, the year of the fort's construction. The fort is administratively part of Cavite City, but is geographically closer to Ternate.

There is parking at the end of the winding road to the site, where you will trek through pasture to the shrine at the foot of Mount Nagpatong.

name: Buntun Bridge

name: Sts. Peter and Paul Metropolitan Cathedral
description: The seat of the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao. The church with the belfry is the biggest Spanish colonial church in Cagayan Valley built by the Dominicans. It was constructed from 1761 to 1767 under the supervision of Fr. Antonio Lobato, OP. The cathedral suffered massive destruction in World War II losing its pipe organ, three wooden retablos, pulpit, wooden choir loft and the painted wooden ceiling all of which were from the early 18th century. The complex was rebuilt by Msgr. Bishop Constance Jurgens who is now entombed inside the church. The Cathedral is also said to be one of the beautiful structures that stood in the land and because of that impression, its portrait can also be seen in Vatican City. The traditional ringing of the cathedral bells for the Angelus and during Mass is still being practiced today. Its belfry is visible from a distance of 15 km.

name: St. Hyacinth Church
alt_name: San Jacinto Church, Ermita de Piedra de San Jacinto
description: An elevated historic chapel established in 1604, 100 years older than the Sts. Peter and Paul Cathedral. American soldiers during the Philippine-American War used it as headquarters in 1899. St Hyacinth is the patron saint of the city whose feast is celebrated every August 15 coinciding with the Pav-vurulun Festival. The oldest brick structure in the city is the first parochial building built by the Dominican fathers in Tuguegarao. The current structure is the latest in a process of rebuilding beginning in 1724, in 1892 after it was destroyed by an earthquake and reconstruction after World War II. The chapel was not heavily damaged during the war and as a result retains its original wooden retablo which dates to the 18th century.

name: Cagayan Provincial Museum and Historical Research Center
description: This is a general museum that houses an extensive collection of artifacts, antiques, ethnography, trade wares, heirloom pieces and liturgical works of the province and fossils of animals that once roamed the valley. The museum houses extensive data on the discovery of Callao Man by the National Museum of the Philippines. Since 2023, it is housed in the old provincial jail, which in turn used to be the Casa Tribunal de Cagayan that was built in 1877.

name: St. Paul University Philippines
description: It was founded by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres in 1907, who came to Cagayan upon the invitation of Bishop Dennis Dougherty. The school had its operation in a Spanish Convento, adjoining the Cathedral of Tuguegarao. The institution transferred to its present location in 1934 after it was acquired from the Dominican Order. The entire building complex became hospital and garrison of the Japanese forces during World War II and was bombed by the combined American and Filipino ground troops during the liberation in 1945. The institution became the first Catholic University in Cagayan Valley in 1982.

name: Horno Ruins
description: A Spanish-era brick kiln located at Barangay Bagumbayan. This was used to fire bricks to be used for various structures during the Spanish colonial era in Tuguegarao such as the Tuguegarao Cathedral and the San Jacinto chapel. It is found beside a basketball court.

name: Mestizo District
description: offers a wonderful glimpse into the Philippines' colonial past. The ancestral houses were mostly built by Chinese traders using a mixture of local, Asian and Spanish architectural styles. Movie fans recognize the streets from the movie Born on the Fourth of July. If someone looks closely, there are still evidence left from the shooting, e.g. signs in Spanish but hastily and thinly painted over with white paint.

name: St. Paul's Metropolitan Cathedral
description: The seat of the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia and built by the Augustinians around 1790, this cathedral features a unique design intended to minimize earthquake damage, called "earthquake baroque". Look out for the brass communion handrails forged in China, complete with Chinese characters scrawled by its ancient installers (if you look closely). The eight-sided bell tower is just south of the cathedral. Its position was actually the safety measure of the earthquake baroque style: it was built separately from the church so that it would not topple into the church in the event of an earthquake. Its eight-sided design reflects its Chinese feng-shui influences. If you look closely inside the cathedral, you can find the tombstone of the great Ilocano poet Leona Florentino (in the column near the entrance facing Plaza Burgos).

name: Plaza Salcedo (Luneta Park Musical Dancing Fountain)
description: west of the cathedral features a 17th-century monument to Juan de Salcedo, and was also the site of resistance leader Gabriela Silang's public hanging in 1763. Also within the site at the lagoon is the Vigan Dancing Fountain. This Korean-engineered attraction is the first of its kind in the country, and rivals the Bellagio Water Fountains in Las Vegas, Nevada.

name: National Museum/Padre Burgos House
description: also known as the Ayala Museum, this showcases the memorabilia of martyred priest Jose Burgos. Behind the house is the national museum (formerly the Ilocos Sur Provincial Jail), housing other ethnic and Ilocano artifacts such as artifacts, weapons, kitchen utensils, basketry, costumes, jewellery and Burgos memorabilia. There are also some dioramas showing important events in the history of Ilocos Sur, and a mini library. It just so happens to be where the Philippines' first Ilocano president, Elpidio Quirino, was born, his father having been a jail warden.

name: Plaza Burgos
description: is a favorite hang out for locals and is also used for staging major public events. It has also food stalls selling local snacks, especially the empanada. It is next to Vigan Cathedral and dedicated to the memory of Father Jose Burgos. Depending on the weather, the streets surrounding it (except for the street adjacent to the Empanadaan) are closed off to motorized traffic every Saturday and Sunday to allow people to walk the streets freely. It is a popular skateboarding venue among the locals.

name: Crisologo Museum
description: used to be the home of assassinated Congressman Floro Crisologo and wife Carmeling, former governor of Ilocos Sur. It contains Crisologo memorabilia.

name: Syquia Mansion
description: Vigan residence of President Elpidio Quirino, who married a member of the Syquia family. There are memorabilia inside the residence, including a campaign portrait of Quirino.

name: Calle Crisologo
description: It is what Vigan City is known for — streets lined with Spanish Era ancestral houses (with ancient tile roofs, massive hardwood floors, balustrades and azoteas in varying Spanish, Mexican, and Chinese architectural styles) and cobblestone streets, which led to Vigan's inscription in the list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Tourists can buy souvenirs or even ride a calesa (horse-drawn buggy). This street is also known as Vigan Heritage Village.

name: Barangay Pagpartian
description: Where the great conquistador Juan de Salcedo landed when he arrived in Vigan through the Mestizo River. Also the site of the city slaughterhouse, built during the Spanish Era (for which the barangay is named).

name: Hidden Garden
description: A wonderland of greenery, with a mini-snack bar nestled in the middle.

name: Quema House
description: The residence of the Quema family, considered by sociologist Fernando Zialcita as most representative of 18th-century Philippine architectural style.

name: Mindoro Beach

name: Simbaan A Bassit
description: This cemetery chapel found at the southern end of Quezon Avenue has a bell-gable design, the only one of its kind in the Ilocos Region. The chapel's name is an Ilocano term meaning "small church."

name: Donato House
description: Ancestral house.

name: Museo Nueva Segovia
description: Just adjacent to the Cathedral is the Archbishop's Palace of the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia, which dates from the 16th century during the Spanish era - the oldest archbishop's residence still in use in the Philippines. It was completed in 1793 after seven years of construction. It features sliding capiz windows and cut-out decorations with floral motifs. It has a back entrance that leads to the nearby Govantes Dike. The palace has a collection of priceless ecclesiastical artifacts and relics from other Ilocos churches.

name: Baluarte Resort and Mini Zoo
description: A zoo founded by local politician and businessman Chavit Singson, featuring the usual animals as well as hunting trophies from his safaris in Africa.

name: Parish of Saint Augustine of Hippo
description: Bantay's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1590. Access to the site has been partially restricted since an earthquake in 2022 that severely damaged the structure.

name: Bantay Watchtower

The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015. Access to the site has been restricted since an earthquake in 2022 that severely damaged the structure.

name: Our Lady of Hope Parish Church

name: Archdiocesan Shrine of Saint Vincent Ferrer
description: San Vicente's main Roman Catholic Church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1795. The site, along with the adjacent town plaza, municipal hall, and a building of the San Vicente Integrated School, which also dates back to the Spanish period, was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2020.

At both ends of the bridge are viewing platforms with panoramic vistas of the area, including the old arch bridge east of the river, which has now lost much of its span following typhoons and flooding.

name: Vigan City Fiesta
description: The Bigueños celebrate the Longganisa Festival every January 22 in accordance to the cityhood of Vigan. With a colorful street dancing competition along the Calle Crisologo, this festival features one of the city's products, the very well-known Vigan longganisa. On the 25th, Vigan celebrates its town fiesta in honor to its patron saint, Saint Paul.

name: Semana Santa

description: Live music.

description: Fan single/double room with own bathroom and cable TV. The inn has its own restaurant.
