name: Catanduanes Midtown Inn
description: AC single/double with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Solybel Lodge
description: Single/double rooms with shared bathroom.

name: Villa Tolledo Travel Lodge
description: Single/double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Minolo Port
description: A small but busy port where travelers can hire boats for island-hopping trips or snorkeling excursions.

name: Aninuan Falls
description: A secluded waterfall in the Aninuan area, offering a tranquil retreat surrounded by lush greenery. The trek to the falls takes visitors through a scenic jungle path with river crossings. The natural pool at the base of the waterfall provides a refreshing spot for swimming and relaxation.
directions: accessible via a short jungle trek from Aninuan

name: Talipanan Falls
description: A small but scenic waterfall hidden in the lush jungle near Talipanan Beach. The trail to the falls passes through Mangyan Village, where visitors can learn about indigenous culture. The falls have a refreshing natural pool, perfect for cooling off after the hike.
directions: a short trek from Talipanan Beach through a forested trail

name: Mangyan Village
description: Mangyan are the indigenous people of Mindoro, known for their distinct culture and traditions. Many Mangyan communities strive to preserve their way of life, avoiding outside influences. Visitors can learn about their customs, traditional crafts, and way of life. A reliable guide is recommended for visiting. Please be respectful and follow local customs.
directions: near Talipanan Beach, accessible by tricycle or motorbike

name: Ponderosa Golf Club
description: A picturesque 9-hole golf course perched in the hills, offering panoramic views of Puerto Galera and the surrounding coastline. Hiking to Ponderosa Golf Club from White Beach takes about an hour, with an uphill trail. The club also features a restaurant and viewing deck.

name: Stairway Foundation
description: An international NGO focused on helping street children and raising awareness about child protection issues. The foundation uses creative arts, education, and advocacy programs to support vulnerable youth. Visitors can tour the center, learn about their initiatives, and support their work.

name: Aninuan Beach
description: A quieter and less crowded alternative to White Beach, with accommodations and dining options.

name: White Beach Reef
description: A shallow coral reef near White Beach, great for snorkeling, beginner diving and underwater photography.

name: Talipanan Beach
description: A peaceful beach, Talipanan Beach is a spot for swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying fresh seafood at beachfront restaurants. The beach is also home to Luca’s Italian Restaurant, a well-known spot for pizzas and homemade pasta.

name: FreeDive School
description: Freediving courses ranging from beginner to instructor levels, including specialized training in breath-hold techniques, deep freediving, and safety protocols. Also offers accommodation.

name: Euronet Worldwide ATM
description: One of the few ATMs on White Beach that accepts international cards. Cash withdrawal fees apply, and the machine may run out of cash during peak tourist season.
directions: on the main strip of White Beach
price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

name: Parkway Shopping Mart
description: A store offering a variety of essential goods, snacks, beverages, toiletries, and some imported items. A good place to stock up on supplies while staying in White Beach.

name: 7-Eleven
description: A convenience store offering a selection of snacks, drinks, basic groceries, and travel essentials.

name: Local Market Street
description: A lively street lined with small shops, fruit stalls, local eateries, and souvenir stores. A place to grab fresh tropical fruits, try local street food, or find handmade crafts and beach essentials.

name: Polycare Pharmacy
description: A small but well-stocked pharmacy offering over-the-counter medications, first-aid supplies, and basic personal care products.

name: Palawan Express
description: Offers currency exchange services. Also provides money transfer, bill payments, and financial services.

name: Resto Veranda
description: A beachfront restaurant offering a mix of Filipino and international cuisine. Known for its seafood dishes, grilled specialties, and refreshing tropical drinks.

name: Café Marco
description: A cozy beach café serving a selection of coffee, pastries, and light meals.

name: Arcobaleno Pizza
description: A casual Italian eatery specializing in wood-fired pizzas, pasta, and Mediterranean dishes.

name: Foodtrip Sa Galera Fastfoods
description: A local eatery serving Filipino fast food and street food favorites.

name: Yego's Restaurant
description: A restaurant offering a variety of Filipino and international dishes, including grilled seafood, rice meals, and refreshing tropical drinks.

name: Il Capo Smoke Haus
description: A barbecue and smokehouse-style restaurant offering grilled meats, smoked specialties, and Filipino-American fusion dishes.

name: Izakaya Abe Chang
description: A Japanese izakaya-style restaurant serving authentic sushi, sashimi, grilled skewers, and ramen.

name: Mai Pho Chaolong House
description: A casual Vietnamese eatery specializing in pho, chaolong (Vietnamese beef stew), and bánh mì.

name: Tamarind Bar & Restaurant
description: This restaurant by the sea side has a wooden roof. Food options are similar to typical bar & grill restaurants.

name: Wally's Bar
description: A beachfront bar known for its cold beers and tropical cocktails and sunset views.

name: Tamarind Bar
description: A beachfront bar with a great selection of cocktails, beers, and bar snacks. Often features live music and fire dancing performances in the evening.

name: Pirata
description: A sports bar and restaurant, offering cold drinks, international cuisine, and live sports screenings. A roadside venue attracting both locals and travelers.

name: Blue Water Lodge
description: Each room is air-conditioned, with cable TV and a private toilet and bath with hot & cold shower. The Standard Rooms have one queen-sized bed, while the Deluxe Rooms have two.

name: Manalo′s Guesthouse
description: Each room is air-conditioned, with a living room/lounge area, kitchenette, and private toilet and shower.
directions: Five-minute walk from famous White Beach

name: Sea Jewel Beach Resort
description: Twin, triple, quad and family rooms, all equipped with air-conditioning, and 21-inch flat screen TV with cable channels. Facilities and services are Restaurant and Free Wi-Fi Internet access.

name: White Beach Resort, Bar and Restaurant
description: Comes with air-conditioning, a toilet and shower, and dining area. In the morning, you can watch the sunshine spill from the skylight through your room's balcony.

name: Aninuan Beach Resort
description: A beachfront resort offering various accommodation options in a quiet and relaxing atmosphere away from the crowds.

name: Tamaraw Beach Resort
description: The owners are building a large conference center 5 meters from the main accommodation block and bungalows. On the other side 2 meters away the Sunset at Aninuan hotel is building a 3-floor extension. The access from the road to the beach is now severely restricted and only a small path remains for foot traffic.
price: Best rates on official website start at ₱2000

name: Surfing at Crystal Beach Resort San Narciso
The Coffeeshop Restaurant and Rooftop Hotel
description: The Coffeeshop Restaurant was built in April 1984 and remains one of the most popular restaurant in Barrio Barretto. It is well-known as the "Home of the Jumbo Tacos" and is located a few meters from several beach resorts. It serves local and international cuisines at affordable prices.
address: 2-3 Rizal Street, Barrio Barretto, corner National Highway, Olongapo City

name: Zamboanga International Airport
description: Well connected to the rest of the Philippines (despite the name and certification, there are only domestic flights).

name: Zamboanga Integrated Transport Terminal
description: Buses headed for Zamboanga all terminate here. There are food stalls, ticket booths, seats for waiting passengers. Jeepneys and tricycles to downtown are available from the terminal.

name: R.T. Lim Boulevard
description: You can visit the place early in the morning for brisk walking or jogging or in the afternoon for its famed sunset view. You can also spend some time at night eating Balut (a fertilized duck embryo that is boiled and eaten with vinegar and salt).

name: Fort Pilar Shrine
description: Founded in 1635 as a garrison during the Spanish period, the Fort Pilar serves as a present day open-air shrine. Built as La Fuerza Real de San Jose, the fort is now named after and dedicated to Our Lady of the Pillar, the patroness of the Archdiocese of Zamboanga. Its image is embossed at the altar (which was then an entrance of the fort).
price: Free, although you are encouraged to buy candles for ₱10

name: Fort Pilar National Museum
description: Fort Pilar also houses a National Museum branch inside the fort. You can appreciate the glorious past of Zamboanga as a Spanish city here in the museum. It also has record of inhabitants and antique items of the early time. It also exhibits paintings, natural marine life and cultural memorabilia. Excellent air conditioning.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Immaculate Conception
description: Founded in 1810 as a parish at the present day Universidad de Zamboanga campus, the Cathedral is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Zamboanga (created in 1910 as diocese and elevated in 1958 as an archdiocese). It is known as one of the most modern cathedrals in Mindanao, built in 1998-2001. The cathedral's structure is cruciform, resembling a cross and its facade is patterned after a candle (which is connected to the Blessed Virgin Mary). The main church is on the second floor, with stained glass portraying the life of Mary and Asian saints as well as the history of Mindanao's dioceses starting from 1910. At the lower level are the columbarium, the day chapel, the adoration chapel at the left wing, the conference hall at the right wing, and the baptistery fronting the day chapel.

name: Old Normal School Building
description: Also known as the Western Mindanao State University (WMSU) Social Hall, the building was built during the American Era and was the center of education for most of Mindanao. It houses the College of Education of WMSU and is also the site where most cultural presentations are held. It also houses a museum.

name: Pasonanca Park
description: Traversed by a gently rippling stream, this park is the only one of its kind in the country. It abounds with trees, flowering plants, ferns, shrubs and 600 different species of orchids. Mindanao Governor John J. Pershing started the construction of Pasonanca Park in 1912. He sent for a parksman in the United States, Thomas Hanley, to prepare the plan and direct its execution. There is a treehouse nestling high in the branches of one big tree where guests could pass the night and hold communion with nature which, in the darkness, could still be perceived in the gentle rustling of the pine trees. Permission to use the treehouse, which is free, can be obtained at the Office of the Mayor.

name: Plaza Pershing
description: Plaza Pershing honors American general John Joseph "Black Jack" Pershing (1860 –1948) who defeated Muslim insurgents in the region.

name: St. Ignatius of Loyola Parish Church, Tetuan
description: Records shows that at the start, there was a small chapel constructed on a lot. Owned by Don Balbino Natividad, a permanent resident of Tetuan. (The Natividad is one of the biggest clans in the Parish spread throughout the city up to the hinterlands and reputed to be large property owners. Members held various positions in the government and parishes. At least one became a Jesuit priest.) In January 1863, apparently having reached the required number of Catholic would be parishioners and with the availability of the would-be parish priest, the St. Ignatius of Loyola Parish was created with a Jesuit, Rev. Fr. Ramon Barua, SJ as its first parish priest.

name: Sta. Cruz Island
description: The Great Santa Cruz island is known for its pink sand beach and sand bar, while the Little Sta. Cruz Island is a typical white beach, with pulverized-like sand. It is also a diving site and is host to a lagoon, a Muslim burial site and a badjao/samal community.
price: Environmental Fee: P20 + P5 (Terminal Fee) Boat Fees: P1000/boat (good for up to 10 pax) Cottage Rental Fee: Small (10 pax), P100; Medium (15 pax), P200; Pavillion (30 pax), P500

name: Taluksangay Mosque
description: This colorful mosque is in the barrio of Taluksangay outside the city center.

name: Yakan Weaving Center
description: Host to the only Yakan community in the city, the center is just across the famed La Vista de Mar beach resort at the border of Barangay Upper Calarian and Sinunuc and along the National Highway. You can witness the local people weaving intricately hand-woven clothes on giant looms as well as traditional brasswares.

name: Zamboanga City Hall
description: The construction of this building started in 1905 and it was completed in 1907, built by the US government for the American Governors of the area. Today, this serves as the City Hall of Zamboanga City where the Mayor holds office.

name: Zamboanga Golf Course and Beach
description: Known to be the "oldest golf course" in the Philippines. It was established during the American Occupation and is overlooking the Basilan Strait. It also is host to a public swimming resort managed by the Philippine Tourism Authority.

name: Bathe in Pasonanca's natural pools
description: Bathe in Pasonanca's natural swimming pools- where water flows freely from the mountains to 3 pools- Rotary Pool, Wee-wee Pool for Kids, Tanada Pool.

name: Sta Cruz Island
description: Swim and scuba diving in a pink sand beach in an unspoilt island

name: Savour the area's delicacies
description: Eat special delicacies like Baolo and Satti.

name: Visit Abong Abong Park
description: Climb the hill and do the Stations of the Cross during Holy week or any day of the year, visit the Scout Camps, the tomb of the unknown soldier and Mayor Cesar C. Climaco.

name: Visit the Aviary at Pasonanca Park
Visit the Fort Pilar Shrine
description: Light candles at the Fort Pilar Shrine.

name: Visit the Maria Clara Lobregat Park
Visit the Zamboanga Museum at Fort Pilar.
Mangroves Boat Tour (Sta. Cruz Grande Island)
description: While Grande Santa Cruz Island allures with its pink radiance, its beauty goes beyond appearances. It also keeps a trove of natural wonders. On the other side of the island is a lagoon fully adorned with mangroves, nourishing wildlife and promoting biodiversity.
address: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)
price: Boat to Yellow Boat Tour Jump-off: P300/boat (up to 10 pax) Yellow Boat Rental: P300/boat (good for 2 pax) Tour Guide Fee: P300 (good for up to 5 boats)

name: Vinta Rowing
description: The vinta is the traditional outrigger boat that is common in Mindanao, especially in the areas of southern Mindanao, Sulu archipelago, and the Zamboanga peninsula. It is famous for its vividly colorful rhombic sail, adding a splash of color to the waters of Sulu Sea.
address: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)
price: P300/boat (good for up to 10 pax) P100 (good for up to 10 pax)

name: Little Sta Cruz Island & Sandbar
description: Sitting northwest of Santa Cruz Grande Island, Little Santa Cruz Island is like a quick dash of paradise off the coast of the Zamboanga peninsula. The most recognizable feature of the island is the sandbar trailing on the easternmost point.
address: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)
price: P300/boat (good for up to 10 pax) P100 (good for up to 10 pax)

name: Once Isla Cruise (11 Islands)
description: A steadily rising tourist attraction is Once Islas (11 Islands), a string of islands and islets off the eastern coast of Zamboanga City. Not all islands are open to the public, but those that are accessible are great for swimming, sunbathing, and further exploring. There are designated snorkeling spots for those who want to take a peek into the underwater scene. Bisaya-Bisaya, Baung-Baung, and Sirommon are those that are accessible to the public.
hours: Mon-Thu Sat Sun 7AM – 3PM; Fri closed; the schedule might change without prior notice, so check first before going

name: La' Guerta Adventure Park
description: A sports and recreational venue.
address: Zone 3, Sitio Pole Diutay, La Paz

name: La Vista del Mar Beach Resort
description: A private resort popular with city dwellers, close to downtown. It has well-manicured and lushly-appointed gardens and a beautiful view of the Basilan Straight water and Santa Cruz Islands in the distance. The resort owners need to do a better job at cleaning the beach sand daily, along with the water that sometimes get covered with garbage in some areas from leftovers by picnickers.

name: Alavar's Seafood House
description: Beyond the extraordinary cuisine, Alavar Restaurant provides a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects the unique spirit of Zamboanga.

name: Hacienda de Palmeras Hotel & Restaurant
description: In a quiet residential area, garden setting; clean, comfortable rooms; hot water, TV, mini bar, quiet A/C; complimentary breakfast, airport transfers, internet access; restaurant on-site.

name: Hotel Salwa
description: An Muslim-owned hotel. Double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: RedDoorz @ Jardin De La Vina Hotel Zamboanga City
description: A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV.

name: Lantaka Hotel by the Sea
description: Rated with 3 stars, this high-quality property provides guests with access to massage, restaurant and hot tub on-site.

name: Preciosa Hotel
description: An affordable old hotel in downtown area.

name: Skypark Hotel
description: A/C double room with own bathroom and cable TV. This hotel is the tallest structure in Zamboanga, and has a Japanese restaurant.

name: Viva Pension House
description: A/C double rooms with own bathroom.

name: Malatapay Market
description: The farmer’s market is equally welcoming to townspeople, shoppers, tourists, and visitors. Specialties include: Handcrafted goods, woven bags and purses, woven floor/beach mats, tools, fruits & vegetables, fish (fresh & dried), Filipino "Good Will" clothing, bamboo furniture, housewares, prepared food, and restaurants with seafood, lechon baboy, cold beer and soft drinks. As you walk past the stalls and towards the ocean, you will enter an area with a livestock market/auction as well as sit-down restaurants, as well as the port where the boats to Apo island depart.
directions: 3 km north, along the National Highway

name: Wellbeach Dive Resort
description: Comfortable rooms, ocean views, garden views, fully equipped resort, equipment rentals, dive shop, large dive boat, daily trips to and from Apo Island. Resort-amenities include fully equipped dive shop, compressor room, fully equipped dive boat, outside rinse-off areas, showers, and drying closets for the equipment. Staff handle nearly all the details.

name: Kav's Beach Resort
description: Pool and restaurant. Dorm beds 450, rooms 2200, bungalow 3500.
